title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
賓興之典創自成周歷世浸
久沿革匪一仰惟
國朝集厥大成雖損益唯時而
道實並行取士專設科目重
經術也教之者唯一道而學
之者無二業類三歲而一試
===
===
馬簡其章者以薦是爲恒
制嘉靖十有九年實維試期東
藩守臣奉行唯謹巡按御史
李〔復初〕實當監臨之任振揚
風紀尤敦化源謂茲重典以
人事
君係焉罔唯專僻唯大同也維時
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

賓興之典，創自成周，歷世浸久，沿革匪一。仰惟國朝集厥大成，雖損益唯時，而道實並行。取士專設科目，重經術也。教之者唯一道，而學之者無二業。類三歲而一試，馬簡其章者以薦，是爲恒制。

嘉靖十有九年，實維試期。東藩守臣奉行唯謹。巡按御史李〔復初〕實當監臨之任，振揚風紀，尤敦化源。謂茲重典，以人事君係焉，罔唯專僻，唯大同也。維時
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

The ceremony of honoring and recommending worthy men originated in the Zhou dynasty. Through the long succession of ages, its continuities and changes have been manifold. We reverently consider how our dynasty has brought these traditions to their fullest realization. Although additions and reductions accord with the times, the Way is indeed carried forward alongside them. Special examination categories have been established for recruiting officials, reflecting the importance accorded to classical learning. Those who teach follow a single Way, and those who learn pursue no divergent studies. As a rule [?], an examination is held every three years, and those whose accomplishments are distinguished are selected for recommendation [?]. This is the established system.

The nineteenth year of Jiajing was duly an examination year. The officials charged with governing Shandong carried out their duties with the utmost care. Regional Inspector Li 〔Fuchu〕 held responsibility as Supervising Official. He upheld discipline and particularly cultivated the sources of moral transformation. He maintained that this important institution concerned serving the ruler through the provision of worthy men: it must not follow narrow or partial preferences, but seek broad agreement. At this time…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
巡撫都御史李〔中〕敷大崇本
敷德作人藩臬俊良咸善政
教乃爰咨諏廣容虛受斟酌
損益不唯其已唯其宜區定
乃檄左布政使沈〔教〕右布政
使張〔時徹〕爲提調官副使孫
〔禬〕僉事樊〔三畏〕爲監試官左
叅政雒〔昂〕右叅政張〔臬〕余〔鍠〕
右叅議李〔允升〕副使王〔揚〕吳
===
〔檄〕吳〔道南〕馬〔紀〕僉事沈〔澧〕饒
〔思聰〕汪〔東洋〕陳〔乙〕朱〔旒〕都指
揮鄔〔祐〕翟〔欽〕防範于外罔有
攸斁先是以禮聘學正王〔應〕
〔槐〕教諭文〔高〕爲考試官學正
punctuated:
巡撫都御史李〔中〕敷大崇本，敷德作人，藩臬俊良咸善政教，乃爰咨諏，廣容虛受，斟酌損益，不唯其已，唯其宜，區定。乃檄左布政使沈〔教〕、右布政使張〔時徹〕爲提調官，副使孫〔禬〕、僉事樊〔三畏〕爲監試官。左叅政雒〔昂〕、右叅政張〔臬〕、余〔鍠〕、右叅議李〔允升〕、副使王〔揚〕、吳〔檄〕、吳〔道南〕、馬〔紀〕、僉事沈〔澧〕、饒〔思聰〕、汪〔東洋〕、陳〔乙〕、朱〔旒〕、都指揮鄔〔祐〕、翟〔欽〕防範于外，罔有攸斁。
先是，以禮聘學正王〔應〕〔槐〕、教諭文〔高〕爲考試官，學正
translation_en:
… Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-chief Li Zhong broadly promoted respect for fundamentals [?], spread virtue, and cultivated talent. The outstanding officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions all excelled in government and instruction. They therefore consulted widely, welcomed diverse views with open minds, and weighed what should be reduced or augmented, considering not merely their own preferences [?] but what was appropriate, and settled the arrangements.
Orders were then issued appointing Shen Jiao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Zhang Shiche, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, as Proctors. Sun Hui, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Fan Sanwei, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, were appointed as examination monitors. Luo Ang, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Zhang Nie and Yu Huang, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners; Li Yunsheng, Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Wang Yang, Wu Xi, Wu Daonan, and Ma Ji, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Shen Li, Rao Sicong, Wang Dongyang, Chen Yi, and Zhu Liu, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Wu You and Zhai Qin, Regional Military Commissioners, maintained security outside. None was remiss in his duties.
Before this, Wang Yinghuai, an instructor in a subprefectural Confucian school, and Wen Gao, an instructor in a county Confucian school, had been formally invited to serve as Examiners. The instructor in a subprefectural Confucian school …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
萬〔宗義〕教諭魏〔廷〕甘〔惠〕袁〔邦〕
〔行〕關〔文〕〔鳴〕王〔賓〕陳〔達〕爲同考
試官〔應〕〔槐〕等被幣而行方秋
入境萃而愳曰艱哉厥任重
也匪唯公明曷其能鑒比至
則監臨而下諸吉藹藹心諧
力協諸需斬斬上裕下懌於
是向而喜曰休哉百度貞遂
吾曹𠫭是或以寡愆乃以丙
寅入院合提學副使呂〔應〕所
簡士二千三試之拔七十有
五人焉於是羣而慶曰彬哉
人文斅也以人事
君茲其庶幾已乃次第其名氏錄
punctuated: 萬〔宗義〕、教諭魏〔廷〕、甘〔惠〕、袁〔邦〕〔行〕、關〔文〕〔鳴〕、王〔賓〕、陳〔達〕爲同考試官。〔應〕〔槐〕等被幣而行，方秋入境，萃而愳曰：「艱哉！厥任重也，匪唯公明，曷其能鑒？」比至，則監臨而下，諸吉藹藹，心諧力協，諸需斬斬，上裕下懌。於是向而喜曰：「休哉！百度貞遂，吾曹𠫭是，或以寡愆。」乃以丙寅入院，合提學副使呂〔應〕所簡士二千，三試之，拔七十有五人焉。於是羣而慶曰：「彬哉！人文斅也，以人事君，茲其庶幾已。」乃次第其名氏，錄
translation_en:
…Wan Zongyi and the Instructors Wei Ting, Gan Hui, Yuan Bangxing, Guan Wenming, Wang Bin, and Chen Da were appointed Associate Examiners. Yinghuai and the others received the ceremonial gifts and set out. Entering the province as autumn began, they gathered and said apprehensively: “How difficult! This responsibility is weighty. Without impartiality and discernment, how could we judge?” When they arrived, however, all the gentlemen [?], from the Supervising Official downward, were gracious and cordial, united in purpose and effort. All the necessary provisions were in good order; those above were generous, and those below were pleased. They then turned to one another and said joyfully: “How excellent! All arrangements have been properly carried through. Taking part in this [?], perhaps we may make few errors.”
On the bingyin day they entered the examination compound, assembled the two thousand candidates selected by Lü Ying, the Education Intendant and Vice Commissioner, and examined them in three sessions, selecting seventy-five men. They then congratulated one another, saying: “How refined! Human culture is cultivated through teaching [?]. In providing men to serve the ruler, we have perhaps come close to fulfilling our charge.” They then arranged the successful candidates’ names in order and recorded…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
其文以
獻〔應 愧〕不佞僣序簡首唯山東
古青兖之疆宗岱浸海雄巨
爲天下冠故精靈之所鍾萃
代産聖哲而吾孔子實出是
邦雖聖神所毓必應昌辰合
上下四方爲土而是邦特專
美焉諸士隷玆恒自慶重而
稱雄焉顧無所謂發藴而演
道者乎孔子之道歷世尊尚
===
至于
國朝尤極崇重我
皇上建極齊聖匹孔而祖述尤
兢兢焉禮樂明備人文煥爗神
punctuated: 其文以獻。〔應 愧〕不佞，僣序簡首。唯山東，古青兖之疆，宗岱浸海，雄巨爲天下冠。故精靈之所鍾萃，代産聖哲，而吾孔子實出是邦。雖聖神所毓必應昌辰，合上下四方爲土，而是邦特專美焉。諸士隷玆，恒自慶重而稱雄焉，顧無所謂發藴而演道者乎？孔子之道，歷世尊尚，至于國朝，尤極崇重。我皇上建極齊聖匹孔，而祖述尤兢兢焉。禮樂明備，人文煥爗，神
translation_en:
…their compositions for presentation. I, Ying Kui [?], unworthy as I am, presume to place a preface at the beginning of this volume. Shandong occupies the ancient territories of Qing and Yan, with Mount Dai as its principal mountain and the sea as its great body of water; its grandeur surpasses all under Heaven. Thus, as a place where numinous essences gather, it has produced sages and worthies in every age, and our Confucius himself came from this land. Although the birth of sages and divine men must accord with an age of flourishing fortune, and the whole expanse above and below and in all four directions constitutes the realm, this land alone enjoys that distinction. Scholars belonging to this place constantly congratulate themselves, esteem their origins, and claim preeminence. Yet should they not also bring forth its latent riches and expound the Way?

The Way of Confucius has been revered through successive ages, and under our dynasty it has received the utmost veneration. Our Emperor establishes the supreme standard, equals the sages, and matches Confucius; he is especially conscientious in following and transmitting his teachings. Ritual and music are resplendent and complete, and human culture shines brilliantly; divine…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
機風運遐壤不遺諸士麗藻
繼輔濡染尤近顧無所謂興
起而速肖者乎乃今觀其文
組織語孟馳驟六經數陳王
道出入百氏崇正黜浮淑大
究邃炳炳蔚蔚罔非道精茲
非䆆
===
聖服孔而有得焉者耶觀乎人文
以化成天下茲其至哉雖然
文亦難言矣孔子以剛柔交
錯爲天文矣而贊天之道曰
純粹精也以文不在茲自任
矣而語其徒曰予欲無言吾
道一以貫之而門弟子德行
punctuated:
機風運，遐壤不遺。諸士麗藻繼輔，濡染尤近，顧無所謂興起而速肖者乎？乃今觀其文，組織語孟，馳驟六經，數陳王道，出入百氏，崇正黜浮，淑大究邃，炳炳蔚蔚，罔非道精。茲非䆆聖服孔而有得焉者耶？觀乎人文，以化成天下，茲其至哉！

雖然，文亦難言矣。孔子以剛柔交錯爲天文矣，而贊天之道曰：「純粹精也。」以「文不在茲」自任矣，而語其徒曰：「予欲無言。」吾道一以貫之，而門弟子德行
translation_en:
…its workings move like the wind, leaving no distant region untouched. The scholars here contribute in succession through their splendid compositions [?], and receive this influence at especially close quarters. Could they fail to be stirred to emulate the sage swiftly? Now, examining their writings, we find them weaving together the Analects and Mencius, ranging freely through the Six Classics, repeatedly expounding the Kingly Way, and moving among the writings of the hundred schools. They esteem the orthodox and reject the superficial, cultivate what is great and probe what is profound. Brilliant and richly accomplished, their writings contain nothing that is not the essence of the Way. Are these not men who have followed the sage [?], submitted to Confucius, and thereby gained understanding? “Observe human culture, thereby transforming and perfecting all under Heaven”: surely this is its highest realization!

Nevertheless, culture is difficult to discuss. Confucius took the interweaving of the hard and soft to constitute the patterns of Heaven, yet praised Heaven’s Way as “pure, unmixed, and essential.” He assumed responsibility for culture with the words, “Does not this culture reside here in me?” Yet he told his disciples, “I wish to say nothing.” “My Way is threaded together by one principle,” yet among his disciples there were those distinguished in virtuous conduct…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
文學言語政事殊能而不爲
異唯精也故交錯而時出唯
無言也故燦然而顯著唯一
也故殊能而崇德諸士於其
所謂精者錯者無言者顯著
者一者殊者參伍而有得焉
則深於文者也左右經綸無
===
往不利矣故曰神而明之存
乎其人默而成之不言而信
存乎德行不然吾不知其所
謂文者何如也雖然性與天
道不出文章之外而聽言觀
行孔子不諱焉則故有所謂
也諸士勗哉庶不負
punctuated: 文學、言語、政事，殊能而不爲異。唯精也，故交錯而時出；唯無言也，故燦然而顯著；唯一也，故殊能而崇德。諸士於其所謂精者、錯者、無言者、顯著者、一者、殊者，參伍而有得焉，則深於文者也。左右經綸，無往不利矣。故曰：「神而明之，存乎其人；默而成之，不言而信，存乎德行。」不然，吾不知其所謂文者何如也。雖然，性與天道不出文章之外，而聽言觀行，孔子不諱焉，則故有所謂也。諸士勗哉！庶不負
translation_en: …literary learning, speech, and government: their abilities differed, yet these did not constitute divergent ways. Precisely because it is pure, it appears in interwoven forms as the occasion requires; precisely because it is wordless, it manifests itself in radiant clarity; precisely because it is one, differing abilities serve to exalt virtue. If you gentlemen compare and examine what is meant by purity and interweaving, wordlessness and manifestation, unity and difference, and thereby gain understanding, you will have penetrated deeply into cultural refinement. In ordering affairs on every side, you will then find nothing that does not go well. Thus it is said: “To make it spiritually efficacious and illuminate it rests with the person; to accomplish it silently and inspire trust without words rests with virtuous conduct.” Otherwise, I do not know what this so-called cultural refinement would amount to. Nevertheless, human nature and the Way of Heaven do not lie outside literary expression; yet Confucius did not hesitate to listen to people’s words and observe their conduct. There was surely a reason for this. Exert yourselves, gentlemen! May you thus not fail…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
皇上求賢之本意也是舉也總理
河道時則有若都御史郭〔持平〕
有事鹺政時則有若御史
党〔承賜〕有事馬政時則有若
御史黎〔循典〕刻勵儒術司宣
文化其有事禮儀者則有若
給事中戴〔夢桂〕行人韓〔一右〕
===
劉〔三畏〕林〔應箕〕禮部員外郎
易〔寬〕咸會茲土樂觀厥成乃
若以
賀入者左參議張〔九敘〕副使錢
〔仝〕都指揮陳〔丹〕以公出者左
參政李〔士文〕以遷行者按察
使屈〔蘊〕夙與勞焉例得書故
punctuated: 皇上求賢之本意也。是舉也，總理河道，時則有若都御史郭〔持平〕；有事鹺政，時則有若御史党〔承賜〕；有事馬政，時則有若御史黎〔循典〕。刻勵儒術，司宣文化。其有事禮儀者，則有若給事中戴〔夢桂〕、行人韓〔一右〕、劉〔三畏〕、林〔應箕〕、禮部員外郎易〔寬〕，咸會茲土，樂觀厥成。乃若以賀入者，左參議張〔九敘〕、副使錢〔仝〕、都指揮陳〔丹〕；以公出者，左參政李〔士文〕；以遷行者，按察使屈〔蘊〕，夙與勞焉，例得書，故
translation_en: …His Majesty’s original intention in seeking worthy men. At this examination, those present included Censor-in-chief Guo Chiping, who had overall charge of river administration; Censor Dang Chengci, engaged in salt administration; and Censor Li Xundian, engaged in horse administration. They diligently cultivated Confucian learning and took responsibility for spreading civilizing instruction. Those engaged in ceremonial affairs included Supervising Secretary Dai Menggui; Messengers Han Yiyou, Liu Sanwei, and Lin Yingji; and Vice Director Yi Kuan of the Ministry of Rites. All assembled in this province and gladly witnessed the examination’s successful completion. As for those who came in connection with congratulations, they were Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Zhang Jiuxu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Qian Tong, and Regional Military Commissioner Chen Dan. Left Administration Vice Commissioner Li Shiwen departed on official business, while Surveillance Commissioner Qu Yun left upon transfer. They had already shared in the work and, according to established practice, were entitled to be recorded here; therefore…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
序
直隸蘇州府太倉州儒學學
正王應槐謹序
punctuated:
序。
直隸蘇州府太倉州儒學學正王應槐謹序。
translation_en:
…composed this preface.
Respectfully prefaced by Wang Yinghuai, Instructor at the Confucian School of Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the Directly Administered Region.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十九年山東鄉試
監臨官
巡按山東監察御史李復初〔學甫山西洪洞縣人　丙子貢士〕
提調官
山東等處承宣布政使司左布政使沈教〔敬敷浙江慈谿縣人　甲戌進士〕
山東等處承宣布政使司右布政使張時徹〔惟靜浙江鄞縣人　癸未進士〕
監試官
山東等處提刑按察司副使孫襘〔以誠錦衣衛匠籍浙江　嘉興縣人甲戌進士〕
山東等處提刑按察司僉事崔三畏〔敬父直隸蠡縣人　己丑進士〕
===
考試官
直隸蘇州府太倉州儒學學正王應槐〔汝旦福建閩縣人　戊子貢士〕
湖廣長沙府湘鄉縣儒學教諭文高〔子中廣西灌陽縣人　甲午貢士〕
河南南陽府鄧州儒學學正萬崇義〔克方江西進賢縣人　辛卯貢士〕
同考試官
河南開封府許州襄城縣儒學教諭魏廷〔子揚山西蒲州人　丁酉貢士〕
直隸寧國府旌德縣儒學教諭甘惠〔仁甫湖廣崇陽縣人　壬午貢士〕
福建汀州府武平縣儒學教諭袁邦行〔信叔江西豐城縣人　辛卯貢士〕
福建泉州府安溪縣儒學教諭關文鳴〔國隆廣東順德縣人　戊子貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖十九年山東鄉試

監臨官
巡按山東監察御史李復初〔學甫，山西洪洞縣人，丙子貢士〕。

提調官
山東等處承宣布政使司左布政使沈教〔敬敷，浙江慈谿縣人，甲戌進士〕。
山東等處承宣布政使司右布政使張時徹〔惟靜，浙江鄞縣人，癸未進士〕。

監試官
山東等處提刑按察司副使孫襘〔以誠，錦衣衛匠籍，浙江嘉興縣人，甲戌進士〕。
山東等處提刑按察司僉事崔三畏〔敬父，直隸蠡縣人，己丑進士〕。

考試官
直隸蘇州府太倉州儒學學正王應槐〔汝旦，福建閩縣人，戊子貢士〕。
湖廣長沙府湘鄉縣儒學教諭文高〔子中，廣西灌陽縣人，甲午貢士〕。
河南南陽府鄧州儒學學正萬崇義〔克方，江西進賢縣人，辛卯貢士〕。

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯子出
門人問曰何謂也曾子曰夫子之道忠
恕而已矣
質諸鬼神而無疑知天也百世以俟聖人
而不惑知人也
言近而指遠者善言也守約而施博者善
道也君子之言也不下帶而道存焉君
===
子之守脩其身而天下平
易
君子行此四德者故曰乾元亨利貞
象曰寒泉之食中正也
夫茅之爲物薄而用可重也慎斯術也以
往其无所失矣
復小而辨於物恒雜而不厭
書
后克艱厥后臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」子出，門人問曰：「何謂也？」曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」

質諸鬼神而無疑，知天也；百世以俟聖人而不惑，知人也。

言近而指遠者，善言也；守約而施博者，善道也。君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉；君子之守，脩其身而天下平。

易

君子行此四德者，故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」

象曰：「寒泉之食，中正也。」

夫茅之爲物薄，而用可重也。慎斯術也以往，其无所失矣。

復，小而辨於物；恒，雜而不厭。

書

后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, “Shen! My Way is threaded together by one principle.” Master Zeng replied, “Yes.” When the Master went out, the disciples asked, “What did he mean?” Master Zeng said, “The Master’s Way is simply doing one’s utmost for others and treating them as one would wish to be treated.”

To put it to the test before ghosts and spirits and have no doubts is to know Heaven; to await a sage a hundred generations hence without misgivings is to know humanity.

Words that are close at hand yet point far beyond are good words; holding to what is simple yet applying it broadly is the good Way. The gentleman’s words do not descend below his belt, yet the Way resides in them. What the gentleman holds to is cultivating his own person, and thereby all under Heaven is brought to peace.

Book of Changes

The gentleman practices these four virtues; hence it is said: “Qian: origination, success, benefit, and steadfastness.”

The Commentary on the Images says: “The cold spring’s water is drunk: this signifies centrality and correctness.”

Thatch is an insignificant material, yet its use can be important. Proceed with this method of caution, and there will be no mistakes.

Fu (Return) is small, yet distinguishes among things; Heng (Constancy) encounters complexity, yet does not grow weary.

Book of Documents

If the ruler can recognize the difficulty of being a ruler, and ministers can recognize the difficulty of being ministers, government will then be well ordered, and the common people will apply themselves diligently …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
德
克綏先王之祿永底烝民之生
君子所其無逸先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則
知小人之依
不良
簡厥修亦簡其或不修進厥良以率其或
詩
六月食鬱及薁七月亨葵及菽八月剝棗
十月穫稻爲此春酒以介眉壽
===
裳裳者華芸其黃矣我覯之子維其有章
矣維其有章矣是以有慶矣
豐水有芑武王豈不仕詒厥孫謀以燕翼
子武王烝哉
武丁孫子武王靡不勝龍旂十乘大糦是
承
春秋
冬十月齊師滅譚譚子奔莒〔莊公十年〕
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦〔文公三年〕秋公
punctuated:
德。
克綏先王之祿，永底烝民之生。
君子所其無逸，先知稼穡之艱難，乃逸，則知小人之依。
不良。
簡厥修，亦簡其或不修；進厥良，以率其或。
詩
六月食鬱及薁，七月亨葵及菽，八月剝棗，十月穫稻，爲此春酒，以介眉壽。
裳裳者華，芸其黃矣。我覯之子，維其有章矣。維其有章矣，是以有慶矣。
豐水有芑，武王豈不仕？詒厥孫謀，以燕翼子。武王烝哉！
武丁孫子，武王靡不勝。龍旂十乘，大糦是承。
春秋
冬十月，齊師滅譚，譚子奔莒。〔莊公十年〕
秦人伐晉。〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦。〔文公三年〕秋，公
translation_en:
…virtue.

Be able to preserve the former kings’ blessings and secure the livelihood of the multitude forever.

The gentleman takes freedom from idle ease as his abiding principle. First understanding the hardships of sowing and reaping, and only then enjoying ease, he understands what the common people depend upon.

Those who are not good. [?]

Distinguish those who cultivate themselves, and also distinguish those who do not; advance the good among them to lead those who … [?; the words “not good” appear separately above in the transcription.]

Book of Odes

In the sixth month they eat bush cherries and wild grapes; in the seventh month they boil mallows and beans. In the eighth month they beat down the jujubes; in the tenth month they harvest rice. With it they make spring wine to promote long life.

Luxuriant are the blossoms, richly yellow. I behold that gentleman: he possesses splendid accomplishments. Because he possesses splendid accomplishments, blessings attend him.

Along the Feng River grows millet. Did King Wu not devote himself to service? He bequeathed plans to his descendants, to bring peace and protection to his children. How great was King Wu!

The descendants of Wu Ding—those martial kings—were victorious in all their undertakings. Ten chariots bearing dragon banners bring forward the abundant sacrificial grain.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In winter, in the tenth month, the army of Qi destroyed Tan. The Viscount of Tan fled to Ju. 〔Tenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

Men of Qin attacked Jin. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕In autumn, the duke …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
伐邾八月己酉入邾以邾子益來〔哀公七〕
〔年〕歸邾子益于邾〔哀公八年〕
宋子哀來奔〔文公十有四年〕公子遂如齊逆
女　夏季孫行父如齊〔俱宣公元年〕夏仲
孫蔑如京師〔宣公九年〕公孫歸父如晉〔宣〕
〔公十有八年〕
春王正月公及齊侯平莒及郯莒人不肯
公伐莒取向〔宣公四年〕
禮記
===
在朝言禮問禮對以禮
樂也者聖人之所樂也而可以善民心其
感人深其移風易俗故先王著其教焉
温良者仁之本也敬慎者仁之地也寬裕
者仁之作也孫接者仁之能也禮節者
仁之貌也言談者仁之文也歌樂者仁
之和也分散者仁之施也儒皆兼此而
有之猶且不敢言仁也其尊讓有如此
者
punctuated:
伐邾，八月己酉，入邾，以邾子益來。〔哀公七〕〔年〕歸邾子益于邾。〔哀公八年〕
宋子哀來奔。〔文公十有四年〕公子遂如齊逆女。夏，季孫行父如齊。〔俱宣公元年〕夏，仲孫蔑如京師。〔宣公九年〕公孫歸父如晉。〔宣〕〔公十有八年〕
春，王正月，公及齊侯平莒及郯，莒人不肯。公伐莒，取向。〔宣公四年〕
禮記
在朝言禮，問禮，對以禮。
樂也者，聖人之所樂也，而可以善民心。其感人深，其移風易俗，故先王著其教焉。
温良者，仁之本也；敬慎者，仁之地也；寬裕者，仁之作也；孫接者，仁之能也；禮節者，仁之貌也；言談者，仁之文也；歌樂者，仁之和也；分散者，仁之施也。儒皆兼此而有之，猶且不敢言仁也。其尊讓有如此者。
translation_en:
…attacked Zhu. In the eighth month, on the jiyou day, he entered Zhu and brought back Yi, Viscount of Zhu. 〔Seventh year of Duke Ai〕 Yi, Viscount of Zhu, was returned to Zhu. 〔Eighth year of Duke Ai〕
Zi Ai of Song fled here. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Wen〕 Prince Sui went to Qi to escort the bride back. In summer, Jisun Xingfu went to Qi. 〔Both in the first year of Duke Xuan〕 In summer, Zhongsun Mie went to the royal capital. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xuan〕 Gongsun Guifu went to Jin. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Xuan〕
In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke and the Marquis of Qi sought to reconcile Ju and Tan. The people of Ju would not agree. The duke attacked Ju and took Xiang. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xuan〕
Record of Rites (Liji)
At court, speak of ritual propriety, inquire about ritual propriety, and respond in accordance with ritual propriety.
Music is what the sages delight in, and it can make the people's hearts good. It moves people deeply and transforms their customs and ways; therefore, the former kings established instruction in music.
Warmth and goodness are the root of benevolence; respect and caution are its foundation; generosity and magnanimity are its expression in action; humility in dealing with others is its capacity; ritual observances are its outward appearance; speech and conversation are its refinement; song and music are its harmony; distributing one's resources is its beneficence. The Confucian scholar possesses all these qualities together, yet still does not dare claim to be benevolent. Such are his deference and humility.

Second Session

Discourse
An established judgment that cannot be altered for ten thousand generations.

Edicts, Letters of Appointment, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
之事業致治太平而後無愧于曆數之
傳也堯之授舜曰天之曆數在爾躬允
執厥中此萬世聖學之源也當時二聖
躬行之實無容議矣禹湯文武皆傳此
者也而事業不同習尚亦異于所謂精
一執中者果能皆不悖與漢唐宋之君
此意微矣而爭國亦稱長乂何與其于
所謂曆數之傳果能無愧與天啓
皇明我
===
太祖高皇帝作
成祖文皇帝繼之皆挺然以堯舜之道自任其
發爲
聖諭以昭示臣民者皆可仰見也
列聖相承益隆紹述我
皇上亶聰明嗣
寶位道冠百王治隆萬世天人協應中外頌歌
真
當今之堯舜矣不知所謂
punctuated: 之事業，致治太平，而後無愧于曆數之傳也。堯之授舜曰：「天之曆數在爾躬，允執厥中。」此萬世聖學之源也。當時二聖躬行之實，無容議矣。禹、湯、文、武皆傳此者也，而事業不同，習尚亦異，于所謂精一執中者，果能皆不悖與？漢、唐、宋之君，此意微矣，而爭國亦稱長乂，何與？其于所謂曆數之傳，果能無愧與？天啓皇明，我太祖高皇帝作，成祖文皇帝繼之，皆挺然以堯舜之道自任。其發爲聖諭，以昭示臣民者，皆可仰見也。列聖相承，益隆紹述。我皇上亶聰明，嗣寶位，道冠百王，治隆萬世，天人協應，中外頌歌，真當今之堯舜矣。不知所謂
translation_en: …in practical achievements, bringing about orderly government and universal peace, and only then being worthy of the transmission of Heaven’s mandate. When Yao entrusted rule to Shun, he said: “Heaven’s appointed succession rests upon your person. Sincerely hold fast to the Mean.” This is the source of sagely learning for all ages. There is no room to question how those two sages personally put it into practice. Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu all transmitted this teaching, yet their achievements differed, as did their customary practices and preferences. Could they truly all have remained faithful to what is called being discerning and single-minded and holding fast to the Mean? Among the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song, this understanding had grown faint; yet their contending states [?] were also said to enjoy prolonged good order. Why was this? Could they truly have been worthy of what is called the transmission of Heaven’s mandate? Heaven inaugurated our august Ming dynasty. Our Emperor Taizu Gao arose, and Emperor Chengzu Wen succeeded him. Both resolutely took upon themselves the responsibility of following the Way of Yao and Shun. This can be reverently discerned in all the sacred instructions they issued to enlighten their subjects. The successive sage emperors carried on this tradition, increasingly honoring and furthering their predecessors’ work. Our present emperor, truly perceptive and wise, succeeded to the imperial throne. His Way surpasses that of the hundred kings, and his government excels through all ages. Heaven and humanity respond in harmony; those within and beyond the realm sing his praises. He is truly the Yao and Shun of our day. Yet we do not know what is meant by…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖學者果何為要與諸士子涵泳
聖化有年矣其悉心對揚以彰
繼往開來之盛
問先儒有云言人便以聖為志言學便以
道為志道者萬世無弊聖則學之的也
闕里儀刑萬古常存試以孔子之學與
諸士究之孔子嘗曰我非生而知之者
好古敏以求之者也又曰加我數年五
十以學易可以無大過矣乃知孔子之
===
所謂好而求者固有在也韋編三絕洪
勳可知十翼之發義昭燦然唐虞三代
之傳萬世生人之道賴以不墜者孔子
之學也可得聞與然而洙泗三千未聞
有以易請者而求仁之說乃諄諄焉何
也子思子述祖者也大本達道戒懼謹
獨於易何準孟子受於子思者也萬物
皆備性無不善於聖何述夫心本大同
道至簡易得意忘象乃為神解昔程子
punctuated:
聖學者，果何為要與？諸士子涵泳聖化有年矣，其悉心對揚，以彰繼往開來之盛。
問：先儒有云：「言人便以聖為志，言學便以道為志。」道者，萬世無弊；聖則學之的也。闕里儀刑，萬古常存。試以孔子之學與諸士究之。孔子嘗曰：「我非生而知之者，好古，敏以求之者也。」又曰：「加我數年，五十以學易，可以無大過矣。」乃知孔子之所謂好而求者，固有在也。韋編三絕，洪勳可知；十翼之發義，昭燦然。唐虞三代之傳，萬世生人之道，賴以不墜者，孔子之學也，可得聞與？然而洙泗三千，未聞有以易請者，而求仁之說乃諄諄焉，何也？子思子，述祖者也；大本達道，戒懼謹獨，於易何準？孟子，受於子思者也；萬物皆備，性無不善，於聖何述？夫心本大同，道至簡易，得意忘象，乃為神解。昔程子
translation_en:
…as for the learning of the sage, what indeed is its essential point? You candidates have been steeped in the sage emperor’s transforming influence for years. Apply yourselves wholeheartedly in responding, thereby making manifest the splendor of carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future.
Question: An earlier Confucian scholar said: “When speaking of being human, set your aspiration on becoming a sage; when speaking of learning, set your aspiration on the Way.” The Way remains free of defects through all ages; the sage is the target of learning. The exemplary model of Queli endures forever. Let us examine Confucius’s learning together with you candidates. Confucius once said: “I am not one who was born with knowledge; I love antiquity and diligently seek it.” He also said: “Give me a few more years, so that at fifty I may study the Book of Changes, and I may be free of great errors.” Thus we know that what Confucius loved and sought indeed had a definite object. His leather binding cords broke three times: from this we can recognize his great achievement. The meanings expounded in the Ten Wings shine brilliantly. It is through Confucius’s learning that the transmission from Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, and the Way for humanity through all ages, have been preserved from falling away. May we hear your account of this? Yet among the three thousand disciples by the Zhu and Si rivers, we hear of none who asked about the Book of Changes, while instruction on seeking benevolence was earnest and repeated. Why was this? Master Zisi transmitted the teachings of his grandfather. How do his teachings on the great foundation and the universally applicable Way, on vigilance and apprehension, and on watchfulness when alone accord with the Book of Changes? Mencius received his learning from Zisi. In teaching that all things are fully present within us and that human nature is invariably good, what did he transmit from the sage? The heart-mind is fundamentally shared by all, and the Way is supremely simple and easy. To grasp the meaning and forget the images is to attain wondrous understanding. Formerly, Master Cheng…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
受學於周茂叔而謂天理二字却是自
家體貼出來諸士學孔顔無所謂自解
若乎試言之毋讓
問治道亦多術矣然惟當務爲急宋儒程
顥曰治天下以正風俗得賢才爲本茲
非所謂當務者耶又謂必脩學校尊師
儒庶得士漸廣風俗日正吉哉言矣間
嘗竊論之禮曰廣谷大川異制民生其
間異俗若之詩書所稱歷代列國之俗
===
厚薄美惡種種異齊風土之說不誣矣
天之生才有君子有小人稽古聖狂賢
不肖忠佞貞回若陰陽晝夜歷歷可指
非天賦爲之爾耶夫謂教化可齊則彼
皆弗信何三代以還比屋可封之俗人
人君子之行邈乎未聞豈學校未脩師
弗隆與倘不由於教化則王制謂一道
德以同俗周敎顔謂師道立而善人多
非矣何三代以前又若彼也豈氣數之
punctuated:
受學於周茂叔，而謂天理二字却是自家體貼出來。諸士學孔顔，無所謂自解若乎？試言之，毋讓。

問：治道亦多術矣，然惟當務爲急。宋儒程顥曰：「治天下以正風俗、得賢才爲本。」茲非所謂當務者耶？又謂：「必脩學校，尊師儒，庶得士漸廣，風俗日正。」吉哉，言矣！間嘗竊論之，《禮》曰：「廣谷大川異制，民生其間，異俗。」若之《詩》《書》所稱歷代列國之俗，厚薄美惡，種種異齊，風土之說不誣矣。天之生才，有君子，有小人。稽古聖狂、賢不肖、忠佞、貞回，若陰陽晝夜，歷歷可指，非天賦爲之爾耶？夫謂教化可齊，則彼皆弗信。何三代以還，比屋可封之俗、人人君子之行，邈乎未聞？豈學校未脩，師弗隆與？倘不由於教化，則《王制》謂「一道德以同俗」，周敎顔謂「師道立而善人多」，非矣。何三代以前又若彼也？豈氣數之
translation_en:
…received instruction from Zhou Maoshu, yet said that the two words “Heavenly principle” were something he had come to understand through his own personal reflection. You gentlemen study Confucius and Yan Hui: do you have no understanding of your own of this kind [?]? Explain it, without demurring.

Question: There are many methods of governing, yet attending to the most pressing tasks is what matters most. The Song Confucian Cheng Hao said: “Governing the realm rests upon rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talent.” Are these not what we call the pressing tasks? He also said: “Schools must be put in order, and teachers and Confucian scholars honored, so that the recruitment of scholars may gradually broaden and customs become more upright by the day.” Excellent words indeed! Yet I have sometimes ventured to reflect upon this. The Book of Rites says: “Broad valleys and great rivers differ in their configurations; the people born among them differ in their customs.” As for the customs of successive dynasties and the various states described in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, their sincerity or shallowness, goodness or badness, vary in every way [?]. The explanation that invokes local environments is surely not unfounded. Among the people Heaven brings forth, there are gentlemen and petty men. Looking back to antiquity, we can clearly distinguish the sage from the deluded, the worthy from the unworthy, the loyal from the sycophantic, and the upright from the crooked, just as we distinguish yin from yang and day from night. Is this not simply the effect of their endowments from Heaven? If one asserts that moral instruction can make them alike, all these cases seem to belie it. Why, since the Three Dynasties, have we scarcely heard of customs under which every household deserved enfeoffment, or of conduct whereby everyone was a gentleman? Could it be that schools were not put in order and teachers were not sufficiently honored? If, however, these things do not depend upon moral instruction, then the statement in Royal Regulations, “Unify the Way and virtue so as to make customs alike,” and the statement attributed to Zhou Jiaoyan [?], “When the way of teachers is established, good people become numerous,” would be wrong. Why, then, were things as they were in the Three Dynasties and earlier? Could it be that the cycles of cosmic forces…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
說時兆同與抑別有其道不瑣瑣於條
教與夫立至治之基崇無爲之化非此
莫適也不審唐虞三代果何繇得以並
臻休美爲後世嘉慕若是哉諸士讀書
考古必有所得其詳著于篇以觀通達
之學
問儒者之學貴理不貴數豈以數與理睽
非學者事耶然盈天地間萬物者莫逃乎數數
即氣也氣之流行即理也而儒者弗知
===
可乎粵自天不愛道而河圖出伏羲則
之以畫卦道之祖也何歷數代而禹獲
洛書厥數乃與圖弗類豈天苞地符之
說顧弗同與說者謂河圖洛書相爲經
緯抑所謂經緯者或有脗契者與大衍
之數聖人教民揲蓍以求數於易曷爲
與圖書卒不一合而朱子又謂縱橫反
復若合符契何也易更四聖而象已著
數固羅絡於斯矣何經世之書更出一
punctuated:
說時兆同與？抑別有其道，不瑣瑣於條教與？夫立至治之基，崇無爲之化，非此莫適也。不審唐虞三代果何繇得以並臻休美，爲後世嘉慕若是哉？諸士讀書考古，必有所得，其詳著于篇，以觀通達之學。
問：儒者之學貴理不貴數，豈以數與理睽，非學者事耶？然盈天地間萬物者，莫逃乎數。數即氣也，氣之流行即理也，而儒者弗知可乎？粵自天不愛道而河圖出，伏羲則之以畫卦，道之祖也。何歷數代而禹獲洛書，厥數乃與圖弗類？豈天苞地符之說顧弗同與？說者謂河圖洛書相爲經緯，抑所謂經緯者，或有脗契者與？大衍之數，聖人教民揲蓍以求數於易，曷爲與圖書卒不一合？而朱子又謂縱橫反復，若合符契，何也？易更四聖而象已著，數固羅絡於斯矣。何經世之書更出一
translation_en:
…does the theory of qi and numerical cycles account for these differing times and signs [?]? Or was there another way, one that did not concern itself with the minutiae of regulations and instruction? For establishing the foundation of perfect government and promoting transformation through nonaction, no other way will serve. Yet by what means did the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties all attain such excellence that later generations admired and yearned for them so greatly? You candidates, having read books and investigated antiquity, must have gained insights. Set these out fully in your essays, so that we may see the breadth and penetration of your learning.
Question: Confucian learning values principle rather than numbers. Is this because numbers are at odds with principle and are no concern of the scholar? Yet none of the myriad things filling heaven and earth can escape numbers. Numbers are qi; the circulation of qi is itself principle. Can Confucian scholars afford to remain ignorant of them? When Heaven ceased to withhold the Way and the River Chart appeared, Fuxi took it as his model in drawing the trigrams: this was the origin of the Way. Why, then, when Yu obtained the Luo Writing several generations later, were its numbers unlike those of the Chart? Could the accounts of Heaven’s treasure and Earth’s token be inconsistent [?]? Commentators say that the River Chart and Luo Writing serve as warp and weft to each other. Does this description mean that there are points at which they correspond? As for the numbers of the Great Expansion, the sages taught people to manipulate yarrow stalks to seek numbers in the Book of Changes. Why do these ultimately fail to agree with the Chart and Writing? Yet Master Zhu also said that, considered vertically and horizontally, forward and backward, they fit together like the matching halves of a tally. Why is this? The Book of Changes passed through four sages, and its images were made manifest; its numbers were surely comprehensively encompassed within it. Why, then, did the Book of Supreme Principles Governing the World (Jingshi) introduce yet another …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
機軸不知與圖書大衍之數亦有所祖
述與範錫神禹而數弗傳宜不可考而
續矣或者補之乃有謂與三聖之易同
功豈源流考據果弗殊也天下理一而
已理同宜數同何先後變態若此茲惑
之夫以數觀數固儒者所弗屑以理觀
數則天時人事無所不該考之易彗可
徵矣若緊謂有之無所禱無之靡所關
然則三聖非與諸士幸不惜究言用數
===
所蘊
問財賦出于土田土田豐于人力此必然
之理也周禮大司徒有土會之法辨五
地之物生有土宜之法辨十有二土壤
之物以任土事以教稼穡樹藝有土均
之法辨五物九等制天下之地征而又
有草人稻人之職焉其教民力田舉賦
之法至精至備也可得言與齊地古稱
富強蘇秦田肯太史公之論皆可考也
punctuated:
機軸，不知與圖書、大衍之數亦有所祖述與？範錫神禹，而數弗傳，宜不可考而續矣。或者補之，乃有謂與三聖之易同功，豈源流考據果弗殊也？天下理一而已，理同宜數同，何先後變態若此？茲惑之。夫以數觀數，固儒者所弗屑；以理觀數，則天時人事無所不該，考之易彗可徵矣。若緊謂有之無所禱，無之靡所關，然則三聖非與？諸士幸不惜究言，用數所蘊。
問：財賦出于土田，土田豐于人力，此必然之理也。《周禮》大司徒有土會之法，辨五地之物生；有土宜之法，辨十有二土壤之物，以任土事，以教稼穡樹藝；有土均之法，辨五物九等，制天下之地征。而又有草人、稻人之職焉。其教民力田、舉賦之法，至精至備也，可得言與？齊地古稱富強，蘇秦、田肯、太史公之論皆可考也。
translation_en:
…a different framework. I wonder whether it, too, follows precedents in the numbers of the River Chart, the Luo Writing, and the Great Expansion. The Great Plan was bestowed upon the divine Yu, but its numbers were not transmitted; presumably they cannot be investigated and carried forward [?]. Yet someone has supplemented them, and some even claim that this work equals the Changes of the Three Sages in achievement. Can their origins, transmission, and evidential foundations really be no different? All under Heaven has but one principle. If the principle is the same, the numbers ought to be the same: why, then, have they undergone such transformations over time? This is what puzzles me. To examine numbers merely as numbers is indeed beneath the concern of Confucian scholars; to examine numbers through principle, however, encompasses every aspect of Heaven’s seasons and human affairs. Examination of the Changes and divination [?] can verify this. If one simply says [?] that their existence gives us nothing to pray to, and their absence has no bearing on anything, would that not make the Three Sages mistaken? You gentlemen, please spare no effort in exploring the matter fully and setting forth its underlying meaning [?].
Question: Revenue derives from farmland, and farmland becomes productive through human labor: this is an inevitable principle. In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education has a method for classifying land, distinguishing what grows in five kinds of terrain; a method for determining the suitability of land, distinguishing the products of twelve kinds of soil, in order to assign agricultural tasks and teach the cultivation of grain and other plants; and a method for equalizing land assessments, distinguishing five classes of products and nine grades, in order to determine land taxes throughout the realm. There are also the offices of the Grass Officer and the Rice Officer. These methods of teaching the people to work their fields diligently and of collecting revenue are exceptionally precise and comprehensive. Can you explain them? The territory of Qi was renowned in antiquity for its wealth and strength; the discussions of Su Qin, Tian Ken, and the Grand Astrologer can all be consulted.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
今之青濟登萊即古之齊也何土曠人
稀逃亡之屋蕭索相依蒿萊之田一望
無際間有一二膏腴民亦安土而又驕
悍逋稅相率為盜至抗令不能治夫土
田人民今昔一也而豐瘠聚散美惡相
懸如此何與往歲憲臣建議欲官給牛
具種子農器招民開墾三年而後舉稅
其謀未為不臧而迄今竟無成效何與
將以為地勢曠遠民不樂居耶然田金
城田許下田河中田豐州又皆為之干
===
干戈倥傯之間尚能收儲積之利我顧
不能復之于中原平治之世與將以為
土脉潟鹵民不見利耶然管子相桓公
致富強遂霸諸侯一匡天下即此地也
果何術以致之與茲欲荒閑闢而流移
歸賦稅完而驕悍格使地無遺利民無
遺力移風易俗以成熙皞之盛何施而
後可
punctuated: 今之青濟登萊，即古之齊也。何土曠人稀，逃亡之屋蕭索相依，蒿萊之田一望無際？間有一二膏腴，民亦安土，而又驕悍逋稅，相率為盜，至抗令不能治。夫土田人民，今昔一也，而豐瘠聚散美惡相懸如此，何與？往歲憲臣建議，欲官給牛具種子農器，招民開墾，三年而後舉稅。其謀未為不臧，而迄今竟無成效，何與？將以為地勢曠遠，民不樂居耶？然田金城，田許下，田河中，田豐州，又皆為之干干戈倥傯之間，尚能收儲積之利，我顧不能復之于中原平治之世與？將以為土脉潟鹵，民不見利耶？然管子相桓公，致富強，遂霸諸侯，一匡天下，即此地也。果何術以致之與？茲欲荒閑闢而流移歸，賦稅完而驕悍格，使地無遺利，民無遺力，移風易俗，以成熙皞之盛，何施而後可？
translation_en:
The present-day regions of Qingzhou, Jinan, Dengzhou, and Laizhou are the ancient territory of Qi. Why, then, is the land so deserted and its population so sparse, with the desolate houses of those who have fled standing beside one another, and fields overgrown with weeds stretching as far as the eye can see? Here and there are a few fertile tracts where the people are content to remain on their land; yet they are also arrogant and fierce, evade taxes, and band together as robbers, even resisting official orders beyond the authorities’ ability to control them. The land and the people are the same now as in antiquity. Why, then, are the differences in fertility and barrenness, settlement and dispersal, and good and bad conduct so great?

In past years, a censorial official proposed that the government supply oxen, equipment, seed, and farming implements, recruit people to reclaim the land, and begin collecting taxes only after three years. This plan was certainly sound; why has it nevertheless produced no results to this day? Should we attribute this to the vastness and remoteness of the terrain, which makes people unwilling to settle there? Yet farming at Jincheng, Xuxia, Hezhong, and Fengzhou was undertaken amid the turmoil of warfare [?], and still yielded the benefit of accumulated stores. Can we really not achieve this again in the Central Plain during an age of peace and good government?

Should we attribute this to saline soil, in which the people see no prospect of profit? Yet it was in this very land that Master Guan, serving as chief minister to Duke Huan, brought wealth and strength, enabled him to become hegemon over the feudal lords, and set all under Heaven in order. By precisely what methods did he accomplish this? Now, if we wish to open up uncultivated land and bring back displaced people, secure full payment of taxes and reform the arrogant and fierce, ensure that no benefit of the land and no strength of the people goes unused, and transform customs to attain an age of flourishing harmony, what measures must we take?

translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Master said, “Shen! My Way is threaded through by a single principle.” Master Zeng replied, “Yes.” When the Master went out, his disciples asked, “What did he mean?” Master Zeng said, “The Master’s Way consists simply of doing one’s utmost for others and extending to others the consideration one would wish for oneself.”

Li Panlong

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “This question on the Analects is intended precisely to assess candidates’ learning in discerning principle. Because essay writers fail to understand how to experience and put into practice doing one’s utmost for others and extending consideration to them, their discussions of the single unifying principle repeatedly become disjointed. In its precise and penetrating integration of the ideas, and its full and elegant expression, no essay surpasses this one.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The response ‘Yes’ and the explanation in terms of doing one’s utmost for others and extending consideration to them amply attest to the level Master Zeng’s cultivation had reached: he truly understood the sage’s teaching. This essay elucidates the purport of that transmission and reception with an immediacy rich in meaning. Anyone lacking profound understanding of principle and skill in expression could certainly not [?] have written it. My admiration! My admiration!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Its grasp of principle is true and penetrating, its expression refined and elegant. Like the plain water offered as ritual wine and the unseasoned sacrificial broth, it is plain yet full of flavor and meaning. Reading it inspires unceasing delight and admiration.” This must be a scholar who has perceived the Way. What doubt can there be about recommending him highly?

Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: “The language and reasoning are pure and correct.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “This is precisely the sort of writing that explains principle.”

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
大賢於聖道之傳契之速而明之盡也蓋一以
貫之聖人之妙道也大賢聞之即契而因以忠
恕明之非深造自得者其孰能與於此昔曾子
服膺聖人之教於道將有得矣夫子從而詔之
曰爲學莫貴於知要而至理不可以泛求爾參
也其知吾之道乎蓋應變而不膠者末也渾融
而有定者本也故事事而酬之用斯周矣而所
以周於用者理之一也物物而應之感斯通矣
而所以通於感者理之一也方其渾然在中也
===
而變化之出未始有虧也及其槩然具陳也而
貞固之存未始或撓也其斯以爲吾道乎曾子
聞斯言也儀刑之真久得於躬行之素而面命
之旨適投其神解之機故一唯之應初無留難
蓋不煩於贅詞矣及夫子既出而門人扣以傳
授之的蓋欲因言而得其心耳曾子於此有難
於直喻者故告之曰夫子之道一以貫之非有
他也亦求之忠恕而已蓋體不信也不可以言
達用之利也必本於存誠故邪僞是屏以盡己
punctuated:
大賢於聖道之傳，契之速而明之盡也。蓋一以貫之，聖人之妙道也。大賢聞之即契，而因以忠恕明之，非深造自得者，其孰能與於此？
昔曾子服膺聖人之教，於道將有得矣。夫子從而詔之曰：「爲學莫貴於知要，而至理不可以泛求。爾參也，其知吾之道乎？蓋應變而不膠者，末也；渾融而有定者，本也。故事事而酬之，用斯周矣，而所以周於用者，理之一也；物物而應之，感斯通矣，而所以通於感者，理之一也。方其渾然在中也，而變化之出未始有虧也；及其槩然具陳也，而貞固之存未始或撓也。其斯以爲吾道乎？」
曾子聞斯言也，儀刑之真，久得於躬行之素；而面命之旨，適投其神解之機。故一唯之應，初無留難，蓋不煩於贅詞矣。及夫子既出，而門人扣以傳授之的，蓋欲因言而得其心耳。曾子於此有難於直喻者，故告之曰：「夫子之道，一以貫之，非有他也，亦求之忠恕而已。蓋體不信也，不可以言達；用之利也，必本於存誠。故邪僞是屏，以盡己
translation_en:
How swiftly the great worthy grasped the transmission of the sage’s Way, and how fully he elucidated it! To have one thread running through all is the sage’s wondrous Way. The great worthy understood it as soon as he heard it, and then elucidated it through wholeheartedness and reciprocity. Who could attain this without profound study and understanding gained for oneself?
Formerly, Zengzi cherished the sage’s teachings and was approaching an understanding of the Way. The Master therefore instructed him: “In learning, nothing is more precious than knowing the essential point; ultimate principle cannot be sought through indiscriminate inquiry. Shen, do you understand my Way? Responding to change without becoming inflexible is the outward manifestation; being integrated as a whole and possessing constancy is the root. Thus, in dealing with each and every affair, its functioning is comprehensive; what makes its functioning comprehensive is the oneness of principle. In responding to each and every thing, its responsiveness extends throughout; what enables this pervasive responsiveness is the oneness of principle. While it resides within as an undivided whole, its manifestations in change never suffer any deficiency. When it is fully displayed in all its breadth, its abiding firmness is never disturbed. Is this not what constitutes my Way?”
When Zengzi heard these words, he had long grasped the true character of his exemplar through habitual personal practice; the purport of this direct instruction came precisely at the moment of intuitive understanding. Thus he responded simply, “Yes,” without the slightest hesitation, having no need for additional words. After the Master had gone out, the disciples asked Zengzi about the precise import of what had been transmitted. They wished, through words, to grasp the Master’s intent. Finding it difficult to explain this directly, Zengzi told them: “The Master’s Way has one thread running through it. There is nothing else: one need only seek it in wholeheartedness and reciprocity. If its substance is not genuine, one cannot speak of reaching understanding; effective functioning must be rooted in preserving sincerity. Thus one rejects perversity and falseness in order to give fully of oneself…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
也而亦因之以盡人篤實是崇以自成也而即
推之以成物由是而體用可一由是而上達可
幾斯非所謂一貫乎斯不足以盡夫子之道乎
是則學有淺深而道無二致觀此則夫子之善
教與曾子之善學胥可見矣雖然昔在孔門如
由之果賜之達求之藝及其他聰明才辯者不
少也而心學之傳乃在於質魯之參與如愚之
回焉何哉盖學在自得不在外求故仲尼之道
昭如日星諸子非不聞且見也而忠恕之要掛
===
約之訓乃唯顏曾從事焉則一貫之唯卓爾之
見又豈他人之所能與耶故曰善教者繼其志
質諸鬼神而無疑知天也百世以俟聖人
而不惑知人也
潘龍

考試官教諭文　批　說知天知人處精切透
徹無杜撰語而通結上節尤爲有見錄之
punctuated:
也，而亦因之以盡人；篤實是崇，以自成也，而即推之以成物。由是而體用可一，由是而上達可幾。斯非所謂一貫乎？斯不足以盡夫子之道乎？是則學有淺深，而道無二致。觀此，則夫子之善教與曾子之善學胥可見矣。雖然，昔在孔門，如由之果、賜之達、求之藝，及其他聰明才辯者不少也，而心學之傳乃在於質魯之參與如愚之回焉，何哉？盖學在自得，不在外求。故仲尼之道昭如日星，諸子非不聞且見也，而忠恕之要、掛約之訓，乃唯顏曾從事焉。則一貫之唯、卓爾之見，又豈他人之所能與耶？故曰：「善教者繼其志。」

質諸鬼神而無疑，知天也；百世以俟聖人而不惑，知人也。

潘龍

同考試官教諭闕，批：「聖人知天知人，本皆實事。此篇發揮明盡，可以占所養矣。」

考試官教諭文，批：「說知天知人處，精切透徹，無杜撰語，而通結上節，尤爲有見。錄之。」
translation_en:
…and thereby also enable others to fulfill themselves; they esteem earnest sincerity so as to perfect themselves, and extend it to perfect other beings. In this way, substance and function can be united, and higher understanding can be approached. Is this not what is meant by the single thread running through all? Is this not sufficient to encompass the Master's Way? Thus, learning has degrees of depth, but the Way has no divergent ultimate principles. From this we can see both the Master's skill in teaching and Zengzi's skill in learning. Nevertheless, among those formerly at Confucius's school, there were many intelligent and eloquent men: You with his decisiveness, Ci with his perceptiveness, Qiu with his accomplishments, and others. Yet the transmission of the learning of the heart-mind rested with Shen, who was plain and slow, and Hui, who seemed foolish. Why was this? Learning consists in grasping things for oneself, not in seeking them externally. Thus, Zhongni's Way shone as brightly as the sun and stars; the other disciples had indeed heard and witnessed it. Yet only Yan Hui and Zeng Shen devoted themselves to the essentials of conscientiousness and reciprocity and the teaching of “hanging and restraint” [?]. How, then, could others equal the assent to the single unifying thread or the vision of what stood loftily before them? Hence the saying: “One who teaches well carries forward the learner's aspirations.”

“To put it to the test before the spirits without doubt is to know Heaven; to await a sage a hundred generations hence without misgivings is to know humanity.”

Pan Long

Associate Examiner Que, an Instructor, comments: “The sage's knowledge of Heaven and humanity is in each case grounded in actual affairs. This essay elucidates the subject clearly and fully, allowing us to discern the author's cultivation.”

Examiner Wen, an Instructor, comments: “The passages explaining knowledge of Heaven and humanity are precise, incisive, and penetrating, with no fabricated assertions. The way the essay connects with and draws together the preceding section is especially insightful. Selected for inclusion.”

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王　批　善言聖人制作之本必
有究心于天人之學者
論君子之制作無間於幽遠者亦惟有以明天
人之理也盖理至於天人止矣君子明之以制
作則其於幽遠也何間哉中庸言居上不驕之
意以明人道及此謂夫君子之議禮制度考文
徵遠近合幽明而一之矣然豈得於偶合者哉
彼鬼神無形而難知何言乎無疑也而君子之
制作有以質之成能於屈伸之感而黙符其變
===
化之機祇見其相協也而無相疑焉盖鬼神者
造化之迹也而天則其統體也君子有以知天
之理於終始之故則大明焉於晝夜之道則通
知焉以之定經制而秩典章也先天而天弗違
後天而奉天時天且弗違而况於鬼神乎故曰
質諸鬼神而無疑知天也後聖未至而難料何
言乎不惑也而君子之制作有以俟之先立其
中正之準而適合其睿哲之謨但見其可因也
而莫之惑焉盖聖人者斯道之管也而人則其
punctuated:
考試官學正王批：善言聖人制作之本，必有究心于天人之學者。

論君子之制作無間於幽遠者，亦惟有以明天人之理也。盖理至於天人止矣，君子明之以制作，則其於幽遠也何間哉？中庸言居上不驕之意，以明人道，及此謂夫君子之議禮、制度、考文，徵遠近，合幽明而一之矣。然豈得於偶合者哉？彼鬼神無形而難知，何言乎無疑也？而君子之制作有以質之，成能於屈伸之感，而黙符其變化之機，祇見其相協也，而無相疑焉。盖鬼神者，造化之迹也，而天則其統體也。君子有以知天之理，於終始之故則大明焉，於晝夜之道則通知焉。以之定經制而秩典章也，先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。天且弗違，而况於鬼神乎？故曰：「質諸鬼神而無疑，知天也。」後聖未至而難料，何言乎不惑也？而君子之制作有以俟之，先立其中正之準，而適合其睿哲之謨，但見其可因也，而莫之惑焉。盖聖人者，斯道之管也，而人則其
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Director: This aptly explains the basis of the sage’s institutions. Its author must have devoted himself to studying Heaven and humanity.

To discuss how the gentleman’s establishment of institutions encounters no barrier even in what is unseen or distant: this rests solely upon his understanding of the principles of Heaven and humanity. For principle extends no further than Heaven and humanity. When the gentleman understands it and establishes institutions accordingly, what barrier can the unseen or distant present to him? The Doctrine of the Mean speaks of occupying a superior position without arrogance to elucidate the human Way. Here it says that the gentleman’s deliberation upon rites, establishment of measures, and examination of written forms seek verification in what is distant and near, uniting the unseen and the manifest. Yet could this agreement be merely accidental? Spirits have no form and are difficult to know: how can one speak of having no doubt? Yet the gentleman’s institutions can be tested against them. He accomplishes his work through the interplay of contraction and expansion, tacitly according with the workings of their transformations. There is only mutual accord, with no cause for doubt. Spirits are the traces of the creative transformations, while Heaven is their unified whole. The gentleman possesses the means to understand Heaven’s principles: he clearly comprehends the reasons for endings and beginnings and thoroughly understands the Way of day and night. By this understanding he establishes enduring institutions and orders statutes and regulations. When he precedes Heaven, Heaven does not depart from him; when he follows Heaven, he observes Heaven’s seasons. If even Heaven does not depart from him, how much less would the spirits? Thus it is said: “To test them against the spirits and have no doubt is to know Heaven.” Future sages have not yet appeared and are difficult to anticipate: how can one speak of being free from uncertainty? Yet the gentleman’s institutions can await them. He first establishes a standard of centrality and correctness, which accords precisely with their wise designs. One sees only that these institutions can be followed, with nothing to cause uncertainty. For the sage is the conduit [?] of this Way, while human beings are his …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
同類也君子有以知人之理莫微於性命而明
焉莫重於人倫而察焉以之昭軌則而成人文
也通變而使民不倦神化而使民宜之人舉弗
達也何獨至於後聖而疑之故曰百世以俟聖
人而不惑知人也夫然則徵庶民也考三王而
不謬也建天地而不悖也孰非理之一哉又孰
非本於吾身哉王天下者當知所從事矣是何
也有天德便可語王道自昔典禮之敘人紀之
修以至因時損益通百世而可知者要皆一德
===
爲之耳故不學則不知性命之理不知性命之
理則不可以立極於天下不知是而強欲以制度
文爲範民心而昭示後世亦末矣故曰作者之
謂聖述者之謂明蓋謂此也
言近而指遠者善言也守約而施博者善
道也君子之言也不下帶而道存焉君
子之守脩其身而天下平
黄觀
同考試官學正萬　批　善言善道乃孟子知要
punctuated:
同類也。君子有以知人之理，莫微於性命而明焉，莫重於人倫而察焉，以之昭軌則而成人文也。通變而使民不倦，神化而使民宜之，人舉弗達也，何獨至於後聖而疑之？故曰：「百世以俟聖人而不惑，知人也。」夫然則徵庶民也，考三王而不謬也，建天地而不悖也，孰非理之一哉？又孰非本於吾身哉？王天下者當知所從事矣。是何也？有天德便可語王道。自昔典禮之敘、人紀之修，以至因時損益，通百世而可知者，要皆一德爲之耳。故不學則不知性命之理，不知性命之理則不可以立極於天下。不知是而強欲以制度文爲範民心而昭示後世，亦末矣。故曰：「作者之謂聖，述者之謂明。」蓋謂此也。
言近而指遠者，善言也；守約而施博者，善道也。君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉；君子之守，脩其身而天下平。
黄觀
同考試官學正萬　批　善言善道，乃孟子知要
translation_en:
…of the same kind. The gentleman has the means to understand the principles of humanity: nothing is subtler than human nature and destiny, yet he understands them; nothing is weightier than human relationships, yet he discerns them. Through this he makes standards manifest and brings human culture to completion. He adapts to change so that the people do not grow weary, and transforms them with unfathomable efficacy so that they find their proper place. People universally fail to comprehend this [?]; why, then, should doubt arise only concerning a sage of later ages? Thus it is said: “To await a sage a hundred generations hence without misgiving is to understand humanity.”
If this is so, then verifying it among the common people, examining it against the Three Kings without error, and establishing it before Heaven and Earth without contradiction—are these not all expressions of the unity of principle? And are they not all rooted in one's own person? Those who rule all under Heaven should know where to direct their efforts. Why is this? Only with Heaven's virtue can one speak of the Kingly Way. From antiquity, the ordering of canonical rites and the cultivation of human relationships, extending to additions and reductions made to suit the times—all that can be understood across a hundred generations depends, in essence, upon this single virtue.
Thus, without learning, one cannot understand the principles of human nature and destiny; without understanding these principles, one cannot establish the supreme standard for all under Heaven. To fail to understand this, yet insist on using institutions, measures, and written forms to mold the people's hearts and provide an enduring example for later ages, is merely to attend to the superficial. Thus it is said: “One who creates is called a sage; one who transmits is called discerning.” This, surely, is what is meant.
“Words that are near at hand yet point far afield are good words; holding to what is essential yet applying it broadly is the good Way. The gentleman's words do not go below his sash, yet the Way resides in them. What the gentleman holds to is the cultivation of his own person, yet all under Heaven is brought to peace.”
Huang Guan
Comment by Associate Examiner Wan, School Director: “Good words and the good Way constitute Mencius's learning of knowing what is essential…”

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
之學此作體貼親切其身有之者乎
考試官教諭文　批　文理嚴整
考試官學正王　批　理達詞莊
大賢表言與道之善者不外於君子而得之也
夫近而指遠言斯善矣約以該博道斯善矣自
君子徵之不有可見者乎此孟子語人以知要
之學也謂夫非言無以明道非道無以廣用然
豈可以槩求之哉蓋天下之言亦多矣語或病
於支離而道不可以觸類非善也惟夫言之當
===
也未始及其他而指之達也自不膠於近聽之
若可忽而繹之則無窮也其斯以爲善言乎天
下之道亦多矣約或泥於致遠而博或流於寡
要非善也惟夫守在我也初非外之求而施諸
用也自足偏乎物操之則甚徵而推之則無盡
也其斯以爲善道乎何也自君子觀之服之有
帶也乃物之至近者也君子之言也離坐離立
隨所扣而應之固不下於帶矣而性命之原顯
焉百物之故昭焉擬議於顧瞻之地而究極乎
punctuated:
之學，此作體貼親切，其身有之者乎？
考試官教諭文批：文理嚴整。
考試官學正王批：理達詞莊。
大賢表言與道之善者，不外於君子而得之也。
夫近而指遠，言斯善矣；約以該博，道斯善矣。自君子徵之，不有可見者乎？此孟子語人以知要之學也。謂夫非言無以明道，非道無以廣用，然豈可以槩求之哉？蓋天下之言亦多矣，語或病於支離，而道不可以觸類，非善也。惟夫言之當也，未始及其他，而指之達也，自不膠於近；聽之若可忽，而繹之則無窮也，其斯以爲善言乎？天下之道亦多矣，約或泥於致遠，而博或流於寡要，非善也。惟夫守在我也，初非外之求，而施諸用也，自足偏乎物；操之則甚徵，而推之則無盡也，其斯以爲善道乎？何也？自君子觀之，服之有帶也，乃物之至近者也。君子之言也，離坐離立，隨所扣而應之，固不下於帶矣，而性命之原顯焉，百物之故昭焉。擬議於顧瞻之地，而究極乎
translation_en:
…learning that grasps what is essential. This composition apprehends it closely and intimately: could its author possess it in his own person?
Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “The composition and its reasoning are rigorous and well ordered.”
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the language dignified.”
The great worthy illustrates excellence in words and in the Way by finding it in the gentleman himself, without looking beyond him.
When words concern what is near yet point to what is distant, they are excellent words; when the Way is succinct yet encompasses what is extensive, it is an excellent Way. If we seek verification in the gentleman, is there not something we can observe? Here Mencius instructs people in learning that grasps what is essential. Without words there is no means of illuminating the Way; without the Way there is no means of extending its application. Yet how could these be sought indiscriminately? There are many kinds of speech in the world. Some utterances suffer from fragmentation, so that the Way cannot be extended by analogy: these are not excellent. Only when words are fitting, though they have yet to touch on other matters, does their import reach far, without being confined to what is near. On hearing them, one might think them negligible; yet their implications, when unraveled, are inexhaustible. Is this not what constitutes excellent speech?
There are also many ways in the world. Concision may become impeded in reaching far [?], while breadth may drift into a failure to grasp essentials: these are not excellent. Only when what one holds fast to lies within oneself, and is never sought outside, does its practical application suffice to extend throughout things [?]. What one grasps is exceedingly subtle [?], yet what one extends from it is limitless. Is this not what constitutes an excellent Way?
Why is this so? Consider the gentleman. The sash on his clothing is something very close at hand. In his speech, whether seated or standing [?], he responds to whatever is asked of him. His words indeed do not descend below his sash, yet through them the source of human nature and Heaven’s mandate becomes manifest, and the principles of the myriad things become clear. He considers and discusses what lies within sight, yet pursues to their ultimate extent…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
廣大之歸以爲止于帶也而實非止于帶也斯
不亦言近而指遠已乎吾之有身也其道之至
約者也君子之守也領惡全好踐其形而肖焉
惟以修吾身耳而所以行王道者在是所以錫
民極者在是率循其庸行之常而懋昭乎協和
之治人徒見天下之平也而不知其由吾身之
修也斯不亦守約而施博已乎善學者由是審
焉可以得修辭之則而成及物之功矣何以他
求爲哉抑易之言曰天道廣矣大矣而孟子乃
諄諄於近約之爲訓何哉蓋道不遠人自兩端
之竭無行不與之教以至於修己以安百姓篤
恭而天下平皆是物也戰國之時王教不行學
術漸裂不惟近約之求而專事於遠者博者不
有以反之將何以章道而淑人哉此孟子憂世
立教之意也
易
象曰寒泉之食中正也
潘龍
punctuated:
廣大之歸。以爲止于帶也，而實非止于帶也，斯不亦言近而指遠已乎？吾之有身也，其道之至約者也。君子之守也，領惡全好，踐其形而肖焉，惟以修吾身耳。而所以行王道者在是，所以錫民極者在是。率循其庸行之常，而懋昭乎協和之治。人徒見天下之平也，而不知其由吾身之修也，斯不亦守約而施博已乎？善學者由是審焉，可以得修辭之則，而成及物之功矣，何以他求爲哉？抑《易》之言曰：「天道廣矣，大矣。」而孟子乃諄諄於近約之爲訓，何哉？蓋道不遠人，自兩端之竭、無行不與之教，以至於修己以安百姓、篤恭而天下平，皆是物也。戰國之時，王教不行，學術漸裂，不惟近約之求，而專事於遠者、博者。不有以反之，將何以章道而淑人哉？此孟子憂世立教之意也。
易
象曰：「寒泉之食，中正也。」
潘龍
translation_en:
…the vast and comprehensive scope to which it ultimately leads. One might suppose that it stops at the belt, yet in truth it does not stop there. Is this not language that is close at hand yet points far beyond? Having this body of mine is where the Way is most concentrated. What the gentleman holds to—taking charge of evil and preserving good [?], fulfilling his bodily form and conforming to it—is simply the cultivation of his own person. Yet herein lies the means of practicing the kingly Way, and herein lies the means of bestowing upon the people their supreme standard. By following the constant norms of everyday conduct, he splendidly manifests harmonious government. People see only that all under Heaven is at peace; they do not know that this proceeds from the cultivation of his own person. Is this not holding to what is concentrated while extending its effects broadly? Those who learn well examine this closely. They can thereby grasp the principles of refining their words and accomplish the work of benefiting others. Why seek elsewhere?
Yet the Changes says, “The Way of Heaven is broad indeed, great indeed.” Why, then, does Mengzi so earnestly teach what is close at hand and concentrated? Because the Way is not distant from people. From exhausting both ends of a question and the teaching that no conduct is withheld from one's disciples, to cultivating oneself so as to bring peace to the common people and bringing peace to all under Heaven through earnest reverence—all concern this same matter. During the Warring States period, the teaching of the ancient kings was no longer practiced, and traditions of learning gradually fragmented. Rather than seeking what was close at hand and concentrated, people devoted themselves exclusively to what was distant and extensive. Without a means of bringing them back, how could the Way be made manifest and people made good? This was Mengzi's intention in establishing his teaching out of concern for the world.
Changes
The Commentary on the Images says: “The cold spring water is drunk: this is because of centrality and correctness.”
Pan Long

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭關 批〔題本冠冕學者累于陳言不能自脫化腐爲奇而題意益尊僅見此子〕
考試官教諭文 批〔詞理正大得象傳本旨〕
考試官學正王 批〔九五澤物之功本于皇極之德此作可謂善發明之矣〕
象傳於井爻即及物之功而著其德焉蓋德者
功之所由出也不然無本之治豈足以及物乎
象傳釋井九五爻義如此若曰王政以養民爲
先君德以敦化爲本兼體而不累者其惟井之
===
九五乎今以寒泉之美而見食於人言乎養之
大也則是善政所敷有以廣曲成之惠而兆民
奠允殖之休道澤所濡有以普兼濟之公而四
海安厚生之利矣若是者豈無其本而然哉蓋
仁之顯者用之藏者出之也達之順者體之信
者基之也今九五以陽剛居上體之中而得其
正則是皇猷允塞而道之萃於己者渾然天下
之大中皇極有建而德之裕於養者粹然天下
之至正由是因心之政自不假於強爲精神心
punctuated:
同考試官教諭關 批〔題本冠冕，學者累于陳言，不能自脫。化腐爲奇，而題意益尊，僅見此子。〕
考試官教諭文 批〔詞理正大，得象傳本旨。〕
考試官學正王 批〔九五澤物之功，本于皇極之德，此作可謂善發明之矣。〕
象傳於井爻，即及物之功而著其德焉。蓋德者，功之所由出也。不然，無本之治，豈足以及物乎？象傳釋井九五爻義如此。若曰：王政以養民爲先，君德以敦化爲本，兼體而不累者，其惟井之九五乎？今以寒泉之美而見食於人，言乎養之大也，則是善政所敷，有以廣曲成之惠，而兆民奠允殖之休；道澤所濡，有以普兼濟之公，而四海安厚生之利矣。若是者，豈無其本而然哉？蓋仁之顯者，用之藏者出之也；達之順者，體之信者基之也。今九五以陽剛居上體之中，而得其正，則是皇猷允塞，而道之萃於己者，渾然天下之大中；皇極有建，而德之裕於養者，粹然天下之至正。由是因心之政，自不假於強爲，精神心
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Guan, Instructor: 〔The topic itself is august, but students are encumbered by conventional expressions and cannot free themselves. Only in this candidate have I seen stale material transformed into something remarkable, further enhancing the dignity of the topic’s meaning.〕
Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: 〔The language and reasoning are upright and grand, capturing the original purport of the Commentary on the Images.〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: 〔The fifth yang line’s achievement in benefiting all things rests upon the virtue of the August Ultimate. This composition may be said to elucidate this well.〕
In discussing the line of the Well hexagram, the Commentary on the Images reveals its virtue through its achievement in benefiting all things. For virtue is the source from which achievement proceeds. Otherwise, how could government without a foundation suffice to benefit all things? Such is the Commentary on the Images’ explanation of the fifth yang line of the Well. It is as though it said: kingly government gives priority to nourishing the people, and the ruler’s virtue takes the deepening of moral transformation as its foundation. Is it not precisely the fifth yang line of the Well that embodies both without impediment?
Now, the excellence of the cold spring’s water makes people drink from it. To speak of the greatness of its nourishment: where good government extends, it spreads the beneficence that brings each thing to fulfillment according to its particular nature, and the myriad people are securely established in the blessings of abundant increase. Where the bounty of the Way permeates, it extends the impartiality of aiding everyone, and all within the Four Seas enjoy securely the benefits of an enriched livelihood. Could such results arise without a foundation? Benevolence made manifest issues from function held concealed; harmonious outward expression is grounded in an inward substance of sincerity.
Now the fifth yang line, with its firm yang character, occupies the center of the upper trigram and holds its correct position. Thus the august plan is truly fulfilled, and the Way gathered within oneself constitutes, in its undivided wholeness, the great Mean of all under Heaven. The August Ultimate is established, and the virtue abundantly expressed in nourishment constitutes, in its purity, the utmost correctness of all under Heaven. Hence government that proceeds from the heart naturally has no need of forced exertion; the workings of spiritual vitality and the mind…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
術之運固博施濟衆之所及也其出也寧有窮
乎有本之仁自不竭於時措至德淵微之地固
深恩厚澤之所發也其被也寧有外乎是則曰
寒泉食者王道之所以弘也曰中正者天德之
所以裕也内外合而體用一化之所以成也彼
德不茂而欲以徒法之政襲取焉者末矣雖然
聖人之仁天下非能人人而庇之也其德也亦
非爲天下而立之也厚德在我而物無不載故
仁及天下而不知其功若夫因民之饑而食之
因民之寒而衣之是霸者之智也烏能以及天
下哉無本故也故曰天地無心而運不積聖人
無情而用與京言乎其德之盛也
===
復小而辨於物恒雜而不厭
胡應潮
同考試官教諭闕　批
封意相屬而文亦對待
此篇組織嚴整而旨趣悠長觀者可以感發興
起
考試官教諭文　批
得潔淨精微之趣
punctuated:
術之運，固博施濟衆之所及也，其出也寧有窮乎？有本之仁，自不竭於時措；至德淵微之地，固深恩厚澤之所發也，其被也寧有外乎？是則曰「寒泉食」者，王道之所以弘也；曰「中正」者，天德之所以裕也。内外合而體用一，化之所以成也。彼德不茂而欲以徒法之政襲取焉者，末矣。雖然，聖人之仁天下，非能人人而庇之也；其德也，亦非爲天下而立之也。厚德在我而物無不載，故仁及天下而不知其功。若夫因民之饑而食之，因民之寒而衣之，是霸者之智也，烏能以及天下哉？無本故也。故曰：「天地無心而運不積，聖人無情而用與京。」言乎其德之盛也。

復小而辨於物，恒雜而不厭。
胡應潮。

同考試官教諭闕批：封意相屬而文亦對待。此篇組織嚴整而旨趣悠長，觀者可以感發興起。

考試官教諭文批：得潔淨精微之趣。
translation_en:
…the workings of the mind are indeed what enable the broad bestowal of benefits and relief of the multitude. Could their expression ever be exhausted? Benevolence that has a foundation does not exhaust itself in measures suited to particular times. The profound and subtle depths of consummate virtue are indeed the source of deep kindness and abundant beneficence. Could anything lie beyond their reach? Thus, the words “the cold spring is drunk” express how the Way of Kings is made extensive; the words “central and correct” express how heavenly virtue is made abundant. The inner and outer unite, and substance and function become one: this is how transforming influence is accomplished. Those whose virtue is not flourishing, yet seek to appropriate these achievements through government consisting merely of regulations, attend only to the inessential.

Nevertheless, when the sage extends benevolence throughout the world, it is not that he can shelter every person individually. Nor is his virtue established for the world's sake. Abundant virtue resides in him, and there is nothing it does not sustain. Thus his benevolence reaches all under Heaven without awareness of his achievement. As for feeding the people because they are hungry and clothing them because they are cold, this is the ingenuity of a hegemon. How could it reach all under Heaven? It lacks a foundation. Hence the saying: “Heaven and Earth have no deliberate mind, yet their movement never stagnates; the sage has no partial feelings, yet his efficacy is vast.” This speaks of the fullness of his virtue.

“Return is small, yet distinguishes among things; Constancy encounters complexity, yet does not weary.”
By Hu Yingchao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Que, Instructor: The meanings of the hexagrams [?] are linked, and the composition likewise sets them in parallel. This essay is rigorously and neatly structured, while its purport is rich and enduring. Readers may be moved and inspired by it.

Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: It captures the spirit of purity, refinement, and subtlety.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王　批　良心在我無往不復貴
察識而固守之耳子能體認親切非得之心易
不足與此
大傳陳復恒之德知幾而固守者也蓋知善之
幾而守之固學之準也復恒以之德焉有不脩
者乎大傳冊陳九卦之德以明處憂患之道若
曰理欲之幾甚微而其擇之也貴精動靜之勢
相乘而其守之也貴一要於其心焉頓之可也
吾有見於復恒二卦之德矣是故復也者良心
===
生於既失之餘者也其端方萌而其勢未盛則
惟微之幾不足以勝其惟危之漸若難乎其不
亂矣殊不知善之復也雖微而幾之動也則著
天人於是乎昭焉臧否於是乎判焉明覺內蘊
炯然有不容昧之幾滋息中涵勃然有不可遏
之勢夫豈物之所能淆耶夫其易淆也而不淆
焉復德之妙也何如恒也者久於其道而不失
者也然時有萬變而事之所遭不齊則湛一之
本不足以勝其攻取之衆若難乎其不易矣殊
punctuated:
考試官學正王批：良心在我，無往不復，貴察識而固守之耳。子能體認親切，非得之心易，不足與此。

大傳陳復恒之德，知幾而固守者也。蓋知善之幾而守之固，學之準也。復恒以之，德焉有不脩者乎？大傳冊陳九卦之德，以明處憂患之道，若曰：理欲之幾甚微，而其擇之也貴精；動靜之勢相乘，而其守之也貴一。要於其心焉，頓之可也。吾有見於復恒二卦之德矣。是故復也者，良心生於既失之餘者也。其端方萌而其勢未盛，則惟微之幾不足以勝其惟危之漸，若難乎其不亂矣。殊不知善之復也雖微，而幾之動也則著。天人於是乎昭焉，臧否於是乎判焉。明覺內蘊，炯然有不容昧之幾；滋息中涵，勃然有不可遏之勢。夫豈物之所能淆耶？夫其易淆也而不淆焉，復德之妙也何如！恒也者，久於其道而不失者也。然時有萬變，而事之所遭不齊，則湛一之本不足以勝其攻取之衆，若難乎其不易矣。殊
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: The moral heart resides within us, and wherever it may stray, it can return. What matters is discerning it and holding firmly to it. You have grasped this intimately. Without apprehending the Changes in your heart [?], you could not have attained this.

The Great Commentary sets forth the virtues of Return and Constancy: recognizing the incipient signs and holding firmly to them. Recognizing the first stirrings of goodness and holding firmly to them is the standard for learning. Practise Return and Constancy in this way, and how could virtue fail to be cultivated? The Great Commentary sets forth in sequence [?] the virtues of the nine hexagrams to illuminate the way of dealing with anxiety and adversity. It is as though it says: the incipient distinction between principle and desire is exceedingly subtle, so choosing between them requires precision; the tendencies of activity and stillness act upon one another, so maintaining one's hold requires singleness of purpose. The essential thing lies in the heart; settling it there [?] will suffice. I have gained insight into the virtues of the two hexagrams, Return and Constancy.

Return means that the moral heart comes to life after having been lost. Its first shoots have only just emerged, and its strength is not yet abundant. Thus, its subtle beginnings seem insufficient to overcome the gradually encroaching danger, as though it could scarcely avoid being thrown into disorder. Yet this overlooks the fact that, although the return of goodness is subtle, the movement of its first stirrings is manifest. The distinction between Heaven and the human becomes clear here; good and bad are distinguished here. Luminous awareness is stored within, shining with an incipient impulse that cannot be obscured; growth and increase are harbored within, surging with a force that cannot be checked. How could external things confuse it? Though easily confused, it remains unconfused: how wondrous is the virtue of Return!

Constancy means enduring in one's way without losing it. Yet circumstances undergo myriad changes, and the affairs one encounters differ. Thus, the foundation of lucid singleness seems insufficient to withstand the many forces that assail and seize it, as though it could scarcely avoid being altered. Yet …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
不知德之堅也既深而物之誘也自小天下之
至賾而不可斁也天下之至動而不可亂也凝
定之功自底乎安止之妙敦篤之至馴致乎日
新之休夫何有於厭乎夫其易厭也而不厭焉
恒德之妙也何如是則復之辨者精之所以不
雜也恒之常者一之所以不離也精以察之一
以守之則德無不脩而於處憂患乎何有雖
然二卦之德固各以類而臻二德之用亦毋相
須以有成何也復也者所以昭其端而成性之
存者由此其致恒也者所以永其終而善端之
復者由此其敦非復則恒何所始非恒則復何
所終故曰先明諸心知所往而後力行以求至
焉學之準也烏可岐而二諸
書
后克艱厥后臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏
德
===
黃觀
同考試官學正萬　批　此題詞雖交微而意亡
punctuated:
不知德之堅也既深，而物之誘也自小。天下之至賾而不可斁也，天下之至動而不可亂也。凝定之功，自底乎安止之妙；敦篤之至，馴致乎日新之休。夫何有於厭乎？夫其易厭也而不厭焉，恒德之妙也何如？是則復之辨者，精之所以不雜也；恒之常者，一之所以不離也。精以察之，一以守之，則德無不脩，而於處憂患乎何有？雖然，二卦之德固各以類而臻，二德之用亦毋相須以有成。何也？復也者，所以昭其端，而成性之存者由此其致；恒也者，所以永其終，而善端之復者由此其敦。非復，則恒何所始？非恒，則復何所終？故曰：「先明諸心，知所往，而後力行以求至焉，學之準也。」烏可岐而二諸？

書
后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。

黃觀

同考試官學正萬批：此題詞雖交微，而意亡
translation_en:
… They fail to understand that, once virtue is deeply established and firm, the enticements of external things naturally diminish. Even amid the utmost complexity under Heaven, it cannot be wearied; even amid the utmost movement under Heaven, it cannot be thrown into disorder. The work of concentration and steadiness naturally reaches the subtle achievement of resting securely in the proper place; the fullest sincerity and earnestness gradually bring the blessing of daily renewal. What occasion could there be for weariness? Where weariness would readily arise, yet does not, how marvelous is the virtue of Constancy! Thus the discernment of Return is what keeps refinement free from admixture; the constancy of Constancy is what keeps singleness from being lost. Examine with refinement and preserve with singleness: then no aspect of virtue will remain uncultivated. What difficulty could there be in facing anxiety and adversity?

Nevertheless, although the virtues of these two hexagrams each reach fulfillment according to their kind, the operation of the two virtues does not depend on their mutual assistance for its accomplishment [?]. Why? Return illuminates the beginning, and through it the preservation of one's fully developed moral nature is achieved. Constancy perpetuates the completion, and through it the returning beginnings of goodness are strengthened. Without Return, where would Constancy begin? Without Constancy, where would Return find its completion? Hence the saying: “First make things clear in the mind and know where to proceed; then strive to act so as to arrive there. This is the standard of learning.” How could one divide them into two separate paths?

Book of Documents
“When the ruler can appreciate the difficulty of being a ruler, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of being a minister, government will be well ordered, and the common people will strive earnestly toward virtue.”

Huang Guan

Comment by Associate Examiner Wan, School Instructor: “Although the wording of this topic is subtly interwoven [?], its meaning is lacking [?] …”

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
責難場中作者兩平則失經旨偏重則背題意
庶乎祇承之心遠矣此篇醇雅平正尺幹轉數
語而大禹言外之意褎然自見非超邁之才無
此步驟得士若此庶幾可貢矣
考試官教諭文　批　忠誠溢于言表
考試官學正王　批　敷演大禹陳謨之意不
費詞而燁然自足佳士佳士
===
聖臣欲上下交修以成治其責難之意至矣蓋
君臣者化之原其道固不易也交修無斁而天
下其有不治者乎此大禹所以祇承於帝也若
曰人情常修於儆戒而治道每病於怠荒帝其
知危矣乎蓋君也者代天而理天下者也以一
人而莘民物之責斯亦艱矣誠能知天命之難
諶民嵒之可畏也而夙夜祇懼務盡其所當
為固難於易爲大於細焉蓋誠以憂勞倡之
矣豈惟君哉臣也者承君之令而致之民者也
以一身而膺臣鄰之任亦云重矣其必思君否
之不易明也袞職之不易補也而朝夕寅恭不
punctuated:
責難。場中作者，兩平則失經旨，偏重則背題意，庶乎祇承之心遠矣。此篇醇雅平正，尺幹轉數語，而大禹言外之意褎然自見。非超邁之才，無此步驟。得士若此，庶幾可貢矣。
考試官教諭文批：忠誠溢于言表。
考試官學正王批：敷演大禹陳謨之意，不費詞而燁然自足。佳士！佳士！
聖臣欲上下交修以成治，其責難之意至矣。蓋君臣者，化之原，其道固不易也。交修無斁，而天下其有不治者乎？此大禹所以祇承於帝也。若曰：人情常修於儆戒，而治道每病於怠荒，帝其知危矣乎？蓋君也者，代天而理天下者也。以一人而莘民物之責，斯亦艱矣。誠能知天命之難諶、民嵒之可畏也，而夙夜祇懼，務盡其所當為，固難於易，爲大於細焉，蓋誠以憂勞倡之矣。豈惟君哉？臣也者，承君之令而致之民者也。以一身而膺臣鄰之任，亦云重矣。其必思君否之不易明也，袞職之不易補也，而朝夕寅恭，不
translation_en:
…requiring the difficult of the ruler. Among those composing answers in the examination hall, treating the two sides equally loses the purport of the Classic, while emphasizing one side contravenes the meaning of the topic; either approach falls far short of the spirit of reverent service. This essay is pure and elegant, balanced and correct. With a few turns of phrase [?], the meaning beyond Great Yu’s words emerges distinctly of itself. Without exceptional talent, one could not attain such mastery. A candidate of this quality may well be recommended to the court.
Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: Loyalty and sincerity overflow beyond the words.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: He elaborates the meaning of Great Yu’s presentation of his counsels, achieving brilliance and completeness without wasting words. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!
The sage minister wished those above and below to cultivate themselves together and thereby bring about good government. His intention in requiring the difficult of the ruler was most profound. Ruler and ministers are the source of moral transformation, and their way is assuredly no easy matter. If they cultivate themselves together without weariness, how could the realm fail to be well governed? This is why Great Yu offered reverent service to the emperor. It was as though he said: Human dispositions are commonly improved through admonition and vigilance, while the way of government is often impaired by negligence and indolence. Does Your Majesty recognize the danger? The ruler governs all under Heaven on Heaven’s behalf. For one man to bear responsibility for the people and all things [?] is indeed difficult. If he truly understands that Heaven’s mandate cannot readily be relied upon and that the people’s precarious condition is to be feared, he will remain reverently apprehensive day and night, striving to fulfill all that he ought to do. He will address difficulties while they are easy [?] and accomplish great things while they are small. Thus he will truly take the lead through anxious toil.
But how could this apply only to the ruler? A minister receives the ruler’s commands and conveys them to the people. For one person to shoulder the charge of serving as the ruler’s close minister is also a weighty responsibility. He must reflect on how difficult it is to bring the ruler’s faults to light [?], and how difficult it is to remedy shortcomings in the imperial office. Then, respectful and reverent morning and evening, he will not…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
忘其所有事爲上爲德焉爲下爲民焉寔能以
艱難承之矣夫然後交修之功已至而出治之
本以端將見政不易乂也而厲精之心自有以
底咸熈之績有典有則也之綱之紀也自朝廷
以達之邦國秩然小大之時叙夫孰有不乂者
乎其或未乂則以克艱之未至耳民不易化也
而精純之德自足以成風動之休遵道遵路也
會極歸極也由京邑以冐於海隅翕然遠邇之
同心又焉有不德者乎如其未化將無交修之
===
尚闕耶夫君臣之爲責如此我之爲臣也固不
敢以自委而作則以先之者實惟君焉帝其可
不念哉抑舜大聖也敷化立極固優爲之矣而
大禹矢謨乃首以克艱爲言何哉蓋於穆不已
天之道也純亦不已聖人之德也使微戒之心
一或有息則與天不相似而驕佚之患作矣此
敬怠之辨治忽之幾也而可不慎與故明良喜
起之歌憲天聰明之訓皆臣子之所不得已者
也此固責難之恭也
punctuated: 忘其所有事，爲上爲德焉，爲下爲民焉，寔能以艱難承之矣。夫然後交修之功已至，而出治之本以端。將見政不易乂也，而厲精之心自有以底咸熈之績；有典有則也，之綱之紀也，自朝廷以達之邦國，秩然小大之時叙，夫孰有不乂者乎？其或未乂，則以克艱之未至耳。民不易化也，而精純之德自足以成風動之休；遵道遵路也，會極歸極也，由京邑以冐於海隅，翕然遠邇之同心，又焉有不德者乎？如其未化，將無交修之尚闕耶？夫君臣之爲責如此，我之爲臣也，固不敢以自委，而作則以先之者，實惟君焉。帝其可不念哉？抑舜大聖也，敷化立極，固優爲之矣，而大禹矢謨，乃首以克艱爲言，何哉？蓋於穆不已，天之道也；純亦不已，聖人之德也。使微戒之心一或有息，則與天不相似，而驕佚之患作矣。此敬怠之辨、治忽之幾也，而可不慎與？故明良喜起之歌、憲天聰明之訓，皆臣子之所不得已者也。此固責難之恭也。
translation_en:
…forget the duties entrusted to them, working for their ruler’s virtue above and for the people below: then they will truly discharge their responsibilities with a sense of their difficulty. Only then will ruler and ministers fully accomplish their mutual cultivation, and the foundation from which good government proceeds be set right. We shall then see that, although governmental affairs are not easily brought into order, a resolve to exert oneself will itself bring about universal prosperity. There will be statutes and standards, guiding principles and regulations; from the court to the states, great and small will take their proper places in orderly succession. What, then, could remain ungoverned? If anything remains so, it is only because they have not yet fully succeeded in treating their task as difficult. Although the people are not easily transformed, refined and pure virtue will itself suffice to produce the beautiful effect of influence spreading like the wind. They will follow the Way and its paths, converge upon and return to the supreme standard. From the capital to the remotest shores, those far and near will unite with one heart. Who, then, could fail to become virtuous? If the people remain untransformed, might mutual cultivation still be deficient?

Such are the responsibilities of ruler and ministers. As a minister, I certainly dare not shirk my part; yet it is indeed the ruler who must establish the example and take the lead. Can the emperor fail to bear this in mind? Now Shun was a great sage: spreading moral transformation and establishing the supreme standard were assuredly well within his powers. Yet when Yu the Great set forth his counsel, why did he begin by speaking of treating rulership as difficult? Because profound and unceasing activity is the Way of Heaven, and purity that likewise never ceases is the virtue of the sage. If the watchful, admonitory disposition [?] should lapse even once, one would cease to resemble Heaven, and the dangers of arrogance and indulgence would arise. Here lies the distinction between reverence and negligence, the critical point upon which order or disorder turns. Can one fail to exercise care?

Thus the song in which the enlightened ruler and worthy ministers rejoice and rise to action, and the admonition to model one’s hearing and sight upon Heaven, are things that ministers cannot refrain from offering. This is precisely the reverence shown by demanding difficult things of one’s ruler.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
君子所其無逸先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則
知小人之依
張大中
同考試官學正萬　批　〔稼穡艱難乃周室傳授心法此周公所以丁寧于成王也子能言之親〕
〔切而意味充暢無乃漸被〕
紀上無逸之化而興起者歟
考試官教諭文　批　〔沖澹典雅而蔚然有光其發出先知二字又非尋常識見可到冠場之〕
===
作也
考試官學正王　批　〔得周公告君之意〕
大臣言君子有居勤之功而必本其所以居之
也蓋保國之道莫先於無逸也使非體民之勞
勤焉亦何以克是哉此周公訓成王於親政之
日也謂夫有國家者非不能承命之患而以不
知憂勤之患王其念之哉何則人情莫不欲逸
也而詎知宴安之毒有不可懷者乎君子是以
防之必豫而不使怠荒之或滋持之有常而罔
punctuated:
「君子所其無逸。先知稼穡之艱難，乃逸，則知小人之依。」
張大中
同考試官學正萬　批：〔稼穡艱難，乃周室傳授心法，此周公所以丁寧于成王也。子能言之親〕〔切而意味充暢，無乃漸被〕紀上無逸之化而興起者歟？
考試官教諭文　批：〔沖澹典雅而蔚然有光，其發出先知二字，又非尋常識見可到，冠場之〕作也。
考試官學正王　批：〔得周公告君之意。〕
大臣言君子有居勤之功，而必本其所以居之也。蓋保國之道，莫先於無逸也。使非體民之勞勤焉，亦何以克是哉？此周公訓成王於親政之日也。謂夫有國家者，非不能承命之患，而以不知憂勤之患。王其念之哉！何則？人情莫不欲逸也，而詎知宴安之毒有不可懷者乎？君子是以防之必豫，而不使怠荒之或滋；持之有常，而罔
translation_en:
“The gentleman takes freedom from ease as his abiding principle. First understanding the hardships of sowing and reaping, and only then enjoying ease, he understands what the common people depend upon.”
Zhang Dazhong
Associate Examiner Wan, School Instructor, comments: “The hardships of sowing and reaping constitute the essential teaching transmitted within the house of Zhou. This is why the Duke of Zhou so earnestly admonished King Cheng. You express this intimately and pertinently, with ample and fully developed meaning. Might you be someone stirred to action through gradually receiving the sovereign’s [?] transforming influence of freedom from ease?”
Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “Serene and restrained, polished and elegant, yet radiant with brilliance. Its elucidation of the two words ‘first understanding’ is beyond the reach of ordinary discernment. This is the finest composition of the examination.”
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “It captures the intention with which the Duke of Zhou admonished his ruler.”
The great minister says that the gentleman achieves the practice of abiding in diligence, but must establish the foundation upon which that practice rests. For among the ways of preserving a state, none takes precedence over freedom from ease. Without appreciating the toil and exertion of the people, how could one accomplish this? These were the Duke of Zhou’s instructions to King Cheng when he assumed personal rule. His meaning was that one who possesses a state should worry less about being unable to receive Heaven’s mandate than about failing to understand anxious concern and diligence. Let the king bear this in mind! Why so? Human feelings incline everyone toward ease; yet do people recognize that the poison of comfortable repose must not be cherished? The gentleman therefore takes precautions beforehand, allowing no negligence or indolence to grow; he maintains his resolve consistently, and never …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
穡勤儩之或息敬以作所而矻矻以勞天下者
動息由是諴誠有藉以為安者矣恒以一德而
孜孜以永天命者出入不違諴其有以之為宅
者矣夫君是者而豈徒為之哉諴民之有稼穡
也播吹播穫勞亦甚矣君子不必身親為之也
而民隱之求願悉其勤勞之狀由是而燕樂之
居也昔以易心乘之哉不必幼嘗習之也而世
故之歷其知其胼胝之艱以之而逸豫是處也
敬以驕心臨之哉諴惟知夫民命之所寄也一
===
或不遂流離將徙而所以厚下安宅者不容緩
矣是尚可以自逸乎有見於民生之所恃也一
有不恤顛仆將至而所以勞民勸相者不但已
也雖欲無勤得乎此君子之所以克自抑畏而
祈天永命不外是矣周公以是訓王其忠愛之
至已乎抑周家以勤勞立國自后稷公劉以至
大王王季文王罔非稼穡之重則無逸之訓其
源流遠矣而周公於成王乃為是諄諄者何耶
蓋儆戒之志難持而宴安之情易溺閭閻之艱
punctuated:
穡勤儩之或息，敬以作所，而矻矻以勞天下者，動息由是諴誠，有藉以為安者矣；恒以一德，而孜孜以永天命者，出入不違，諴其有以之為宅者矣。夫君是者，而豈徒為之哉？諴民之有稼穡也，播吹播穫，勞亦甚矣。君子不必身親為之也，而民隱之求，願悉其勤勞之狀，由是而燕樂之居也，昔以易心乘之哉？不必幼嘗習之也，而世故之歷，其知其胼胝之艱，以之而逸豫是處也，敬以驕心臨之哉？諴惟知夫民命之所寄也，一或不遂，流離將徙，而所以厚下安宅者不容緩矣，是尚可以自逸乎？有見於民生之所恃也，一有不恤，顛仆將至，而所以勞民勸相者不但已也，雖欲無勤得乎？此君子之所以克自抑畏，而祈天永命不外是矣。

周公以是訓王，其忠愛之至已乎！抑周家以勤勞立國，自后稷、公劉以至大王、王季、文王，罔非稼穡之重，則無逸之訓，其源流遠矣。而周公於成王乃為是諄諄者，何耶？蓋儆戒之志難持，而宴安之情易溺，閭閻之艱
translation_en:
…allowing agricultural toil [?] to cease. Through reverence he establishes his place [?], laboring tirelessly for all under Heaven; in movement and rest he thus maintains sincerity [?], having something upon which to ground his security. Constant in his single virtue, he strives unremittingly to perpetuate Heaven’s Mandate; in going out and coming in he does not depart from it, truly having therein a dwelling place [?]. Would a ruler who acts thus do so without purpose? Consider the people’s agricultural work: sowing and harvesting [?] entail very great toil. The gentleman need not personally perform it, but, seeking out the people’s hidden hardships, he wishes to understand fully the circumstances of their labor. When he consequently dwells in ease and pleasure, could he approach this with a heedless heart [?]? He need not have practiced such work in childhood, but through experience of worldly affairs he comes to understand the hardship that produces calloused hands and feet. When he thus occupies a position of comfort and leisure, could he preside over it with an arrogant heart [?]? Truly [?], he understands upon what the people’s lives depend: should their endeavors fail even once, they will become displaced and wander away. Thus, measures to enrich those below and secure their dwelling places cannot be delayed. Could he still indulge himself in ease? He perceives what sustains the people’s livelihood: if their needs go unattended even once, ruin will follow. Thus, efforts to comfort the people and encourage and assist them must not cease [?]. Even if he wished to dispense with diligence, could he do so? This is how the gentleman succeeds in restraining himself and maintaining apprehensive reverence; his prayer to Heaven for an enduring Mandate rests on nothing beyond this.
