title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
壁弘新式重作人之地蓋首善莫先乎太
學而敦興有望於英君師貴道尊庠均義
重故漢帝屈臨雍之拜肆唐宗篤齒胄之
風遐稽致治之隆寔本右儒之化道因言
闡論思允賴於名賢才以養成陶沃必資
乎碩德事誠有待教不虛行若賜侈桓榮
曷任式和之體必望隆韓愈庶幾先覺之
貞貴任匪輕簡掄宜慎如臣庸鄙特荷甄
旌雖
===
璧祼不棄于采葑而微德有懷于負乘恭惟
神凝聖域
識際道真
懋湯德之日新誕開章閣
邁高宗之時敏夙御經筵
玉質金相綱紀協文章之用鳶飛魚躍作興
妙鼓舞之機謂振育英才敦化允基乎三
舍而主盟庠序立賢當廣於無方詎知樗
punctuated: 壁弘新，式重作人之地。蓋首善莫先乎太學，而敦興有望於英君。師貴道尊，庠均義重，故漢帝屈臨雍之拜，肆唐宗篤齒胄之風。遐稽致治之隆，寔本右儒之化。道因言闡，論思允賴於名賢；才以養成，陶沃必資乎碩德。事誠有待，教不虛行。若賜侈桓榮，曷任式和之體；必望隆韓愈，庶幾先覺之貞。貴任匪輕，簡掄宜慎。如臣庸鄙，特荷甄旌。雖璧祼不棄于采葑，而微德有懷于負乘。恭惟神凝聖域，識際道真，懋湯德之日新，誕開章閣；邁高宗之時敏，夙御經筵。玉質金相，綱紀協文章之用；鳶飛魚躍，作興妙鼓舞之機。謂振育英才，敦化允基乎三舍；而主盟庠序，立賢當廣於無方。詎知樗
translation_en:
…the precincts were magnificently renewed [?], giving renewed importance to the place where men of talent are nurtured. For establishing exemplary goodness, nothing takes precedence over the Imperial University; for its vigorous promotion, hopes rest upon an enlightened ruler. Teachers are esteemed and the Way revered: weighty indeed is the significance of the schools. Thus a Han emperor humbled himself to bow when visiting the imperial school, and a Tang sovereign earnestly upheld the custom whereby princes took their places according to age. Looking far back at the heights of good government, we find that they truly rested upon the transforming influence of honoring Confucian learning. The Way is elucidated through words, and deliberation and reflection depend upon eminent worthies; talent develops through nurture, and its cultivation requires men of great virtue. These undertakings truly await suitable men; teaching cannot proceed without substance. If lavish gifts such as those bestowed upon Huan Rong alone were given, how could one fulfill the requirements of harmonious instruction [?]? Only with standing as lofty as Han Yu’s might one approach the steadfastness of those first to attain understanding. This honored responsibility is no light matter; selection should be cautious. Commonplace and uncultivated as your servant is, I have nevertheless received special recognition and distinction. Though the precious ritual favor does not reject even one who gathers turnips [?], my scant virtue makes me apprehensive, like a man carrying a burden while riding in a carriage—a man occupying a station beyond his deserts.

I respectfully reflect that Your Majesty’s spirit is concentrated in the realm of sagehood, and your understanding reaches the truth of the Way. Emulating Tang’s daily renewal of virtue, you have magnificently opened the literary pavilion; surpassing Gaozong’s diligence in timely study, you have early attended the Classics Colloquium. With the substance of jade and the form of gold, you harmonize governing principles with the uses of literary refinement. As kites fly and fish leap, your promotion of learning wonderfully sets encouragement and inspiration in motion. You hold that fostering outstanding talent and deepening moral transformation must indeed rest upon the Three Hall system, and that, in choosing leaders for the schools, the appointment of worthy men should extend broadly, without restriction. Who could have imagined that a useless ailanthus…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
樸之散材謬典菁莪之重寄官崇道講位
列賢宗秩望接于成均衣冠率乎胄子登
堂釆藻斯文昭化日之光鼓篋升階多士
藹如雲之集此
王道丕亨之會而儒者至足之榮也切念臣海
陵遐賤草野至庸岱麓窮居志徒勤於仰
止蘇湖分迪功莫答於涓埃橫碧帳以明
經自分倉貢海嶠對青衿而敬業何期貴
釆雲宮慚非頴達之倫謏辱仲淹之薦興
===
曰蘭芷譸移入室之情不自淵源曷足欽
河之願智易窮於小知仁何異以出成激
切由衷勉圖知分臣敢不益敦舊學用答
新恩勤勞來匡直之功備春夏秋冬之教攄
平生望道之志上不負於
所知振先哲成物之方下不孤於所學門墻
桃李仰歸
雨露之仁泮水魚龍共沐江河之潤伏望
數嘗弟以作人
punctuated:
樸之散材，謬典菁莪之重寄。官崇道講，位列賢宗，秩望接于成均，衣冠率乎胄子。登堂釆藻，斯文昭化日之光；鼓篋升階，多士藹如雲之集。此王道丕亨之會，而儒者至足之榮也。
切念臣海陵遐賤，草野至庸。岱麓窮居，志徒勤於仰止；蘇湖分迪，功莫答於涓埃。橫碧帳以明經，自分倉貢海嶠；對青衿而敬業，何期貴釆雲宮。慚非頴達之倫，謏辱仲淹之薦。興曰蘭芷，譸移入室之情；不自淵源，曷足欽河之願？智易窮於小知，仁何異以出成？激切由衷，勉圖知分。
臣敢不益敦舊學，用答新恩，勤勞來匡直之功，備春夏秋冬之教？攄平生望道之志，上不負於所知；振先哲成物之方，下不孤於所學。門墻桃李，仰歸雨露之仁；泮水魚龍，共沐江河之潤。伏望數嘗弟以作人。
translation_en:
…an unserviceable piece of timber, I have undeservedly been entrusted with the weighty charge of nurturing scholars. My office is exalted through the exposition of the Way, and my position ranks among the leaders of the worthy. In rank and prestige it approaches the Imperial University; in ceremonial dress I lead the sons of the elite. Ascending the hall to gather literary adornments, our cultural tradition displays the radiance of Your Majesty’s transforming influence; opening their book chests and mounting the steps, the many scholars gather thick as clouds. This is an occasion when the kingly Way flourishes greatly, and an honor that fully satisfies a scholar.
I reflect that I, Your servant, am a lowly man from distant Hailing, utterly ordinary and of rustic origins. Living in poverty at the foot of Mount Tai, I merely strove in my aspirations to look up to the heights. Sharing in the instruction of students in Suzhou and Huzhou, my achievements could not repay even the smallest fraction of the favor received. Setting up a blue teaching curtain to elucidate the Classics, I expected only to offer tribute from a remote coastal region [?]; facing the blue-collared students and attending reverently to my vocation, how could I have anticipated being honored with selection by the lofty palace? Ashamed that I am not of Yingda’s stature, I, with my meager learning, have undeservedly received Zhongyan’s recommendation. The text invokes fragrant orchids and angelica, then speaks obscurely of the feelings of one entering the chamber [?]. Without proceeding from the source, how could I fulfill my wish to revere the river [?]? Wisdom is easily exhausted by petty knowledge; as for benevolence, how does it differ in bringing things to completion [?]? Deeply stirred from the heart, I strive to understand my allotted duty.
How could Your servant dare not further cultivate his former learning to repay this new favor, diligently exert himself in encouraging, attracting, correcting, and rectifying students, and provide instruction throughout spring, summer, autumn, and winter? I shall give expression to my lifelong aspiration toward the Way, so that above I do not disappoint the one who recognizes me; I shall revive the former sages’ methods of bringing others to fulfillment, so that below I do not betray what I have learned. May the peach and plum trees within the school’s walls—the students—look upward in gratitude for Your Majesty’s benevolence, like rain and dew; may the fish and dragons in the school’s waters together bathe in bounty as abundant as rivers. I humbly hope that You will [unclear wording: 數嘗弟] foster men of talent …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
本經術而致治
皇極著表儀之式
冄袁切敬教之思有翼有馮濟濟詠周楨于
王國乃文乃武
明明協唐運於中天臣瑗無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
===
第叁場
策
第一問
李攀龍
同考試官教諭袁　批　此策敘述我
聖祖開闢之功精一之學
成祖再造
皇上中興
punctuated:
本經術而致治，皇極著表儀之式，冄袁切敬教之思。有翼有馮，濟濟詠周楨于王國；乃文乃武，明明協唐運於中天。臣瑗無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
李攀龍
同考試官教諭袁批：此策敘述我聖祖開闢之功、精一之學，成祖再造，皇上中興
translation_en:
…to bring about good government through mastery of the Classics. The Imperial Ultimate establishes the pattern of exemplary conduct; [冄袁, unclear] expresses an earnest concern for reverently attending to instruction. With helpers and supporters, the many worthy men are celebrated as pillars of Zhou in the royal realm; accomplished in civil and military affairs, they brilliantly accord with the fortunes of Tang at its zenith. Your servant Yuan is overcome with fervent emotion and trembling reverence as he gazes toward Heaven and looks up to Your Sagely Majesty. I respectfully submit this memorial to convey my thanks to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Li Panlong
Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: This policy essay recounts the achievement of our sagely founder in establishing the dynasty and his learning of refinement and single-mindedness, Chengzu’s refounding of the dynasty, and the reigning emperor’s restoration of its prosperity…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖聖相承心法之妙皆能舉其要而合其同庶不負
聖朝作養之恩矣宜取之以貢
同考試官教諭王　批
皇上睿資天錫
聖學性成近法
祖宗遠追堯舜誠不世出之
聖主也此篇能莊頌而揚厲之必嘗服習
聖化而有得焉者况才思深長文理精到而忠愛之意溢于上
君子不爲盛世慶乎
===
同考試官教諭陳　批　此策重
皇上聖學不獨見于
製作十九年間隱顯一誠久暫無二真允蹈之矣恪究玄微之妙仰述
功業之隆僅見此作謹當録之以爲
當宁獻
考試官教諭文　批　有忠敬之心有臣鄰之
願用世之才也可取可取
考試官學正王　批　善言
皇上爲學之要而遡流窮源得我
punctuated:
聖聖相承，心法之妙，皆能舉其要而合其同，庶不負聖朝作養之恩矣。宜取之以貢。

同考試官教諭王批：皇上睿資天錫，聖學性成，近法祖宗，遠追堯舜，誠不世出之聖主也。此篇能莊頌而揚厲之，必嘗服習聖化而有得焉者。况才思深長，文理精到，而忠愛之意溢于上，君子不爲盛世慶乎？

同考試官教諭陳批：此策重皇上聖學，不獨見于製作。十九年間，隱顯一誠，久暫無二，真允蹈之矣。恪究玄微之妙，仰述功業之隆，僅見此作。謹當録之，以爲當宁獻。

考試官教諭文批：有忠敬之心，有臣鄰之願，用世之才也。可取，可取。

考試官學正王批：善言皇上爲學之要，而遡流窮源，得我
translation_en:
…the wondrous essentials of the teaching of the mind transmitted from sage sovereign to sage sovereign: he can bring out their crucial points and show what they share. Thus he may prove worthy of the sagely dynasty’s gracious nurture. He should be selected for presentation to the court.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: His Majesty’s discerning gifts are Heaven-bestowed, and his sagely learning is innate. He models himself on his nearer forebears and reaches back to Yao and Shun: truly, he is a sage ruler such as does not appear in every age. This essay solemnly praises and extols him; its author must have practiced what he learned under the imperial civilizing influence and gained something from it. Moreover, his inventive thought is profound and far-reaching, his composition precise and accomplished, and his feelings of loyalty and affection overflow above [?]. Should gentlemen not rejoice for this flourishing age?

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: This policy essay emphasizes His Majesty’s sagely learning, which is manifested not only in his institutional creations. Throughout nineteen years, in private and in public, his sincerity has been one; over long periods and short, it has never varied. He has truly put it into practice. Only in this composition have I seen such a scrupulous investigation of its profound subtleties and such a reverent account of the greatness of his achievements. I respectfully deem it worthy of recording for presentation to the reigning sovereign.

Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: He has a loyal and reverent heart and the aspirations of a minister close to his sovereign. His is a talent fit for public service. Worth selecting, worth selecting.

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: He ably explains the essentials of His Majesty’s pursuit of learning and, tracing the current back to its ultimate source, grasps our…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
祖宗
列聖統緒之傳必參倸之士也可敬可敬
帝王之學非徒博聞廣志而已也將以昭
德塞違而布之政也達天命之原通古今
之變察民物之紀廣聰明之實非學何繇
矣古之聖哲豈不能師心以爲治而必爲
是孜孜者誠以理欲之賓難明而心志之
蠱易入乾行當法而鏡戒不可不昭其所
以亹亹孜孜而不隆譽者以其戀天立極存
===
此道也雜之者霸忽焉則幾乎殆矣在昔
成湯之誥曰惟皇上帝降衷于下民若有
恒性克綏厥猷惟后泰誓曰天佑下民作
之君作之師惟其克相上帝此言天之所
期於人君至篤厚也羲黄氏之有天下尚
矣唐虞以下不能無憂焉故堯之命舜曰
天之曆數在爾躬允執其中舜亦命禹曰
人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中
此言君所以承天之道也由今觀之親九
punctuated:
祖宗列聖統緒之傳，必參倸之士也，可敬，可敬。

帝王之學，非徒博聞廣志而已也，將以昭德塞違而布之政也。達天命之原，通古今之變，察民物之紀，廣聰明之實，非學何繇矣？古之聖哲，豈不能師心以爲治，而必爲是孜孜者？誠以理欲之賓難明，而心志之蠱易入，乾行當法，而鏡戒不可不昭。其所以亹亹孜孜而不隆譽者，以其戀天立極，存此道也。雜之者霸，忽焉則幾乎殆矣。在昔成湯之誥曰：「惟皇上帝，降衷于下民，若有恒性，克綏厥猷惟后。」《泰誓》曰：「天佑下民，作之君，作之師，惟其克相上帝。」此言天之所期於人君至篤厚也。羲黄氏之有天下尚矣，唐虞以下，不能無憂焉。故堯之命舜曰：「天之曆數在爾躬，允執其中。」舜亦命禹曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」此言君所以承天之道也。由今觀之，親九
translation_en:
…the transmission of the dynastic succession through our founding ancestors and successive sage sovereigns. He must be a scholar of wide learning [?]. Worthy of respect, worthy of respect!

The learning of emperors and kings is not merely a matter of extensive knowledge and broad understanding. Its purpose is to illuminate virtue, restrain wrongdoing, and put these principles into practice in government. To reach the source of Heaven’s mandate, comprehend the changes of past and present, discern the ordering of people and things, and enlarge the substance of one’s perceptiveness—how could these be achieved without learning? Could the sages and wise men of antiquity not have governed by taking their own minds as teachers? Why, then, did they insist on such unremitting diligence? It was indeed because the distinction [?] between moral principle and desire is difficult to discern, while corruption readily enters the heart and will. The ceaseless activity of Heaven must be emulated, and cautionary examples must be clearly understood. The reason they labored so diligently and tirelessly without exalting their reputation [?] was that they revered Heaven [?], established the supreme standard, and preserved this Way. Those who adulterate it become hegemons; those who neglect it approach peril.

In antiquity, the proclamation of Cheng Tang said: “August Shangdi bestowed an inner moral norm upon the people below. In accordance with their constant nature, it is the sovereign alone who can bring stability to their course.” The Great Declaration says: “Heaven aids the people below, providing them with rulers and teachers, so that these may assist Shangdi.” These words show how profoundly earnest are Heaven’s expectations of the ruler. The possession of All under Heaven by Fuxi and Huangdi lies far back in antiquity. From Tang Yao and Yu Shun onward, rulers could not be without concern. Thus Yao, in charging Shun, said: “Heaven’s appointed succession rests upon your person. Sincerely hold fast to the mean.” Shun likewise charged Yu: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded; sincerely hold fast to the mean.” These words describe the Way by which a ruler responds to Heaven. Viewed from the present, bringing affection to the nine…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
族和萬邦被四表格上下堯之德其至矣
從五典敘百揆和神人以和百獸率舞舜之
德其至矣此猶天地之高厚日月之著明
後有作者二帝爲不可及已自時厥後祗
台德先禹之所以繼舜也聖敬日躋湯之
所以繼禹也緝熙敬止受戒丹書文武之
所以繼湯也明辟之道克享天心以隆大
命其見於治也夏之道尚忠商變之而尚
質周變之而尚文蓋與時推移雖聖人無
===
如之何今其風動之休允殖之治永清之
功與世而比隆非一德誰能致之故孔子
曰大道之行也與三代之英丘未之逮也
而有志焉蓋宗之也自周而下則有可議
者矣過魯祠聖似矣而不事詩書銳情經
術似矣而內多慚德闢門諭心似矣而得
國非正帝王之學槩未有得以先天下然
跡其所爲易秦項之暴也除隋室之亂也
洗五代之陋也其功在生民天亦不得而
punctuated:
族，和萬邦，被四表，格上下，堯之德其至矣！從五典，敘百揆，和神人，以和百獸率舞，舜之德其至矣！此猶天地之高厚，日月之著明，後有作者，二帝爲不可及已。自時厥後，祗台德先，禹之所以繼舜也；聖敬日躋，湯之所以繼禹也；緝熙敬止，受戒丹書，文武之所以繼湯也。明辟之道，克享天心，以隆大命。其見於治也，夏之道尚忠，商變之而尚質，周變之而尚文，蓋與時推移，雖聖人無如之何。今其風動之休，允殖之治，永清之功，與世而比隆，非一德誰能致之？故孔子曰：「大道之行也，與三代之英，丘未之逮也，而有志焉。」蓋宗之也。
自周而下，則有可議者矣。過魯祠聖似矣，而不事詩書；銳情經術似矣，而內多慚德；闢門諭心似矣，而得國非正。帝王之學，槩未有得以先天下。然跡其所爲，易秦項之暴也，除隋室之亂也，洗五代之陋也，其功在生民，天亦不得而
translation_en:
…clans, bringing harmony to the myriad states, extending his influence to the four outer quarters, and reaching Heaven above and Earth below: Yao’s virtue had indeed attained perfection! Following the five teachings [?], setting the hundred offices in order, harmonizing spirits and human beings, and bringing such harmony that all the beasts danced together: Shun’s virtue had indeed attained perfection! This was like the height and breadth of Heaven and Earth, or the radiance of the sun and moon. Among those who arose afterward, none could equal these two emperors. From that time onward, “Reverently give precedence to my virtue” was how Yu succeeded Shun; “His sagely reverence rose daily higher” was how Tang succeeded Yu; and maintaining luminous virtue and abiding in reverence, and receiving the admonitions of the Cinnabar Writing, were how Wen and Wu succeeded Tang. The way of enlightened rulers could win Heaven’s favor and thereby magnify its great mandate. As manifested in government, the way of Xia esteemed loyalty; Shang changed this to esteem simplicity; Zhou changed this to esteem refinement. These shifted with the times, and even sages could not do otherwise. Now, the blessings of their transforming influence, their governance that truly fostered prosperity, and their achievements in securing enduring peace each attained greatness in their own age. Without undivided virtue, who could have brought this about? Thus Confucius said: “The practice of the Great Way and the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties—I, Qiu, did not live to see them, yet there are records of them.” He took them as his models.
After Zhou, however, there were matters open to criticism. Passing through Lu and offering sacrifice to the Sage seemed fitting, yet there was no devotion to the Odes and Documents. Eager dedication to classical learning seemed fitting, yet inwardly there was much conduct to be ashamed of. Opening the gates and declaring one’s heart seemed fitting, yet the realm had been acquired illegitimately. In the learning proper to emperors and kings, virtually none had attained what was needed to lead all under Heaven. Yet, tracing what they accomplished, they replaced the brutality of Qin and Xiang, ended the disorder of the Sui ruling house, and swept away the debasement of the Five Dynasties. Their achievements benefited the people, and even Heaven could not…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
棄之是以漢祚四百唐祚三百宋實次之
方之他姓爲烈然而異於三代遠矣論者
曰漢治雜霸唐治雜夷宋治優柔不振蓋
少之也天之眷明德久矣鑒觀四方求民
之莫未始一日而替也而聖王不作大道
不彰天之心不能若是恝矣
高皇帝以神武之資膺曆數之歸明命有赫實
祗承之投戈講道典學不怠故論智詹以
欲求堯舜之心喻宋濂以當謹操存之戒
===
與陶安論學術而深明邪說之害因宋善
讀心箴而極言人心道心倚伏之幾斯心
也其即堯舜之心乎故釋洪範而天人徵
應之理昭矣書大學衍義而古今治亂之
原彰矣他如存心省躬之錄表其誠也通
訓集禮之編陳其度也
聖謨洋洋不有可徵者乎
文皇帝親得
聖哲之儀刑善繼善述以光
punctuated:
棄之。是以漢祚四百，唐祚三百，宋實次之，方之他姓爲烈。然而異於三代遠矣。論者曰：「漢治雜霸，唐治雜夷，宋治優柔不振。」蓋少之也。天之眷明德久矣，鑒觀四方，求民之莫，未始一日而替也。而聖王不作，大道不彰，天之心不能若是恝矣。
高皇帝以神武之資，膺曆數之歸，明命有赫，實祗承之。投戈講道，典學不怠。故論智詹以欲求堯舜之心，喻宋濂以當謹操存之戒，與陶安論學術而深明邪說之害，因宋善讀心箴而極言人心道心倚伏之幾。斯心也，其即堯舜之心乎？故釋《洪範》而天人徵應之理昭矣，書《大學衍義》而古今治亂之原彰矣。他如存心省躬之錄，表其誠也；通訓集禮之編，陳其度也。聖謨洋洋，不有可徵者乎？
文皇帝親得聖哲之儀刑，善繼善述，以光
translation_en:
…cast them aside. Thus the Han dynasty endured for four hundred years, the Tang for three hundred, and the Song ranked next. Compared with other ruling houses, their achievements were illustrious. Yet they fell far short of the Three Dynasties. Critics say: “Han government mingled kingly rule with hegemonic methods; Tang government mingled Chinese ways with those of the barbarians; Song government was irresolute and lacked vigor.” This was to judge them deficient. Heaven has long cherished luminous virtue. It surveys the four quarters, seeking repose for the people, and has never ceased to do so for even a day. Yet sage kings did not arise, and the Great Way remained obscure. Heaven’s heart could not remain so indifferent.
Emperor Gao, endowed with divine martial prowess, received the succession ordained by Heaven. The radiant mandate shone forth, and he reverently accepted it. He laid aside his weapons to discuss the Way and pursued learning without flagging. Thus he spoke with Zhi Zhan [?] of his wish to seek the heart of Yao and Shun, and admonished Song Lian to take care to hold fast to and preserve the mind. In discussing learning with Tao An, he elucidated the harm caused by heterodox doctrines. When Song Shan [?] read the Admonition on the Mind, he spoke at length about the subtle workings through which the human mind and the mind of the Way alternately lie latent and come to the fore. Was not this heart of his the very heart of Yao and Shun? Thus, in interpreting the Great Plan, he made manifest the principles of portents and responses between Heaven and humanity; in writing on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, he revealed the sources of order and disorder throughout history. Other records concerning preserving the mind and examining oneself expressed his sincerity; compilations of Comprehensive Instructions and Collected Rituals set forth his standards. His sage counsels were abundant: is there not ample evidence to attest to them?
Emperor Wen personally received the example of the sage sovereign. He excelled in carrying on his predecessor’s work and purposes, thereby bringing luster to…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
先德故其論
皇太子曰堯舜相傳惟曰允執厥中帝王之學
貴乎知要諭學士曰朕嘗退朝默坐而思
管束此心諭御史曰朕每一飲一食未嘗
不念及軍民斯心也其即堯舜之心乎故
輯
帝王之學弘矣他如六經之表章崇正學
文華寶鑑而昭鑒之義廣矣輯聖學心法而
也內訓之頒布正倫理也世德作求不有
===
克纂神明之統而聿追隆古之休豈不盛
列聖相承勿替引之是以大道宣昭至治濯俗
可見者乎
皇上憲天聰明嗣有歷服益懋建中之德以顯
丕承之烈是故敬一有箴傳聖王之心法
與肆我
也五箴有訓闡先哲之微言也揭無逸之
篇以勤稼穡著憂勤也解本末終始之章
以頒諸史局盡精微也以至除夕有作崇
punctuated:
先德。故其論皇太子曰：「堯舜相傳，惟曰允執厥中。帝王之學，貴乎知要。」諭學士曰：「朕嘗退朝，默坐而思，管束此心。」諭御史曰：「朕每一飲一食，未嘗不念及軍民。」斯心也，其即堯舜之心乎？故輯帝王之學弘矣。他如六經之表章，崇正學《文華寶鑑》而昭鑒之義廣矣，輯《聖學心法》而也，內訓之頒布，正倫理也。世德作求，不有克纂神明之統，而聿追隆古之休，豈不盛？列聖相承，勿替引之，是以大道宣昭，至治濯俗。可見者乎？
皇上憲天聰明，嗣有歷服，益懋建中之德，以顯丕承之烈。是故《敬一》有箴，傳聖王之心法，與肆我也。五箴有訓，闡先哲之微言也。揭《無逸》之篇，以勤稼穡，著憂勤也。解本末終始之章，以頒諸史局，盡精微也。以至除夕有作，崇
translation_en:
…the virtue of his predecessors. Thus, in addressing the imperial heir apparent, he said: “What Yao and Shun transmitted to one another was simply this: ‘Sincerely hold fast to the mean.’ In the learning of emperors and kings, what matters is knowing the essentials.” He instructed the academicians: “After retiring from court, I have often sat silently in thought, keeping this mind under control.” He instructed the investigating censors: “Whenever I drink or eat, I never fail to think of the soldiers and the people.” Was this mind not the very mind of Yao and Shun? Thus he compiled … the learning of emperors and kings was enlarged [?]. Other instances include his honoring and elucidating the Six Classics, promoting orthodox learning … the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian), whereby the meaning of taking illuminating examples as a guide was broadened; and compiling the Essential Methods of Sage Learning (Shengxue xinfa), whereby … [?]. The promulgation of the Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun) rectified ethical relationships. Seeking to carry forward the virtue of successive generations, was there not … the ability to continue the divinely enlightened succession and pursue the excellence of high antiquity—was this not magnificent [?]? Successive sage emperors inherited it, extending it without letting it lapse. Thus the Great Way shone forth, and consummate government purified popular customs. Could this not be seen [?]?
His Majesty models himself upon Heaven in his perceptiveness and intelligence, succeeding to the imperial mandate and office. He strives still further in the virtue of establishing the mean, thereby manifesting the splendid achievement of carrying on his inheritance. Thus his Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness (Jingyi) transmits the essential methods of the sage kings’ minds. “And … thus our …” [?]. His explanations of the Five Admonitions elucidate the subtle words of earlier worthies. By displaying the chapter “Against Idleness” (Wuyi) to encourage diligence in sowing and reaping, he manifests his anxious care and industry. By explaining the passage on roots and branches, endings and beginnings, and distributing it to the historiographical offices, he fully explores its subtle meaning. Furthermore, he composed a work on New Year’s Eve, exalting …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
修省也星變有
救謹時幾也此天德之修蓋即二帝三王之爲
德也
郊祀定而典禮秩矣耕籍舉而民事興矣罷四
方無益之獻而百度貞矣塞諸途倖進之
門而百官正矣節妄費以足食而國用經
矣減租稅以裕民而邦本重矣此王道之
敷蓋即二帝三王之爲政也是以十九年
間禮樂明備和氣薰蒸以僻雍以式九
===
圍以合天地以享百神以興萬物以協四
靈洋洋乎至治哉草野荒裔之氓猶得以
咏歌太平之盛而況夙在漸被者乎內外
臣工固宜踴躍而不能自已者也然四時
常運不息其機日月貞明不改其照王者
法天以行健不輟其功故終始典學傅說
所以訓于王而不顯亦臨無斁亦保聖人
之所以懋敬厥德也求輔弼之益慎好惡
之幾察機祥之應納矇瞽之規謹幽獨之
punctuated:
修省也。星變有救，謹時幾也。此天德之修，蓋即二帝三王之爲德也。
郊祀定而典禮秩矣，耕籍舉而民事興矣，罷四方無益之獻而百度貞矣，塞諸途倖進之門而百官正矣，節妄費以足食而國用經矣，減租稅以裕民而邦本重矣。此王道之敷，蓋即二帝三王之爲政也。是以十九年間，禮樂明備，和氣薰蒸，以僻雍，以式九圍，以合天地，以享百神，以興萬物，以協四靈。洋洋乎至治哉！草野荒裔之氓，猶得以咏歌太平之盛，而況夙在漸被者乎？內外臣工，固宜踴躍而不能自已者也。
然四時常運，不息其機；日月貞明，不改其照。王者法天以行健，不輟其功。故終始典學，傅說所以訓于王；而「不顯亦臨，無斁亦保」，聖人之所以懋敬厥德也。求輔弼之益，慎好惡之幾，察機祥之應，納矇瞽之規，謹幽獨之
translation_en:
…self-cultivation and self-examination. When anomalous celestial phenomena appear, remedial measures are taken, showing vigilance toward the incipient signs of the times. This cultivation of heavenly virtue is indeed the same practice of virtue as that of the Two Emperors and Three Kings.
The suburban sacrifices have been settled, and ceremonial observances are duly ordered. The imperial ploughing rite has been performed, and the people’s agricultural labors flourish. Useless offerings from the four quarters have been abolished, and all institutions have been set right. The various avenues to advancement through favor have been closed, and the officials have been rectified. Wasteful expenditure has been restrained to ensure adequate provisions, and state finances have been put in order. Taxes have been reduced to enrich the people, and the foundation of the state has been strengthened. This extension of the Kingly Way is indeed the same practice of government as that of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. Thus, over these nineteen years, rites and music have become illustrious and complete, and harmonious vital influences have spread everywhere: reaching the imperial academy [?], setting an example for the nine regions, bringing accord with Heaven and Earth, offering sacrifice to the hundred spirits, fostering the myriad things, and bringing harmony to the four numinous creatures. How abundant is this consummate governance! Even the people of the countryside and remote borderlands can sing in celebration of the flourishing Great Peace; how much more those who have long been steeped in its influence! Officials serving within and outside the capital should assuredly leap for joy, unable to contain themselves.
Yet the four seasons move perpetually, their workings never ceasing; the sun and moon remain constant in their brightness, never changing their illumination. The king models himself upon Heaven in vigorous action, never interrupting his efforts. Thus, to remain devoted to learning from beginning to end was what Fu Yue taught his king. And “Even where nothing is manifest, be present; without weariness, maintain your care” expresses how the sage diligently attends to his virtue. Seek the benefits of assistance from chief counselors; exercise caution over the first stirrings of likes and dislikes; examine the responses manifested in portents [?]; accept the admonitions of blind musicians; attend carefully, in solitude and seclusion, to…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
修建中和之極此
聖心之所有事臣下之所祗承而不懈者也愚
何容於贅詞乎虞廷之歌曰元首明哉股
肱良哉庶事康哉言敕天之功也周成王
之頌曰昊天有成命二后受之成王不敢
康夙夜基命宥密言法祖之治也先聖
後聖其道同歸愚敢以是爲
今日獻
===
第二問
潘龍
同考試官教諭闞　批　道顯于造化闡于伏羲
孔子得之易子思述之孟子傳之于子思也
此篇推明玄妙究極天人而聖賢相傳之旨異
世同符非深于易而會于道者無此說豪傑之
士非俗學可擬也
考試官教諭文　批　聖賢之言雖殊而實同
歸于道但學者不知察識體驗之耳發明旨趣
合異爲同僅見此作
punctuated:
修，建中和之極，此聖心之所有事、臣下之所祗承而不懈者也。愚何容於贅詞乎？虞廷之歌曰：「元首明哉，股肱良哉，庶事康哉！」言敕天之功也。周成王之頌曰：「昊天有成命，二后受之。成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。」言法祖之治也。先聖後聖，其道同歸。愚敢以是爲今日獻。

第二問
潘龍

同考試官教諭闞批：道顯于造化，闡于伏羲。孔子得之易，子思述之，孟子傳之于子思也。此篇推明玄妙，究極天人，而聖賢相傳之旨，異世同符。非深于易而會于道者，無此說。豪傑之士，非俗學可擬也。

考試官教諭文批：聖賢之言雖殊，而實同歸于道，但學者不知察識體驗之耳。發明旨趣，合異爲同，僅見此作。
translation_en:
…cultivation, and establish the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony: these are the concerns of Your Majesty’s sagely mind, which your servants must reverently uphold without slackening. What room is there for a foolish man like me to add superfluous words? The song at the court of Shun says: “When the head is enlightened, and the limbs are worthy, all affairs prosper!” This speaks of the achievement of carrying out Heaven’s charge. The hymn concerning King Cheng of Zhou says: “August Heaven has an established mandate; the two sovereigns received it. King Cheng dared not rest at ease; day and night he secured the mandate with profound deliberation.” This speaks of governing by following the ancestors. Earlier and later sages alike converge upon the same Way. I venture to offer these words today.

Second Policy Question
Pan Long

Comment by Associate Examiner Kan, Instructor: The Way is manifest in the transformations of creation and was elucidated by Fu Xi. Confucius apprehended it in the Book of Changes; Zisi expounded it; and Mencius received its transmission from Zisi. This essay elucidates its profound subtleties and probes Heaven and humanity to their utmost depths. The essential meaning transmitted among sages and worthies accords across different ages. Only someone deeply versed in the Book of Changes and comprehending the Way could produce such an exposition. Here is a man of exceptional talent, beyond comparison with those of commonplace learning.

Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: Though the words of sages and worthies differ, they all in fact converge upon the Way. It is simply that students do not know how to discern and recognize this, or to realize it through personal experience. In elucidating their essential meaning and bringing differences into unity, this composition alone stands out among those I have seen.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王　批　易其天地鬼神之奧斯
文之作祖乎求道于易斯爲知本子能得之其
殆庶幾神解者耶何其言之親切有味如此高
士
執事發策秋闈以孔子之學爲問而俯以
神解之說進之豈以十室之邑必有忠信
而聖人者天人可學而至與雖然聖道大
矣果也如由猶晝於升堂達也如賜不踰
於及肩愚也何人可以語此雖然性本同
有聖匪由外有爲者亦若是聖人先得我
心之所同然者也敢不掇拾以就正焉夫
曷言乎孔子之學曰易而已曷言乎易曰
大極而已大極之理根抵乎天地萬物之
賾而流行乎天地萬物之中者也自夫立
象設卦伏羲示人精矣係辭盡言周文示
人博矣吾孔子承三聖之統而極修賛之
勤因卦以發藴而中正之教昭隨爻以廣
義而趨時之辨明故十翼之旨夫子韋求
punctuated:
考試官學正王批：易，其天地鬼神之奧、斯文之作祖乎？求道于易，斯爲知本。子能得之，其殆庶幾神解者耶？何其言之親切有味如此！高士！

執事發策秋闈，以孔子之學爲問，而俯以神解之說進之，豈以十室之邑必有忠信，而聖人者天人可學而至與？雖然，聖道大矣！果也如由，猶晝於升堂；達也如賜，不踰於及肩。愚也何人，可以語此？雖然，性本同有，聖匪由外，有爲者亦若是。聖人先得我心之所同然者也，敢不掇拾以就正焉？夫曷言乎孔子之學？曰易而已。曷言乎易？曰大極而已。大極之理，根抵乎天地萬物之賾，而流行乎天地萬物之中者也。自夫立象設卦，伏羲示人精矣；係辭盡言，周文示人博矣。吾孔子承三聖之統，而極修賛之勤，因卦以發藴，而中正之教昭；隨爻以廣義，而趨時之辨明。故十翼之旨，夫子韋求
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: The Book of Changes—is it not the repository of the mysteries of Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits, and the fountainhead of our cultural tradition? To seek the Way in the Changes is to understand the root. Since you have grasped this, are you not perhaps close to a spiritual comprehension? How immediate and rich in meaning your words are! An outstanding scholar!

You, honored examiners, have posed a policy question in the autumn Provincial Examination, asking about Confucius’s learning, and have graciously encouraged us with the idea of spiritual comprehension. Is this because even a hamlet of ten households must contain someone loyal and trustworthy, and because the sage’s heavenly stature can be attained through learning [?]? Yet vast indeed is the Way of the sages! Even one as resolute as You remained confined to having ascended the hall [?]; even one as accomplished as Ci rose no higher than shoulder height. Who am I, in my ignorance, to speak of this? Nevertheless, we all possess the same original nature, and sagehood does not come from outside. Whoever strives can likewise become such a person. The sage has simply grasped before us what our hearts alike acknowledge. How could I fail to gather what I can and submit it for your correction?

What, then, expresses Confucius’s learning? The Changes alone. What expresses the Changes? The Supreme Ultimate alone. The principle of the Supreme Ultimate is rooted in the profound mysteries of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, and flows throughout them. By establishing images and arranging hexagrams, Fuxi showed people what is subtle; by appending statements and fully expressing their meaning, King Wen of Zhou showed people what is comprehensive. Our Confucius inherited the tradition of the three sages and devoted his utmost efforts to elaborating their work. Through the hexagrams he disclosed hidden meanings, making the teaching of centrality and correctness manifest; through the individual lines he expanded their significance, clarifying the distinctions involved in acting according to the time. Thus the purport of the Ten Wings, and the Master’s labors in pursuing [the Changes?] …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
之功也夫然后精者闡而彰博者爍而著
也其曰易知簡能者著其道也曰顯仁蔵
用者彰其化也曰陰陽不測者替其神也
曰貞觀貞明貞一者昭其同也究其原也
陰陽盡之矣故曰一陰一陽之謂道又曰
立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔與剛
立人之道曰仁與義三才一貫之道玆其
的乎曰終則有始者著其運也曰變化云
爲者類其動也曰探幾而神者賛其妙也
===
曰成變化行鬼神者明其功也究其致也
動靜晢矣故曰變通者趨時者也又曰
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉夫
坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉三才
流行之機玆其至乎夫陰陽立三極之根
動靜神變化之用命之所以不已道之所
以無窮者其以是乎此古今流行之機也
嗚呼孔其至德矣乎此其所以承唐虞三
代之統而開萬世生民之的也三千之徒
punctuated:
之功也。夫然后精者闡而彰，博者爍而著也。其曰「易知簡能」者，著其道也；曰「顯仁蔵用」者，彰其化也；曰「陰陽不測」者，替其神也；曰「貞觀貞明貞一」者，昭其同也。究其原也，陰陽盡之矣。故曰：「一陰一陽之謂道。」又曰：「立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。」三才一貫之道，玆其的乎！曰「終則有始」者，著其運也；曰「變化云爲」者，類其動也；曰「探幾而神」者，賛其妙也；曰「成變化行鬼神」者，明其功也。究其致也，動靜晢矣。故曰：「變通者，趨時者也。」又曰：「夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。」三才流行之機，玆其至乎！夫陰陽立三極之根，動靜神變化之用，命之所以不已、道之所以無窮者，其以是乎？此古今流行之機也。
嗚呼！孔其至德矣乎！此其所以承唐虞三代之統，而開萬世生民之的也。三千之徒
translation_en:
…the fruit of his efforts. Only then were the subtle teachings unfolded and made manifest, and the comprehensive teachings illuminated and brought to light. When the Changes speaks of “knowing through ease and accomplishing through simplicity,” it makes its Way evident; when it speaks of “manifesting benevolence and concealing function,” it reveals its transforming activity; when it speaks of “what cannot be fathomed through yin and yang,” it extols [?] its spiritual efficacy; and when it speaks of “constancy in displaying, constancy in illumination, and constancy in unity,” it illuminates their common principle. Traced to their source, yin and yang encompass them all. Thus it says: “One yin and one yang are called the Way.” It also says: “The Way established for Heaven is called yin and yang; the Way established for Earth is called yielding and firm; the Way established for humankind is called benevolence and righteousness.” Is this not the definitive expression of the single Way running through the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humankind?
When it speaks of “an ending followed by a beginning,” it makes evident its cyclical operation; when it speaks of “transformations, speech, and action,” it classifies its movements; when it speaks of “probing incipient tendencies and attaining spiritual efficacy,” it praises its subtlety; and when it speaks of “accomplishing transformations and setting ghosts and spirits in operation,” it clarifies its achievements. Examined to their fullest extent, movement and stillness become clear. Thus it says: “Adapting through change means keeping pace with the times.” It also says: “Qian, in stillness, is concentrated; in movement, it is direct. Thus it brings forth on a great scale. Kun, in stillness, is closed; in movement, it opens. Thus it brings forth far and wide.” Is this not the fullest expression of the dynamic through which the Three Powers circulate? Yin and yang establish the foundation of the Three Ultimates; movement and stillness lend spiritual efficacy to the workings of transformation. Is this not why Heaven’s mandate never ceases and the Way has no end? This is the dynamic that circulates through past and present.
Ah! Surely Confucius possessed consummate virtue! This is how he carried forward the succession of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, and established a standard for the people of all generations. His three thousand disciples…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
授受一道而克復之訓敬恕之目無倦
於求仁之學何哉豈易之外復有所謂仁
耶蓋道一而已矣易者言乎流行而不息
者也仁者言乎純粹而至善者也剛柔善
惡雜揉弗齊唯仁則動靜無間流行之機
罔非天則天地萬物精粗隱顯舉該之矣
故曰動靜不失其時其道光明者此之謂
也苟不至德至道不凝君子去仁惡乎成
名故聖人著其教焉夫本一以垂訓時措
===
以成物同歸殊途百慮一致孔子而下可
以觀矣中庸一書子思衛道而作也原性
命之與立會通之準故中者言乎其不偏
也庸者言乎其不易也其曰大本云者所
以明人性之蘊靜而虛而天下之動而實
者之基也孔子所謂寂然不動者是也其
曰達道云者所以明人性之發動而神而
實靜而虛者之彰也孔子之所謂感而遂
通天下之故者是也發有已未而性無內
punctuated:
授受一道，而克復之訓、敬恕之目，無倦於求仁之學，何哉？豈易之外復有所謂仁耶？蓋道一而已矣。易者，言乎流行而不息者也；仁者，言乎純粹而至善者也。剛柔善惡，雜揉弗齊，唯仁則動靜無間，流行之機罔非天則，天地萬物，精粗隱顯，舉該之矣。故曰：「動靜不失其時，其道光明。」者此之謂也。苟不至德，至道不凝；君子去仁，惡乎成名？故聖人著其教焉。夫本一以垂訓，時措以成物，同歸殊途，百慮一致，孔子而下可以觀矣。
《中庸》一書，子思衛道而作也。原性命之與，立會通之準。故中者，言乎其不偏也；庸者，言乎其不易也。其曰大本云者，所以明人性之蘊，靜而虛，而天下之動而實者之基也。孔子所謂寂然不動者，是也。其曰達道云者，所以明人性之發，動而神，而實靜而虛者之彰也。孔子之所謂感而遂通天下之故者，是也。發有已未，而性無內
translation_en:
…transmitted and received a single Way. Yet why, with the instruction to overcome the self and return to ritual propriety, and the specific teachings of reverence and reciprocity, did they remain tireless in learning to seek benevolence? Could there be something called benevolence apart from the Changes? The Way is simply one. The Changes speaks of its ceaseless circulation; benevolence speaks of its purity and utmost goodness. Firmness and yielding, good and evil, are mingled and uneven. Only in benevolence is there no interruption between activity and stillness: the workings of its circulation invariably accord with Heaven’s norms. Heaven, earth, and the myriad things, whether fine or coarse, hidden or manifest, are all encompassed within it. Thus the saying, “In activity and stillness, never missing the proper time, its Way is radiant,” means precisely this. Without consummate virtue, the consummate Way cannot become firmly established. If a gentleman abandons benevolence, how can he fulfill that name? Therefore the sage made his teaching manifest. Taking the One as his basis, he handed down instruction; applying it as circumstances required, he brought things to fulfillment. Different paths reach the same destination, and a hundred deliberations arrive at one conclusion. This can be observed from Kongzi onward.
Zisi wrote the Doctrine of the Mean to defend the Way. It traces the bestowal of human nature and Heaven’s mandate [?] and establishes a standard for comprehensive understanding. Thus “centrality” means being without partiality, and “constancy” means being unchanging. Its expression “the great foundation” illuminates what lies latent in human nature: still and empty, it is the foundation of all that is active and substantial under Heaven. This is what Kongzi called “quiescent and unmoving.” Its expression “the universally operative Way” illuminates the manifestation of human nature: active and wondrous in its workings, it is indeed the outward expression of what is still and empty. This is what Kongzi called “responding to stimulation and thereby comprehending the affairs of all under Heaven.” Manifestation may have already occurred or may not yet have occurred, but human nature has no inner…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
外其流行不息之機乎其曰戒懼謹獨云
者所以致其功也動靜交相存省顯微實
無間矣孔子所謂敬以直內義以方外者
是也夫動靜相生者心之神也動靜不違
者學之則也致中和而位育出焉復其初
矣子思子其善於學易者與七篇之作孟
子所以闢邪說而明王道也指本心之良
爲作聖之機故四德者言乎其藴也純粹
精也四端者言乎其發也直方大也其曰
===
萬物皆備云者所以明人心之神靈明不
昧順以動焉四端萬善以時出之廣大悉
備也其即子思之所謂大本達道者乎其
曰性善云者蓋以人生而靜本自純粹帝
降之衷物我之所同具者也其即孔子之
所謂繼之者善而成之者性乎夫良知良
能元不喪失先立乎其大者則動靜皆定
而物欲不累窮理盡性以至於命道在我
矣孟子其善於祖述者與故曰先聖後聖
punctuated:
外，其流行不息之機乎？其曰戒懼謹獨云者，所以致其功也。動靜交相存省，顯微實無間矣。孔子所謂敬以直內、義以方外者是也。夫動靜相生者，心之神也；動靜不違者，學之則也。致中和而位育出焉，復其初矣。子思子其善於學易者與？
七篇之作，孟子所以闢邪說而明王道也。指本心之良爲作聖之機，故四德者，言乎其藴也，純粹精也；四端者，言乎其發也，直方大也。其曰萬物皆備云者，所以明人心之神，靈明不昧，順以動焉，四端萬善以時出之，廣大悉備也。其即子思之所謂大本達道者乎？其曰性善云者，蓋以人生而靜，本自純粹，帝降之衷，物我之所同具者也。其即孔子之所謂繼之者善而成之者性乎？夫良知良能元不喪失，先立乎其大者，則動靜皆定，而物欲不累。窮理盡性以至於命，道在我矣。孟子其善於祖述者與？故曰：「先聖後聖
translation_en:
…or outer: is this not the dynamic whereby it flows without ceasing? His statements about vigilance and apprehension, and about being watchful when alone, explain how to bring this effort to fulfillment. In activity and stillness alike, preservation and self-examination sustain one another; between the manifest and the subtle there is truly no gap. This is what Confucius meant by “reverence to straighten the inner self and righteousness to square outward conduct.” Activity and stillness generating one another constitute the spirit-like efficacy of the mind; not departing from what is proper in either activity or stillness is the rule of learning. When equilibrium and harmony are fully realized, Heaven and Earth take their places and the myriad things are nourished: the original condition is restored. Was Master Zisi not skilled in studying the Book of Changes?
The composition of the seven books was the means by which Mengzi refuted heterodox doctrines and clarified the Way of the Kings. He identified the goodness of the original mind as the key to becoming a sage. Thus, the four virtues describe what it contains: purity, integrity, and refinement. The four beginnings describe its manifestations: straightness, squareness, and greatness. His statement that “the myriad things are all complete within me” explains the spirit-like efficacy of the human mind: numinously perceptive and unobscured, it acts in accord with what is right. The four beginnings and all forms of goodness emerge from it at their proper times; it is vast and fully endowed. Is this not precisely what Zisi called the great foundation and the universally prevailing Way? His statement that human nature is good means that human beings are still at birth and originally pure. The balanced nature bestowed by the Lord on High is something that other beings and oneself alike possess. Is this not what Confucius meant by “what continues it is goodness, and what completes it is nature”? Innate moral knowledge and innate moral capacity are never originally lost. If one first establishes the greater part of oneself, one will be settled in both activity and stillness, unburdened by material desires. By fathoming principle and fully realizing one's nature, thereby reaching an understanding of Heaven's mandate, one possesses the Way within oneself. Was Mengzi not skilled in transmitting the teachings of his predecessors? Thus it is said: “The earlier sages and the later sages…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
其揆一也雖然神而明之存乎其人道無
古今而學有機要故君子識往以論世當
求其故也是故自強不息孔子之所以配
天也戒懼謹獨子思之所以法祖也勿忘
勿助孟子之所以希孔也苟徒知其同而
不求所以同則亦空言而已夫何有哉夫
學貴自得也神解則自得矣乃若程子受
學周子而謂天理二字是自家體貼出來
非所謂神解者乎此正達于天道與聖人
一之時也是道也必優游涵泳長裕不設
脫然冰融凍解默識心悟有莫知其所以
然而然者矣非言語所可及也愚何足以
知之
===
第三問
黃覲
同考試官學正葛　批　風俗人才關係世道最
要而其機實在于上風土氣禀之說不盡然也
識見明透議論醇雅而才氣英發如長江大河
punctuated:
其揆一也。雖然，神而明之，存乎其人。道無古今，而學有機要，故君子識往以論世，當求其故也。是故自強不息，孔子之所以配天也；戒懼謹獨，子思之所以法祖也；勿忘勿助，孟子之所以希孔也。苟徒知其同而不求所以同，則亦空言而已，夫何有哉！夫學貴自得也，神解則自得矣。乃若程子受學周子，而謂天理二字是自家體貼出來，非所謂神解者乎？此正達于天道、與聖人一之時也。是道也，必優游涵泳，長裕不設，脫然冰融凍解，默識心悟，有莫知其所以然而然者矣，非言語所可及也。愚何足以知之！

第三問
黃覲

同考試官學正葛批：風俗人才關係世道最要，而其機實在于上，風土氣禀之說不盡然也。識見明透，議論醇雅，而才氣英發，如長江大河，
translation_en:
…their standard is one and the same. Nevertheless, to comprehend it with spiritual insight rests with the individual. The Way does not differ between ancient and modern times, but learning has its crucial points. Thus, when the gentleman understands the past in order to assess an age, he should seek the reasons behind this. Unceasing self-strengthening was how Confucius matched Heaven; vigilance, apprehension, and care in solitude were how Zisi took his ancestor as his model; neither forgetting nor forcing growth was how Mengzi aspired to emulate Confucius. If one merely knows that they are alike without seeking what makes them alike, this amounts to empty words. What substance could it have? Learning prizes understanding attained for oneself; spiritual insight brings such understanding. Master Cheng studied under Master Zhou, yet said that he had personally discerned the meaning of the two characters “Heavenly principle.” Was this not what is called spiritual insight? This was precisely the moment when he attained the Way of Heaven and became one with the sages. In pursuing this Way, one must dwell at ease in it and immerse oneself deeply, growing in abundance without constraint [?], until suddenly the ice melts and the frost thaws: one recognizes it silently and awakens to it in the heart. This happens without one's knowing why it happens; words cannot reach it. How could someone as unworthy as I be capable of understanding it?

Third Policy Question
Huang Jin

Comment by Associate Examiner Ge, Instructor: Customs and human talent are of the greatest consequence for the moral condition of the age, and the decisive influence in fact lies with those above. Explanations based on local climate and terrain and on endowments of vital energy are not entirely correct. His discernment is clear and penetrating, his arguments sound and elegant, and his talent shines forth like the Yangzi and the Yellow River…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
愈流而愈無盡通塲無出子右者遠到之器也
可羨可羨
考試官教諭文　批　前二塲文氣雄渾浩然
不獨此策尤爲終塲之冠奇士奇士
考試官學正王　批　有學實有筆力非素養
之士遽無此作録之
治天下者有化民之道有作人之功然有
本焉而統會之至一也有機焉而轉移之
至神也何也民以習染而爲風俗士以習
學而爲人才惟其成於習故有美有惡有
===
正有邪教化者所導以歸美適正之路也
然雖本之人性而或不能以強從持以漸
陶而或沮撓於時勢是以教化之不淑也
惟建極者端其本善其機以爲教化先是
故示之以觀而化自普也通之以感而應
自順也如是而家有殊俗士有異趨未之
聞也非天下之至聖其孰能與於此執事
發策以風俗人才爲問其深知王道之本
punctuated:
愈流而愈無盡，通塲無出子右者，遠到之器也。可羨，可羨！
考試官教諭文批：前二塲文氣雄渾浩然，不獨此策，尤爲終塲之冠。奇士，奇士！
考試官學正王批：有學實，有筆力，非素養之士，遽無此作。録之。
治天下者，有化民之道，有作人之功。然有本焉，而統會之至一也；有機焉，而轉移之至神也。何也？民以習染而爲風俗，士以習學而爲人才。惟其成於習，故有美有惡，有正有邪。教化者，所導以歸美適正之路也。然雖本之人性，而或不能以強從；持以漸陶，而或沮撓於時勢，是以教化之不淑也。惟建極者，端其本，善其機，以爲教化先。是故示之以觀，而化自普也；通之以感，而應自順也。如是而家有殊俗，士有異趨，未之聞也。非天下之至聖，其孰能與於此？執事發策，以風俗人才爲問，其深知王道之本
translation_en:
…the farther it flows, the more inexhaustible it becomes. No one in the entire examination surpasses you: you have the capacity to go far. Admirable, admirable!
Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: The writing in the first two sessions was vigorous, full-bodied, and expansive; these qualities are not confined to this policy essay, which is, moreover, the finest of the final session. An extraordinary scholar, an extraordinary scholar!
Examiner Wang, School Director, comments: He has substantial learning and strength of expression. Without sustained cultivation, a scholar could never produce such a work at short notice. Include it in the record.
Those who govern All-under-Heaven have a way of transforming the people and accomplish the work of nurturing men of talent. Yet there is a root through which these endeavors are brought into perfect unity, and a pivotal means through which change is effected with consummate subtlety. Why is this? Among the people, customs arise through habitual influence; among scholars, talent develops through habitual study. Precisely because these are formed through habituation, there are both good and bad, both upright and deviant. Moral instruction is the path by which they are guided toward goodness and rectitude. Yet although it is grounded in human nature, compliance sometimes cannot be compelled; although one perseveres in gradually molding people, the circumstances of the times sometimes obstruct the effort. This is why moral instruction fails to produce good results. Only one who establishes the supreme standard can set its root aright and make good use of its pivotal means, thereby taking the lead in moral instruction. Thus, when an example is displayed for people to behold, transformation naturally spreads everywhere; when contact is made by moving their hearts, their response naturally accords with it. Under such conditions, I have never heard of households having divergent customs or scholars pursuing different courses. Who but the supreme sage of All-under-Heaven could achieve this? You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question asking about customs and men of talent, showing your profound understanding of the root of the kingly way…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
教化其有興乎愚敢不究極言之宋儒程
顥曰治天下以正風俗得賢才爲本盖風
俗者象治之迹賢才者輔治之具也民無
美俗何以善國國無其賢誰與共理先王
知其然故首重教化學校之隆師儒之選
恒究心焉而表率之道感動之理又有不
疾而速不行而至者矣是故休明之世無
澆漓之俗聖哲之朝無壬佞之臣凡以是
耳豈時數氣化之自然適會其逢哉說者
===
謂俗之不齊恒地勢拘之考古若秦齊晉
楚諸列國之風或強悍或悲怨或奢靡儉
勤種種異習大都狃於水土風氣之一偏
者雖賢者有所不免王制曰廣谷大川異
制民生其間異俗若聲音言語之不相比
是奚害哉修其教不易其俗齊其政不異
其宜而已謂才之弗齊亦天賦拘之稽古
若皐夔稷契共驩苗鯀暨諸叔季之臣或
聖或狂或賢或不肖邈乎弗類大都定於
punctuated:
教化其有興乎？愚敢不究極言之！宋儒程顥曰：「治天下以正風俗、得賢才爲本。」盖風俗者，象治之迹；賢才者，輔治之具也。民無美俗，何以善國？國無其賢，誰與共理？先王知其然，故首重教化，學校之隆、師儒之選，恒究心焉。而表率之道、感動之理，又有不疾而速、不行而至者矣。是故休明之世無澆漓之俗，聖哲之朝無壬佞之臣，凡以是耳。豈時數氣化之自然適會其逢哉？
說者謂俗之不齊，恒地勢拘之。考古，若秦、齊、晉、楚諸列國之風，或強悍，或悲怨，或奢靡、儉勤，種種異習，大都狃於水土風氣之一偏者，雖賢者有所不免。《王制》曰：「廣谷大川異制，民生其間異俗。」若聲音言語之不相比，是奚害哉？修其教，不易其俗；齊其政，不異其宜而已。謂才之弗齊，亦天賦拘之。稽古，若皐、夔、稷、契、共、驩、苗、鯀，暨諸叔季之臣，或聖，或狂，或賢，或不肖，邈乎弗類，大都定於
translation_en:
…might moral transformation flourish? How could I, in my ignorance, dare not discuss this exhaustively? The Song Confucian Cheng Hao said: “Governing the realm rests upon rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talent.” Customs are the visible traces of government; worthy men are the means of assisting it. If the people lack good customs, how can the state be well governed? If the state lacks worthy men, with whom can its ruler share the work of governing? The former kings understood this and therefore gave foremost importance to moral instruction. They constantly devoted their attention to promoting schools and selecting learned teachers. Moreover, the way of leading by example and the principle of moving others through moral influence produce effects that are swift without haste and arrive without movement. Thus, in an age of splendid and enlightened rule, customs are not shallow and debased; at the court of a sagely and wise ruler, there are no crafty, flattering ministers. All this comes from these means alone. Could it merely be a chance coincidence arising naturally from the cycles of time and the transformations of vital energy?
Some argue that differences in customs are invariably constrained by geography. Looking back to antiquity, the customs of the various states, such as Qin, Qi, Jin, and Chu, were sometimes fierce and headstrong, sometimes sorrowful and resentful, sometimes extravagant, and sometimes frugal and industrious. These varied habits generally arose from habituation to one particular tendency of the local terrain, waters, climate, and atmosphere; even worthy men could not entirely escape them. The “Royal Regulations” states: “Broad valleys and great rivers differ in configuration; the people living among them differ in customs.” If their sounds and speech do not match one another, what harm is there in that? One need only cultivate their instruction without changing their customs, and bring order to their government without departing from what suits them.
Others say that differences in talent are likewise constrained by natural endowment. Looking back to antiquity, figures such as Gao, Kui, Ji, Xie, Gong, Huan, Miao, and Gun, together with the ministers of declining ages, were variously sagely or wayward, worthy or unworthy, and vastly unlike one another. These differences were largely determined by …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
氣質清濁之殊絶者雖聖代有不能齊孔
子曰惟上智與下愚不移直若陰陽晝夜
之相反然豈盡若是哉性本同善而緣習
則殊教以反同亦因材以篤而已是故先
王有教民之制若禮樂刑政詳於周禮而
掌於大司徒以施十有二教所以納民於
軌物範俗於大同者莫良矣然後世之教
不盡殊而協和時雍之風邈乎絶響何也
蓋媚茲一人者百姓之心而朝廷則四方
===
之極教化之所從出也順帝之則本於篤
恭之盛若好尚舉動又自近達遠四望以
為趨向者也先王所以化成俗美者亦率
之以德行端之以好尚潛乎而默化之不
獨禮樂刑政而已傳云堯舜率天下以仁
而民從之桀紂率天下以暴而民從之言
教有本也商之政尚猛故其俗激昂而奮
厲周之政尚寬故其俗和柔而寬緩言化
有機也後世君漢文帝躬行元默而黎民
punctuated: 氣質清濁之殊絶者，雖聖代有不能齊。孔子曰：「惟上智與下愚不移。」直若陰陽晝夜之相反然，豈盡若是哉？性本同善，而緣習則殊，教以反同，亦因材以篤而已。是故先王有教民之制，若禮樂刑政，詳於《周禮》，而掌於大司徒，以施十有二教，所以納民於軌物、範俗於大同者，莫良矣。然後世之教不盡殊，而協和時雍之風邈乎絶響，何也？蓋媚茲一人者，百姓之心，而朝廷則四方之極，教化之所從出也。順帝之則，本於篤恭之盛；若好尚舉動，又自近達遠，四望以為趨向者也。先王所以化成俗美者，亦率之以德行，端之以好尚，潛乎而默化之，不獨禮樂刑政而已。傳云：「堯舜率天下以仁，而民從之；桀紂率天下以暴，而民從之。」言教有本也。商之政尚猛，故其俗激昂而奮厲；周之政尚寬，故其俗和柔而寬緩。言化有機也。後世君漢文帝躬行元默，而黎民
translation_en: …the stark differences in the purity or turbidity of their psychophysical endowments; even in an age of sage rule, some could not be made alike. Confucius said, “Only the wisest and the most foolish do not change.” They seem as opposed as yin and yang, day and night—but can everyone be like this? Human nature is originally alike in its goodness; differences arise through habituation. Teaching that restores this original sameness merely nurtures each according to his capacities. Thus the former kings established institutions for teaching the people, including ritual, music, punishments, and government. These are detailed in the Rites of Zhou and administered by the Minister of Education, who implements the twelve teachings. Nothing could better bring the people within proper norms and shape their customs toward a great common order. Yet the teachings of later ages were not entirely different: why, then, did the spirit of concord and universal harmony fall so utterly silent? For affection for this one man, the ruler, lies in the hearts of the common people, while the court is the pole toward which all quarters turn and the source from which moral instruction proceeds. Conformity to the standards of the Lord on High is rooted in profound reverence at its fullest. The ruler’s preferences and actions also extend their influence from near to far; people everywhere look to them for direction. The former kings transformed the people and perfected their customs by leading them through virtuous conduct, setting them straight through their own preferences, and quietly transforming them without words—not solely through ritual, music, punishments, and government. The commentary says, “Yao and Shun led the world with benevolence, and the people followed them; Jie and Zhou led the world with violence, and the people followed them.” This means that teaching has a root. Shang government prized severity, so its customs were spirited and vigorous; Zhou government prized leniency, so its customs were gentle and relaxed. This means that transformation has a motivating force. Among rulers of later ages, Emperor Wen of Han personally practiced tranquil noninterference, and the common people…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
醇厚唐太宗篤行仁義而外戶不閉亦其
效之不然晉崇虛浮而清談縱恣之風熾
當時禮樂之教遽淪絕哉由是觀之禮
樂刑政者教化之具譬則舟楫也師儒其
篙師也朝廷之德化譬則江海而好尚則
天之風也舟楫非風水之利能自運哉風
俗之醇王道之應也有天德便可語王道
謂教化不本於朝廷而能一道德同風俗
可乎先王有教士之法若詩書學校備於
===
周禮而詳於後世經制之書無非推廣三
物之教所以正德以成賢育才以昌業者
莫美矣然後世之法制益詳而賢聖忠貞
之士代不多見何也蓋共惟帝臣者士之
心而帝則兼君師之責教化之主盟也觀
化之樞本於中和之極若好惡用舍又中
智之士恒覘以轉移者也先王所以教乎
而人化者亦視之以率履端之以好惡身
教而默諭之不獨詩書學校而已觀堯以
punctuated:
醇厚，唐太宗篤行仁義而外戶不閉，亦其效之。不然，晉崇虛浮而清談縱恣之風熾，當時禮樂之教遽淪絕哉？由是觀之，禮樂刑政者，教化之具，譬則舟楫也；師儒，其篙師也；朝廷之德化，譬則江海，而好尚則天之風也。舟楫非風水之利，能自運哉？風俗之醇，王道之應也。有天德便可語王道，謂教化不本於朝廷而能一道德、同風俗，可乎？

先王有教士之法，若詩書學校，備於《周禮》而詳於後世經制之書，無非推廣三物之教，所以正德以成賢、育才以昌業者，莫美矣。然後世之法制益詳，而賢聖忠貞之士代不多見，何也？蓋共惟帝臣者，士之心，而帝則兼君師之責，教化之主盟也。觀化之樞，本於中和之極；若好惡用舍，又中智之士恒覘以轉移者也。先王所以教乎而人化者，亦視之以率履，端之以好惡，身教而默諭之，不獨詩書學校而已。觀堯以
translation_en:
…became sincere and generous. Tang Taizong earnestly practiced benevolence and righteousness, and outer doors were left unbarred: this, too, was an effect of such influence. Otherwise, when the Jin exalted empty superficiality and the fashion for unrestrained “pure conversation” flourished, had instruction through ritual and music suddenly fallen into oblivion? Viewed in this light, ritual, music, punishments, and government are instruments of moral transformation, like boats and oars; Confucian teachers are their boatmen. The court’s transforming virtue is like rivers and seas, while its preferences are like the wind from Heaven. Can boats and oars move of themselves without favorable wind and water? The purity of customs is the response to the Kingly Way. With heavenly virtue, one can speak of the Kingly Way. Can one claim that moral instruction need not be rooted in the court, yet can still unify moral principles and make customs uniform?

The former kings had methods for educating scholars, including the Poetry, the Documents, and schools. These are fully set out in the Rites of Zhou and elaborated in later writings on institutions and regulations. All extend instruction in the three categories; nothing could better rectify virtue to form worthy men and nurture talent to advance the work of government. Yet the institutions and regulations of later ages became ever more detailed, while worthy, sagely, loyal, and steadfast men were seldom seen in any generation. Why was this? To regard themselves as all being the emperor’s subjects is the disposition of scholars; the emperor, for his part, bears the responsibilities of both ruler and teacher and presides over moral transformation. The pivot of transformation through example rests upon the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. As for his likes and dislikes, and whom he employs or sets aside, these are also what men of middling understanding constantly watch, adjusting their conduct accordingly. The former kings taught and thereby transformed people by showing them proper conduct and directing them through their likes and dislikes. They taught through personal example and instructed without words, rather than relying solely on the Poetry, the Documents, and schools. Consider how Yao, by…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
執中命舜而開羣聖道統之源文王以豈
弟作人而臻棫樸菁莪之化非躬行心得
之教乎舜選於衆舉皋陶而不仁者遠湯
選於衆舉伊尹而不仁者遠非轉移鼔舞
之機乎後世若唐尚詞章而窮達皆藝苑
之士宋崇道學而朝野多希聖之英亦其
驗矣不然漢靈帝喜陳方俗語而無行趨
勢之徒並列鴻都門學非當時學校之崇
亦罔而已耶由是觀之詩書學校者教化
===
之文譬則風雨霜露也師儒則四時五行
之吏也人主之淵德抑天之於穆不已好
惡則陰陽舒慘也風雨霜露非於穆舒慘
之運能不忒哉人文之盛王化之昭也有
內聖之德斯有外王之業謂教化不本於
人主而謂師道得善人多可乎嗚呼茲至
治之基大化之本而恭己無爲之業也並
休麗美不有待於
今日哉愚何幸躬逢其
punctuated: 執中命舜，而開羣聖道統之源；文王以豈弟作人，而臻棫樸菁莪之化，非躬行心得之教乎？舜選於衆，舉皋陶而不仁者遠；湯選於衆，舉伊尹而不仁者遠，非轉移鼔舞之機乎？後世若唐尚詞章，而窮達皆藝苑之士；宋崇道學，而朝野多希聖之英，亦其驗矣。不然，漢靈帝喜陳方俗語，而無行趨勢之徒並列鴻都門學，非當時學校之崇亦罔而已耶？由是觀之，詩書學校者，教化之文，譬則風雨霜露也；師儒則四時五行之吏也；人主之淵德，抑天之於穆不已；好惡則陰陽舒慘也。風雨霜露，非於穆舒慘之運，能不忒哉？人文之盛，王化之昭也。有內聖之德，斯有外王之業。謂教化不本於人主，而謂師道得、善人多，可乎？嗚呼！茲至治之基、大化之本，而恭己無爲之業也。並休麗美，不有待於今日哉？愚何幸躬逢其
translation_en:
…instructed Shun to hold fast to the mean, thereby opening the source of the succession through which the sages transmitted the Way. King Wen, through his gracious ease, nurtured men of worth and achieved the transforming influence celebrated in “The Oak Trees” (Yupu) and “The Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing’e). Was this not teaching through personal practice and inward understanding? Shun selected from the multitude and raised up Gao Yao, and those lacking benevolence withdrew; Tang selected from the multitude and raised up Yi Yin, and those lacking benevolence withdrew. Was this not the means of redirecting and inspiring people? In later ages, the Tang prized literary composition, and men both obscure and eminent belonged to the literary world; the Song honored the Learning of the Way, and both at court and beyond it there were many outstanding men who aspired to sagehood. These, too, bear witness to its efficacy. Conversely, Emperor Ling of Han delighted in presentations of regional and colloquial expressions [?], and men without moral conduct who courted the powerful were enrolled together in the Hongdu Gate School. Was not the esteem accorded to schools at that time consequently futile?
Viewed in this light, the Book of Odes, the Book of Documents, and the schools are the outward forms of moral transformation, comparable to wind, rain, frost, and dew. Confucian teachers are the officials administering the four seasons and the Five Phases. The ruler’s profound virtue is like Heaven’s unceasing, unfathomable activity; his likes and dislikes are like the genial and harsh workings of yin and yang. Without this unfathomable activity and the cycles of geniality and harshness, could wind, rain, frost, and dew remain free from deviation? The flourishing of human culture manifests the transforming influence of kingly rule. Only with the virtue of inward sagehood can there be the achievement of outward kingship. Can one claim that moral transformation is not rooted in the ruler, yet maintain that the way of teaching is properly realized and good men abound?
Ah! This is the foundation of perfect governance, the root of great transformation, and the achievement of reverently ordering oneself and ruling without deliberate action. Does not the joint realization of such excellence and beauty await this very day? How fortunate am I, in my humble station, to witness its …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
盛
第四問
孫元卿
同考試官教諭甘　批〔數乃天地自然之妙而理〕
〔實主之此作以理論數以數準理得之矣故表〕
〔而出之〕
考試官教諭文　批〔博洽之學明決之才正〕
〔大之氣俱于此策見之〕
考試官學正王　批〔理數之學精到不忒而〕
〔議論無窮天下事可與言矣可敬可敬〕
===
洩天地之蘊者其數乎數之精者其神
乎數也者理之時也化之紀也天地非數
則道化幾不可測而識矣神也者道之樞
也聖之極也數非神聖則精閟殆不可會
而通矣是故一定而不易者數之體變動
而不居者數之用錯綜皆合而變化無窮
茲其爲天地之蘊乎茲其爲數之精乎非
天下之至神其孰能與於此故曰神而明
punctuated:
盛。

第四問
孫元卿
同考試官教諭甘批〔數乃天地自然之妙，而理〕〔實主之。此作以理論數，以數準理，得之矣，故表〕〔而出之。〕
考試官教諭文批〔博洽之學，明決之才，正〕〔大之氣，俱于此策見之。〕
考試官學正王批〔理數之學，精到不忒，而〕〔議論無窮，天下事可與言矣。可敬！可敬！〕

洩天地之蘊者，其數乎？數之精者，其神乎？數也者，理之時也，化之紀也。天地非數，則道化幾不可測而識矣。神也者，道之樞也，聖之極也。數非神聖，則精閟殆不可會而通矣。是故一定而不易者，數之體；變動而不居者，數之用。錯綜皆合，而變化無窮，茲其爲天地之蘊乎？茲其爲數之精乎？非天下之至神，其孰能與於此？故曰：「神而明
translation_en:
…its flourishing.

Fourth Question
Sun Yuanqing

Comment by Associate Examiner Gan, Instructor: 〔Numbers embody the naturally arising marvels of Heaven and Earth, yet principle〕〔truly governs them. This essay discusses numbers through principle and uses numbers to verify principle. It has grasped the matter; therefore I single it out〕〔for presentation.〕

Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: 〔Wide-ranging learning, clear and decisive ability, and upright〕〔and magnanimous spirit are all evident in this policy essay.〕

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: 〔His understanding of principle and numbers is penetrating and unerring, and〕〔his arguments are inexhaustible. Here is someone with whom one may discuss the affairs of the world. Admirable! Admirable!〕

Is it not numbers that disclose what Heaven and Earth hold hidden? Is it not spiritual efficacy that constitutes the essence of numbers? Numbers are the temporal expression of principle and the ordering framework of transformation. Without numbers, the workings of the Way and of transformation in Heaven and Earth could scarcely be fathomed and understood. Spiritual efficacy is the pivot of the Way and the culmination of sagehood. Without spiritually efficacious sages, the subtle mysteries of numbers could scarcely be comprehended and fully penetrated. Thus, what is fixed and unchanging constitutes the substance of numbers; what changes and never remains still constitutes their operation. In their interweaving and combination, all accords, while their transformations are inexhaustible. Is this not what Heaven and Earth hold hidden? Is this not the essence of numbers? Who but one possessing the utmost spiritual efficacy in the world could participate in this? Thus it is said: “To render it spiritually efficacious and illuminate…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
之存乎其人知此則圖書衍極之數可詳
而言矣夫是數也原於冥漠之無形而推
於儀象之既判極之日月星辰之麗山岳
川澤之奠皆數之著也四時五行之運萬
類羣形之布皆數之化也玄覽於象帝之
先是即畫前之易矣誰謂數昉於圖書哉
可以順性命之理可以研事物之端推之
典禮秩於聖人者數之教也經畫備於王
制者數之度也深明乎天地之撰斯亦形
上之道也誰謂儒者不貫數哉惟河圖之
===
出適值夫伏羲之神靈仰觀俯察遠求近
取蓋已默感而冥會之故天苞之說雖甚
誣而其彰乾坤之象以昭文明之瑞若開
物成務之必於其時謂天無因而不受茲
道不可也洛書之出適當夫大禹之神聖
治水底績地平天成蓋亦冥召而洞契之
故地符之說雖甚誕而其濺玄武之精以
昭水德之盛若陳疇類範之必於其人謂
punctuated: 之，存乎其人。」知此，則圖書衍極之數可詳而言矣。夫是數也，原於冥漠之無形，而推於儀象之既判。極之，日月星辰之麗，山岳川澤之奠，皆數之著也；四時五行之運，萬類羣形之布，皆數之化也。玄覽於象帝之先，是即畫前之易矣，誰謂數昉於圖書哉？可以順性命之理，可以研事物之端。推之，典禮秩於聖人者，數之教也；經畫備於王制者，數之度也。深明乎天地之撰，斯亦形上之道也，誰謂儒者不貫數哉？惟河圖之出，適值夫伏羲之神靈，仰觀俯察，遠求近取，蓋已默感而冥會之。故天苞之說雖甚誣，而其彰乾坤之象，以昭文明之瑞，若開物成務之必於其時，謂天無因而不受茲道，不可也。洛書之出，適當夫大禹之神聖，治水底績，地平天成，蓋亦冥召而洞契之。故地符之說雖甚誕，而其濺玄武之精，以昭水德之盛，若陳疇類範之必於其人，謂
translation_en:
…“making it spiritually efficacious and illuminating it rests with the person.” Once this is understood, the numbers unfolded to their utmost in the River Chart and Luo Writing can be discussed in detail. These numbers originate in the obscure and formless and extend into the differentiated configurations and images. Pursued to their fullest extent, the sun, moon, and stars arrayed above, and the mountains, rivers, and marshes established below, are all manifestations of number. The movements of the four seasons and five phases, and the distribution of the myriad kinds and forms of things, are all transformations of number. To contemplate profoundly what seems to precede the Lord on High is to apprehend the Changes before its lines were drawn. Who could say that number began with the Chart and Writing?

Through number one can follow the principles of human nature and destiny and investigate the beginnings of things and affairs. Extending this further, the statutes and rites ordered by the sages constitute the teaching of number; the comprehensive arrangements embodied in royal institutions constitute its measures. To understand profoundly the workings of Heaven and Earth is also to understand the Way that lies beyond physical form. Who could say that Confucian scholars do not comprehend number?

The appearance of the River Chart coincided precisely with the spiritual sagacity of Fuxi. Looking upward and examining below, seeking afar and drawing upon what was near, he had surely already responded to it silently and apprehended it inwardly. Thus, although the account of a heavenly envelope is thoroughly unfounded, the Chart displayed the images of Heaven and Earth and revealed an auspicious sign of cultural illumination, as though disclosing things and accomplishing affairs had necessarily to occur at that time. It is untenable to say that Heaven had no cause and did not receive this Way [?].

The appearance of the Luo Writing coincided precisely with the divine sagacity of Yu the Great. He brought the work of controlling the waters to completion, set the earth in order, and fulfilled Heaven’s work; surely he too had inwardly summoned it and thoroughly accorded with it. Thus, although the account of an earthly talisman is thoroughly fantastic, its splashing forth the essence of the Dark Warrior [?] revealed the flourishing potency of Water, as though setting forth the categories and arranging the models necessarily depended on this particular man. To say…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
地無故而不爲兹實不可也然今考圖之
數五十有五書之數四十有五多寡不同
而方圓弗類何也盖圖員象天而爲數十
偶贏奇乏數之全也書方象地而爲數九
奇贏偶乏數之變也圖書皆以五居中虛
其中則太極也奇偶均二十者兩儀也圖
虛其十亦四十五數也書九疇之子數則
亦五十五數也參伍錯綜而無適不合其
變化之道神之所爲乎二數之名異而理
===
同二聖之時異而心同所謂聖人成能均
也劉歆經緯之說不可見哉倚數之法聖
人參天兩地教天下揲蓍求易使不迷於
吉凶悔吝之途者然圖數五十有五大衍
五十而虛一何也盖其用四十九者蓍之
德七重之則爲四十九猶卦之德八重之
而爲六十四也虛一者不用而用以之通
非數而數與之成斯太極也故參於圖則
其虛五而爲五十之數矣質於書即其以
punctuated:
地無故而不爲兹，實不可也。然今考圖之數五十有五，書之數四十有五，多寡不同，而方圓弗類，何也？盖圖員象天，而爲數十，偶贏奇乏，數之全也；書方象地，而爲數九，奇贏偶乏，數之變也。圖書皆以五居中，虛其中則太極也；奇偶均二十者，兩儀也。圖虛其十，亦四十五數也；書九疇之子數，則亦五十五數也。參伍錯綜，而無適不合，其變化之道，神之所爲乎！二數之名異而理同，二聖之時異而心同，所謂聖人成能，均也。劉歆經緯之說，不可見哉？
倚數之法，聖人參天兩地，教天下揲蓍求易，使不迷於吉凶悔吝之途者。然圖數五十有五，大衍五十而虛一，何也？盖其用四十九者，蓍之德七，重之則爲四十九，猶卦之德八，重之而爲六十四也。虛一者，不用而用以之通，非數而數與之成，斯太極也。故參於圖，則其虛五而爲五十之數矣；質於書，即其以
translation_en:
…it is truly impossible to say that Earth produced this without cause. Yet if we now examine them, the numbers of the River Chart total fifty-five, while those of the Luo Writing total forty-five. Why do their totals differ, and why are their shapes, square and round, unlike? The Chart is round, imaging Heaven, and its numbers extend to ten: the even numbers exceed the odd, representing number in its completeness. The Writing is square, imaging Earth, and its numbers extend to nine: the odd numbers exceed the even, representing number in its transformation. Both the Chart and the Writing place five at the center. Leaving the center empty represents the Supreme Ultimate; the odd and even numbers each totaling twenty represent the Two Modes. If ten is left out of the Chart, its numbers likewise total forty-five. The subsidiary numbers [?] of the Writing’s Nine Categories likewise total fifty-five. Grouped in threes and fives, interwoven and rearranged, they agree in every application. Is this way of change and transformation the working of the numinous? The two numerical schemes differ in name but share the same principle; the two sages lived at different times but shared the same mind. In what is called the sages’ consummation of their capacities, they were alike. Can we not see here Liu Xin’s explanation of warp and weft?
As for the method of reckoning by numbers, the sages assigned three to Heaven and two to Earth, teaching all under Heaven to manipulate yarrow stalks and consult the Changes, so that they would not lose their way amid good fortune, misfortune, regret, and humiliation. Yet the Chart’s numbers total fifty-five, while the Great Expansion has fifty, with one set aside. Why is this? Forty-nine are used because the potency of the yarrow stalks is seven, which, multiplied by itself, makes forty-nine—just as the potency of the trigrams is eight, which, multiplied by itself, makes sixty-four. The one set aside is unused, yet through it use becomes possible; it is outside the reckoning, yet through it the numbers attain completion. This is the Supreme Ultimate. Thus, comparing this with the Chart, setting aside five yields the number fifty; checking it against the Writing, it is precisely by…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
五含五而爲五十之數矣横斜曲直無所
不通其造化之精天機之妙乎諸數殊塗
而同歸三聖異慮而一致所謂窮神知化
均也朱子符契之説其不然哉易更四聖
而象已著孰有演其數如邵康節者今觀
皇極經世之書以元會運世而羅絡天地
萬物之終始治道人事之得失汪洋浩大
無所不該雖作用不同辭近牽合而妙悟
神契祖述羲畫雄成一家之言斯亦作者
===
之流亞與考其數則易用三十陰用十二
元會運世歲月日辰之數極於六十四而
一元之運始於日月星辰甲子皆造化自
然之妙而圖衍之派詳矣不然振古之豪
傑程子屑許之哉惜門戶不同學偏術數
使天根月窟之襟内聖外王之道不獲與
於斯文之正印耳範錫神禹而數弗傳孰
有補之如蔡九峯者今觀洪範皇極之篇
以性命禮義爲宗而體尚中正教主民彜
punctuated:
五含五而爲五十之數矣。横斜曲直，無所不通，其造化之精、天機之妙乎！諸數殊塗而同歸，三聖異慮而一致，所謂窮神知化均也。朱子符契之説，其不然哉！易更四聖而象已著，孰有演其數如邵康節者？今觀《皇極經世》之書，以元會運世而羅絡天地萬物之終始、治道人事之得失，汪洋浩大，無所不該。雖作用不同，辭近牽合，而妙悟神契，祖述羲畫，雄成一家之言，斯亦作者之流亞與！考其數，則易用三十，陰用十二，元會運世、歲月日辰之數極於六十四，而一元之運始於日月星辰甲子，皆造化自然之妙，而圖衍之派詳矣。不然，振古之豪傑程子屑許之哉？惜門戶不同，學偏術數，使天根月窟之襟、内聖外王之道，不獲與於斯文之正印耳。
範錫神禹而數弗傳，孰有補之如蔡九峯者？今觀《洪範皇極》之篇，以性命禮義爲宗，而體尚中正，教主民彜
translation_en:
…five containing five, thus making the number fifty. Horizontally, diagonally, curving or straight, the numbers interconnect in every way: is this not the essence of creation and the subtlety of Heaven’s workings? The various numbers follow different paths but reach the same destination; the Three Sages deliberate differently but arrive at one conclusion. They are alike in what is called plumbing the spiritual and understanding transformation. Is Master Zhu’s explanation of their correspondence like matching halves of a tally not correct?
The Changes passed through four sages, and its images were already manifest; yet who has elaborated its numbers as Shao Kangjie did? Consider his Book of the Supreme Ultimate Ordering the World (Huangji jingshi): through epochs, assemblies, cycles, and generations, it encompasses the beginnings and endings of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, and success and failure in governance and human affairs. Vast and expansive, it includes everything. Although its applications differ and its wording verges on forced connections, its subtle insights accord with the spiritual. Continuing and expounding Fuxi’s hexagram lines, it establishes an imposing school of thought. Surely its author ranks next to the originating sages!
Examining its numbers, we find that “the Changes uses thirty” [?], while yin uses twelve. The numbers of epochs, assemblies, cycles, and generations, and of years, months, days, and double-hours, reach their limit at sixty-four. The course of a single epoch begins with the sun, moon, stars, and celestial stations, and with the sexagenary cycle beginning in jiazi. All embody the spontaneous subtleties of creation, elaborating the tradition derived from the River Chart and the Great Expansion numbers. Otherwise, would Master Cheng, an outstanding figure through the ages, have deigned to approve it? Regrettably, its affiliation differed, and its learning inclined toward numerical techniques. Thus its breadth of mind, embracing the ‘root of Heaven’ and ‘cavern of the moon,’ and its Way of inner sagehood and outer kingship, were denied recognition within the orthodox transmission of this cultural tradition.
The Great Plan was bestowed upon the divine Yu, but its numbers were not transmitted. Who has supplied what was missing as Cai Jiufeng did? Consider his work on the Great Plan and the Supreme Ultimate (Hongfan huangji): it takes human nature, destiny, ritual propriety, and righteousness as its guiding principles; in its substance it esteems centrality and correctness, and in its teaching it gives primacy to the constant moral norms of the people…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
祛迷障愆因事示戒維學紹父師靡同易
象然深造自得同歸易理直欲完補古文
之缺斯亦述者之雄傑與求其數則始於
一參於三究於九成於八十一備於六千
五百六十一散之無外卷之無內體諸造
化而不可遺而洛數之原昭矣不然與三
聖之易同功真氏其浪言哉惜乎數弗遐
擇數未備使知來藏往之妙獨立物表之
見不能無俟於後之君子耳由是觀之因
===
道契數而因數闡道者羲禹孔子也聖之
神者也以靜觀數而緣數見道者邵子也
人之豪者也邵蔡之餘若洞極用書潛虛
用圖非無作也而牽合附會數滋晦矣京
房之易郭璞之技非無作也而非禮畔道
君子不由焉程子謂有之無所補無之靡
所闕非若斯人之所為乎執事曰數即氣
也氣之流行即理也茲不亦達道之言而
深乎其數者哉愚請得究言之物必有則
punctuated: 祛迷障愆，因事示戒。維學紹父師，靡同易象；然深造自得，同歸易理，直欲完補古文之缺，斯亦述者之雄傑與！求其數，則始於一，參於三，究於九，成於八十一，備於六千五百六十一。散之無外，卷之無內，體諸造化而不可遺，而洛數之原昭矣。不然，與三聖之易同功，真氏其浪言哉？惜乎數弗遐擇，數未備，使知來藏往之妙、獨立物表之見，不能無俟於後之君子耳。由是觀之，因道契數而因數闡道者，羲、禹、孔子也，聖之神者也；以靜觀數而緣數見道者，邵子也，人之豪者也。邵、蔡之餘，若洞極用書，潛虛用圖，非無作也，而牽合附會，數滋晦矣。京房之易、郭璞之技，非無作也，而非禮畔道，君子不由焉。程子謂「有之無所補，無之靡所闕」，非若斯人之所為乎？執事曰：「數即氣也，氣之流行即理也。」茲不亦達道之言，而深乎其數者哉？愚請得究言之：物必有則。
translation_en:
…dispels delusion and wards off error, offering admonitions through particular affairs. His learning carried on that of his father and teacher, though it did not follow the images of the Book of Changes. Yet through profound study and personal understanding, it arrived at the same principles as the Changes. His aim was nothing less than to make good the deficiencies of the ancient text. Was he not an outstanding figure among those who transmit the tradition? Examining his numerical system, we find that it begins with one, proceeds through three, reaches nine, takes form at eighty-one, and attains completeness at six thousand five hundred and sixty-one. Expanded, it leaves nothing outside; rolled up, it leaves nothing within. It embodies the processes of creation, leaving nothing out, and thus makes clear the source of the numbers of the Luo River Diagram. Otherwise, when Master Zhen said that it accomplished the same work as the Changes of the three sages, could he have been speaking recklessly? It is regrettable that the numbers were not extensively selected [?] and the numerical system remained incomplete. Consequently, the marvel of knowing what is to come and storing up what has passed, and the insight that stands alone beyond material things, still had to await later gentlemen.

Viewed in this light, those who apprehended numbers through the Way and elucidated the Way through numbers were Fu Xi, Yu, and Kongzi: sages of divine insight. The one who contemplated numbers in stillness and discerned the Way through them was Master Shao: an outstanding man. Beyond Shao and Cai, works such as Penetrating the Ultimate (Dongji), which uses writing, and Hidden Emptiness (Qianxu), which uses diagrams, certainly made their contributions. Yet their strained connections and forced correspondences only rendered numbers more obscure. Jing Fang’s interpretation of the Changes and Guo Pu’s techniques likewise made contributions, but they violated ritual propriety and departed from the Way; the gentleman does not follow them. Master Cheng said, “Their existence adds nothing; their absence leaves nothing lacking.” Was he not referring to achievements like those of these men?

You, sir, say: “Numbers are precisely qi; the circulation of qi is precisely principle.” Are these not words that comprehend the Way and show profound understanding of numbers? Permit me, in my ignorance, to explain this fully: things necessarily have their governing standards…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
數者盡天下之物則也事必有理數者盡
天下之事理也中人以上達乎數者也中
人以下囿於數者也聖人因數以明理所
以教天下後世也君子因數以明理所以
自淑其身也是故探天地運化之原參人
物古今之變窮義理之精微究興亡之徵
兆微顯闡幽彝倫攸敘秩然有天地萬物
各得其所之妙夫是謂以理觀數而非以
數觀數者與邵子曰天地之本其起於中
===
乎人居天地之中心居人之中君子能本
靜以觀中之體致一以窺數之原則未發
之中即天地之蘊既發之和即率理之道
斯可以得意而忘言窮理而樂天矣斯可
以達命而順義循理而致和矣尚有理與
數之殊哉是以君子貴中也謹對
第五問
殷士儋
同考試官教諭魏 批 時務一策難認識亦難
punctuated:
數者，盡天下之物則也。事必有理，數者，盡天下之事理也。中人以上，達乎數者也；中人以下，囿於數者也。聖人因數以明理，所以教天下後世也；君子因數以明理，所以自淑其身也。是故探天地運化之原，參人物古今之變，窮義理之精微，究興亡之徵兆，微顯闡幽，彝倫攸敘，秩然有天地萬物各得其所之妙。夫是謂以理觀數，而非以數觀數者與！邵子曰：「天地之本，其起於中乎！」人居天地之中，心居人之中。君子能本靜以觀中之體，致一以窺數之原，則未發之中，即天地之蘊；既發之和，即率理之道。斯可以得意而忘言，窮理而樂天矣；斯可以達命而順義，循理而致和矣。尚有理與數之殊哉？是以君子貴中也。謹對。

第五問
殷士儋

同考試官教諭魏批：時務一策，難認識，亦難
translation_en:
… Numbers encompass the norms of all things under Heaven. Every affair necessarily has its principle; numbers encompass the principles of all affairs under Heaven. Those of above-average capacity comprehend numbers; those of below-average capacity are confined by them. The sage uses numbers to illuminate principle, thereby teaching the world and later generations; the gentleman uses numbers to illuminate principle, thereby cultivating his own person. Thus he explores the source of Heaven and Earth’s transformations, examines changes in people and things throughout past and present, exhaustively investigates the subtleties of moral principle, and probes the portents of rise and fall. He brings the manifest into subtle focus [?] and reveals the hidden, setting the enduring human relationships in order. Within this order lies the wondrous working by which Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things each find their proper place. This is surely what is meant by contemplating numbers through principle, rather than contemplating numbers through numbers!

Master Shao said: “Does not the foundation of Heaven and Earth arise from the center?” Human beings occupy the center of Heaven and Earth, and the mind occupies the center of the human being. If the gentleman can take stillness as his foundation to contemplate the substance of equilibrium, and attain unity to discern the source of numbers, then equilibrium before the feelings are aroused is the inner substance of Heaven and Earth, and harmony after they are aroused is the Way of following principle. He can then grasp the meaning and forget the words, fathom principle and delight in Heaven. He can comprehend his allotted destiny and accord with righteousness, follow principle and achieve harmony. What distinction between principle and numbers would then remain? This is why the gentleman prizes equilibrium. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question
Yin Shidan 殷士儋
