title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
議處此作曲盡利弊而作用有條真奇見之施
設況才思充周如天馬行空無所拘泥經濟之
才也錄之錄之
考試官教諭文　批　有學有才有用是之取
爾
考試官學正王　批　識時務者在俊傑此子
以之
===
裕民厚俗之道何先亦曰知興替之端也
達利害之原也明得失之故也妙通變之
術也知其端而後措施有方矣達其原而
後興革有機矣明其故而後斟酌有地矣
通其變而後法制可久矣盡是四者則上
順天時下盡地理中盡物情以之疏民困
而民困疏以之經國用而國用足以之厚
風俗而風俗美蓋不惟復豐阜之舊而熙
皞之休猶將致之舍是弗圖而欲苟且一
切以幾幸於目前吾恐植之者未幾而仆
之者即繼一時之績効未收而歷年之積
punctuated:
議處。此作曲盡利弊，而作用有條，真奇見之施設。況才思充周，如天馬行空，無所拘泥，經濟之才也。錄之，錄之！

考試官教諭文，批：有學，有才，有用，是之取爾。

考試官學正王，批：識時務者在俊傑，此子以之。

裕民厚俗之道何先？亦曰知興替之端也，達利害之原也，明得失之故也，妙通變之術也。知其端而後措施有方矣，達其原而後興革有機矣，明其故而後斟酌有地矣，通其變而後法制可久矣。盡是四者，則上順天時，下盡地理，中盡物情。以之疏民困，而民困疏；以之經國用，而國用足；以之厚風俗，而風俗美。蓋不惟復豐阜之舊，而熙皞之休猶將致之。舍是弗圖，而欲苟且一切，以幾幸於目前，吾恐植之者未幾，而仆之者即繼，一時之績効未收，而歷年之積
translation_en:
…to deliberate on their handling. This essay fully explores the benefits and drawbacks in all their particulars and sets out orderly practical measures: truly an application of exceptional insight. Moreover, its talent and imagination are ample and comprehensive, like a celestial horse coursing through the sky, constrained by nothing. Here is a talent for statecraft. Select him, select him!

Examiner Wen, Confucian School Instructor, comments: “He has learning, talent, and practical ability. These are the grounds for selecting him.”

Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “Those who understand the affairs of the times are outstanding talents. This candidate is such a man.”

What comes first in the way of enriching the people and strengthening their customs? It is to recognize the beginnings of rise and decline, comprehend the sources of benefit and harm, understand the causes of success and failure, and master the art of adapting to change. Only after recognizing those beginnings can measures be properly directed; only after comprehending those sources can one find the right opportunities to institute or abolish practices; only after understanding those causes can deliberation have a sound basis; and only by adapting to change can laws and institutions endure. Fully accomplishing these four things means conforming above to Heaven’s seasons, making full use below of the advantages of the land, and fully accounting in between for the circumstances of all things. Apply these principles to relieving the people’s distress, and their distress will be relieved; to managing state expenditure, and the state’s resources will suffice; to strengthening customs, and customs will become good. Indeed, not only can the abundance of former times be restored, but the blessings of harmonious prosperity can also be attained. If one abandons these aims and instead seeks to muddle through everything, hoping for good fortune in the immediate present, I fear that scarcely will something have been established before its destruction follows, and before the achievements of a single period have borne fruit, the accumulation of successive years …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
孅滋甚矣此誠父母斯民者所宜深長思
也愚嘗讀周禮而知成周所以裕民之法
矣大司徒有土會之法以辨五地之物生
而時其賦令以土宜之法辨十有二壤之
物以教稼穡樹蓺以土均之法辨五物九
等以制天下之地征而又有草人掌土化
之法以物地相宜而爲之種稻人掌稼下
之地以時其蓄洩蓺種其所以盡之力田
畢賦至纖悉也厥後太公明之以治齊因
===
其俗簡其禮通商工之業便魚鹽之利而
人民歸管仲假之以修政相地而衰征山
澤各致其時連五家之兵設魚鹽之利而
至於霸諸侯何其盛也是故全齊之盛轂
擊肩摩家殷人足其見於蘇秦之說者可
徵也東有瑯邪即墨之饒北有渤海之利
其見於田肯之說者可徵也膏壤千里洋
洋乎大國之風其見於太史公之說者可
徵也自井田廢而阡陌興貧富不均民務
punctuated: 孅滋甚矣。此誠父母斯民者所宜深長思也。愚嘗讀《周禮》，而知成周所以裕民之法矣。大司徒有土會之法，以辨五地之物生，而時其賦令；以土宜之法，辨十有二壤之物，以教稼穡樹蓺；以土均之法，辨五物九等，以制天下之地征。而又有草人掌土化之法，以物地相宜而爲之種；稻人掌稼下之地，以時其蓄洩蓺種。其所以盡之力田畢賦，至纖悉也。厥後太公明之以治齊，因其俗，簡其禮，通商工之業，便魚鹽之利，而人民歸。管仲假之以修政，相地而衰征，山澤各致其時，連五家之兵，設魚鹽之利，而至於霸諸侯。何其盛也！是故全齊之盛，轂擊肩摩，家殷人足，其見於蘇秦之說者可徵也；東有瑯邪、即墨之饒，北有渤海之利，其見於田肯之說者可徵也；膏壤千里，洋洋乎大國之風，其見於太史公之說者可徵也。自井田廢而阡陌興，貧富不均，民務
translation_en:
…the accumulated troubles [?] grow still more severe. This is indeed something that those who act as parents to these people ought to ponder deeply and at length. I have read the Rites of Zhou and thereby learned the methods by which the Zhou in its flourishing age enriched the people. The Minister of Education employed methods of classifying land to distinguish the living products of five kinds of terrain and to issue levy orders at the proper seasons. Through methods of determining the suitability of soils, he distinguished the products of twelve kinds of soil and taught the cultivation of grain and the planting of trees and other crops. Through methods of equalizing land assessments, he distinguished five categories of products and nine grades of land, thereby determining land taxes throughout the realm. There was also the Officer of Soil Improvement, who administered methods of transforming soil, matching crops to the land and arranging their planting; and the Officer of Rice Cultivation, who oversaw cultivation in low-lying lands, regulating the timing of water retention, drainage, and planting. The provisions for applying these methods to diligent farming and the full payment of taxes [?] extended to the smallest details.

Later, Taigong elucidated these methods in governing Qi. He accommodated its customs, simplified its rites, facilitated commerce and handicrafts, and made the benefits of fish and salt readily available; thus the people flocked to him. Guan Zhong drew upon these methods to reform government: he assessed the land and graded its taxes accordingly, ensured that mountains and marshes yielded their resources at the proper seasons, linked the soldiers of every five households, and developed the benefits of fish and salt. He thereby brought Qi to hegemony over the feudal lords. How flourishing it was! Thus, at the height of prosperity throughout Qi, carriage hubs struck one another and shoulders rubbed together; households were wealthy and individuals had enough. Su Qin’s account provides evidence of this. To the east lay the abundance of Langye and Jimo, and to the north the resources of Bohai: Tian Ken’s account provides evidence of this. Fertile soil stretched for a thousand li, displaying in full measure the grandeur of a great state: the Grand Astrologer’s account provides evidence of this. Since the well-field system was abolished and fields divided by boundary paths arose, wealth and poverty have become unequal, and the people have devoted themselves to …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
逯末周官樹藝之教既罷不行而太公管
仲之政亦復斬焉歷代以來雖時有功令
之布而經界不正四民失業今日之齊非
復昔日之齊矣故在昔禹貢青州之田厥
等上下而今且以爲潟鹵之區何惟於嵩
萊之彌望而室廬之不保哉故曰知與替
之端而後擯盜有方者此也夫人情莫不
懷舊土而畏流離則其所以棄親戚墳墓
而逃亡者豈其得已哉夫不得已而爲之
===
其弊可知已蓋徭役之不均也賦斂之不
公也催科之太急也稽覈不實則戶口之
登耗非真勾稽不密則土田之飛詭無藝
富者巧於欺蒙而得免重大之賦貧者坐
以縮懦而代輸額外之征有司據簿以追
呼吏胥倚法而迫脅凋瘵之民其不受斃
者鮮矣又況貪黷之吏非止此也藉征斂
之常而行其饕餮之欲甚者偰揄其民而
用之奈之何民不失業也是故弱者挈老
punctuated:
逯末，周官樹藝之教既罷不行，而太公管仲之政亦復斬焉。歷代以來，雖時有功令之布，而經界不正，四民失業，今日之齊非復昔日之齊矣。故在昔《禹貢》，青州之田厥等上下，而今且以爲潟鹵之區，何惟於嵩萊之彌望而室廬之不保哉？故曰知與替之端而後擯盜有方者，此也。
夫人情莫不懷舊土而畏流離，則其所以棄親戚墳墓而逃亡者，豈其得已哉？夫不得已而爲之，其弊可知已。蓋徭役之不均也，賦斂之不公也，催科之太急也。稽覈不實，則戶口之登耗非真；勾稽不密，則土田之飛詭無藝。富者巧於欺蒙而得免重大之賦，貧者坐以縮懦而代輸額外之征。有司據簿以追呼，吏胥倚法而迫脅，凋瘵之民，其不受斃者鮮矣。又況貪黷之吏非止此也，藉征斂之常而行其饕餮之欲，甚者偰揄其民而用之，奈之何民不失業也？是故弱者挈老
translation_en:
…pursuing secondary occupations [?]. Once the instructions on planting and cultivation in the Offices of Zhou had been abandoned and were no longer implemented, the policies of Taigong and Guan Zhong likewise came to an end. Through successive dynasties, although statutory regulations were promulgated from time to time, field boundaries were not properly established, and the four occupational groups lost their livelihoods. The Qi of today is no longer the Qi of former times. Thus, in antiquity, the Tribute of Yu ranked Qingzhou’s fields in the lower division of the upper grade; now the region is regarded as saline wasteland. How could the problem be confined to overgrowth stretching as far as the eye can see [?] and homes that cannot be preserved? This is what is meant by saying that only after understanding the beginnings of rise and decline [?] can one find a proper means of eliminating banditry.
It is human nature to cherish one’s native soil and fear displacement. When people abandon their relatives and ancestral graves and flee, could they possibly be doing so willingly? If they act because they have no alternative, the abuses behind their actions are readily apparent: unequal labor service, unfair taxation, and excessively urgent demands for payment. When verification is unsound, the recorded increases and decreases in households and population are inaccurate; when cross-checking is lax, fraudulent transfers and concealment of land know no bounds. The rich, skilled at deception, secure exemption from heavy taxes; the poor, through their timidity, must pay additional levies in their stead. The responsible officials pursue and summon them on the authority of the registers, while clerks use the law to intimidate and coerce them. Among the exhausted and impoverished people, few escape being driven to death. Moreover, the abuses of corrupt officials do not stop here. They use routine tax collection to satisfy their ravenous appetites; the worst even extort resources from their people for their own use [?]. How, then, could the people avoid losing their livelihoods? Consequently, the weak take their elderly along…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
幼而移之四方其強者則暴悍抗令已耳
去生人之樂而即于囘其罪豈獨在下哉
故曰達利害之原而後興革有幾者此也
在昔滕若修井田之政四方歸之唐李絳
開營田之法即有明效今之土地即古之
土地也歸逋而與利宜無難者何乃招之
耕藝而民反避而去之若陷阱然者往歲
憲臣建議欲官給牛種矣官給農器矣三
年而後舉稅矣而迄臣無成豈其終不可
===
爲乎亦曰主持之未定也奉行之未至也
倡率之無方也計口按業而或爾為豪強
之兼幷給資散利而或歸於奸猾之侵漁
復之稅矣而其後又或責以歷歲之需是
以死易生也而民其爲之乎故曰知得失
之故而後斟酌有定者此也夫是議也苟
不欲行之則已如欲行之則復業之民姓
名可別籍也而力役不可緊征也輕稅可
稍出也而積逋不可幷責也勸課可行也
punctuated:
幼而移之四方，其強者則暴悍抗令已耳。去生人之樂而即于囘，其罪豈獨在下哉？故曰：「達利害之原而後興革有幾」者，此也。
在昔滕若修井田之政，四方歸之；唐李絳開營田之法，即有明效。今之土地即古之土地也，歸逋而與利，宜無難者。何乃招之耕藝，而民反避而去之，若陷阱然者？往歲憲臣建議，欲官給牛種矣，官給農器矣，三年而後舉稅矣，而迄臣無成，豈其終不可爲乎？亦曰主持之未定也，奉行之未至也，倡率之無方也。計口按業，而或爾為豪強之兼幷；給資散利，而或歸於奸猾之侵漁；復之稅矣，而其後又或責以歷歲之需。是以死易生也，而民其爲之乎？故曰：「知得失之故而後斟酌有定」者，此也。
夫是議也，苟不欲行之則已；如欲行之，則復業之民姓名可別籍也，而力役不可緊征也；輕稅可稍出也，而積逋不可幷責也；勸課可行也。
translation_en:
…and the young, and migrate in all directions; the stronger simply become violent and defy orders. They abandon the joys of ordinary life and turn to wrongdoing [?]. Can the blame lie solely with those below? This is what is meant by saying, “Only after understanding the sources of benefit and harm can one have some prospect of success in instituting reforms and abolishing abuses.”
In former times, when Teng implemented the well-field system [?], people from all directions flocked there. Under the Tang, Li Jiang instituted a system of agricultural colonies, which immediately produced clear results. The land of today is the same land as in antiquity. Bringing fugitives back and providing them with benefits should present no difficulty. Why, then, when people are invited to cultivate the land, do they instead shun it and flee as though it were a pitfall? In past years, a censor proposed that the government supply oxen and seed, that it supply agricultural implements, and that taxes be levied only after three years. Yet to this day [?] nothing has been accomplished. Can it really be impossible to carry out? It is simply that direction has been indecisive, implementation inadequate, and leadership ineffective. Landholdings are assessed according to the number of mouths, yet may fall prey to engrossment by the powerful; funds and benefits are distributed, yet may be diverted through the depredations of the unscrupulous. People are exempted from taxes, yet afterward may still be required to meet demands for past years. This is to exchange life for death: would the people undertake it? This is what is meant by saying, “Only after understanding the causes of success and failure can one arrive at settled judgments.”
As for this proposal, if there is no intention of carrying it out, let it rest. If it is to be carried out, the names of those returning to their livelihoods may be entered in a separate register, but labor services must not be exacted urgently. Light taxes may gradually be collected, but accumulated arrears must not be demanded all at once. Measures to encourage and oversee cultivation may be implemented …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
而刑督不可遽施也賑貸可先也而輸償
不可驟入也井田雖復而稍爲限制可也
讀法未舉而稍爲聯屬可也鼓舞倡率宜
責之監司而不期以近效可也權宜施設
宜責之有司而不裁以禁忌可也故曰妙
通變之術而後法制可久者此也然其要
則惟在乎人焉耳矣孔子曰文武之政布
在方冊其人存則其政舉其人亡則其政
息是故趙充國之田金城曹孟德之田許
下郭子儀之田河中夏師德之田豐州爲
之兵戈倥偬之時而迄有成效得非數子
者以身任其責而不惑於異議耶爲今之
===
計莫若
朝廷之上申敕監司慎選守令專其責成緩
其遷代任其張弛明其功課表其循良黜
其貪刻績著則褒勞秩久則超遷六事不
舉則旌薦不及使爲守令者不得以苟且
目前之圖以應上之期會而僥倖於一旦
banxin: 鄉試錄 文 十五
punctuated: 而刑督不可遽施也；賑貸可先也，而輸償不可驟入也。井田雖復，而稍爲限制可也；讀法未舉，而稍爲聯屬可也。鼓舞倡率，宜責之監司，而不期以近效可也；權宜施設，宜責之有司，而不裁以禁忌可也。故曰：「妙通變之術而後法制可久」者，此也。然其要則惟在乎人焉耳矣。孔子曰：「文武之政，布在方冊。其人存，則其政舉；其人亡，則其政息。」是故趙充國之田金城、曹孟德之田許下、郭子儀之田河中、夏師德之田豐州，爲之兵戈倥偬之時，而迄有成效，得非數子者以身任其責，而不惑於異議耶？爲今之計，莫若朝廷之上申敕監司，慎選守令，專其責成，緩其遷代，任其張弛，明其功課，表其循良，黜其貪刻。績著則褒勞，秩久則超遷，六事不舉則旌薦不及，使爲守令者不得以苟且目前之圖，以應上之期會，而僥倖於一旦
translation_en:
…but punitive enforcement must not be imposed precipitately. Relief loans may be provided first, but repayment must not be exacted abruptly. Although the well-field system is restored, it is acceptable to introduce limits gradually; although public readings of the laws have not been instituted, it is acceptable gradually to organize the people into linked groups. Encouragement and leadership should be made the responsibility of the surveillance officials, without expecting immediate results. Discretionary measures suited to circumstances should be entrusted to the responsible authorities, without constraining them by prohibitions. This is what is meant by saying, “Only after mastering the art of adapting to change can laws and institutions endure.” Yet the essential point lies solely in the people entrusted with them. Confucius said: “The government of Kings Wen and Wu is set forth in the written records. When the right men are present, that government flourishes; when those men are gone, that government ceases.” Thus Zhao Chongguo’s agricultural colonies at Jincheng, Cao Mengde’s at Xuxia, Guo Ziyi’s at Hezhong, and Xia Shide’s [?; probably Lou Shide] at Fengzhou were established amid the turmoil of warfare, yet ultimately achieved results. Was this not because these men personally assumed responsibility and were not swayed by dissenting opinions?

For present purposes, nothing would be better than for the court to renew its injunctions to the surveillance officials and carefully select prefects and magistrates: hold them individually responsible for results, defer their transfers and replacement, allow them discretion in tightening or relaxing measures, make their performance assessments clear, honor the conscientious and benevolent, and dismiss the corrupt and harsh. Those with conspicuous achievements should be commended for their service; those who have served long in their rank should receive exceptional promotion. Those who fail to discharge the six duties should receive neither commendation nor recommendation. Thus prefects and magistrates would be prevented from using makeshift plans for the immediate moment merely to meet the deadlines imposed by their superiors and secure some fleeting advantage…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
其於民也省其刑罰薄其稅斂賑其凶饑
恤其禍災時其力役息其鬬爭聯其什伍
禦其攘掠使之相生相養相糾相受真若
赤子之依於慈母者而又先之以仁義孝
弟導之以睦婣任卹以作其良心而匡其
不逮由是而流離可歸由是而地利可興
由是而經賦可足由是而儲偫可充由是
而禮義可作復豐阜之舊而成熙皞之休
葢運之掌矣又何必屑屑於周官之經畫
===
與太公管仲之令而後爲得哉愚青齊之
民也目擊時弊而欲以進聞久矣敢因明
問以對
punctuated: 其於民也，省其刑罰，薄其稅斂，賑其凶饑，恤其禍災，時其力役，息其鬬爭，聯其什伍，禦其攘掠，使之相生相養，相糾相受，真若赤子之依於慈母者。而又先之以仁義孝弟，導之以睦婣任卹，以作其良心，而匡其不逮。由是而流離可歸，由是而地利可興，由是而經賦可足，由是而儲偫可充，由是而禮義可作。復豐阜之舊，而成熙皞之休，葢運之掌矣。又何必屑屑於《周官》之經畫與太公、管仲之令，而後爲得哉？愚，青齊之民也，目擊時弊，而欲以進聞久矣。敢因明問以對。
translation_en:
…In their dealings with the people, they should reduce punishments, lighten taxation, provide relief in famine, succor those afflicted by calamity, time labor service appropriately, settle disputes, organize households into groups of ten and five, and protect them against plunder. They should enable the people to sustain and support one another, correct one another and offer one another shelter, so that they truly become like infants depending on a loving mother. They should further lead them through benevolence, righteousness, filial piety, and brotherly respect, and guide them toward harmony among kin, amity through marriage, mutual responsibility, and relief for those in need, thereby awakening their good hearts and remedying their shortcomings. In this way the displaced can return, the productive potential of the land can be developed, regular tax revenues can become sufficient, reserves can be replenished, and ritual propriety and righteousness can flourish. Restoring former abundance and achieving the blessings of radiant harmony would then be as easy as turning something in the palm of one's hand. Why must one fuss over the arrangements in the Offices of Zhou and the ordinances of Taigong and Guan Zhong before considering the task properly accomplished?

I, an unworthy man, am a native of the Qing and Qi region. Having witnessed the abuses of the age, I have long wished to bring them to the authorities’ attention. I venture to offer this reply in response to your illuminating question.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
洪濛既闢聖哲迭生天下古
今獨宗師孔子顏曾二子乃
親得其傳者然皆山東之產
焉或者泰山渤海巉巖浩瀚
秀靈鬱積鍾而爲人有此盛
耶抑天生聖哲氣數不偶又
===
弗在山川之秀靈而已也孔
子之後厥孫子思子出繹演
道原紹述先業再傳而得孟
子明仁義息邪說挺然以孔
子自任然亦不出鄒魯之墟
焉今讀其書真足以想見當
時之盛信乎一元之氣妙合
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

洪濛既闢，聖哲迭生，天下古今獨宗師孔子。顏曾二子乃親得其傳者，然皆山東之產焉。或者泰山渤海巉巖浩瀚，秀靈鬱積，鍾而爲人，有此盛耶？抑天生聖哲，氣數不偶，又弗在山川之秀靈而已也。孔子之後，厥孫子思子出，繹演道原，紹述先業，再傳而得孟子，明仁義，息邪說，挺然以孔子自任，然亦不出鄒魯之墟焉。今讀其書，真足以想見當時之盛。信乎，一元之氣妙合
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

Once primordial chaos had opened, sages and wise men arose in succession; yet throughout the world, past and present, Confucius alone has been revered as the supreme teacher. The two masters Yan Hui and Zeng Shen personally received his transmission, and all were natives of Shandong. Might the precipitous heights of Mount Tai and the vast expanse of the Bohai Sea have accumulated such spiritual excellence that, concentrated in human beings, it produced this flourishing? Or rather, Heaven’s production of sages and wise men follows patterns of vital energy and destiny that are no mere coincidence, and does not depend solely on the spiritual excellence of mountains and rivers.

After Confucius, his grandson, Master Zisi, emerged to elucidate and expand upon the source of the Way and carry forward the work of his predecessor. Two transmissions later came Mengzi, who clarified benevolence and righteousness, quelled heterodox doctrines, and resolutely took upon himself the mission of Confucius. Yet he too came from the territory of Zou and Lu. Reading their books today, one can truly envision the flourishing of that age. Indeed, the vital energy of the primal unity wondrously combined…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
凝定發洩于是邦太史公謂
齊魯文學乃其天性良有見
也我
皇明尊崇孔孟之道以治天下建
學設科數求俊彥山東取士
每三歲必七十五人重文邦
也然才藝彬彬蜚聲海內後
===
先相望代不鮮人而孔孟之
統吾今于爾多士屬望焉夫
文章道德本一也人自二之
耳孔子之教曰博文約禮多
識畜德何嘗不欲人學文哉
今縱觀爾多士通貫六經旁
搜子史厥文雄渾玄奧變化
punctuated:
凝定，發洩于是邦。太史公謂齊魯文學乃其天性，良有見也。我皇明尊崇孔孟之道以治天下，建學設科，數求俊彥。山東取士，每三歲必七十五人，重文邦也。然才藝彬彬，蜚聲海內，後先相望，代不鮮人，而孔孟之統，吾今于爾多士屬望焉。
夫文章道德本一也，人自二之耳。孔子之教曰博文約禮、多識畜德，何嘗不欲人學文哉？今縱觀爾多士，通貫六經，旁搜子史，厥文雄渾玄奧，變化
translation_en:
…coalesces and settles, finding expression in this land. The Grand Historian said that literary learning was inherent in the nature of the people of Qi and Lu: truly an insightful observation. Our august Ming dynasty reveres the Way of Confucius and Mencius in governing all under Heaven, establishing schools and examinations and repeatedly seeking outstanding talent. In Shandong, seventy-five men must be selected every three years, in recognition of this land of literary culture. Men of refined talent and accomplishment, renowned throughout the realm, have followed one another in succession; no generation has lacked them. Yet it is upon you assembled scholars that I now place my hopes for carrying on the tradition of Confucius and Mencius.
Literary accomplishment and moral virtue are fundamentally one; people themselves divide them into two. Confucius taught broad learning in letters and restraint through ritual, extensive knowledge and the cultivation of virtue. When did he ever wish people not to study letters? Surveying you assembled scholars now, I see that you have mastered the Six Classics and searched widely through the philosophers and histories. Your writing is powerful and full, profound and subtle, varying and transforming…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
抑揚而其氣亦浩然剛大塞
乎天地之間莫非一世之英
也而吾尤以孔孟之統惓惓
焉者豈好迂哉蓋攻于博文
而忽約禮鋭于多識而不暇
畜德固學者之通患也夫以
包羅該括之才苦心極力終
===
身所得盡役役于詞鋒筆勢
之間以馳騁于一世厥藝誠
精專奇絶足以煇煌化理矣
復能反之此心而擬議于言
動發揮于事業進而獮
皇猷賛國是僃和庶政振舉紀綱
感通華夷昭格天地以成俊
punctuated: 抑揚，而其氣亦浩然剛大，塞乎天地之間，莫非一世之英也。而吾尤以孔孟之統惓惓焉者，豈好迂哉？蓋攻于博文而忽約禮，鋭于多識而不暇畜德，固學者之通患也。夫以包羅該括之才，苦心極力，終身所得，盡役役于詞鋒筆勢之間，以馳騁于一世，厥藝誠精專奇絶，足以煇煌化理矣。復能反之此心，而擬議于言動，發揮于事業，進而獮皇猷，賛國是，僃和庶政，振舉紀綱，感通華夷，昭格天地，以成俊
translation_en: …with its rising and falling cadences, while your vital energy, too, is vast, strong, and great, filling the space between Heaven and Earth: you are all outstanding men of your age. Yet why am I particularly solicitous about the tradition of Confucius and Mencius? Is it because I delight in impractical pursuits? Surely it is a common failing among scholars to devote themselves to breadth of learning while neglecting the restraint of ritual, and to pursue extensive knowledge eagerly while finding no time to nurture virtue. With talents capable of embracing and comprehending everything, they labor painstakingly and exert themselves to the utmost, yet devote all their lifelong attainments to the sharpness of their phrasing and the vigor of their writing, thereby making their mark upon their age. Their literary skill is indeed refined, concentrated, extraordinary, and unsurpassed—sufficient to lend splendor to moral transformation and good government. If you can further turn this back upon your own hearts, deliberate upon it in speech and action, and give it expression in practical undertakings, advancing to further[?] imperial plans, support the proper course of state policy, bring harmony to all affairs of government, uphold the governing principles and regulations, move and unite Chinese and non-Chinese peoples, and manifestly reach Heaven and Earth, so as to achieve outstanding …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
偉光明之烈則六經子史既
擲其華復覈其實表裏本末
渾融透徹而
國家元氣將有賴焉孰與文藝
獨成名者為得耶斯道已在
我惟一轉移之耳爾多士其
猛省之哉陸贄司考校得韓
===
愈至今為科目美談豈徒為
文耶蓋愈丁道衰文弊之日
雄裁灼見識孟子于異端擾
攘之中慨然歸于一世真吾
道之豪傑也而爾多士每每
淺之誠謂因文見道也若究
厥攸詣復徒文而已焉無乃
punctuated: 偉光明之烈，則六經子史既擲其華，復覈其實，表裏本末，渾融透徹，而國家元氣將有賴焉。孰與文藝獨成名者為得耶？斯道已在我，惟一轉移之耳。爾多士其猛省之哉！陸贄司考校，得韓愈，至今為科目美談，豈徒為文耶？蓋愈丁道衰文弊之日，雄裁灼見，識孟子于異端擾攘之中，慨然歸于一世，真吾道之豪傑也。而爾多士每每淺之，誠謂因文見道也。若究厥攸詣，復徒文而已焉，無乃
translation_en:
…great and illustrious achievements. Then, having discarded the ornamentation of the Six Classics, the philosophical masters, and the histories, and further examined their substance, you will thoroughly comprehend their outward and inward aspects, their roots and ramifications, as an integrated whole. The vital energy of the state will have something upon which to depend. Compared with those who win fame through literary accomplishment alone, which course is more worthwhile? This Way already lies within us; all that is needed is a change of direction. You assembled scholars should awaken sharply to this!

When Lu Zhi administered the examinations, he selected Han Yu. To this day, this remains a celebrated story in examination history. Was it merely on account of literary composition? Han Yu lived when the Way was declining and writing had become corrupt. With powerful judgment and penetrating insight, he recognized Mencius amid the turmoil of heterodox teachings and resolutely returned to the Way before the whole age [?]. He was truly a hero of our Way. Yet you scholars repeatedly regard him superficially. Indeed, this is what is meant by discerning the Way through writing. If you investigate what he attained, yet still regard it as merely writing, would this not be…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
賔興之典創自成周歷世浸
久沿革匪一仰惟
國朝集厥大成雖損益唯時而
道寔並行取士專設科目重
經術也教之者唯一道而學
之者無二業類三歲而一試
===
焉簡其章者以薦是爲恒
制嘉靖十有九年寔維試期東
藩守臣奉行唯謹廵按御史
李〔復初〕寔當監臨之任振揚
風紀尤敦化源謂茲重典以
人事
君係焉罔唯專僻唯大同也維時
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

賔興之典，創自成周，歷世浸久，沿革匪一。仰惟國朝集厥大成，雖損益唯時，而道寔並行。取士專設科目，重經術也。教之者唯一道，而學之者無二業。類三歲而一試焉，簡其章者以薦，是爲恒制。

嘉靖十有九年，寔維試期。東藩守臣奉行唯謹。廵按御史李〔復初〕寔當監臨之任，振揚風紀，尤敦化源。謂茲重典，以人事君係焉，罔唯專僻，唯大同也。維時
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

The ceremony of honoring and recommending worthy men originated in the Zhou dynasty. Over the long succession of ages, its continuities and changes have taken many forms. We reverently consider that our dynasty has brought these practices to their fullest realization. Although additions and reductions accord with the times, the Way is indeed carried forward alongside them. The selection of men for office is conducted specifically through established examination categories, thereby honoring learning in the Classics. Those who teach follow a single Way, and those who study pursue no divergent vocation. As a rule, an examination is held once every three years; those who distinguish themselves are selected for recommendation. This is the standing system.

The nineteenth year of Jiajing [1540] was indeed an examination year. The officials charged with administering Shandong carried out the regulations with utmost care. The Regional Inspector, Censor Li〔Fuchu〕, undertook the duties of Supervising Official. He upheld discipline and especially strengthened the foundations of moral transformation. He held that this weighty institution concerned serving the sovereign through the provision of worthy men, and that it should be guided by broad impartiality, rather than narrow partiality [?]. At that time…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
巡撫都御史李〔中〕敦大崇本
敷德作人藩臬俊良咸善政
教乃爰咨諏廣容虛受斟酌
損益不唯其已唯其宜區定
乃檄左布政使沈〔教〕右布政
使張〔時徹〕爲提調官副使孫
〔檜〕僉事崔〔三畏〕爲監試官左
===
參政錐〔昂〕右參政張〔臬〕余〔録〕
右參議李〔允升〕副使王〔揚〕吳
〔檄〕吳〔道南〕馬〔紀〕僉事沈〔灃〕饒
〔思聰〕汪〔東洋〕陳〔乙〕朱〔㮣〕都指
揮鄔〔祐〕翟〔欽〕防範于外罔有
攸斁先是以禮聘學正王〔應〕
〔槐〕教諭文〔高〕爲考試官學正
punctuated:
巡撫都御史李〔中〕敦大崇本，敷德作人，藩臬俊良咸善政教。乃爰咨諏，廣容虛受，斟酌損益，不唯其已，唯其宜。區定，乃檄左布政使沈〔教〕、右布政使張〔時徹〕爲提調官，副使孫〔檜〕、僉事崔〔三畏〕爲監試官。左參政錐〔昂〕、右參政張〔臬〕、余〔録〕、右參議李〔允升〕、副使王〔揚〕、吳〔檄〕、吳〔道南〕、馬〔紀〕、僉事沈〔灃〕、饒〔思聰〕、汪〔東洋〕、陳〔乙〕、朱〔㮣〕、都指揮鄔〔祐〕、翟〔欽〕防範于外，罔有攸斁。
先是，以禮聘學正王〔應〕〔槐〕、教諭文〔高〕爲考試官，學正
translation_en:
… Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Li Zhong cultivated generosity and upheld fundamentals, spreading virtue and nurturing talent. The outstanding officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions all excelled in government and instruction. They therefore consulted widely, welcomed diverse views, and received advice with open minds, weighing what should be reduced or added, guided by what was appropriate rather than by their own preferences [?]. Once the arrangements were settled, written orders appointed Shen Jiao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Zhang Shiche, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, as Proctors; Sun Gui, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Cui Sanwei, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, were appointed as examination monitors. Zhui Ang [?], Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Zhang Nie and Yu Lu, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners; Li Yunsheng, Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Wang Yang, Wu Xi, Wu Daonan, and Ma Ji, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Shen Feng, Rao Sicong, Wang Dongyang, Chen Yi, and Zhu Gai [?], Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Wu You and Zhai Qin, Regional Military Commissioners, maintained safeguards outside, none flagging in their duties.
Previously, Wang Yinghuai, an instructor in a subprefectural Confucian school, and Wen Gao, an instructor in a county Confucian school, had been formally invited to serve as Examiners, and the instructor in a subprefectural Confucian school …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
萬〔宗義〕教諭魏〔廷〕甘〔惠〕袠〔邦〕
行〔文〕〔鳴〕關〔應〕〔槐〕王〔賓〕陳〔達〕爲同考
試官〔應〕〔槐〕等被幣而行方秋
入境萃而愳曰艱哉厥任重
也匪唯公明曷其能鑒比至
則監臨而下諸吉藹藹心諧
力協諸需斬斬上裕下懌於
===
是向而喜曰休哉百度貞也
吾曹亦是或以寡愆乃以丙
寅入院合提學副使呂〔顒〕所
簡士二千三試之拔七十有
五人焉於是羣而慶曰彬彬哉
人文敷也以人事
君茲其庶幾已乃次第其名氏錄
punctuated: 萬〔宗義〕、教諭魏〔廷〕、甘〔惠〕、袠〔邦〕、行〔文〕〔鳴〕、關〔應〕〔槐〕、王〔賓〕、陳〔達〕爲同考試官。〔應〕〔槐〕等被幣而行，方秋入境，萃而愳曰：「艱哉，厥任重也！匪唯公明，曷其能鑒？」比至，則監臨而下諸吉藹藹，心諧力協，諸需斬斬，上裕下懌。於是向而喜曰：「休哉，百度貞也！吾曹亦是或以寡愆。」乃以丙寅入院，合提學副使呂〔顒〕所簡士二千，三試之，拔七十有五人焉。於是羣而慶曰：「彬彬哉，人文敷也！以人事君，茲其庶幾已。」乃次第其名氏，錄
translation_en:
…Wan Zongyi and the Instructors Wei Ting, Gan Hui, Zhi Bang [?], Xing Wenming, Guan Yinghuai, Wang Bin, and Chen Da were appointed Associate Examiners. Yinghuai and the others accepted the ceremonial gifts and set out. Entering the province just as autumn began, they gathered and said apprehensively: “How difficult this is! Our responsibility is weighty. Without impartiality and discernment, how can we judge?” When they arrived, they found all the worthy officials [?], from the Supervising Official downward, cordial and harmonious, united in purpose and effort. All necessary provisions were in good order; those above had ample resources, and those below were content. They then turned to one another and said joyfully: “How excellent! Every arrangement is proper. We too may thereby make fewer mistakes.”

On the bingyin day, they entered the examination compound and assembled the two thousand scholars selected by Lü Yong, the Education Intendant holding the rank of Surveillance Vice Commissioner. They examined them in three sessions and selected seventy-five. Together they offered congratulations, saying: “How richly cultivated they are! Literary accomplishment flourishes! In serving the ruler by providing worthy men, we have perhaps come close to fulfilling our duty.” They then arranged the candidates’ names in order and recorded…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
其文以
獻〔應愧〕不佞僣序簡首唯山東
古青兗之疆宗岱浸海雄巨
爲天下冠故精靈之所鍾萃
代産聖哲而吾孔子實出是
邦雖聖神所毓必應昌辰合
上下四方爲土而是邦特專
美焉諸士隸茲恒自慶重而
稱雄焉顧無所謂發藴而演
道者乎孔子之道歷世尊尚
===
至于
國朝尤極崇重我
皇上建極齊聖匹孔而祖述尤兢
兢焉禮樂明備人文煥燁神
punctuated: 其文以獻。〔應愧〕不佞，僣序簡首。唯山東，古青兗之疆，宗岱浸海，雄巨爲天下冠。故精靈之所鍾萃，代産聖哲，而吾孔子實出是邦。雖聖神所毓，必應昌辰，合上下四方爲土，而是邦特專美焉。諸士隸茲，恒自慶重而稱雄焉，顧無所謂發藴而演道者乎？孔子之道，歷世尊尚，至于國朝，尤極崇重。我皇上建極，齊聖匹孔，而祖述尤兢兢焉。禮樂明備，人文煥燁，神
translation_en:
…their compositions for presentation to the throne. I, Yingkui 應愧, unworthy though I am, have presumptuously placed this preface at the beginning of the volume.

Shandong occupies the ancient territories of Qing and Yan. With Mount Dai as its principal mountain and the sea as its great body of water, its grandeur ranks foremost in the realm. Thus, numinous essences gather here, producing sages and wise men in every age; indeed, our Confucius came from this land. Although the birth of sages and divine men must answer to an auspicious age, and the whole expanse of heaven and earth and the four quarters provides their native soil, this land alone enjoys that distinction. The scholars belonging here constantly congratulate themselves, esteem their origins, and claim preeminence. Yet should they not also bring forth what lies within them and expound the Way?

The Way of Confucius has been revered through successive ages; under our dynasty, its veneration has reached the utmost height. Our Emperor establishes the supreme standard, equals the sages, and matches Confucius; he is especially conscientious in carrying forward the teachings of his predecessors. Rites and music are manifest and complete, cultural accomplishment shines brilliantly, and divine…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
機風運遐壤不遺諸士靡然
嚮輔濡染尤近顧無所謂興
起而速肖者乎乃今觀其文
組織語孟馳驟六經敷陳王
道出入百氏崇正黜浮激大
究遼炳炳蔚蔚罔非道精茲
非憲
===
聖朕孔而有得焉者耶觀乎人文
以化成天下茲其至哉雖然
文亦難言矣孔子以剛柔交
錯爲天文矣而贊天之道曰
純粹精也以文不在茲自任
矣而語其徒曰予欲無言吾
道一以貫之而門弟子德行
punctuated:
機風運，遐壤不遺，諸士靡然嚮輔，濡染尤近，顧無所謂興起而速肖者乎？乃今觀其文，組織語孟，馳驟六經，敷陳王道，出入百氏，崇正黜浮，激大究遼，炳炳蔚蔚，罔非道精。茲非憲聖朕孔而有得焉者耶？觀乎人文，以化成天下，茲其至哉！

雖然，文亦難言矣。孔子以剛柔交錯爲天文矣，而贊天之道曰：「純粹精也。」以「文不在茲」自任矣，而語其徒曰：「予欲無言。」「吾道一以貫之。」而門弟子德行
translation_en:
…workings move like the wind, leaving no distant region untouched. The scholars turn toward and support them with one accord; receiving this influence especially directly, could they fail to be stirred to action and swiftly resemble their exemplar? Now, examining their compositions, we find them weaving together the Analects and the Mencius, ranging freely through the Six Classics, expounding the kingly Way, and drawing upon the hundred schools. They uphold the correct and reject the superficial, give impetus to the great and investigate the far-reaching. Brilliant and richly accomplished, their writings all embody the essence of the Way. Are these not men who have gained understanding by taking the sages as their standard and emulating Confucius [?]? “Observe human culture, and thereby transform and perfect all under Heaven”: surely this is its highest realization!

Nevertheless, literary pattern is difficult to discuss. Confucius took the interweaving of the firm and yielding to constitute the pattern of Heaven, yet praised Heaven’s Way by saying: “It is pure, unalloyed, and quintessential.” He assumed responsibility for the cultural tradition with the words, “Does not this culture reside here in me?” Yet he told his disciples, “I wish to say nothing,” and “My Way is threaded together by a single principle.” And among his disciples, virtuous conduct…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
文學言語政事殊能而不爲
異唯精也故交錯而時出唯
無言也故燦然而顯著唯一
也故殊能而崇德諸士於其
所謂精者錯者無言者顯著
者一者殊者參伍而有得焉
則深於文者也左右經綸無
===
往不利矣故曰神而明之存
乎其人默而成之不言而信
存乎德行不然吾不知其所
謂文者何如也雖然性與天
道不出文章之外而聽言觀
行孔子不諱焉則故有所謂
也諸士勗哉庶不負
punctuated: 文學、言語、政事，殊能而不爲異。唯精也，故交錯而時出；唯無言也，故燦然而顯著；唯一也，故殊能而崇德。諸士於其所謂精者、錯者、無言者、顯著者、一者、殊者，參伍而有得焉，則深於文者也。左右經綸，無往不利矣。故曰：「神而明之，存乎其人；默而成之，不言而信，存乎德行。」不然，吾不知其所謂文者何如也。雖然，性與天道不出文章之外，而聽言觀行，孔子不諱焉，則故有所謂也。諸士勗哉！庶不負
translation_en: …literary learning, speech, and government: their abilities differed, yet did not constitute divergent ways. Precisely because it is pure, it interweaves and manifests itself at the appropriate times; precisely because it is wordless, it shines forth conspicuously; precisely because it is one, it exalts virtue through diverse abilities. If you gentlemen compare and ponder what is meant by purity and interweaving, wordlessness and conspicuous manifestation, unity and diversity, and thereby gain understanding, you will have penetrated deeply into cultural refinement. In ordering affairs on every side, you will succeed wherever you turn. Thus it is said: “To comprehend it with spirit-like insight rests with the person; to accomplish silently and inspire trust without words rests with virtuous conduct.” Otherwise, I do not know what this so-called cultural refinement amounts to. Nevertheless, human nature and the Way of Heaven do not lie outside literary expression; yet Confucius did not shrink from listening to people’s words and observing their conduct. There was thus a reason for what he said. Strive, gentlemen! May you thereby not disappoint…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
皇上求賢之本意也是舉也總理
河道時則有若都御史郭〔持平〕
有事鹺政時則有若御史
党〔承賜〕有事馬政時則有若
御史黎〔循典〕刻勵儒術司宣
文化其有事禮儀者則有若
給事中戴〔夢桂〕行人韓〔一右〕
===
劉〔三畏〕林〔應箕〕禮部員外郎
易〔寬〕咸會茲土樂觀厥成乃
若以
賀入者左叅議張〔九敘〕副使錢
〔仝〕都指揮陳〔丹〕以公出者左
叅政李〔士文〕以遷行者按察
使屈〔蘊〕夙與勞焉例得書故
punctuated: 皇上求賢之本意也。是舉也，總理河道，時則有若都御史郭〔持平〕；有事鹺政，時則有若御史党〔承賜〕；有事馬政，時則有若御史黎〔循典〕。刻勵儒術，司宣文化。其有事禮儀者，則有若給事中戴〔夢桂〕、行人韓〔一右〕、劉〔三畏〕、林〔應箕〕、禮部員外郎易〔寬〕，咸會茲土，樂觀厥成。乃若以賀入者，左叅議張〔九敘〕、副使錢〔仝〕、都指揮陳〔丹〕；以公出者，左叅政李〔士文〕；以遷行者，按察使屈〔蘊〕，夙與勞焉，例得書，故
translation_en: …His Majesty’s original intention in seeking worthy men. On the occasion of this examination, there was Guo Chiping, Censor-in-Chief, overseeing river conservancy; Dang Chengci, Investigating Censor, attending to salt administration; and Li Xundian, Investigating Censor, attending to horse administration. They diligently cultivated Confucian learning and took charge of disseminating civilizing instruction. Those attending to ceremonial duties included Dai Menggui, Supervising Secretary; Han Yiyou, Liu Sanwei, and Lin Yingji, Messengers; and Yi Kuan, Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites. All assembled in this province and delighted in witnessing the examination’s successful completion. As for those who went to the capital to offer congratulations—Zhang Jiuxu, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; Qian Tong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and Chen Dan, Regional Military Commissioner—as well as Li Shiwen, Left Administration Vice Commissioner, who departed on official business, and Qu Yun, Surveillance Commissioner, who left upon reassignment, they had already shared in the work. By customary practice their names may be recorded; therefore…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯子出
門人問曰何謂也曾子曰夫子之道忠
恕而已矣
質諸鬼神而無疑知天也百世以俟聖人
而不惑知人也
言近而指遠者善言也守約而施博者善
道也君子之言也不下帶而道存焉君
子之守脩其身而天下平
===
易
君子行此四德者故曰乾元亨利貞
象曰寒泉之食中正也
夫茅之爲物薄而用可重也慎斯術也以
往其无所失矣
復小而辨於物恒雜而不厭
書
后克艱厥后臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」子出，門人問曰：「何謂也？」曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」
質諸鬼神而無疑，知天也；百世以俟聖人而不惑，知人也。
言近而指遠者，善言也；守約而施博者，善道也。君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉；君子之守，脩其身而天下平。

易
君子行此四德者，故曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」
象曰：「寒泉之食，中正也。」
夫茅之爲物薄，而用可重也。慎斯術也以往，其无所失矣。
復，小而辨於物；恒，雜而不厭。

書
后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
The Master said, “Shen! My Way is bound together by a single thread.” Zengzi replied, “Yes.” When the Master had gone out, the disciples asked, “What did he mean?” Zengzi said, “The Master’s Way consists simply in doing one’s utmost for others and treating them as one would wish to be treated.”
To test it before the spirits and have no doubts is to know Heaven; to await a sage a hundred generations hence without misgivings is to know humanity.
Words that are close at hand yet point far afield are good words; what one holds to that is simple yet has broad application is a good Way. The gentleman’s words do not reach below his belt, yet the Way resides in them. What the gentleman holds to is the cultivation of his own person, and thereby the world is brought to peace.

Book of Changes
The gentleman puts these four virtues into practice; hence it is said: “Qian: origination, free passage, benefit, and constancy.”
The Commentary on the Images says: “The cold spring water is drunk because it is central and correct.”
As a material, white grass is slight, yet its use can be weighty. Proceed with care in this method, and nothing will go amiss.
Fu (Return) is small, yet distinguishes among things; Heng (Constancy) encounters varied circumstances, yet does not weary.

Book of Documents
If the ruler can recognize the difficulty of being a ruler, and ministers can recognize the difficulty of being ministers, government will then be well ordered, and the common people will be diligent …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
德
克綏先王之祿永底烝民之生
君子所其無逸先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則
知小人之依
簡厥修亦簡其或不修進厥良以率其或
不良
詩
六月食鬱及薁七月亨葵及菽八月剝棗
十月穫稻爲此春酒以介眉壽
裳裳者華芸其黄矣我覯之子維其有章
矣維其有章矣是以有慶矣
豐水有芑武王豈不仕詒厥孫謀以燕翼
子武王烝哉
武丁孫子武王靡不勝龍旂十乘大糦是
承
春秋
冬十月齊師滅譚譚子奔莒〔莊公十年〕
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦〔文公三年〕秋公
punctuated:
德。
克綏先王之祿，永底烝民之生。
君子所其無逸，先知稼穡之艱難，乃逸，則知小人之依。
簡厥修，亦簡其或不修；進厥良，以率其或不良。

詩
六月食鬱及薁，七月亨葵及菽，八月剝棗，十月穫稻，爲此春酒，以介眉壽。
裳裳者華，芸其黄矣。我覯之子，維其有章矣。維其有章矣，是以有慶矣。
豐水有芑，武王豈不仕？詒厥孫謀，以燕翼子。武王烝哉！
武丁孫子，武王靡不勝。龍旂十乘，大糦是承。

春秋
冬十月，齊師滅譚，譚子奔莒〔莊公十年〕。
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕。晉侯伐秦〔文公三年〕。秋，公
translation_en:
…virtue.
May you preserve the blessings of the former kings and forever secure the livelihood of the people.
The gentleman takes freedom from idleness as his abiding principle. He first understands the hardships of sowing and reaping, and only then enjoys ease; thus he knows what the common people depend upon.
Examine those who cultivate themselves, and also examine those who fail to do so. Advance the worthy, so that they may lead those who are not worthy.

Book of Odes
In the sixth month we eat wild plums and wild grapes; in the seventh month we boil mallows and beans; in the eighth month we beat down the jujubes; in the tenth month we harvest rice. With it we make spring wine, to promote long life.
Luxuriant are the blossoms, yellow in profusion. I behold that gentleman, resplendent in his accomplishments. Because he possesses such accomplishments, blessings attend him.
By the Feng River grows the white millet. Was King Wu not intent upon his work? He bequeathed plans to his descendants, to bring peace and protection to his children. How great was King Wu!
The descendants of Wuding—the martial kings—were victorious in all things. Ten chariots with dragon banners bear the great offerings of sacrificial grain.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In winter, in the tenth month, the army of Qi destroyed Tan. The Viscount of Tan fled to Ju. 〔Tenth year of Duke Zhuang〕
The men of Qin attacked Jin. 〔Third year of Duke Wen〕 The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin. 〔Third year of Duke Wen〕 In autumn, the duke…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
伐邾八月己酉入邾以邾子益來〔哀公七〕
〔年〕歸邾子益于邾〔哀公八年〕
宋子哀來奔〔文公十有四年〕公子遂如齊逆
女　夏季孫行父如齊〔俱宣公元年〕夏仲
孫蔑如京師〔宣公九年〕公孫歸父如晉〔宣〕
〔公十有八年〕
春王正月公及齊侯平莒及郯莒人不肯
公伐莒取向〔宣公四年〕
禮記
===
在朝言禮問禮對以禮
樂也者聖人之所樂也而可以善民心其
感人深其移風易俗故先王著其教焉
温良者仁之本也敬慎者仁之地也寬裕
者仁之作也孫接者仁之能也禮節者
仁之貌也言談者仁之文也歌樂者仁
之和也分散者仁之施也儒皆兼此而
有之猶且不敢言仁也其尊讓有如此
者
punctuated:
伐邾，八月己酉，入邾，以邾子益來。〔哀公七〕〔年〕歸邾子益于邾。〔哀公八年〕
宋子哀來奔。〔文公十有四年〕公子遂如齊逆女。夏，季孫行父如齊。〔俱宣公元年〕夏，仲孫蔑如京師。〔宣公九年〕公孫歸父如晉。〔宣〕〔公十有八年〕
春，王正月，公及齊侯平莒及郯，莒人不肯，公伐莒，取向。〔宣公四年〕
禮記
在朝言禮，問禮對以禮。
樂也者，聖人之所樂也，而可以善民心。其感人深，其移風易俗，故先王著其教焉。
温良者，仁之本也；敬慎者，仁之地也；寬裕者，仁之作也；孫接者，仁之能也；禮節者，仁之貌也；言談者，仁之文也；歌樂者，仁之和也；分散者，仁之施也。儒皆兼此而有之，猶且不敢言仁也。其尊讓有如此者。
translation_en:
…attacked Zhu. In the eighth month, on the jiyou day, he entered Zhu and brought back Yi, Viscount of Zhu. 〔Seventh year of Duke Ai〕 Yi, Viscount of Zhu, was returned to Zhu. 〔Eighth year of Duke Ai〕
Zi’ai of Song came seeking refuge. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Wen〕 Prince Sui went to Qi to fetch a bride. In summer, Jisun Xingfu went to Qi. 〔Both in the first year of Duke Xuan〕 In summer, Zhongsun Mie went to the royal capital. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xuan〕 Gongsun Guifu went to Jin. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Xuan〕
In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke and the Marquis of Qi sought to make peace between Ju and Tan. The people of Ju would not agree. The duke attacked Ju and took Xiang. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xuan〕
Record of Rites (Liji)
At court, speak of ritual propriety; when asked about ritual propriety, answer in accordance with it.
Music is what the sages delight in, and it can make the people’s hearts good. It moves people deeply and transforms their customs; therefore the former kings established instruction in music.
Gentleness and goodness are the root of benevolence; reverence and caution are its foundation; generosity and forbearance are its expression in action; humility in dealing with others is its capacity; ritual observances are its outward form; speech and conversation are its refinement; song and music are its harmony; distributing one’s resources is its beneficence. The Confucian scholar possesses all these qualities together, yet still does not dare to claim benevolence. Such is his reverence and modesty.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
問歌三終合樂三終
第貳場
論
萬世不可易之定論
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢兵親耕桑禮儀詔〔文帝十三年〕
擬唐以張玄素爲銀青光祿大夫誥〔貞觀十〕
〔四年〕
擬宋以胡瑗爲國子監直講謝表〔皇祐四年〕
===
判語〔五條〕
磨勘卷宗
禁革主保里長
服舍違式
私出外境及違禁下海
越訴
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問帝王之學務得其要蓋將措之躬行發
punctuated:
問：歌三終，合樂三終。

第貳場
論：萬世不可易之定論。
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢兵親耕桑禮儀詔〔文帝十三年〕。
擬唐以張玄素爲銀青光祿大夫誥〔貞觀十四年〕。
擬宋以胡瑗爲國子監直講謝表〔皇祐四年〕。

判語〔五條〕
磨勘卷宗。
禁革主保里長。
服舍違式。
私出外境及違禁下海。
越訴。

第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：帝王之學，務得其要，蓋將措之躬行，發
translation_en:
Question: The singing is performed three times, and the combined music is performed three times.

Second Session
Discourse: A settled judgment that cannot be changed for ten thousand generations.
Edicts, proclamations of appointment, and memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]; the transcription reads 内科一道.〕
Compose, in historical imitation, a Han edict concerning the ceremonial procedures for personally plowing and tending mulberries [?; 兵 is unclear]. 〔Thirteenth year of Emperor Wen.〕
Compose, in historical imitation, a Tang proclamation appointing Zhang Xuansu Grand Master of the Palace with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon. 〔Fourteenth year of Zhenguan.〕
Compose, in historical imitation, a Song memorial of thanks for the appointment of Hu Yuan as Instructor in the Directorate of Education. 〔Fourth year of Huangyou.〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items〕
Reviewing case dossiers.
Prohibiting and abolishing the practice of acting as guarantor for village heads [?].
Clothing and residences that contravene prescribed standards.
Leaving the realm without authorization and going to sea in violation of prohibitions.
Bypassing the proper authorities to lodge a complaint.

Third Session
Policy Questions 〔Five questions〕
Question: In the learning of emperors and kings, the task is to grasp its essentials, for the intention is to put them into personal practice and give them expression …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
之事業致治太平而後無愧于曆數之
傳也堯之授舜曰天之曆數在爾躬允
執厥中此萬世聖學之源也當時二聖
躬行之實無容議矣禹湯文武皆傳此
者也而事業不同習尚亦異于所謂精
一執中者果能皆不悖與漢唐宋之君
此意微矣而享國亦稱長久何與其于
所謂曆數之傳果能無愧與天啓
皇明我
===
太祖高皇帝作
成祖文皇帝繼之皆挺然以堯舜之道自任其
發爲
聖諭以昭示臣民者皆可仰見也
列聖相承益隆紹述我
皇上亶聰明嗣
寶位道冠百王治隆萬世天人協應中外頌歌
真
當今之堯舜矣不知所謂
punctuated: 之事業，致治太平，而後無愧于曆數之傳也。堯之授舜曰：「天之曆數在爾躬，允執厥中。」此萬世聖學之源也。當時二聖躬行之實，無容議矣。禹湯文武皆傳此者也，而事業不同，習尚亦異，于所謂精一執中者，果能皆不悖與？漢唐宋之君，此意微矣，而享國亦稱長久，何與？其于所謂曆數之傳，果能無愧與？天啓皇明，我太祖高皇帝作，成祖文皇帝繼之，皆挺然以堯舜之道自任。其發爲聖諭，以昭示臣民者，皆可仰見也。列聖相承，益隆紹述。我皇上亶聰明，嗣寶位，道冠百王，治隆萬世，天人協應，中外頌歌，真當今之堯舜矣。不知所謂
translation_en:
…in accomplishments, bringing about orderly government and great peace, and only then proving worthy of the transmission of Heaven’s appointed succession. When Yao entrusted the realm to Shun, he said: “Heaven’s appointed succession rests upon your person. Sincerely hold fast to the Mean.” This is the source of sagely learning for all ages. There can be no question about how these two sages actually put it into practice. Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu all transmitted this teaching, yet their accomplishments differed, as did their customary practices. Did they truly all remain faithful to what is called discerning the essential, maintaining single-mindedness, and holding fast to the Mean? Among the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song, this understanding had grown faint, yet their dynasties are also said to have endured for a long time. Why was this? Could they truly have been worthy of what is called the transmission of Heaven’s appointed succession?

Heaven inaugurated our august Ming. Our Emperor Taizu Gao arose, and Emperor Chengzu Wen succeeded him. Both resolutely took upon themselves the Way of Yao and Shun. This can be reverently discerned in the sacred instructions they issued to enlighten their officials and people. The successive sage emperors carried on this tradition, increasingly honoring and developing their predecessors’ work. Our reigning emperor, truly perceptive and enlightened, succeeded to the precious throne. His Way surpasses that of the hundred kings, and his government excels through all ages. Heaven and humanity respond in harmony; those within and beyond the realm sing his praises. He is truly the Yao and Shun of our day. Yet we would ask, concerning what is called …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖學者果何爲要與諸士子涵泳
聖化有年矣其悉心對揚以彰
繼往開來之盛
問先儒有云言人便以聖爲志言學便以
道爲志道者萬世無弊聖則學之的也
闕里儀刑萬古常存試以孔子之學與
諸士究之孔子嘗曰我非生而知之者
好古敏以求之者也又曰加我數年五
十以學易可以無大過矣乃知孔子之
===
所謂好而求者固有在也韋編三絕其
勤可知十翼之發羲吉爕然唐虞三代
之傳萬世生人之道賴以不墜者孔子
之學也可得聞與然而洙泗三千未聞
有以易請者而求仁之說乃諄諄焉何
也子思子述祖者也大本達道戒懼謹
獨於易何準孟子受於子思者也萬物
皆備性無不善於聖何述夫心本大同
道至簡易得意忘象乃爲神解昔程子
punctuated:
聖學者，果何爲要與？諸士子涵泳聖化有年矣，其悉心對揚，以彰繼往開來之盛。

問：先儒有云：「言人便以聖爲志，言學便以道爲志。」道者，萬世無弊；聖則學之的也。闕里儀刑，萬古常存。試以孔子之學，與諸士究之。孔子嘗曰：「我非生而知之者，好古，敏以求之者也。」又曰：「加我數年，五十以學易，可以無大過矣。」乃知孔子之所謂好而求者，固有在也。韋編三絕，其勤可知。十翼之發，羲吉爕然，唐虞三代之傳，萬世生人之道，賴以不墜者，孔子之學也，可得聞與？然而洙泗三千，未聞有以易請者，而求仁之說乃諄諄焉，何也？子思子，述祖者也，大本達道，戒懼謹獨，於易何準？孟子，受於子思者也，萬物皆備，性無不善，於聖何述？夫心本大同，道至簡易，得意忘象，乃爲神解。昔程子
translation_en:
…the learning of the sage: what, indeed, is its essential point? You candidates have been steeped in the sage emperor’s transforming influence for years. Apply your minds fully in your answers, giving expression to his virtue and making manifest the grandeur of carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future.

Question: An earlier Confucian scholar said: “When speaking of being a person, take sagehood as your aspiration; when speaking of learning, take the Way as your aspiration.” The Way remains free of defects through all ages; the sage is the target of learning. The exemplary model of Queli endures for all eternity. Let us examine Confucius’s learning together with you candidates. Confucius once said: “I am not one who was born knowing; I love antiquity and diligently seek knowledge of it.” He also said: “Grant me a few more years, so that at fifty I may study the Book of Changes, and I may be free of great errors.” Thus we know that what Confucius spoke of loving and seeking certainly had a particular object. The leather bindings broke three times: his diligence is evident. Through the exposition of the Ten Wings, Fuxi’s auspiciousness was harmonized [?]; that the transmitted teachings of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, and the Way for humankind through all ages, have not fallen into oblivion is owing to Confucius’s learning. May we hear your account of this?

Yet among the three thousand disciples by the Zhu and Si rivers, we hear of none who asked about the Book of Changes, while discussions of seeking benevolence were earnest and repeated. Why was this? Master Zisi transmitted the teachings of his grandfather: the great foundation and the universally applicable Way, vigilance and apprehension, and watchfulness over oneself when alone—how do these accord with the Book of Changes? Mengzi received his learning from Zisi: that all things are fully present within us, and that human nature is invariably good—what did these teachings transmit from the sage? The mind is fundamentally the same in all people, and the Way is supremely simple and easy. To grasp the meaning and forget the images is true spiritual understanding. Formerly, Master Cheng…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
受學於周茂叔而謂天理二字却是自
家體貼出來諸士學孔顏無所謂自解
者乎試言之毋讓
問治道亦多術矣然惟當務爲急宋儒程
顥曰治天下以正風俗得賢才爲本茲
非所謂當務者耶又謂必脩學校尊師
儒庶得士漸廣風俗日正旨哉言矣間
嘗竊論之禮曰廣谷大川異制民生其
問異俗考之詩書所稱歷代列國之俗
===
厚薄美惡種種異齊風土之說不誣矣
天之生才有君子有小人稽古聖狂賢
不肖忠佞貞回若陰陽晝夜歷歷可指
非天賦爲之爾耶夫謂教化可齊則彼
皆弗信何三代以還比屋可封之俗人
人君子之行邈乎未聞豈學校未脩師
弗隆與倘不由於教化則王制謂一道
德以同俗周敦頤謂師道立而善人多
非矣何三代以前又若彼也豈氣數之
punctuated:
受學於周茂叔，而謂「天理」二字却是自家體貼出來。諸士學孔顏，無所謂自解者乎？試言之，毋讓。

問：治道亦多術矣，然惟當務爲急。宋儒程顥曰：「治天下以正風俗、得賢才爲本。」茲非所謂當務者耶？又謂：「必脩學校，尊師儒，庶得士漸廣，風俗日正。」旨哉言矣！間嘗竊論之，禮曰：「廣谷大川異制，民生其問異俗。」考之詩書所稱歷代列國之俗，厚薄美惡，種種異齊，風土之說不誣矣。天之生才，有君子，有小人；稽古聖狂、賢不肖、忠佞、貞回，若陰陽晝夜，歷歷可指，非天賦爲之爾耶？夫謂教化可齊，則彼皆弗信。何三代以還，比屋可封之俗、人人君子之行，邈乎未聞？豈學校未脩、師弗隆與？倘不由於教化，則王制謂「一道德以同俗」、周敦頤謂「師道立而善人多」，非矣。何三代以前又若彼也？豈氣數之
translation_en:
…received instruction from Zhou Maoshu, yet said that he had arrived at the meaning of the two words “Heavenly principle” through his own personal understanding. You gentlemen study Kongzi and Yan Hui: do you have no understanding of your own to speak of? Explain it, without holding back.

Question: There are many methods of governing, yet attending to the most pressing tasks must take priority. The Song Confucian Cheng Hao said: “Governing the realm rests upon rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talent.” Is this not what is meant by the most pressing tasks? He also said: “Schools must be put in order, and teachers and Confucian scholars honored, so that the recruitment of scholars may gradually broaden and customs become more upright each day.” How profound these words are! I have sometimes ventured to consider this privately. The Book of Rites says: “Broad valleys and great rivers differ in configuration, and the people born among them [?] differ in customs.” Examining the customs of successive dynasties and the various states described in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, we find generosity and meanness, goodness and badness, with differences of every kind [?]. The account that attributes these to local conditions is not unfounded. Among the talents Heaven brings forth are gentlemen and petty men. Looking back into antiquity, we can distinctly identify the sage and the foolish, the worthy and the unworthy, the loyal and the sycophantic, the upright and the perverse, as clearly as yin and yang, day and night. Are these not simply the results of Heaven’s endowments? As for the claim that moral instruction can bring them into conformity, those people all disbelieve it. Why, since the Three Dynasties, have customs under which every household was worthy of enfeoffment, and conduct by which everyone was a gentleman, been so remote as to be unheard of? Is it because schools have not been put in order and teachers have not been accorded honor? If these things do not depend upon moral instruction, then the statement in “Royal Regulations,” “Unify the Way and virtue to make customs alike,” and Zhou Dunyi’s statement, “When the way of teachers is established, good people become numerous,” must be wrong. Why, then, were things as they were in the Three Dynasties and earlier? Could it be that the workings of cosmic forces and their allotted cycles…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
說特弗同與抑別有其道不瑣瑣於條
教與夫立至治之基崇無爲之化非此
莫適也不審唐虞三代果何緣得以並
臻休美爲後世嘉慕若是哉諸士讀書
考古必有所得其詳著于篇以觀通達
之學
問儒者之學貴理不貴數豈以數與理睽
非學者事耶然言爲物者莫逃乎數數
即氣也氣之流行即理也而儒者弗知
===
可乎粤自天不愛道而河圖出伏羲則
之以畫卦道之祖也何歷數代而禹獲
洛書厥數乃與圖弗類豈天苞地符之
說顧弗同與說者謂河圖洛書相爲經
緯抑所謂經緯者或有脗契者與大衍
之數聖人教民揲蓍以求數於易曷爲
與圖書卒不一合而朱子又謂縱橫反
復若合符契何也易更四聖而象已著
數固羅絡於斯矣何經世之書更出一
punctuated:
說特弗同與？抑別有其道，不瑣瑣於條教與？夫立至治之基，崇無爲之化，非此莫適也。不審唐虞三代果何緣得以並臻休美，爲後世嘉慕若是哉？諸士讀書考古，必有所得，其詳著于篇，以觀通達之學。
問：儒者之學貴理不貴數，豈以數與理睽，非學者事耶？然言爲物者莫逃乎數，數即氣也，氣之流行即理也，而儒者弗知可乎？粤自天不愛道而河圖出，伏羲則之以畫卦，道之祖也。何歷數代而禹獲洛書，厥數乃與圖弗類？豈天苞地符之說顧弗同與？說者謂河圖洛書相爲經緯，抑所謂經緯者或有脗契者與？大衍之數，聖人教民揲蓍以求數於易，曷爲與圖書卒不一合？而朱子又謂縱橫反復，若合符契，何也？易更四聖而象已著，數固羅絡於斯矣。何經世之書更出一
translation_en:
…is the explanation in terms of the cycles of cosmic qi simply different? Or is there another way, one that does not busy itself with detailed instructional regulations? To establish the foundation of consummate government and exalt the transforming influence of nonaction, no other approach will suffice. Yet through what means did the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties all attain such excellence, becoming objects of admiration and longing for later generations? You candidates, having read books and investigated antiquity, must have gained some understanding. Set it out fully in your essays, so that your breadth of learning and understanding may be seen.
Question: Confucian learning values principle rather than number. Is this because numbers diverge from principle and are no concern of scholars? Yet nothing that can be called a thing escapes number. Number is qi, and the circulation of qi is principle. Can Confucian scholars remain ignorant of it? When Heaven ceased to withhold the Way and the River Chart appeared, Fu Xi took it as his model in drawing the trigrams: this was the origin of the Way. Why, after several generations had passed and Yu obtained the Luo Writing, were its numbers unlike those of the Chart? Could the accounts of Heaven's Enfolding and Earth's Talisman refer to different things [?]? Commentators say that the River Chart and the Luo Writing serve as warp and weft to one another. Might this so-called warp and weft mean that they correspond in some way? As for the numbers of the Great Expansion, the sage taught the people to manipulate milfoil stalks to seek numbers in the Book of Changes. Why do these ultimately fail to agree with the Chart and the Writing? Yet Master Zhu says that, taken vertically or horizontally, forward or backward, they fit together like the matching halves of a tally. Why is this? The Book of Changes passed through the hands of four sages, and its images were thereby made manifest; its numbers were surely comprehensively embraced within it. Why, then, does the Book of Ordering the World introduce yet another…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
機軸不知與圖書大衍之數亦有所祖
述與範錫神禹而數弗傳宜不可考而
續夫或者補之乃有謂與三聖之易同
功豈源流考據果弗殊也天下理一而
已理同宜數同何先後變態若此茲惑
之夫以數觀數固儒者所弗屑以理觀
數則天時人事無所不該考之易疇可
徵矣若槩謂有之無所禱無之靡所闕
然則三聖非與諸士幸不惜究言用觀
===
所蘊
問財賦出于土田土田豊于人力此必然
之理也周禮大司徒有土會之法辨五
地之物生有土宜之法辨十有二土壤
之物以任土事以教稼穡樹藝有土均
之法辨五物九等制天下之地征而又
有草人稻人之職焉其教民力田舉賦
之法至精至備也可得言與齊地古稱
富强蘇秦田肯太史公之論皆可考也
punctuated:
機軸，不知與圖書、大衍之數亦有所祖述與？範錫神禹，而數弗傳，宜不可考；而續夫或者補之，乃有謂與三聖之易同功，豈源流考據果弗殊也？天下理一而已，理同宜數同，何先後變態若此？茲惑之。夫以數觀數，固儒者所弗屑；以理觀數，則天時人事無所不該，考之易疇可徵矣。若槩謂有之無所禱，無之靡所闕，然則三聖非與？諸士幸不惜究言，用觀所蘊。
問：財賦出于土田，土田豊于人力，此必然之理也。《周禮》大司徒有土會之法，辨五地之物生；有土宜之法，辨十有二土壤之物，以任土事，以教稼穡樹藝；有土均之法，辨五物九等，制天下之地征；而又有草人、稻人之職焉。其教民力田舉賦之法，至精至備也，可得言與？齊地古稱富强，蘇秦、田肯、太史公之論皆可考也。
translation_en:
…a different framework. I wonder whether it, too, follows precedents in the numbers of the River Chart, the Luo Writing, and the Great Expansion. The Great Plan was bestowed upon the divine Yu, but its numerical teachings were not transmitted and should therefore be beyond investigation. Yet later continuators have perhaps supplied what was missing [?], and some even claim that their work matches the achievement of the Changes of the Three Sages. Can their origins, transmission, and evidential foundations really be no different? All principles under Heaven are ultimately one. If the principles are the same, the numbers ought to be the same: why, then, have their configurations varied so greatly over time? This is what puzzles me. To examine numbers merely as numbers is indeed beneath the concern of Confucian scholars; but to examine numbers through principle encompasses everything in the seasons of Heaven and the affairs of humanity. This can be verified by examining the Changes and the categories of the Great Plan. If one declares indiscriminately that, with these teachings, there is nothing for which to pray [?], and without them, nothing is lacking, does this mean that the Three Sages were wrong? You candidates are requested to spare no effort in explaining this fully, so that we may see the learning you possess.
Question: Revenue comes from agricultural land, and the abundance of agricultural land comes from human labor. This is an invariable principle. In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education has a method of surveying land that distinguishes the living things produced by five kinds of terrain; a method of determining the suitability of land that distinguishes the products of twelve kinds of soil, in order to assign work on the land and teach the cultivation of grain and other plants; and a method of equalizing land assessments that distinguishes five kinds of land and nine grades, in order to regulate land taxes throughout the realm. There are also the offices of the Officer of Vegetation and the Officer of Rice Cultivation. These methods for teaching the people to cultivate their fields diligently and furnish revenue are supremely precise and comprehensive. Can you explain them? The territory of Qi was renowned in antiquity for its wealth and strength. The discussions of Su Qin, Tian Ken, and the Grand Astrologer are all available for examination.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
今之青濟登萊即古之齊也何土曠人
稀逃亡之屋蕭索相依蒿萊之田一望
無際間有一二膏腴民亦安土而又驕
悍逋稅相率爲盜至抗令不能治夫土
田人民今昔一也而豐瘠聚散美惡相
懸如此何與往歲憲臣建議欲官給牛
犋種子農器招民開墾三年而後舉稅
其謀未爲不臧而迄今竟無成效何與
將以爲地勢曠遠民不樂居耶然田今
===
城田許下田河中田豐州又皆爲之於
干戈倥偬之間尚能收儲積之利我顧
不能復之于中原平治之世與將以爲
土脉瀉鹵民不見利耶然管子相桓公
致富強遂霸諸侯一匡天下即此地也
果何術以致之與茲欲荒閒闢而流移
歸賦稅完而驕悍格使地無遺利民無
遺力移風易俗以成熙皞之盛何施而
後可
punctuated: 今之青濟登萊，即古之齊也。何土曠人稀，逃亡之屋蕭索相依，蒿萊之田一望無際？間有一二膏腴，民亦安土，而又驕悍逋稅，相率爲盜，至抗令不能治。夫土田人民，今昔一也，而豐瘠聚散美惡相懸如此，何與？往歲憲臣建議，欲官給牛犋種子農器，招民開墾，三年而後舉稅，其謀未爲不臧，而迄今竟無成效，何與？將以爲地勢曠遠，民不樂居耶？然田今城，田許下，田河中，田豐州，又皆爲之於干戈倥偬之間，尚能收儲積之利，我顧不能復之于中原平治之世與？將以爲土脉瀉鹵，民不見利耶？然管子相桓公，致富強，遂霸諸侯，一匡天下，即此地也，果何術以致之與？茲欲荒閒闢而流移歸，賦稅完而驕悍格，使地無遺利，民無遺力，移風易俗，以成熙皞之盛，何施而後可？
translation_en:
The present-day regions of Qing, Ji, Deng, and Lai constitute ancient Qi. Why, then, is the land so empty and the population so sparse, with the desolate houses of those who have fled standing beside one another, and fields overgrown with wormwood and weeds stretching as far as the eye can see? Here and there are a few fertile tracts where the people are content to remain on their land; yet they are also arrogant and unruly, default on their taxes, and band together as robbers, even resisting official orders so that they cannot be governed. The land and the people are the same now as in antiquity. Why, then, are fertility and barrenness, settlement and dispersal, and good and bad conditions so vastly different?

In past years, censorial officials proposed that the government supply teams of oxen, seed, and farming implements, recruit people to reclaim the land, and begin collecting taxes only after three years. Their plan was by no means unsound, yet to this day it has produced no results. Why is this? Is it because the territory is vast and remote, and people are unwilling to settle there? Yet agricultural colonies were established at Jincheng [?], Xuxia, Hezhong, and Fengzhou, all amid the pressing demands of warfare, and still yielded the benefit of accumulated stores. Can we alone not achieve this again in the Central Plain in an age of peace and orderly government?

Is it because the soil is saline [?], so that the people see no profit in farming it? Yet it was in this very land that Master Guan, serving as chief minister to Duke Huan, brought wealth and strength, enabled him to become hegemon over the feudal lords, and set all under Heaven in order. By what methods did he accomplish this? We now wish to open up waste and idle land, bring back those who have wandered away, secure full payment of taxes, and reform the arrogant and unruly, so that no benefit of the land is left unrealized and none of the people's capacity for work is left unused. What measures must be taken to transform customs and achieve an age of flourishing harmony?

text:
第壹場
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯子出
門人問曰何謂也曾子曰夫子之道忠
恕而已矣
李攀龍
同考試官教諭袁　批　論語一題正欲觀士子
認理之學作者惟不知體驗忠恕故每每支離于
一貫融會精切詞氣詳雅無踰此篇
同考試官教諭王　批　一唯之應忠恕之說足驗
曾子功夫到處聖人之教真有見也是篇發明
授受旨趣親切有味非邃于理善于言者決不
===
能作敬服敬服
同考試官教諭陳　批　理趣真切詞致典雅如玄
酒太羹乎淡而意味充足讀之令人忻羡不已
此必見道之士也高薦何疑
考試官教諭文　批　詞理醇正
考試官學正王　批　正是說理文字
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」子出，門人問曰：「何謂也？」曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」

李攀龍

同考試官教諭袁批：論語一題，正欲觀士子認理之學。作者惟不知體驗忠恕，故每每支離。于一貫融會精切，詞氣詳雅，無踰此篇。

同考試官教諭王批：一唯之應，忠恕之說，足驗曾子功夫到處，聖人之教真有見也。是篇發明授受旨趣，親切有味，非邃于理、善于言者，決不能作。敬服！敬服！

同考試官教諭陳批：理趣真切，詞致典雅，如玄酒太羹乎！淡而意味充足，讀之令人忻羡不已。此必見道之士也，高薦何疑？

考試官教諭文批：詞理醇正。

考試官學正王批：正是說理文字。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “Shen! My Way is threaded together by one principle.” Master Zeng replied: “Yes.” The Master went out, and his disciples asked: “What did he mean?” Master Zeng said: “The Master’s Way consists simply of doing one’s utmost for others and treating others with consideration.”

Li Panlong

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “This question from the Analects is intended precisely to assess the candidates’ learning in apprehending principle. Writers, because they do not know how to experience and embody conscientiousness and consideration for others, repeatedly produce fragmented accounts. For precise and penetrating integration of the ‘one thread,’ and for a full and elegant manner of expression, no essay surpasses this one.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The single response ‘Yes’ and the explanation in terms of conscientiousness and consideration for others amply demonstrate the level Master Zeng’s cultivation had reached: he truly understood the sage’s teaching. This essay elucidates the purport of that transmission and reception with an immediacy and richness of meaning that could certainly only come from someone deeply versed in principle and skilled in expression. My admiration! My admiration!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Its understanding of principle is genuine and exact; its expression is refined and elegant. Is it not like the ritual water and the unseasoned sacrificial broth? Plain, yet full of flavor and meaning, it inspires unceasing delight and admiration as one reads. This must be a scholar who has perceived the Way. What doubt can there be about recommending him highly?”

Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: “Both expression and reasoning are pure and correct.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Director of Studies: “This is precisely the sort of writing that elucidates principle.”

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
大賢於聖道之傳契之速而明之盡也蓋一以
貫之聖人之妙道也大賢聞之即契而因以忠
恕明之非深造自得者其孰能與於此昔曾子
服膺聖人之教於道將有得矣夫子從而詔之
曰爲學莫貴於知要而至理不可以泛求爾參
也其知吾之道乎蓋應變而不膠者末也渾融
而有定者本也故事事而酬之用斯周矣而所
以周於用者理之一也物物而應之感斯通矣
而所以通於感者理之一也方其渾然在中也
===
而變化之出未始有虧也及其犂然具陳也而
貞固之存未始或撓也其斯以爲吾道乎曾子
聞斯言也儀刑之真久得於躬行之素而面命
之旨適投其神解之機故一唯之應初無留難
蓋不煩於費詞矣及夫子既出而門人扣以傳
授之的蓋欲因言而得其心耳曾子於此有難
於直喻者故告之曰夫子之道一以貫之非有
他也亦求之忠恕而已蓋體不信也不可以言
達用之利也必本於存誠故邪僞是屏以盡己
punctuated: 大賢於聖道之傳，契之速而明之盡也。蓋一以貫之，聖人之妙道也。大賢聞之即契，而因以忠恕明之，非深造自得者，其孰能與於此？昔曾子服膺聖人之教，於道將有得矣。夫子從而詔之曰：「爲學莫貴於知要，而至理不可以泛求。爾參也，其知吾之道乎？蓋應變而不膠者，末也；渾融而有定者，本也。故事事而酬之，用斯周矣，而所以周於用者，理之一也；物物而應之，感斯通矣，而所以通於感者，理之一也。方其渾然在中也，而變化之出未始有虧也；及其犂然具陳也，而貞固之存未始或撓也。其斯以爲吾道乎？」曾子聞斯言也，儀刑之真，久得於躬行之素，而面命之旨，適投其神解之機，故一唯之應，初無留難，蓋不煩於費詞矣。及夫子既出，而門人扣以傳授之的，蓋欲因言而得其心耳。曾子於此有難於直喻者，故告之曰：「夫子之道，一以貫之，非有他也，亦求之忠恕而已。蓋體不信也，不可以言達；用之利也，必本於存誠。故邪僞是屏，以盡己
translation_en:
The great worthy, upon receiving the transmission of the sage’s Way, grasped it swiftly and elucidated it fully. For a single thread running through all things is the sage’s wondrous Way. The great worthy understood it as soon as he heard it, and then explained it through conscientiousness and reciprocity. Who could attain this without profound study and personal realization?

Formerly, Zengzi took the sage’s teachings to heart and was approaching an understanding of the Way. The Master then instructed him, saying: “In learning, nothing is more precious than knowing what is essential, and ultimate principle cannot be sought through indiscriminate inquiry. Shen, do you understand my Way? Responding to change without becoming rigid is its outward aspect; being an integrated whole with a fixed foundation is its root. Thus, as one deals with each successive affair, one’s functioning becomes comprehensive; what makes it comprehensive is the unity of principle. As one responds to each successive thing, one’s responsiveness becomes all-pervading; what makes it all-pervading is the unity of principle. While it exists within as an undivided whole, its manifestations in changing circumstances are never deficient. When it is distinctly displayed in all its particulars, its abiding firmness is never disturbed. Is this not what constitutes my Way?”

When Zengzi heard these words, he had long apprehended the true exemplar through his habitual personal practice. The purport of this direct instruction precisely met the moment of his intuitive understanding. Thus he answered with a single ‘Yes,’ without the slightest hesitation; there was no need to expend further words. After the Master had gone out, the disciples asked Zengzi about the essential point of this transmission, hoping through its words to grasp the Master’s intention. Finding it difficult to convey this directly, Zengzi therefore told them: “The Master’s Way has a single thread running through it. There is nothing else: one need only seek it in conscientiousness and reciprocity. If the underlying substance is not genuine, one cannot speak of full realization; effective functioning must be rooted in preserving sincerity. Therefore, one puts aside perversity and falsity in order to fulfill oneself …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
也而亦因之以盡人篤實是崇以自成也而即
推之以成物由是而體用可一由是而上達可
幾斯非所謂一貫乎斯不足以盡夫子之道乎
是則學有淺深而道無二致觀此則夫子之善
教與曾子之善學胥可見矣雖然昔在孔門如
由之果賜之達求之藝及其他聰明才辯者不
少也而心學之傳乃在於質魯之參與如愚之
回焉何哉盖學在自得不在外求故仲尼之道
昭如日星諸子非不聞且見也而忠恕之要博
約之訓乃唯顔曾從事焉則一貫之唯卓爾之
見又豈他人之所能與耶故曰善教者繼其志
===
質諸鬼神而無疑知天也百世以俟聖人
而不惑知人也
潘龍
同考試官教諭闕　批　聖人知天知人本皆實事此篇發揮明盡可以占所養矣
考試官教諭文　批　說知天知人處精切透徹無杜撰語而通結上節尤爲有見録之
punctuated:
也，而亦因之以盡人；篤實是崇以自成也，而即推之以成物。由是而體用可一，由是而上達可幾。斯非所謂一貫乎？斯不足以盡夫子之道乎？是則學有淺深，而道無二致。觀此，則夫子之善教與曾子之善學胥可見矣。雖然，昔在孔門，如由之果、賜之達、求之藝，及其他聰明才辯者不少也，而心學之傳乃在於質魯之參與如愚之回焉，何哉？盖學在自得，不在外求。故仲尼之道昭如日星，諸子非不聞且見也，而忠恕之要、博約之訓，乃唯顔曾從事焉。則一貫之唯、卓爾之見，又豈他人之所能與耶？故曰：「善教者繼其志。」

質諸鬼神而無疑，知天也；百世以俟聖人而不惑，知人也。
潘龍。
同考試官教諭闕，批：「聖人知天知人，本皆實事。此篇發揮明盡，可以占所養矣。」
考試官教諭文，批：「說知天知人處精切透徹，無杜撰語，而通結上節，尤爲有見，録之。」
translation_en:
…and thereby also enable others to fulfill themselves; one honors earnest sincerity to perfect oneself, and extends it to bring other beings to fulfillment. Through this, substance and function can be united; through this, higher understanding can be approached. Is this not what is meant by the single thread running through all? Is this not sufficient to encompass the Master's Way? Thus, learning has its shallow and profound levels, but the Way admits of no divergence. From this we can see both the Master's excellence in teaching and Zengzi's excellence in learning. Yet among Confucius's disciples there were many with such gifts as You's decisiveness, Ci's discernment, and Qiu's accomplishments, as well as others possessing intelligence, talent, and eloquence. Why, then, was the learning of the mind transmitted to Shen, who was plain and slow, and Hui, who seemed foolish? Because learning lies in attaining understanding for oneself, not in seeking it externally. Zhongni's Way shone as clearly as the sun and stars; the other disciples certainly heard and saw it. Yet only Yan Hui and Zeng Shen devoted themselves to the essentials of wholeheartedness and sympathetic understanding, and to the teaching of broadening learning and restraining oneself through ritual. How, then, could others have matched the assent to the single thread or the vision of what stood loftily before them? Hence the saying: “A good teacher carries forward the learner's aspirations.”

“To test it against the ghosts and spirits and have no doubt is to know Heaven; to await a sage a hundred generations hence and remain unperplexed is to know humanity.”
Pan Long.

Associate Examiner Que, an Instructor, comments: “The sage's knowledge of Heaven and humanity is grounded throughout in actual matters. This essay expounds these clearly and fully, allowing us to discern the author's cultivation.”

Examiner Wen, an Instructor, comments: “The passages explaining knowledge of Heaven and humanity are precise, pertinent, and penetrating, without fabricated assertions. The way the conclusion connects with the preceding section shows particular insight. Select it.”

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王　批　〔嘗究心于天人之學者　善言聖人制作之本必〕
論君子之制作無間於幽遠者亦惟有以明天
人之理也盖理至於天人止矣君子明之以制
作則其於幽遠也何間哉中庸言居上不驕之
意以明人道及此謂夫君子之議禮制度考文
徵遠近合幽明而一之矣然豈得於偶合者哉
彼鬼神無形而難知何言乎無疑也而君子之
制作有以質之成能於屈伸之感而黙符其變
===
化之機秪見其相協也而無相疑焉盖鬼神者
造化之迹也而天則其統體也君子有以知天
之理於終始之故則大明焉於晝夜之道則通
知焉以之定經制而秩典章也先天而天弗違
後天而奉天時天且弗違而况於鬼神乎故曰
質諸鬼神而無疑知天也後聖未至而難料何
言乎不惑也而君子之制作有以俟之先立其
中正之準而適合其睿哲之謨但見其可因也
而莫之惑焉盖聖人者斯道之管也而人則其
punctuated:
考試官學正王批〔嘗究心于天人之學者，善言聖人制作之本必〕

論君子之制作無間於幽遠者，亦惟有以明天人之理也。盖理至於天人止矣，君子明之以制作，則其於幽遠也何間哉？中庸言居上不驕之意，以明人道，及此謂夫君子之議禮、制度、考文，徵遠近、合幽明而一之矣。然豈得於偶合者哉？彼鬼神無形而難知，何言乎無疑也？而君子之制作有以質之，成能於屈伸之感，而黙符其變化之機，秪見其相協也，而無相疑焉。盖鬼神者，造化之迹也，而天則其統體也。君子有以知天之理，於終始之故則大明焉，於晝夜之道則通知焉。以之定經制而秩典章也，先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。天且弗違，而况於鬼神乎？故曰：「質諸鬼神而無疑，知天也。」後聖未至而難料，何言乎不惑也？而君子之制作有以俟之，先立其中正之準，而適合其睿哲之謨，但見其可因也，而莫之惑焉。盖聖人者，斯道之管也，而人則其
translation_en:
Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔One who has devoted thought to the study of Heaven and humanity; one who speaks well of the basis of the sages’ institutional creations must… [?]〕

As for the gentleman’s institutional creations reaching without impediment into the unseen and the distant, this is solely because he can comprehend the principles of Heaven and humanity. Principles extend no further than Heaven and humanity. When the gentleman understands them and thereby establishes institutions, what impediment can there be in his reaching into the unseen and the distant? The Doctrine of the Mean explains the meaning of occupying a high position without arrogance in order to elucidate the human Way. Here it says that the gentleman, in deliberating on ritual, establishing regulations, and examining written forms, seeks verification both far and near, unites the unseen and the manifest, and makes them one. But could this be achieved through mere coincidence?

Spirits are formless and difficult to know: how can one speak of having no doubts? Yet the gentleman’s institutional creations can be tested against them. He realizes his capacities through the interplay of contraction and expansion and silently accords with the workings of their transformations. There is only mutual accord, with no occasion for doubt. For spirits are the traces of creation and transformation, while Heaven is their encompassing unity. The gentleman can understand the principles of Heaven: he clearly comprehends the causes of endings and beginnings and thoroughly understands the Way of day and night. Through this understanding he establishes enduring institutions and orders statutes and regulations. When he precedes Heaven, Heaven does not run counter to him; when he follows Heaven, he complies with Heaven’s seasons. If even Heaven does not run counter to him, how much less would the spirits? Thus it is said: “To test them against the spirits and have no doubts is to know Heaven.”

Sages yet to come have not appeared and are difficult to anticipate: how can one speak of being free from uncertainty? Yet the gentleman’s institutional creations can await them. He establishes in advance a standard of centrality and correctness that accords precisely with their wise designs. One sees only that these institutions can be followed, with nothing to cause uncertainty about them. For sages are the custodians [?] of this Way, while human beings are their…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
同類也君子有以知人之理莫微於性命而明
焉莫重於人倫而察焉以之昭軌則而成人文
也通變而使民不倦神化而使民宜之人舉弗
違也何獨至於後聖而疑之故曰百世以俟聖
人而不惑知人也夫然則徵庶民也考三王而
不謬也建天地而不悖也孰非理之一哉又孰
非本於吾身哉王天下者當知所從事矣是何
也有天德便可語王道自昔典禮之敘人紀之
修以至因時損益通百世而可知者要皆一德
===
為之耳故不學則不知性命之理不知性命之
理則不可以立極於天下如是而強欲以制度
文為範民心而昭示後世亦末矣故曰作者之
謂聖述者之謂明蓋謂此也
言近而指遠者善言也守約而施博者善
道也君子之言也不下帶而道存焉君
子之守脩其身而天下平
黃觀
同考試官學正萬　批　善言善道乃孟子知要
punctuated:
同類也。君子有以知人之理，莫微於性命而明焉，莫重於人倫而察焉，以之昭軌則而成人文也。通變而使民不倦，神化而使民宜之，人舉弗違也，何獨至於後聖而疑之？故曰：「百世以俟聖人而不惑，知人也。」夫然則徵庶民也，考三王而不謬也，建天地而不悖也，孰非理之一哉？又孰非本於吾身哉？王天下者當知所從事矣。是何也？有天德便可語王道。自昔典禮之敘、人紀之修，以至因時損益、通百世而可知者，要皆一德為之耳。故不學則不知性命之理，不知性命之理則不可以立極於天下。如是而強欲以制度文為範民心而昭示後世，亦末矣。故曰：「作者之謂聖，述者之謂明。」蓋謂此也。
言近而指遠者，善言也；守約而施博者，善道也。君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉；君子之守，脩其身而天下平。
黃觀
同考試官學正萬批：善言善道，乃孟子知要
translation_en:
…are of the same kind. The gentleman has the means to understand the principles governing humanity: nothing is subtler than human nature and destiny, yet he comprehends them; nothing is weightier than human relationships, yet he discerns them. With this understanding he makes standards clear and brings human culture to completion. By adapting to change, he keeps the people from growing weary; through transformation of wondrous efficacy, he enables them to find what suits them. People universally accord with him. Why, then, should doubt arise only in the case of a later sage? Thus it is said: “To await a sage a hundred generations hence without misgivings is to understand humanity.” Accordingly, whether he seeks confirmation among the common people, examines the institutions of the Three Kings without falling into error, or establishes his institutions before Heaven and Earth without contradiction, which of these does not manifest the unity of principle? And which is not rooted in his own person? One who rules all under Heaven should know where to direct his efforts. Why is this? Only with the virtue of Heaven can one speak of the Way of the true king. From antiquity, the ordering of canonical rites and the cultivation of human relationships, extending to additions and reductions suited to the times and arrangements intelligible across a hundred generations—all depend, in essence, upon this single virtue.
Thus, without learning, one cannot understand the principles of human nature and destiny; without understanding these principles, one cannot establish the supreme standard for all under Heaven. In such a condition, to insist on using institutions and ceremonial forms [?] to regulate the people's hearts and provide a clear example for later generations is merely to attend to secondary matters. Thus it is said: “He who creates is called a sage; he who transmits is called discerning.” This, surely, is what is meant.
“Words that are close at hand yet far-reaching in their import are good words. Holding to what is essential while extending it broadly is the good Way. The gentleman's words do not reach below his sash, yet the Way resides in them. What the gentleman holds to is the cultivation of his own person, yet all under Heaven is brought to peace.”
Huang Guan 黃觀
Comment by Associate Examiner Wan 萬, School Instructor: “Good words and the good Way constitute Mencius's understanding of what is essential…”

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
之學此作體貼親切其身有之者乎
考試官教諭文　批　文理嚴整
考試官學正王　批　理達詞莊
大賢表言與道之善者不外於君子而得之也
夫近而指遠言斯善矣約以該博道斯善矣自
君子徵之不有可見者乎此孟子語人以知要
之學也謂夫非言無以明道非道無以廣用然
豈可以槩求之哉蓋天下之言亦多矣語或病
於支離而道不可以觸類非善也惟夫言之寡
===
也未始及其他而指之遠也自不膠於近聽之
者可忽而繹之則無窮也其斯以爲善言乎天
下之道亦多矣約或泥於致遠而博或流於寡
要非善也惟夫守在我也初非外之求而施諸
用也自足徧乎物操之則甚微而推之則無盡
也其斯以爲善道乎何也自君子觀之服之有
帶也乃物之至近者也君子之言也離坐離立
隨所扣而應之固不下於帶矣而性命之原顯
焉百物之故昭焉擬議於顧瞻之地而究極乎
punctuated:
之學。此作體貼親切，其身有之者乎？

考試官教諭文，批：文理嚴整。

考試官學正王，批：理達詞莊。

大賢表言與道之善者，不外於君子而得之也。夫近而指遠，言斯善矣；約以該博，道斯善矣。自君子徵之，不有可見者乎？此孟子語人以知要之學也。謂夫非言無以明道，非道無以廣用，然豈可以槩求之哉？蓋天下之言亦多矣，語或病於支離，而道不可以觸類，非善也。惟夫言之寡也，未始及其他，而指之遠也，自不膠於近，聽之者可忽，而繹之則無窮也，其斯以爲善言乎？天下之道亦多矣，約或泥於致遠，而博或流於寡要，非善也。惟夫守在我也，初非外之求，而施諸用也，自足徧乎物，操之則甚微，而推之則無盡也，其斯以爲善道乎？何也？自君子觀之，服之有帶也，乃物之至近者也。君子之言也，離坐離立，隨所扣而應之，固不下於帶矣，而性命之原顯焉，百物之故昭焉。擬議於顧瞻之地，而究極乎
translation_en:
…learning. This composition grasps its subject closely and intimately. Does its author himself embody this learning?

Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “The composition’s reasoning is rigorous and well ordered.”

Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the diction dignified.”

In making manifest what is good in speech and in the Way, the great worthy finds it without looking beyond the gentleman. Speech that concerns what is near yet points far afield is good speech; a Way that is concise yet encompasses the broad is a good Way. If we seek evidence in the gentleman, is there not something we can discern? Here Mencius teaches people the learning of grasping essentials. His meaning is that without speech there is no means to illuminate the Way, and without the Way there is no means to extend its application. Yet how could these be sought indiscriminately?

There are many kinds of speech in the world. Some utterances suffer from fragmentation, so that the Way cannot be understood through analogous cases: this is not good speech. Only when words are few, never straying into other matters, yet their meaning reaches far and does not cling to what is near—when a listener might overlook them, but their implications unfold without end—may we call this good speech.

There are also many ways in the world. Concision may become an impediment to reaching far, while breadth may lapse into a lack of essentials: this is not a good Way. Only when what one holds to lies within oneself, never having been sought outside, yet its practical application is sufficient to extend to all things—when what one grasps is exceedingly subtle, but its extension is inexhaustible—may we call this a good Way.

Why is this so? Consider the gentleman. The sash upon his clothing is among the things nearest to him. In his speech, whether sitting or standing apart [?], he responds to whatever he is asked. His words indeed do not reach below his sash, yet through them the source of human nature and Heaven’s decree becomes manifest, and the reasons underlying all things become clear. He considers and discusses what lies within his gaze, yet probes to the utmost …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
廣大之歸以爲止于帶也而實非止于帶也斯
不亦言近而指遠已乎吾之有身也其道之至
約者也君子之守也領惡全好踐其形而肖焉
惟以修吾身耳而所以行王道者在是所以錫
民極者在是率循其庸行之常而懋昭于協和
之治人徒見天下之平也而不知其由吾身之
修也斯不亦守約而施博已乎善學者由是審
焉可以得修辭之則而成及物之功矣何以他
求爲哉抑易之言曰夫道廣矣大矣而孟子乃
===
諄諄於近約之爲訓何哉蓋道之不遠人自兩端
之竭無行不與之教以至於修己以安百姓篤
恭而天下平皆是物也戰國之時王教不行學
術漸裂不惟近約之求而專事於遠者博者不
有以反之將何以章道而淑人哉此孟子憂世
立教之意也
易
象曰寒泉之食中正也
潘龍
punctuated:
廣大之歸。以爲止于帶也，而實非止于帶也，斯不亦言近而指遠已乎？吾之有身也，其道之至約者也。君子之守也，領惡全好，踐其形而肖焉，惟以修吾身耳。而所以行王道者在是，所以錫民極者在是。率循其庸行之常，而懋昭于協和之治。人徒見天下之平也，而不知其由吾身之修也，斯不亦守約而施博已乎？善學者由是審焉，可以得修辭之則，而成及物之功矣，何以他求爲哉？抑《易》之言曰：「夫道廣矣，大矣。」而孟子乃諄諄於近約之爲訓，何哉？蓋道之不遠人，自兩端之竭、無行不與之教，以至於修己以安百姓、篤恭而天下平，皆是物也。戰國之時，王教不行，學術漸裂，不惟近約之求，而專事於遠者、博者。不有以反之，將何以章道而淑人哉？此孟子憂世立教之意也。

《易》
象曰：「寒泉之食，中正也。」
潘龍
translation_en:
…the vast and comprehensive end to which it leads. One might suppose that such speech stops at the belt, yet in truth it does not stop there. Is this not speech that is close at hand yet points far beyond? Having this body of mine provides the most concentrated focus of the Way. What the gentleman holds to—taking charge of what is bad and preserving what is good [?], fulfilling his bodily form and conforming to its pattern—is simply the cultivation of his own person. Yet herein lies the means to practice the kingly Way; herein lies the means to bestow upon the people their supreme standard. By following the constant norms of everyday conduct, he splendidly manifests a harmonious order. People see only peace throughout the world, without knowing that it proceeds from the cultivation of his own person. Is this not holding to what is concentrated while extending its effects broadly? Those who learn well examine this carefully. They can thereby grasp the principles of refining their words and accomplish the work of benefiting others. Why seek elsewhere?

Yet the Book of Changes says, “The Way is broad indeed, and great indeed.” Why, then, does Mengzi so insistently teach what is close at hand and concentrated? It is because the Way is never far from people.
