It is like living in Qi and speaking the language of Qi, or living in Chu and speaking the language of Chu. Which of these two ways shall one choose? The Book of Odes says: “He bequeathed plans to his descendants, thereby bringing peace to and aiding his children.” This is why the sage kings attached such weight to dynastic succession, to the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, and to the lives of all the people under Heaven. The injunction to exercise care reaches its fullest significance here.

Let the ruler ponder the words of the loyal and wise, take warning from the causes of success and failure, reflect upon the clear admonitions of ‘Against Ease,’ and make lasting plans to bequeath prosperity. Let men like the Dukes of Zhou and Shao and the Scribe Yi each offer their loyal counsel. Once his virtue is perfected and all under Heaven uphold him, he can match the flourishing of the Three Dynasties and lay the foundation for an enterprise as firmly rooted as a clump of mulberry trees…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
業尚何景命之不申哉書曰一人元良萬邦以
貞此之謂也
表
擬宋以胡瑗爲國子監直講謝表〔皇祐四年〕
黄覲
同考試官學正萬　批〔不刻意騈儷而鋪叙揄　揚自有典則刻此足以正奇巧之習〕
考試官教諭文　批〔温潤經切說出胡瑗心　意亦但工于四六者〕
===
考試官學正王　批〔立意措詞最得稱謝之　體平實中文藻爛然他作鮮及〕
皇祐四年某月某日伏蒙
聖恩以臣爲國子監直講者
聖世弘文國學重化成之本
明王崇教儒紳承寵命之榮譽髦忝就乎陶鎔
師責寔慚于模範
恩逾晋錫感切震驚臣瑗誠惶誠恐稽首頓
首上言伏以東膠肇啓爰咨典樂之官靈
punctuated:
業，尚何景命之不申哉？書曰：「一人元良，萬邦以貞。」此之謂也。

表
擬宋以胡瑗爲國子監直講謝表〔皇祐四年〕
黄覲
同考試官學正萬批〔不刻意騈儷，而鋪叙揄揚，自有典則。刻此足以正奇巧之習。〕
考試官教諭文批〔温潤經切，說出胡瑗心意，亦但工于四六者。〕
考試官學正王批〔立意措詞，最得稱謝之體。平實中文藻爛然，他作鮮及。〕
皇祐四年某月某日，伏蒙聖恩，以臣爲國子監直講者。聖世弘文，國學重化成之本；明王崇教，儒紳承寵命之榮。譽髦忝就乎陶鎔，師責寔慚于模範。恩逾晋錫，感切震驚。臣瑗誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：伏以東膠肇啓，爰咨典樂之官；靈
translation_en:
…an enduring foundation—how could the great mandate fail to be renewed? The Book of Documents says: “When the one man is supremely good, the myriad states are thereby set right.” This is what it means.

Memorial
A memorial of thanks, composed as if on the occasion of the Song appointment of Hu Yuan as Lecturer in the Directorate of Education. 〔Fourth year of Huangyou [1052].〕
By Huang Jin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wan, School Instructor: 〔Without laboriously pursuing parallel phrasing, its exposition and praise possess their own classical order. Printing this piece will suffice to correct the fashion for ingenious extravagance.〕

Comment by Examiner Wen, School Instructor: 〔Gentle and polished, grounded in the classics and pertinent, it expresses Hu Yuan’s thoughts; yet it is merely the work of one skilled in four-and-six-character parallel prose [?].〕

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: 〔Its conception and wording capture exceptionally well the proper form of an expression of thanks. Amid its plainness and solidity, literary elegance shines forth; few other compositions match it.〕

On a certain day of a certain month in the fourth year of Huangyou, I humbly received your sagely favor appointing me Lecturer in the Directorate of Education.

In this sagely age, literary culture flourishes, and the National University is esteemed as the foundation of moral transformation. The enlightened sovereign exalts instruction, and scholars receive the honor of your gracious appointment. Among eminent scholars [?], I undeservedly undertake the work of molding others; charged with teaching, I am truly ashamed of my inadequacy as an exemplar. Your favor exceeds the distinction conferred by this promotion, and my gratitude is mingled with profound trembling. Your servant Yuan, in utmost fear and trepidation, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtows, submitting these words:

I humbly consider that when the Eastern School was first opened, the official in charge of music was consulted; the Ling…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
壁弘新式重作人之地蓋首善莫先乎太
學而敦典有望於英君師貴道尊庠均義
重故漢帝屈臨雍之拜肆唐宗篤齒胄之
風遐稽致治之隆寔本右儒之化道因言
闡論思允賴於名賢才以養成陶沃必資
乎碩德事誠有待教不虛行若賜侈桓榮
曷任式和之體必望隆韓愈庶幾先覺之
貞責任匪輕簡掄宜慎如臣〔庸鄙〕特荷甄
旌雖
===
臺朝不棄于采葑而微德有懷乎負乘恭惟
○○○○
神凝聖域
識際道真
懋湯德之日新誕開章閣
邁高宗之時敏夙御經筵
玉質金相綱紀協文章之用鳶飛魚躍作興
妙鼓舞之機謂振育英才敦化允基乎三
舍而主盟庠序立賢當廣於無方詎知樗
punctuated:
壁弘新，式重作人之地。蓋首善莫先乎太學，而敦典有望於英君。師貴道尊，庠均義重。故漢帝屈臨雍之拜，肆唐宗篤齒胄之風。遐稽致治之隆，寔本右儒之化。道因言闡，論思允賴於名賢；才以養成，陶沃必資乎碩德。事誠有待，教不虛行。若賜侈桓榮，曷任式和之體；必望隆韓愈，庶幾先覺之貞。責任匪輕，簡掄宜慎。如臣〔庸鄙〕，特荷甄旌。雖臺朝不棄于采葑，而微德有懷乎負乘。
恭惟○○○○，神凝聖域，識際道真。懋湯德之日新，誕開章閣；邁高宗之時敏，夙御經筵。玉質金相，綱紀協文章之用；鳶飛魚躍，作興妙鼓舞之機。謂振育英才，敦化允基乎三舍；而主盟庠序，立賢當廣於無方。詎知樗
translation_en:
…the walls are grandly renewed, giving fresh importance to the place where men of talent are formed. For establishing exemplary goodness, nothing takes precedence over the Imperial University; for upholding the canonical teachings, our hopes rest upon an enlightened ruler. Teachers are esteemed and the Way honored: weighty indeed is the significance of the schools. Thus the Han emperor humbled himself to bow when visiting the imperial academy, and the Tang sovereign strengthened the practice of having the heir attend school among his peers. Looking far back to the heights of good government, these truly rested upon the transforming influence of honoring Confucian learning. The Way is elucidated through words, and deliberation and reflection depend upon eminent worthies; talent develops through nurture, and its cultivation must draw upon men of great virtue. Such undertakings indeed await the right men; teaching cannot proceed in vain. If lavish rewards like those bestowed upon Huan Rong are granted, how could one fulfill the ideal of harmonious instruction [?]? One must command esteem as high as Han Yu’s to approach the steadfastness of those first awakened to the Way. The responsibility is no light one; selection should be cautious. Such a man as your servant 〔mediocre and uncultivated〕 has nevertheless received special recognition. Though the court does not reject me—as one gathering turnips does not discard them for their imperfect leaves—my scant virtue makes me fear that I am a burden-bearer riding in a carriage beyond my station.
Reverently considering ○○○○: Your spirit is concentrated in the realm of sagehood, and your understanding reaches the truth of the Way. Emulating Tang’s daily renewal of virtue, you have magnificently opened the literary halls; surpassing Gaozong’s constant diligence in learning, you have early attended the Classics Colloquium. With substance like jade and outward form like gold, your ordering of government accords with the uses of literary cultivation. As kites soar and fish leap, your fostering of talent wondrously sets encouragement in motion. You hold that, in promoting and nurturing outstanding talent, the deepening of moral transformation is truly founded upon the Three Colleges system; and that, in choosing leaders for the schools, the appointment of worthy men should extend broadly, without fixed limitations. How could it have been imagined that an ailanthus…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
櫟之散材謬典胄義之重寄官崇直講位
列贊宗秩望接千成均衣冠率乎胄子登
堂釆藻斯文昭化日之光鼓篋升階多士
藹如雲之集此
王道不亨之會而儒者至足之榮也切念臣海
陵遐賤草野至庸岱麓窮居志徒勤於仰
止蘇湖分迪功莫答於涓埃横碧帳以明
經自分含貞海嵎對青衿而敬業何期貴
釆雲宮慚非顥達之倫謬辱仲淹之薦伊
===
日蘭芷譸移入室之情不自淵源易足欽
河之願智易窮於小知仁何與以曲成激
切由衷勉圖知分臣敢不益敦舊學用荅
新恩勤勞來匡直之功備春夏秋冬之教攄
平生望道之志上不負於
所知振先哲成物之方下不孤於所學門墻
桃李仰歸
雨露之仁泮水魚龍共沐江河之潤伏望
敷崇第以作人
punctuated:
櫟之散材，謬典胄義之重寄。官崇直講，位列贊宗，秩望接千成均，衣冠率乎胄子。登堂釆藻，斯文昭化日之光；鼓篋升階，多士藹如雲之集。此王道不亨之會，而儒者至足之榮也。
切念臣海陵遐賤，草野至庸。岱麓窮居，志徒勤於仰止；蘇湖分迪，功莫答於涓埃。横碧帳以明經，自分含貞海嵎；對青衿而敬業，何期貴釆雲宮。慚非顥達之倫，謬辱仲淹之薦。伊日蘭芷譸移，入室之情不自；淵源易足，欽河之願。智易窮於小知，仁何與以曲成？激切由衷，勉圖知分。
臣敢不益敦舊學，用荅新恩，勤勞來匡直之功，備春夏秋冬之教。攄平生望道之志，上不負於所知；振先哲成物之方，下不孤於所學。門墻桃李，仰歸雨露之仁；泮水魚龍，共沐江河之潤。伏望敷崇第以作人。
translation_en:
…an oak of useless timber, I have undeservedly been entrusted with the weighty charge of educating the sons of the state [?]. My office is honored as that of Lecturer; my position ranks among those assisting the ancestral line [?]. My rank and standing connect me with the Imperial University [?], and in cap and gown I lead its students. Ascending the hall and gathering literary adornments, our cultural tradition manifests the radiance of your transforming sun; opening their book satchels and mounting the steps, the many scholars assemble thick as clouds. This is an occasion when the Kingly Way does not flourish [?], yet an honor that brings a Confucian scholar the fullest satisfaction.
I reflect that I, your servant, am a lowly man from distant Hailing, utterly ordinary and of rustic origins. Living in poverty at the foot of Mount Dai, I could only devote my aspirations to looking up to the sages. Sharing in the work of instruction in Suzhou and Huzhou, my achievements could not repay even a drop or speck of your favor. Setting up a blue-green teaching curtain to elucidate the Classics, I expected only to preserve my integrity in a remote coastal corner. Facing the blue-collared students and diligently pursuing my calling, how could I have expected to be prized and selected for the cloud-high palace? Ashamed that I am not of the company of Hao and Da [?], I have undeservedly received Zhongyan’s recommendation. On that day, the fragrant orchids and angelica were moved [?]; my feelings on entering the master’s chamber were beyond my control [?]. The wellspring was readily sufficient [?], yet I longed to revere the river. My wisdom is soon exhausted by its petty knowledge; how could my benevolence contribute to bringing each person to fulfillment? Deeply moved from the heart, I strive to understand my allotted duty.
How dare I fail to deepen my former learning in repayment of this new favor, diligently undertaking the work of encouraging, attracting, correcting, and setting students upright, and providing instruction through spring, summer, autumn, and winter? I shall express my lifelong aspiration toward the Way, so that above I do not disappoint the one who has recognized me; I shall advance the former sages’ methods of bringing others to fulfillment, so that below I do not betray what I have learned. The peach and plum trees within my school’s walls look upward to the benevolence of your rain and dew; the fish and dragons in the school’s pond alike bathe in the nourishing waters of rivers. I humbly hope that you will exalt the ranks [?] to cultivate worthy men…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
本經術而致治
皇極著表儀之式
丹扆切敬教之思有翼有馮濟濟詠周楨于
王國乃文乃武
明明協唐運於中天臣瑗無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
===
第叁場
策
第一問
李攀龍
同考試官教諭袁　批〔此策敘述我〕
聖祖開闢之功精一之學
成祖再造
皇上中興
punctuated:
本經術而致治，皇極著表儀之式，丹扆切敬教之思。有翼有馮，濟濟詠周楨于王國；乃文乃武，明明協唐運於中天。臣瑗無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
李攀龍
同考試官教諭袁　批：〔此策敘述我〕聖祖開闢之功、精一之學，成祖再造，皇上中興
translation_en:
…to bring about good government grounded in classical learning. May the sovereign standard manifest a model for all to follow, and may Your Majesty, upon the vermilion throne, earnestly cherish reverence for instruction. With assistance and support, may the assembled worthies sing of the pillars of Zhou within the royal realm; accomplished in civil and military affairs, may they gloriously accord with the flourishing fortunes of Tang (Yao) at their zenith. Your servant Yuan, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to the Sage, cannot contain his profound emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and make it known to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Li Panlong
Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: 〔This policy essay recounts our〕 sagely founder’s achievement in establishing the realm and his learning of refinement and single-mindedness, Chengzu’s restoration of the dynasty, and the reigning emperor’s revival of its fortunes…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖聖相承心法之妙皆能舉其要而合其同庶不負
聖朝作養之恩矣宜取之以貢
同考試官教諭王　批
皇上睿資天錫
聖學性成近法
祖宗遠追堯舜誠不世出之
聖主也此篇能莊頌而揚厲之必嘗服習
聖化而有得焉者况才思深長文理精到而忠愛之意溢于
君子不爲盛世慶乎
===
同考試官教諭陳　批　此策重
皇上聖學不獨見于
製作十九年間隱顯一誠久暫無二真允蹈之矣恪究玄微之妙仰述
功業之隆僅見此作謹當錄之以爲
當宁獻
考試官教諭文　批　有忠敬之心有臣隣之
願用世之才也可取可取
考試官學正王　批　善言
皇上爲學之要而遡流窮源得我
punctuated:
聖聖相承，心法之妙，皆能舉其要而合其同，庶不負聖朝作養之恩矣。宜取之以貢。

同考試官教諭王，批：皇上睿資天錫，聖學性成，近法祖宗，遠追堯舜，誠不世出之聖主也。此篇能莊頌而揚厲之，必嘗服習聖化而有得焉者。况才思深長，文理精到，而忠愛之意溢于君子，不爲盛世慶乎？

同考試官教諭陳，批：此策重皇上聖學，不獨見于製作。十九年間，隱顯一誠，久暫無二，真允蹈之矣。恪究玄微之妙，仰述功業之隆，僅見此作。謹當錄之，以爲當宁獻。

考試官教諭文，批：有忠敬之心，有臣隣之願，用世之才也。可取，可取！

考試官學正王，批：善言皇上爲學之要，而遡流窮源，得我
translation_en:
…As sage succeeds sage, this essay identifies the essentials of the wondrous teachings of the mind and brings out what they share. The author may thus prove worthy of the sagely dynasty’s gracious cultivation of talent. He should be selected for presentation to the court.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: His Majesty’s penetrating intelligence is Heaven’s gift, and his sagely learning is innate. He models himself on his imperial ancestors in the nearer past and follows Yao and Shun in distant antiquity. Truly, he is a sage sovereign such as rarely appears. This essay solemnly praises and splendidly celebrates him; its author must have practiced and absorbed his sagely transforming influence and gained something thereby. Moreover, his imaginative powers are profound and far-reaching, his writing’s reasoning refined and exact, and his loyal affection overflows “unto the gentleman” [?]. Is this not cause for rejoicing in a flourishing age?

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: This policy essay emphasizes His Majesty’s sagely learning, which is manifest not only in his institutions and enactments. Throughout nineteen years, in things hidden and apparent alike, his sincerity has remained one; whether over long periods or brief moments, it has never varied. He has indeed faithfully put this learning into practice. Only this composition have I seen that reverently probes its profound subtleties and respectfully recounts the grandeur of his achievements. It should duly be recorded and offered to the reigning sovereign.

Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: He has a heart full of loyalty and reverence and the aspirations of a close servant of the throne. His is a talent fit for public service. Worth selecting, worth selecting!

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
祖宗
列聖統緒之傳必豪傑之士也可敬可敬
帝王之學非徒博聞廣志而已也將以昭
德塞違而布之政也達天命之原通古今
之變察民物之紀廣聰明之實非學何繇
矣古之聖哲豈不能師心以爲治而必爲
是孜孜者誠以理欲之賓難明而心志之
蠱易入乾行當法而鏡戒不可不昭其所
以亹邁軌而永隆譽者以其憲天立極有
此道也雜之者霸忽焉則幾乎殆矣在昔
成湯之誥曰惟皇上帝降衷于下民若有
恒性克綏厥猷惟后泰誓曰天佑下民作
之君作之師惟其克相上帝此言天之所
期於人君至篤厚也羲黃氏之有天下尚
矣唐虞以下不能無憂焉故堯之命舜曰
天之曆數在爾躬允執其中舜亦命禹曰
人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中
此言君所以承天之道也由今觀之親九
punctuated:
祖宗列聖統緒之傳，必豪傑之士也，可敬可敬！

帝王之學，非徒博聞廣志而已也，將以昭德塞違而布之政也。達天命之原，通古今之變，察民物之紀，廣聰明之實，非學何繇矣？古之聖哲，豈不能師心以爲治，而必爲是孜孜者，誠以理欲之賓難明，而心志之蠱易入。乾行當法，而鏡戒不可不昭。其所以亹邁軌而永隆譽者，以其憲天立極，有此道也。雜之者霸，忽焉則幾乎殆矣。在昔成湯之誥曰：「惟皇上帝，降衷于下民，若有恒性，克綏厥猷惟后。」《泰誓》曰：「天佑下民，作之君，作之師，惟其克相上帝。」此言天之所期於人君至篤厚也。羲黃氏之有天下，尚矣。唐虞以下，不能無憂焉。故堯之命舜曰：「天之曆數在爾躬，允執其中。」舜亦命禹曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」此言君所以承天之道也。由今觀之，親九
translation_en:
…the transmission of the line of succession of our imperial ancestors and successive sage rulers. He must surely be a man of outstanding ability. Admirable indeed, admirable indeed!

The learning of emperors and kings is not merely a matter of extensive knowledge and breadth of understanding. Its purpose is to make virtue manifest, restrain wrongdoing, and put these principles into effect in government. To reach the source of Heaven’s mandate, comprehend changes past and present, discern the ordering of people and things, and enlarge one’s actual powers of perception and understanding—without learning, by what means could these be achieved? Could the sages of antiquity not have governed by taking their own minds as their teachers? Yet they invariably applied themselves so diligently because the distinction between principle and desire [?] is difficult to discern, while corrupting influences readily enter the mind and will. Heaven’s vigorous activity must be emulated, and admonitory examples must be made clear. The means by which they diligently advanced along the proper course [?] and perpetually enhanced their renown lay in this Way, through which they modeled themselves on Heaven and established the supreme standard. Those who adulterate it become hegemons; those who neglect it come close to peril.

Long ago, the Proclamation of Cheng Tang stated: “August Heaven on High bestowed an inner moral norm upon the people below. By following it, they possess a constant nature; it is the sovereign who can bring them peacefully to follow their proper way.” The Great Declaration states: “Heaven aids the people below, making rulers for them and making teachers for them, so that these may assist the Lord on High.” These words show how profoundly earnest are Heaven’s expectations of the ruler. The possession of All under Heaven by Fuxi and Huangdi belongs to remote antiquity. From the time of Yao and Shun onward, rulers could not be without apprehension. Thus Yao charged Shun, saying: “Heaven’s ordained succession rests upon your person. Sincerely hold fast to the mean.” Shun likewise charged Yu, saying: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning, be single-minded, and sincerely hold fast to the mean.” These words describe the Way by which the ruler accords with Heaven. Viewed from the present, bringing affection to the nine…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
族和萬邦被四表格上下堯之德其至矣
從五典叙百揆神人以和百獸率舞舜之
德其至矣此猶天地之高厚日月之著明
後有作者二帝爲不可及已自時厥後祗
台德先禹之所以繼舜也聖敬日躋湯之
所以繼禹也緝熙敬止受戒丹書文武之
所以繼湯也明辟之道克享天心以隆大
命其見於治也夏之道尚忠商變之而尚
質周變之而尚文蓋與時推移雖聖人無
===
如之何令其風動之休允殖之治亦清之
功異世而比隆非一德誰能致之故孔子
曰大道之行也與三代之英丘未之逮也
而有志焉蓋宗之也自周而下則有可議
者矣過魯祠聖似矣而不事詩書鋭情經
術似矣而內多慚德闢門諭心似矣而得
國非正帝王之學槩未有得以先天下然
跡其所爲易秦項之暴也除隋室之亂也
洗五代之陋也其功在生民天亦不得而
punctuated:
族，和萬邦，被四表，格上下，堯之德其至矣！從五典，叙百揆，神人以和，百獸率舞，舜之德其至矣！此猶天地之高厚，日月之著明，後有作者，二帝爲不可及已。自時厥後，「祗台德先」，禹之所以繼舜也；「聖敬日躋」，湯之所以繼禹也；「緝熙敬止」，受戒丹書，文武之所以繼湯也。明辟之道，克享天心，以隆大命。其見於治也，夏之道尚忠，商變之而尚質，周變之而尚文，蓋與時推移，雖聖人無如之何。令其風動之休、允殖之治、亦清之功，異世而比隆，非一德誰能致之？故孔子曰：「大道之行也，與三代之英，丘未之逮也，而有志焉。」蓋宗之也。
自周而下，則有可議者矣。過魯祠聖似矣，而不事詩書；鋭情經術似矣，而內多慚德；闢門諭心似矣，而得國非正。帝王之學，槩未有得以先天下。然跡其所爲，易秦項之暴也，除隋室之亂也，洗五代之陋也，其功在生民，天亦不得而
translation_en:
…clans, bringing harmony to the myriad states, extending his influence to the four distant quarters, and reaching above and below: Yao’s virtue was indeed consummate! Following the five constant norms, ordering the hundred offices, bringing spirits and people into harmony, and causing all the beasts to dance: Shun’s virtue was indeed consummate! This was like the height and breadth of Heaven and Earth, and the brilliance of the sun and moon. For those who arose afterward, these two emperors were beyond attainment. From that time onward, “Reverently putting my virtue first” was how Yu succeeded Shun; “His sageliness and reverence rose daily” was how Tang succeeded Yu; “Continuing in brightness and abiding in reverence,” and receiving admonitions from the Cinnabar Writing, were how Kings Wen and Wu succeeded Tang. The way of these enlightened sovereigns won Heaven’s favor and strengthened their great mandate. As manifested in government, the way of Xia prized loyalty; Shang changed this to prize simplicity; Zhou changed this to prize refinement. These shifts followed the times, and even sages could not prevent them. Their beneficent influence, which moved people like the wind, their flourishing government, and their achievements in purification [?] matched one another in greatness across different ages. Who could have accomplished this without constant virtue? Thus Confucius said: “The practice of the Great Way and the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties—I, Qiu, did not live to see them, but I have records of them.” He took them as his exemplars.
From Zhou onward, however, there are grounds for criticism. Passing through Lu and offering sacrifice to the Sage seemed fitting, yet there was no devotion to the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. Eager commitment to classical learning seemed fitting, yet inwardly there was much shameful conduct. Opening the gates to counsel and making one’s intentions known seemed fitting, yet the realm had been acquired illegitimately. In the learning proper to emperors and kings, none had, on the whole, attained what was needed to lead the world. Yet if we examine what they accomplished, they displaced the violence of Qin and Xiang, eliminated the disorder of the Sui ruling house, and swept away the degraded practices of the Five Dynasties. Their achievements benefited the people, and even Heaven could not…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
棄之是以漢祚四百唐祚三百宋實次之
方之他姓爲烈然而異於三代遠矣論者
曰漢治雜霸唐治雜夷宋治優柔不振蓋
少之也天之眷明德久矣鑒觀四方求民
之莫未始一日而替也而聖王不作大道
不彰天之心不能若是恝矣
高皇帝以神武之資膺曆數之歸明命有赫實
祇承之投戈講道典學不怠故諭曾魯以
欲求堯舜之心喻宋濂以當謹操存之戒
===
與陶安論學術而深明邪說之害因宋善
讀心箴而極言人心道心倚伏之幾斯心
也其即堯舜之心乎故釋洪範而奕人徵
應之理昭矣書大學衍義而古今治亂之
原彰矣他如存心省躬之錄表其誠也通
訓集禮之編陳其度也
聖謨洋洋不有可徵者乎
文皇帝親得
聖哲之儀刑善繼善述以光
punctuated:
棄之。是以漢祚四百，唐祚三百，宋實次之，方之他姓爲烈。然而異於三代遠矣。論者曰：「漢治雜霸，唐治雜夷，宋治優柔不振。」蓋少之也。天之眷明德久矣，鑒觀四方，求民之莫，未始一日而替也。而聖王不作，大道不彰，天之心不能若是恝矣。
高皇帝以神武之資，膺曆數之歸，明命有赫，實祇承之。投戈講道，典學不怠。故諭曾魯以欲求堯舜之心，喻宋濂以當謹操存之戒，與陶安論學術而深明邪說之害，因宋善讀《心箴》而極言人心道心倚伏之幾。斯心也，其即堯舜之心乎？故釋《洪範》而奕人徵應之理昭矣，書《大學衍義》而古今治亂之原彰矣。他如《存心省躬》之錄，表其誠也；《通訓》《集禮》之編，陳其度也。聖謨洋洋，不有可徵者乎？
文皇帝親得聖哲之儀刑，善繼善述，以光
translation_en:
…cast them aside. Thus the Han enjoyed four hundred years of dynastic rule, the Tang three hundred, and the Song ranked next. Compared with other ruling houses, their achievements were outstanding. Yet they remained far removed from the Three Dynasties. Critics say: “Han government mixed in the methods of hegemons; Tang government mixed in barbarian practices; Song government was irresolute and lacked vigor.” They thus judged them wanting. Heaven has long cherished luminous virtue. It surveys the four quarters, seeking repose for the people, and has never ceased doing so for even a day. Yet sage kings did not arise, and the Great Way remained unmanifest. Heaven’s heart could not be so indifferent to this.
Emperor Gao, endowed with divine martial prowess, received the succession ordained by Heaven. The luminous mandate shone brilliantly, and he reverently accepted it. Laying aside his spear, he expounded the Way and pursued learning without flagging. Thus he told Zeng Lu that he wished to seek the heart of Yao and Shun, and admonished Song Lian to attend carefully to holding fast to and preserving the mind. In discussing learning with Tao An, he elucidated the harm caused by heterodox doctrines. When Song Shan [?] read the Admonition on the Mind, he discoursed fully on the subtle workings through which the human mind and the mind of the Way alternately predominate and lie latent. Was this heart of his not the very heart of Yao and Shun? Thus, in explaining the Great Plan, he made clear the principles of portents and responses between Heaven and humanity [?]; in writing out the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, he revealed the sources of order and disorder, past and present. Other works, such as the record Preserving the Mind and Examining Oneself, displayed his sincerity; the compilations Comprehensive Instructions and Collected Rites set forth his standards. So abundant were his sagely counsels—are there not things here that bear witness to them?
Emperor Wen personally received the exemplary guidance of the sagely and wise ruler. Skillfully carrying on his predecessor’s purposes and undertakings, he thereby brought luster to…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
先德故其論
皇太子曰堯舜相傳惟曰允執厥中帝王之學
貴乎知要諭學士曰朕嘗退朝默坐而思
管束此心諭御史曰朕每一飲一食未嘗
不念及軍民斯心也其即堯舜之心乎故
輯
帝王之學弘矣他如六經之表章崇正學
文華寶鑑而昭鑒之義廣矣輯聖學心法而
也內訓之頒布正倫理也世世德作求不有
===
列聖相承勿替引之是以大道宣昭至治濯俗
克纂神明之統而聿追隆古之休豈不盛
可見者乎
與肆我
皇上憲天聰明嗣有歷服益懋建中之德以顯
丕承之烈是故敬一有箴傳聖王之心法
也五箴有訓闡先哲之微言也揭無逸之
篇以勤稼穡著憂勤也解本末終始之章
以頒諸史局盡精微也以至除夕有作崇
punctuated:
先德。故其論皇太子曰：「堯舜相傳，惟曰允執厥中。帝王之學，貴乎知要。」諭學士曰：「朕嘗退朝默坐而思，管束此心。」諭御史曰：「朕每一飲一食，未嘗不念及軍民。」斯心也，其即堯舜之心乎？故輯，帝王之學弘矣。他如六經之表章，崇正學；《文華寶鑑》而昭鑒之義廣矣，輯《聖學心法》而也。《內訓》之頒布，正倫理也。世世德作求，不有列聖相承，勿替引之？是以大道宣昭，至治濯俗，克纂神明之統，而聿追隆古之休，豈不盛？可見者乎？
與肆我皇上憲天聰明，嗣有歷服，益懋建中之德，以顯丕承之烈。是故《敬一》有箴，傳聖王之心法也；五箴有訓，闡先哲之微言也。揭《無逸》之篇，以勤稼穡，著憂勤也；解本末終始之章，以頒諸史局，盡精微也。以至除夕有作，崇
translation_en:
…the virtue of his forebears. Thus, in speaking to the imperial heir apparent, he said: “What Yao and Shun transmitted to one another was simply this: ‘Sincerely hold fast to the Mean.’ In the learning of emperors and kings, what matters is grasping the essentials.” He instructed the academicians: “After withdrawing from court, I have often sat silently in reflection, keeping this mind under control.” He instructed the investigating censors: “Whenever I drink or eat, I never fail to think of the soldiers and the people.” Was not this very mind the mind of Yao and Shun?
Thus he compiled …, and the learning of emperors and kings was enlarged [?]. Other measures included honoring the Six Classics and promoting orthodox learning. The Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian) broadened the principles of taking illuminating examples as a mirror; he compiled the Essential Methods of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), and … [?]. The promulgation of Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun) rectified ethical relationships. In generation after generation, virtue was sought and cultivated. Did not the successive sage sovereigns carry this forward without letting it lapse? Thus the Great Way shone forth, and consummate government purified popular customs. They succeeded to the divinely enlightened line of rule and attained the excellence of high antiquity. Was this not magnificent? Could it not be seen [?]? [The transcription appears to have several passages out of order here.]
Thus our emperor, taking Heaven as his model in perceptiveness and understanding, has inherited the imperial charge. He strives still harder to establish the Mean as his virtue, thereby manifesting the glorious achievement of carrying forward his inheritance. Accordingly, his Admonition on Reverent Unity transmits the essential methods of the sage kings’ minds; his instructions on the Five Admonitions elucidate the subtle words of earlier sages. By displaying the chapter “Against Idleness,” he encourages diligence in sowing and harvesting and manifests his anxious devotion to duty. By explaining the passage on roots and branches, endings and beginnings, and distributing his explanation to the offices compiling history, he fully explores its subtle meaning. He has even composed a work on New Year’s Eve, exalting …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
修建中和之極此
聖心之所有事臣下之所祗承而不懈者也愚
何容於贅詞乎虞廷之歌曰元首明哉股
肱良哉庶事康哉言敕天之功也周成王
之頌曰昊天有成命二后受之成王不敢
康夙夜基命宥密言法祖之治也先聖
後聖其道同歸愚敢以是爲
今日獻
第二問
===
同考試官教諭闞　批　道顯于造化闡于伏羲
孔子得之易子思述之祖孟子傳之于子思也
此篇推明玄妙究極天人而聖賢相傳之旨異
世同符非深于易而會于道者無此說豪傑之
士非俗學可擬也
考試官教諭文　批　聖賢之言雖殊而實同
歸于道但學者不知察識體驗之耳發明旨趣
合異爲同僅見此作
punctuated:
修建中和之極，此聖心之所有事，臣下之所祗承而不懈者也。愚何容於贅詞乎？虞廷之歌曰：「元首明哉，股肱良哉，庶事康哉！」言敕天之功也。周成王之頌曰：「昊天有成命，二后受之。成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。」言法祖之治也。先聖後聖，其道同歸。愚敢以是爲今日獻。

第二問

同考試官教諭闞批：道顯于造化，闡于伏羲。孔子得之易，子思述之祖，孟子傳之于子思也。此篇推明玄妙，究極天人，而聖賢相傳之旨，異世同符。非深于易而會于道者，無此說。豪傑之士，非俗學可擬也。

考試官教諭文批：聖賢之言雖殊，而實同歸于道，但學者不知察識體驗之耳。發明旨趣，合異爲同，僅見此作。
translation_en:
…cultivating and establishing the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. These are the concerns of His Majesty’s sagely mind, which his servants reverently uphold without flagging. What room is there for superfluous words from one as humble as myself? The song of the court of Shun says: “When the head is enlightened and the limbs are worthy, all affairs prosper!” This speaks of the achievement of reverently heeding Heaven. The hymn to King Cheng of Zhou says: “August Heaven has an established mandate; the two sovereigns received it. King Cheng dared not rest at ease; morning and night he secured the mandate with profound serenity.” This speaks of government modeled on the ancestors. Earlier and later sages alike converge upon the same Way. I humbly venture to offer these words today.

Second Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Kan, Instructor: The Way is manifest in the workings of creation and was elucidated by Fu Xi. Confucius apprehended it in the Book of Changes; Zisi expounded it from his ancestor’s teaching [?]; and Mengzi received its transmission from Zisi. This essay elucidates profound mysteries and explores Heaven and humanity to their furthest limits, showing how the essential teaching transmitted by sages and worthies tallies across different ages. Only someone deeply versed in the Book of Changes and comprehending the Way could offer such an account. Here is a man of outstanding ability, beyond comparison with conventional scholars.

Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: Though the words of sages and worthies differ, they in fact converge upon the Way. It is simply that students do not know how to discern and understand them or realize them through personal experience. In elucidating their purport and bringing their differences into unity, this composition stands alone among those I have seen.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王　批
〔易其天地鬼神之奧斯文之鼻祖乎求道于易斯爲知本子能得之其〕
〔殆庶幾神解者耶何其言之親切有味如此高〕
〔士高士〕
執事發策秋闈以孔子之學爲問而徦以
神解之說進之豈以十室之邑必有忠信
而聖人者夫人可學而至與雖然聖道大
矣果也如由猶畫於升堂達也如賜不踰
於及有愚也何人可以語此雖然性本同
===
有聖匪由外有爲者亦若是聖人先得我
心之所同然者也敢不掇拾以就正焉夫
曷言乎孔子之學曰易而已曷言乎易曰
大極而已大極之理根抵乎天地萬物之
賾而流行乎天地萬物之中者也自夫立
象設卦伏羲示人精矣係辭盡言周文示
人博矣吾孔子承三聖之統而極修賛之
勤因卦以發藴而中正之教昭隨爻以廣
義而趨時之辨明故十翼之旨夫子斂求
punctuated:
考試官學正王批：〔易，其天地鬼神之奧、斯文之鼻祖乎？求道于易，斯爲知本。子能得之，其〕〔殆庶幾神解者耶？何其言之親切有味如此！高〕〔士，高士！〕

執事發策秋闈，以孔子之學爲問，而徦以神解之說進之，豈以十室之邑必有忠信，而聖人者夫人可學而至與？雖然，聖道大矣！果也如由，猶畫於升堂；達也如賜，不踰於及有。愚也何人，可以語此？雖然，性本同有，聖匪由外，有爲者亦若是，聖人先得我心之所同然者也。敢不掇拾以就正焉？夫曷言乎孔子之學？曰：易而已。曷言乎易？曰：大極而已。大極之理，根抵乎天地萬物之賾，而流行乎天地萬物之中者也。自夫立象設卦，伏羲示人精矣；係辭盡言，周文示人博矣。吾孔子承三聖之統，而極修賛之勤，因卦以發藴，而中正之教昭；隨爻以廣義，而趨時之辨明。故十翼之旨，夫子斂求
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔Is not the Changes the repository of the mysteries of Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits, and the progenitor of this cultural tradition? To seek the Way in the Changes is indeed to know its foundation. You have grasped it:〕〔might you have nearly attained a spiritual understanding? How immediate and full of savor your words are! An outstanding〕〔scholar, an outstanding scholar!〕

You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question for the autumn Provincial Examination, asking about Confucius’s learning and further advancing the discussion through the notion of spiritual understanding [?]. Is this because even a hamlet of ten households must contain someone loyal and trustworthy, and because anyone may attain sagehood through learning? Yet vast indeed is the Way of the sages! Even You, with his decisiveness, stopped at ascending the hall; even Ci, with his discernment, did not advance beyond “reaching and having” [?]. Who am I, in my ignorance, to speak of this? Nevertheless, human nature is something we all possess alike, and sagehood does not come from outside. Those who exert themselves can likewise become such men; the sage is simply the first to grasp what our hearts alike affirm. How could I fail to gather what I can and submit it for your correction?

What, then, can be said of Confucius’s learning? It is simply the Changes. What can be said of the Changes? It is simply the Supreme Ultimate. The principle of the Supreme Ultimate is rooted in the profundities of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, and flows throughout them. By establishing images and setting out hexagrams, Fuxi showed people what is subtle; by appending statements and fully expressing their meaning, King Wen of Zhou showed people what is extensive. Our Confucius inherited the tradition of the three sages and devoted the utmost diligence to compiling explanatory commentaries. Through the hexagrams he disclosed their hidden import, making manifest the teaching of centrality and correctness; through the individual lines he expanded their meaning, clarifying the distinctions involved in acting according to the time. Thus the purport of the Ten Wings, the Master’s gathering and seeking …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
之功也夫然后精者闡而彰博者燦而著
也其曰易知簡能者著其道也曰顯仁藏
用者彰其化也曰陰陽不測者替其神也
曰貞觀貞明貞一者昭其同也究其原也
陰陽盡之矣故曰一陰一陽之謂道又曰
立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔與剛
立人之道曰仁與義三才一貫之道茲其
的乎曰終則有始者著其運也曰變化云
爲者類其動也曰深幾而神者發其妙也
曰成變化行鬼神者明其功也究其致也
動靜貫之矣故曰變通者趨時者也又曰
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉夫
坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉三才
流行之機茲其至乎夫陰陽立三極之根
動靜神變化之用命之所以不已道之所
以無窮者其以是乎此古今流行之機也
嗚呼孔其至德矣乎此其所以承唐虞三
代之統而開萬世生民之的也三千之徒
punctuated: 之功也。夫然后精者闡而彰，博者燦而著也。其曰「易知簡能」者，著其道也；曰「顯仁藏用」者，彰其化也；曰「陰陽不測」者，替其神也；曰「貞觀貞明貞一」者，昭其同也。究其原也，陰陽盡之矣。故曰：「一陰一陽之謂道。」又曰：「立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。」三才一貫之道，茲其的乎？曰「終則有始」者，著其運也；曰「變化云爲」者，類其動也；曰「深幾而神」者，發其妙也；曰「成變化行鬼神」者，明其功也。究其致也，動靜貫之矣。故曰：「變通者，趨時者也。」又曰：「夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉；夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。」三才流行之機，茲其至乎？夫陰陽立三極之根，動靜神變化之用，命之所以不已、道之所以無窮者，其以是乎？此古今流行之機也。嗚呼！孔其至德矣乎！此其所以承唐虞三代之統，而開萬世生民之的也。三千之徒
translation_en:
…the achievement of his efforts. Only then were its subtleties expounded and made manifest, and its breadth displayed in all its brilliance. When the Changes speaks of “easy to know and simple in capability,” it makes its Way evident; when it speaks of “manifesting benevolence and concealing its functioning,” it reveals its transformations; when it speaks of “what cannot be fathomed through yin and yang,” it extols [?] its spiritual efficacy; when it speaks of “constancy in observation, constancy in illumination, and constancy in unity,” it reveals their underlying sameness. Traced to their source, they are fully comprehended by yin and yang. Thus it says: “One yin and one yang are called the Way.” It also says: “Establishing the Way of Heaven, we speak of yin and yang; establishing the Way of Earth, we speak of yielding and firm; establishing the Way of humankind, we speak of benevolence and righteousness.” Is this not the essential principle of the single Way that runs through the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humankind?

When it speaks of “an ending followed by a beginning,” it makes their cycles evident; when it speaks of “transformations, words, and deeds,” it classifies their movements; when it speaks of “depth, incipient workings, and spiritual efficacy,” it discloses their subtlety; when it speaks of “accomplishing transformations and setting ghosts and spirits in motion,” it explains their efficacy. Examined to their furthest extent, movement and stillness run through them all. Thus it says: “To change and adapt is to accord with the times.” It also says: “Qian, when still, is concentrated; when moving, it is direct. Thus it generates on a great scale. Kun, when still, is closed; when moving, it opens. Thus it generates far and wide.” Is this not the fullest expression of the workings by which the Three Powers circulate and unfold?

Yin and yang establish the root of the Three Ultimates; movement and stillness give spiritual efficacy to the operation of transformation. Is this not why Heaven’s mandate never ceases and the Way is inexhaustible? These are the workings that have circulated and unfolded throughout past and present. Ah! Surely Kongzi possessed the highest virtue! This is how he continued the succession of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, and established a standard for the people of all generations to come. His three thousand disciples…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
授受一道而克復之訓敬恕之目每惓惓
於求仁之學何哉豈易之外復有所謂仁
耶蓋道一而已矣易者言乎流行而不息
者也仁者言乎純粹而至善者也剛柔聾
慝雜揉弗齊唯仁則動靜無間流行之機
罔非天則天地萬物精粗隱顯畢該之矣
故曰動靜不失其時其道光明者此之謂
也苟不至德至道不凝君子去仁惡乎成
名故聖人著其教焉夫本一以垂訓時措
===
以成物同歸殊途百慮一致孔子而下可
以觀矣中庸一書子思衛道而作也原性
命之與立會通之準故中者言乎其不偏
也庸者言乎其不易也其曰大本云者所
以明人性之蘊靜而虛而天下之動而實
者之基也孔子所謂寂然不動者是也其
曰達道云者所以明人性之發動而神而
實靜而虛者之彰也孔子之所謂感而遂
通天下之故者是也發有已未而性無內
punctuated:
授受一道，而克復之訓、敬恕之目，每惓惓於求仁之學，何哉？豈易之外復有所謂仁耶？蓋道一而已矣。易者，言乎流行而不息者也；仁者，言乎純粹而至善者也。剛柔聾慝，雜揉弗齊；唯仁則動靜無間，流行之機罔非天則，天地萬物精粗隱顯畢該之矣。故曰：「動靜不失其時，其道光明。」者，此之謂也。苟不至德，至道不凝；君子去仁，惡乎成名？故聖人著其教焉。夫本一以垂訓，時措以成物，同歸殊途，百慮一致，孔子而下可以觀矣。
《中庸》一書，子思衛道而作也。原性命之與立，會通之準。故中者，言乎其不偏也；庸者，言乎其不易也。其曰「大本」云者，所以明人性之蘊，靜而虛，而天下之動而實者之基也。孔子所謂「寂然不動」者是也。其曰「達道」云者，所以明人性之發，動而神而實，靜而虛者之彰也。孔子之所謂「感而遂通天下之故」者是也。發有已未，而性無內
translation_en:
…transmitted and received a single Way. Yet why did the instruction to overcome the self and return to ritual propriety, and the precepts of reverence and reciprocity, repeatedly dwell upon the pursuit of benevolence? Could there be something called benevolence apart from the Changes? The Way is simply one. “Change” speaks of its ceaseless flow; “benevolence” speaks of its purity and supreme goodness. The firm and yielding, [good?] and evil, are mingled and uneven. Only in benevolence is there no interruption between activity and stillness: the workings of its flow invariably accord with Heaven’s rule, encompassing Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, whether refined or coarse, hidden or manifest. Thus the saying, “When activity and stillness do not miss their proper times, the Way is luminous,” refers to precisely this. Without consummate virtue, the consummate Way cannot be firmly established. If a gentleman abandons benevolence, how can he make good his name? Hence the sage set forth his teaching. Grounding his instruction in the one principle, he applied it as circumstances required to bring things to completion. Different paths lead to the same destination; a hundred deliberations converge upon one end. This can be observed in Confucius and those who followed him.
Zisi wrote the Doctrine of the Mean to defend the Way. It traces the foundation of human nature and Heaven’s mandate [?] and establishes a standard for comprehending their interconnections. Thus “centrality” speaks of being without偏向, and “constancy” of being unchanging. What it calls the “great foundation” elucidates what lies within human nature: still and empty, it is the basis of all that is active and substantial in the world. This is what Confucius meant by “quiescent and unmoving.” What it calls the “universally operative Way” elucidates the manifestation of human nature: active, numinous, and substantial, it is the disclosure of what is still and empty. This is what Confucius meant by “when stimulated, it thereupon penetrates the circumstances of all under Heaven.” Manifestation may have occurred or may not yet have occurred, but human nature has no inner…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
外其流行不息之機乎其曰戒懼謹獨云
者所以致其功也動靜交相存省顯微實
無間矣孔子所謂敬以直內義以方外者
是也夫動靜相生者心之神也動靜不違
者學之則也致中和而位育出焉復其初
矣子思子其善於學易者與七篇之作孟
子所以闢邪說而明王道也指本心之良
爲作聖之機故四德著言乎其蘊也純粹
精也四端著言乎其發也直方大也其曰
===
萬物皆備云者所以明人心之神靈明不
昧順以動焉四端篤善以時出之廣大悉
備也其即子思之所謂大本達道者乎其
曰性善云者蓋以人生而靜本自純粹帝
降之衷物我之所同具者也其即孔子之
所謂繼之者善而成之者性乎夫良知良
能元不喪失先立乎其大者則動靜皆定
而物欲不累窮理盡性以至於命道在我
矣孟子其善於祖述者與故曰先聖後聖
punctuated:
外，其流行不息之機乎？其曰戒懼謹獨云者，所以致其功也。動靜交相存省，顯微實無間矣。孔子所謂敬以直內，義以方外者是也。夫動靜相生者，心之神也；動靜不違者，學之則也。致中和而位育出焉，復其初矣。子思子其善於學《易》者與！
七篇之作，孟子所以闢邪說而明王道也。指本心之良爲作聖之機，故四德著，言乎其蘊也，純粹精也；四端著，言乎其發也，直方大也。其曰萬物皆備云者，所以明人心之神，靈明不昧，順以動焉，四端篤善，以時出之，廣大悉備也。其即子思之所謂大本達道者乎？其曰性善云者，蓋以人生而靜，本自純粹，帝降之衷，物我之所同具者也。其即孔子之所謂繼之者善而成之者性乎？夫良知良能元不喪失，先立乎其大者，則動靜皆定，而物欲不累。窮理盡性以至於命，道在我矣。孟子其善於祖述者與！故曰：「先聖後聖
translation_en:
…or exterior: is this not the vital working of its ceaseless flow? His statements about vigilance and apprehension, and watchfulness when alone, explain how to bring this cultivation to fulfillment. In activity and stillness, preservation and self-examination sustain one another; between the manifest and the subtle there is truly no gap. This is what Confucius meant by “reverence to straighten the inner self, righteousness to square outward conduct.” That activity and stillness generate one another is the wondrous functioning of the mind; that neither departs from its proper course is the rule of learning. When equilibrium and harmony are fully realized, Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things are nurtured: the original condition is restored. Was Master Zisi not adept at studying the Book of Changes!
Mencius composed his seven books to refute heterodox teachings and elucidate the Kingly Way. He identified the goodness of the original mind as the vital basis for becoming a sage. Thus, his exposition of the four virtues speaks of what is held within: pure, unalloyed, and refined. His exposition of the four beginnings speaks of its manifestation: straight, square, and great. His statement that “all things are complete within us” elucidates the wondrous functioning of the human mind: spiritually luminous and unobscured, it acts in accord with its nature. The four beginnings are firmly rooted in goodness [?] and are expressed at the proper times, vast and fully comprehensive. Is this not what Zisi called the great foundation and the universally prevailing Way? His statement that human nature is good rests on the understanding that human beings are still at birth and originally pure and unalloyed. The moral norm bestowed by the Lord on High is something that other beings and we ourselves alike possess. Is this not what Confucius meant by “that which continues it is goodness; that which completes it is nature”? Innate moral knowledge and innate moral ability are originally never lost. If one first establishes the greater part of oneself, both activity and stillness become settled, and material desires cease to encumber one. By investigating principle exhaustively and fully realizing one's nature, one reaches Heaven's mandate: the Way lies within oneself. Was Mencius not adept at transmitting the teachings of his predecessors! Thus it is said: “The earlier sages and the later sages …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
其揆一也雖然神而明之存乎其人道無
古今而學有機要故君子識往以論世當
求其故也是故自強不息孔子之所以配
天也戒懼謹獨子思之所以法祖也勿忘
勿助孟子之所以希孔也茍徒知其同而
不求所以同則亦空言而已夫何有哉夫
學貴自得也神解則自得矣乃若程子受
學周子而謂天理二字是自家體貼出來
非所謂神解者乎此正達于天道與聖人
===
一之時也是道也必優游涵泳長裕不設
脫然冰融凍解默識心悟有莫知其所以
然而然者矣非言語所可及也愚何足以
知之
第三問
黄觀
同考試官學正萬　批〔風俗人才關係世道最要而其機會在于上風土氣稟之說不盡然也〕
識見明透議論醇雅而才氣英發如長江大河
punctuated:
其揆一也。雖然，神而明之，存乎其人。道無古今，而學有機要，故君子識往以論世，當求其故也。是故自強不息，孔子之所以配天也；戒懼謹獨，子思之所以法祖也；勿忘勿助，孟子之所以希孔也。茍徒知其同，而不求所以同，則亦空言而已，夫何有哉？夫學貴自得也，神解則自得矣。乃若程子受學周子，而謂天理二字是自家體貼出來，非所謂神解者乎？此正達于天道、與聖人一之時也。是道也，必優游涵泳，長裕不設，脫然冰融凍解，默識心悟，有莫知其所以然而然者矣，非言語所可及也。愚何足以知之？

第三問
黄觀
同考試官學正萬，批〔風俗人才關係世道最要，而其機會在于上，風土氣稟之說不盡然也。〕
識見明透，議論醇雅，而才氣英發，如長江大河
translation_en:
…their guiding principles are one. Nevertheless, to comprehend it with spiritual insight depends upon the person. The Way does not differ between ancient and modern times, yet learning has its crucial points. Thus, when the gentleman understands the past in order to assess an age, he must seek the reasons behind it. Hence unceasing self-strengthening was how Confucius matched Heaven; vigilance, apprehension, and watchfulness when alone were how Zisi emulated his ancestor; neither forgetting nor forcing growth was how Mencius aspired to Confucius. If one merely knows that they are alike without seeking what makes them alike, this amounts only to empty words. What substance could it have? Learning values understanding attained for oneself. Through spiritual comprehension, one attains such understanding. Master Cheng studied under Master Zhou, yet said that he had personally discerned the meaning of the two characters “Heavenly principle.” Is this not what is called spiritual comprehension? This is precisely the moment when one apprehends the Way of Heaven and becomes one with the sages. In pursuing this Way, one must dwell at ease and immerse oneself in it, nurturing expansiveness without contrivance [?], until suddenly the ice melts and the frost thaws. Through silent recognition and inward awakening, something comes about without one's knowing how it does so. Words cannot reach it. How could someone as foolish as I presume to understand it?

Third Question
Huang Guan
Associate Examiner Wan, Instructor, comments: 〔Customs and talented men are of the utmost importance to the moral condition of the age, and the pivotal opportunity for shaping them lies with those above. Explanations based on local conditions and innate endowments are not entirely correct.〕
His understanding is clear and penetrating, his argumentation sound and refined, and his talent and spirit shine forth like the Yangzi and the Yellow River…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
愈流而愈無盡通塲無出子右者遠到之器也
可羨可羨
考試官教諭文　批　前二塲文氣雄渾浩然
不弱此策尤爲終塲之冠奇士奇士
考試官學正王　批　有學實有筆力非素養
之士遽無此作錄之
治天下者有化民之道有作人之功然有
本焉而統會之至一也有機焉而轉移之
至神也何也民以習染而爲風俗士以習
===
學而爲人才惟其成於習故有美有惡有
正有邪教化者所導以歸美適正之路也
然雖本之人性而或不能以強從持以漸
陶而或沮撓於時勢是以教化之不淑也
惟建極者端其本善其機以爲教化先是
故示之以觀而化自普也道之以感而應
自順也如是而家有殊俗士有異趨未之
聞也非天下之至聖其孰能與於此執事
發策以風俗人才爲問其深知王道之本
punctuated:
愈流而愈無盡，通塲無出子右者，遠到之器也。可羨！可羨！
考試官教諭文批：前二塲文氣雄渾，浩然不弱，此策尤爲終塲之冠。奇士！奇士！
考試官學正王批：有學實，有筆力，非素養之士，遽無此作。錄之。
治天下者，有化民之道，有作人之功。然有本焉，而統會之至一也；有機焉，而轉移之至神也。何也？民以習染而爲風俗，士以習學而爲人才。惟其成於習，故有美有惡，有正有邪。教化者，所導以歸美適正之路也。然雖本之人性，而或不能以強從；持以漸陶，而或沮撓於時勢。是以教化之不淑也。惟建極者，端其本，善其機，以爲教化先。是故示之以觀，而化自普也；道之以感，而應自順也。如是而家有殊俗，士有異趨，未之聞也。非天下之至聖，其孰能與於此？執事發策，以風俗人才爲問，其深知王道之本
translation_en:
…the farther it flows, the more inexhaustible it becomes. Among all the candidates, none surpasses you: you have the capacity to go far. Admirable! Admirable!
Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “The writing in the first two sessions was powerful and expansive, its vigorous spirit never flagging. This policy essay is especially outstanding, the finest of the final session. An exceptional scholar! An exceptional scholar!”
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “There is substance in his learning and strength in his writing. Someone without sustained cultivation could never produce such a composition on the spot. Include it in the record.”
Those who govern All-under-Heaven have a way of transforming the people and the task of cultivating men of talent. Yet there is a root through which these are brought into perfect unity, and a critical means through which change is effected with wondrous efficacy. Why is this? Through habitual influences, the people develop their customs; through habitual study, scholars develop into men of talent. Precisely because these are formed through habituation, there are good and bad, upright and deviant. Moral instruction is the path by which they are guided toward goodness and uprightness. Yet although it is rooted in human nature, compliance cannot always be compelled; although one persists in gradually molding people, prevailing circumstances may obstruct and frustrate the effort. This is why moral instruction fails to produce good results. Only one who establishes the supreme standard can rectify its root and properly employ its critical means, thereby taking the lead in moral instruction. Thus, when he presents an example for people to behold, transformation naturally spreads everywhere; when he guides them by moving their hearts, their response is naturally compliant. That households should then have divergent customs and scholars pursue different courses is unheard of. Who but the consummate sage of All-under-Heaven could attain this?
You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question concerning customs and men of talent, showing your profound understanding of the foundation of the Kingly Way…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
教化其有與乎愚敢不究極言之宋儒程
顥曰治天下以正風俗得賢才爲本盖風
俗者象治之迹賢才者輔治之具也民無
美俗何以善國國無其賢誰與共理先王
知其然故首重教化學校之隆師儒之選
恒究心焉而表率之道感動之理又有不
疾而速不行而至者矣是故休明之世無
澆漓之俗聖哲之朝無壬佞之臣凡以是
耳豈時數氣化之自然適會其逢哉說者
===
謂俗之不齊恒地勢拘之考古若秦齊晉
楚諸列國之風或強捍或悲愁或夸靡儉
嗇種種異習大都狃於水土風氣之一偏
者雖賢者有所不免王制曰廣谷大川異
制民生其間異俗若聲音言語之不相比
是奚害哉修其教不易其俗齊其政不異
其宜而已謂才之弗齊亦天賦拘之稽古
若皐夔稷契共驩苗鯀暨諸叔季之臣或
聖或狂或賢或不肖邈乎弗類大都定於
punctuated:
教化其有與乎？愚敢不究極言之！宋儒程顥曰：「治天下以正風俗、得賢才爲本。」盖風俗者，象治之迹；賢才者，輔治之具也。民無美俗，何以善國？國無其賢，誰與共理？先王知其然，故首重教化。學校之隆、師儒之選，恒究心焉。而表率之道、感動之理，又有不疾而速、不行而至者矣。是故休明之世無澆漓之俗，聖哲之朝無壬佞之臣，凡以是耳。豈時數氣化之自然，適會其逢哉？
說者謂俗之不齊，恒地勢拘之。考古若秦、齊、晉、楚諸列國之風，或強捍，或悲愁，或夸靡、儉嗇，種種異習，大都狃於水土風氣之一偏者，雖賢者有所不免。《王制》曰：「廣谷大川異制，民生其間異俗。」若聲音言語之不相比，是奚害哉？修其教，不易其俗；齊其政，不異其宜而已。謂才之弗齊，亦天賦拘之。稽古若皐、夔、稷、契、共、驩、苗、鯀，暨諸叔季之臣，或聖，或狂，或賢，或不肖，邈乎弗類，大都定於
translation_en:
…might you have a part in moral instruction? How could I, in my ignorance, dare not discuss this exhaustively! The Song Confucian Cheng Hao said: “Governing All under Heaven rests on rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talent.” Customs are the visible traces of government; worthy talents are the means of assisting it. Without good customs among the people, how can the state be made good? Without worthy men in the state, with whom can one share its governance? The former kings understood this and therefore gave foremost importance to moral instruction. They constantly applied their minds to fostering schools and selecting learned teachers. Moreover, the way of setting an example and the principle of moving others can produce swift results without haste and reach their goal without going forth. Thus, an age of enlightened peace has no degenerate customs, and a court of sagely wisdom has no deceitful, flattering ministers. All this comes from these means alone. Could it merely be a fortunate coincidence arising naturally from the cycles of time and transformations of vital energy?
Some argue that differences in customs are invariably constrained by geography. Looking back to antiquity, the customs of the various states—Qin, Qi, Jin, Chu, and others—were sometimes fierce and defiant, sometimes sorrowful, sometimes extravagant or frugal and parsimonious. These diverse habits largely arose from habituation to a particular local influence of water, soil, climate, and vital energy; even worthy men could not entirely escape them. “Royal Regulations” states: “Broad valleys and great rivers differ in configuration; the people living among them differ in customs.” If their sounds and speech do not match, what harm is there in that? Simply improve their instruction without changing their customs, and bring their government into order without departing from what suits them.
Others argue that differences in talent are likewise constrained by Heaven’s endowment. Looking back to antiquity, Gao, Kui, Ji, Xie, Gonggong, Huandou, the Sanmiao, and Gun, together with the ministers of declining ages, were variously sagely or wayward, worthy or unworthy, and vastly unlike one another. These differences were largely determined by…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
氣質清濁之殊絶者雖聖代有不能齊孔
子曰惟上智與下愚不移真若陰陽晝夜
之相反然豈盡若是哉性本同善而緣習
則殊教以反同亦因材以篤而已是故先
王有教民之制若禮樂刑政詳於周禮而
掌於大司徒以施十有二教所以納民於
軌物範俗於大同者莫良矣然後世之教
不盡殊而協和時雍之風遠乎絶響何也
蓋媚兹一人者百姓之心而朝廷則四方
===
之極教化之所從出也順帝之則本於篤
恭之盛若好尚舉動又自近達遠四望以
爲趨向者也先王所以化成俗美者亦率
之以德行端之以好尚潛乎而黙化之不
獨禮樂刑政而已傳云堯舜率天下以仁
而民從之桀紂率天下以暴而民從之言
教有本也商之政尚猛故其俗激昂而奮
厲周之政尚寛故其俗和柔而寛緩言化
有機也後世若漢文帝躬行元黙而黎民
punctuated:
氣質清濁之殊絶者，雖聖代有不能齊。孔子曰：「惟上智與下愚不移。」真若陰陽晝夜之相反然，豈盡若是哉？性本同善，而緣習則殊；教以反同，亦因材以篤而已。是故先王有教民之制，若禮樂刑政，詳於《周禮》，而掌於大司徒，以施十有二教，所以納民於軌物、範俗於大同者，莫良矣。然後世之教不盡殊，而協和時雍之風遠乎絶響，何也？
蓋媚兹一人者，百姓之心，而朝廷則四方之極，教化之所從出也。順帝之則，本於篤恭之盛；若好尚舉動，又自近達遠，四望以爲趨向者也。先王所以化成俗美者，亦率之以德行，端之以好尚，潛乎而黙化之，不獨禮樂刑政而已。傳云：「堯舜率天下以仁，而民從之；桀紂率天下以暴，而民從之。」言教有本也。商之政尚猛，故其俗激昂而奮厲；周之政尚寛，故其俗和柔而寛緩。言化有機也。後世若漢文帝躬行元黙，而黎民
translation_en:
…the profound differences in the clarity or turbidity of their psychophysical endowments: even in an age of sage rule, some cannot be brought into uniformity. Confucius said, “Only the highest in wisdom and the lowest in folly do not change.” They truly seem as opposed as yin and yang, or day and night. Yet can everyone be like this? Human nature is originally alike in goodness, but acquired habits produce differences. Teaching restores that original likeness, simply nurturing each according to their capacities. Thus the former kings established institutions for educating the people, such as rites, music, punishments, and government. These are set out in detail in the Rites of Zhou and administered by the Minister of Education, who implements the twelve teachings. Nothing could better bring the people within proper norms and shape customs toward great unity. Yet the teachings of later ages are not entirely different, while the spirit of harmony and concord has long ceased to be heard. Why is this?
For it is the heart of the common people to love this one man, the sovereign; and the court is the pole toward which the four quarters turn, the source from which moral instruction proceeds. Conformity to the standards of the Lord on High rests upon the fullness of the ruler’s profound reverence. His preferences and actions, moreover, exert an influence that spreads from near to far: people in every direction look to them for guidance. The former kings transformed the people and perfected their customs by leading them through virtuous conduct, setting them right through their preferences, and transforming them imperceptibly and silently. They did not rely solely on rites, music, punishments, and government. The commentary says, “Yao and Shun led all under Heaven through benevolence, and the people followed them; Jie and Zhou led all under Heaven through violence, and the people followed them.” This means that teaching has a root. The government of Shang prized severity, and therefore its customs were impassioned and forceful; the government of Zhou prized leniency, and therefore its customs were gentle and relaxed. This means that transformation has a moving spring. In later ages, for example, Emperor Wen of Han personally practiced quiet restraint, and the common people …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
醇厚唐太宗篤行仁義而外戶不閉亦其
近之不然晉尚崇虛浮而清談縱恣之風熾
豈當時禮樂之教遽淪絕哉由是觀之禮
樂刑政者教化之具譬則舟楫也師儒其
篙師也朝廷之德化譬則江海而好尚則
天之風也舟楫非風水之利能自運哉風
俗之醇王道之應也有天德便可語王道
謂教化不本於朝廷而能一道德同風俗
可乎先王有教士之法若詩書學校備於
===
周禮而詳於後世經制之書無非推廣三
物之教所以正德以成賢育才以昌業者
莫美矣然後世之法制益詳而賢聖忠貞
之士代不多見何也蓋共惟帝臣者士之
心而帝則兼君師之責教化之主盟也觀
化之樞本於中和之極若好惡用舍乂中
智之士恒覘以轉移者也先王所以教孚
而人化者亦視之以率履端之以好惡身
教而默諭之不獨詩書學校而已觀堯以
banxin: 鄉試錄 文 三十三
punctuated:
醇厚，唐太宗篤行仁義而外戶不閉，亦其近之。不然，晉尚崇虛浮，而清談縱恣之風熾，豈當時禮樂之教遽淪絕哉？由是觀之，禮樂刑政者，教化之具，譬則舟楫也；師儒，其篙師也；朝廷之德化，譬則江海，而好尚則天之風也。舟楫非風水之利，能自運哉？風俗之醇，王道之應也。有天德，便可語王道。謂教化不本於朝廷，而能一道德、同風俗，可乎？

先王有教士之法，若詩書學校，備於《周禮》，而詳於後世經制之書，無非推廣三物之教。所以正德以成賢、育才以昌業者，莫美矣。然後世之法制益詳，而賢聖忠貞之士代不多見，何也？蓋共惟帝臣者，士之心，而帝則兼君師之責，教化之主盟也。觀化之樞，本於中和之極；若好惡用舍，乂中智之士恒覘以轉移者也。先王所以教孚而人化者，亦視之以率履，端之以好惡，身教而默諭之，不獨詩書學校而已。觀堯以
translation_en:
…were simple and honest. Emperor Taizong of the Tang earnestly practiced benevolence and righteousness, so that outer doors were left unbolted: this, too, approached that ideal. Conversely, under the Jin, people prized vacuity and superficiality, and a fashion for unrestrained “pure conversation” flourished. Could instruction through rites and music then have suddenly fallen into complete neglect? Viewed in this light, rites, music, punishments, and government are the instruments of moral transformation, comparable to boats and oars; teachers and Confucian scholars are their boatmen. The court’s transforming virtue is like the rivers and seas, and its preferences are like the winds of Heaven. Without favorable wind and water, can boats and oars move of themselves? The purity of customs is the response elicited by the Kingly Way. Only with Heaven’s virtue can one speak of the Kingly Way. Is it possible to claim that moral instruction need not have its foundation in the court, yet can unify moral principles and make customs uniform?

The former kings had methods for educating scholars, such as the Poetry, the Documents, and schools. These are fully set out in the Rites of Zhou and elaborated in later books on institutions and regulations; all extend instruction in the three categories of virtue, conduct, and the arts. Nothing could better rectify virtue to form worthy men, or nurture talent to make great undertakings flourish. Yet although the institutions and regulations of later ages became increasingly detailed, worthy, sagely, loyal, and steadfast scholars were seldom seen in any generation. Why was this? It is because “all are the emperor’s ministers” expresses the scholars’ disposition, while the emperor combines the responsibilities of ruler and teacher and presides over moral transformation. The pivot of the transformation people observe lies in the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. As for likes and dislikes, appointments and dismissals, these are also [?] what men of middling understanding constantly watch, adjusting themselves accordingly. The former kings made their teaching inspire trust and transform people by showing them proper conduct and rectifying them through their likes and dislikes. They taught through personal example and imparted understanding without words, rather than relying solely on the Poetry, the Documents, and schools. Consider how Yao, by …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
執中命舜而開羣聖道統之源文王以豈
弟作人而臻棫樸菁莪之化非躬行心得
之教乎舜選於衆舉皋陶而不仁者遠湯
選於衆舉伊尹而不仁者遠非轉移鼓舞
之機乎後世若唐尚詞章而窮達皆藝苑
之士宋崇道學而朝野多希聖之英亦其
驗矣不然漢靈帝喜陳方俗語而無行趨
勢之徒並列鴻都門學非當時學校之崇
亦罔而已耶由是觀之詩書學校者教化
===
之文譬則風雨霜露也師儒則四時五行
之吏也人主之淵德耶天之於穆不已好
惡則陰陽舒慘也風雨霜露非於穆舒慘
之運能不忒哉人文之盛王化之昭也有
內聖之德斯有外王之業謂教化不本於
人主而謂師道得善人多可乎嗚呼玆至
治之基大化之本而恭己無爲之業也並
休麗美不有待於
今日哉愚何幸躬逢其
punctuated: 執中命舜，而開羣聖道統之源；文王以豈弟作人，而臻棫樸菁莪之化，非躬行心得之教乎？舜選於衆，舉皋陶，而不仁者遠；湯選於衆，舉伊尹，而不仁者遠，非轉移鼓舞之機乎？後世若唐尚詞章，而窮達皆藝苑之士；宋崇道學，而朝野多希聖之英，亦其驗矣。不然，漢靈帝喜陳方俗語，而無行趨勢之徒並列鴻都門學，非當時學校之崇亦罔而已耶？由是觀之，詩書學校者，教化之文，譬則風雨霜露也；師儒則四時五行之吏也。人主之淵德耶，天之於穆不已；好惡則陰陽舒慘也。風雨霜露非於穆舒慘之運，能不忒哉？人文之盛，王化之昭也。有內聖之德，斯有外王之業。謂教化不本於人主，而謂師道得、善人多，可乎？嗚呼！玆至治之基、大化之本，而恭己無爲之業也。並休麗美，不有待於今日哉？愚何幸躬逢其
translation_en:
…charged Shun to hold fast to the mean, thereby opening the source of the succession of the Way among the sages. King Wen cultivated men through his ease and graciousness, bringing about the transforming influence celebrated in “The Oak Trees” (Yupu) and “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing’e). Was this not instruction through personal practice and inward understanding? Shun selected from the multitude and raised Gao Yao to office, and those lacking benevolence withdrew; Tang selected from the multitude and raised Yi Yin to office, and those lacking benevolence withdrew. Was this not the means of transforming and inspiring people? In later ages, the Tang esteemed literary composition, and men both obscure and prominent belonged to the literary world; the Song honored the Learning of the Way, and both at court and outside it there were many outstanding men who aspired to sagehood. These, too, bear witness to its efficacy. Conversely, Emperor Ling of the Han delighted in presentations of local vernacular expressions, and men without moral conduct who courted the powerful filled the Hongdu Gate School. Was not the exaltation of schools at that time therefore futile?

Viewed in this light, the Poetry and Documents and the schools are the outward forms of moral instruction, comparable to wind, rain, frost, and dew. Confucian teachers are the officials administering the four seasons and five phases. The ruler’s profound virtue is like Heaven’s unfathomable, unceasing activity [?]; his likes and dislikes are like the gentleness and severity of yin and yang. Without the operation of that unfathomable activity, with its gentleness and severity, could wind, rain, frost, and dew remain free of deviation? The flourishing of human culture manifests the transforming influence of kingship. Only with the virtue of inward sagehood can there be the achievement of outward kingship. Can one claim that moral instruction is not rooted in the ruler, yet also claim that the Way of teaching is properly realized and good men are numerous?

Ah! This is the foundation of perfect order, the root of great transformation, and the achievement of reverently ordering oneself and governing without action. Does the matching of past excellence and the display of beauty not await this very day? How fortunate am I, in my ignorance, personally to witness its…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
盛
第四問
孫元卿
同考試官教諭甘　批　數乃天地自然之妙而理
實主之此作以理論數以數準理得之矣故表
而出之
考試官教諭文　批　博洽之學明決之才正
大之氣俱于此策見之
考試官學正王　批　理數之學精到不忒而
議論無窮天下事可與言矣可敬可敬
===
洩天地之蘊者其數乎會數之精者其神
乎數也者理之時也化之紀也天地非數
則道化幾不可測而識矣神也者道之樞
也聖之極也數非神聖則精閟殆不可會
而通矣是故一定而不易者數之體變動
而不居者數之用錯綜皆合而變化無窮
茲其爲天地之蘊乎茲其爲數之精乎非
天下之至神其孰能與於此故曰神而明
punctuated:
盛。
第四問
孫元卿
同考試官教諭甘批：數乃天地自然之妙，而理實主之。此作以理論數，以數準理，得之矣，故表而出之。
考試官教諭文批：博洽之學，明決之才，正大之氣，俱于此策見之。
考試官學正王批：理數之學，精到不忒，而議論無窮，天下事可與言矣。可敬！可敬！
洩天地之蘊者，其數乎？會數之精者，其神乎？數也者，理之時也，化之紀也。天地非數，則道化幾不可測而識矣。神也者，道之樞也，聖之極也。數非神聖，則精閟殆不可會而通矣。是故一定而不易者，數之體；變動而不居者，數之用。錯綜皆合，而變化無窮，茲其爲天地之蘊乎？茲其爲數之精乎？非天下之至神，其孰能與於此？故曰：「神而明
translation_en:
…this flourishing age.

Fourth Policy Question
Sun Yuanqing

Comment by Associate Examiner Gan, Instructor: Numerical order is the naturally arising marvel of Heaven and Earth, yet principle truly governs it. This essay discusses numerical order through principle and uses numerical order to verify principle. It has grasped the matter; hence I single it out for presentation.

Comment by Examiner Wen, Instructor: Extensive learning, a discerning and decisive talent, and an upright and noble spirit are all manifest in this policy essay.

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: His learning concerning principle and numerical order is penetrating and unerring, and his arguments are inexhaustible. One may discuss the affairs of the world with him. Admirable! Admirable!

Is it not numerical order that discloses the hidden mysteries of Heaven and Earth? Is it not spiritual efficacy that comprehends the essence of numerical order? Numerical order is the temporal expression of principle and the ordering framework of transformation. Without numerical order, the transformations of the Way in Heaven and Earth would scarcely be fathomable or knowable. Spiritual efficacy is the pivot of the Way and the highest reach of sagehood. Without spiritual insight and sagehood, the hidden essence of numerical order could scarcely be comprehended and penetrated. Thus, what is fixed and unchanging is the substance of numerical order; what shifts and never rests is its operation. Its interweavings all accord, while its transformations are inexhaustible: is this not the hidden mystery of Heaven and Earth? Is this not the essence of numerical order? Who but one possessing the utmost spiritual insight in the world could participate in this? Hence it is said: “To apprehend it spiritually and make it clear…”

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
之存乎其人知此則圖書衍極之數可得
而言矣夫是數也原於冥漠之無形而拆
於儀象之既判極之日月星辰之麗山岳
川澤之奠皆數之著也四時五行之運萬
類羣形之布皆數之化也玄覽於象帝之
先是即畫前之易矣誰謂數昉於圖書哉
可以順性命之理可以研事物之端推之
典禮秩於聖人蓍數之教也經畫備於王
制蓍數之度也深明乎天地之撰斯亦形
===
上之道也誰謂儒者不貴數哉惟河圖之
出適值夫伏羲之神靈仰觀俯察遠求近
取蓋已默感而冥會之故天苞之說雖甚
誣而其彰乾坤之象以昭文明之瑞若開
物成務之必於其時謂天無因而不愛玆
道不可也洛書之出適當夫大禹之神聖
治水底績地平天成蓋亦冥召而洞契之
故地符之說雖甚誕而其演玄武之精以
昭水德之盛若陳疇類範之必於其人謂
punctuated: 之，存乎其人。」知此，則圖書衍極之數可得而言矣。夫是數也，原於冥漠之無形，而拆於儀象之既判。極之，日月星辰之麗，山岳川澤之奠，皆數之著也；四時五行之運，萬類羣形之布，皆數之化也。玄覽於象帝之先，是即畫前之易矣，誰謂數昉於圖書哉？可以順性命之理，可以研事物之端。推之，典禮秩於聖人，蓍數之教也；經畫備於王制，蓍數之度也。深明乎天地之撰，斯亦形上之道也，誰謂儒者不貴數哉？惟河圖之出，適值夫伏羲之神靈，仰觀俯察，遠求近取，蓋已默感而冥會之。故天苞之說雖甚誣，而其彰乾坤之象，以昭文明之瑞，若開物成務之必於其時，謂天無因而不愛玆道，不可也。洛書之出，適當夫大禹之神聖，治水底績，地平天成，蓋亦冥召而洞契之。故地符之說雖甚誕，而其演玄武之精，以昭水德之盛，若陳疇類範之必於其人，謂
translation_en:
…bringing it to spiritual efficacy and illumination depends upon the person.” Knowing this, we can discuss the numbers of the River Chart and Luo Writing and their extension to the utmost.

These numbers originate in the formless obscurity and become differentiated [?] once configurations and images have taken distinct form. Pursuing this to its fullest extent, the sun, moon, and stars arrayed above, and the mountains, rivers, and marshes established below, are all manifestations of number. The movements of the four seasons and five phases, and the distribution of the myriad kinds and forms, are all transformations of number. To contemplate mysteriously what precedes even the Lord on High is to apprehend the Changes before its lines were drawn. Who says that number began with the Chart and Writing? Through it one can follow the principles of human nature and destiny and investigate the beginnings of things and affairs. Extending this further, the ordering of ceremonies and rites by the sages is the instruction of yarrow-stalk numbers; the comprehensive arrangements of kingly institutions are their measures. To understand profoundly the workings of Heaven and Earth is also the Way beyond physical form. Who says that Confucians do not value number?

The emergence of the River Chart coincided precisely with the numinous wisdom of Fu Xi. Looking upward and examining below, seeking afar and drawing upon what was near, he had already responded to it silently and comprehended it in mystery. Thus, although the account of a heavenly envelope is deeply false, the Chart displayed the images of Qian and Kun, Heaven and Earth, revealing an auspicious sign of cultural illumination, as though the disclosure of things and accomplishment of affairs necessarily belonged to that time. It would be unacceptable to say that Heaven had no reason for ceasing to withhold this Way.

The emergence of the Luo Writing coincided precisely with the spiritual sagacity of Yu the Great. He brought the control of the waters to completion: the earth was made level and Heaven’s work accomplished. He too had summoned it mysteriously and attained a penetrating accord with it. Thus, although the account of an earthly talisman is deeply extravagant, the Writing unfolded the essence of the Dark Warrior, revealing the fullness of the virtue of Water, as though setting forth the categories and arranging the norms necessarily depended upon that person. To say…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
地無故而不愛茲寶不可也然今考圖之
數五十有五書之數四十有五多寡不同
而方圓弗類何也蓋圖員象天而爲數十
偶贏奇乏之數之全也書方象地而爲數九
奇贏偶乏數之變也圖書皆以五居中虛
其中則太極也奇偶均二十者兩儀也圖
虛其十亦四十五數也書九疇之子數則
亦五十五數也參伍錯綜而無適不合其
變化之道神之所爲乎二數之名異而理
===
同二聖之時異而心同所謂聖人成能均
也劉歆經緯之說不可見哉倚數之法聖
人參天兩地教天下揲蓍求易使不迷於
吉凶悔吝之途者然圖數五十有五大衍
五十而虛一何也蓋其用四十九者蓍之
德七重之則爲四十九猶卦之德八重之
而爲六十四也虛一者不用而用以之通
非數而數興之成斯太極也故參於圖則
其虛五而爲五十之數矣質於書即其以
punctuated:
地無故而不愛茲寶，不可也。然今考圖之數五十有五，書之數四十有五，多寡不同，而方圓弗類，何也？蓋圖員象天，而爲數十，偶贏奇乏之數之全也；書方象地，而爲數九，奇贏偶乏，數之變也。圖書皆以五居中，虛其中則太極也；奇偶均二十者，兩儀也。圖虛其十，亦四十五數也；書九疇之子數，則亦五十五數也。參伍錯綜，而無適不合，其變化之道，神之所爲乎？二數之名異而理同，二聖之時異而心同，所謂聖人成能，均也。劉歆經緯之說，不可見哉？

倚數之法，聖人參天兩地，教天下揲蓍求易，使不迷於吉凶悔吝之途者。然圖數五十有五，大衍五十而虛一，何也？蓋其用四十九者，蓍之德七，重之則爲四十九，猶卦之德八，重之而爲六十四也。虛一者，不用而用以之通，非數而數興之成，斯太極也。故參於圖，則其虛五而爲五十之數矣；質於書，即其以
translation_en:
…it cannot be said that Earth had no reason for cherishing this treasure. Yet if we now examine the numbers of the River Chart, they total fifty-five, while those of the Luo Writing total forty-five. Why do their totals differ, and why are their forms unlike, one square and the other round? The Chart is round, imaging Heaven, and its numbers extend to ten: with the even numbers exceeding the odd, it represents the completeness of number. The Writing is square, imaging Earth, and its numbers extend to nine: with the odd numbers exceeding the even, it represents the transformation of number. Both the Chart and the Writing place five at the center; leaving that center empty represents the Supreme Ultimate. The odd and even numbers each totaling twenty represent the Two Modes. If ten is omitted from the Chart, its numbers likewise total forty-five; the subsidiary numbers of the Writing’s Nine Categories likewise total fifty-five. Combined and interwoven in diverse ways, they agree in every instance. Is this way of change and transformation the working of the numinous? The two numerical systems differ in name but share the same principle; the two sages lived in different ages but shared the same mind. In what is called the sage’s bringing inherent capacities to fulfillment, they were alike. Can we not discern here Liu Xin’s explanation in terms of warp and weft?

As for the method of reckoning by numbers, the sages assigned three to Heaven and two to Earth, teaching all under Heaven to manipulate yarrow stalks and consult the Changes, so that they would not lose their way amid good fortune, misfortune, remorse, and humiliation. Yet the Chart’s numbers total fifty-five, whereas the Great Expansion uses fifty and sets one aside. Why is this? Forty-nine are used because the inherent numerical potency of the yarrow stalks is seven; multiplying it by itself gives forty-nine, just as the inherent numerical potency of the trigrams is eight, which, multiplied by itself, gives sixty-four. The one set aside is unused, yet through it use becomes possible; it is not a number, yet through it numbers attain completion [?]. This is the Supreme Ultimate. Thus, compared with the Chart, it is the number fifty obtained by leaving out five; checked against the Writing, it is its taking…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
五含五而爲五十之數矣橫斜曲直無所
不通其造化之精天機之妙乎諸數殊塗
而同歸三聖異慮而一致所謂窮神知化
均也朱子符契之說其不然哉易更四聖
而象已著孰有演其數如邵康節者令觀
皇極經世之書以元會運世而羅絡天地
萬物之終始治道人事之得失汪洋浩大
無所不該雖作用不同辭近牽合而妙悟
神契祖述羲畫雄成一家之言斯亦作者
===
之流亞與考其數則陽用三十陰用十二
元會運世歲月日辰之數極於六十四而
一元之運始於日月星辰甲子皆造化自
然之妙而圖衍之派詳矣不然振古之豪
傑程子屑許之哉惜門戶不同學偏術數
使天根月窟之襟内聖外王之道不獲與
於斯文之正印耳範錫神禹而數弗傳孰
有補之如蔡九峯者令觀洪範皇極之篇
以性命禮義爲宗而體尚中正教主民彝
punctuated:
五含五而爲五十之數矣。橫斜曲直，無所不通，其造化之精、天機之妙乎！諸數殊塗而同歸，三聖異慮而一致，所謂窮神知化均也。朱子符契之說，其不然哉！
易更四聖而象已著，孰有演其數如邵康節者？令觀《皇極經世》之書，以元會運世而羅絡天地萬物之終始、治道人事之得失，汪洋浩大，無所不該。雖作用不同，辭近牽合，而妙悟神契，祖述羲畫，雄成一家之言，斯亦作者之流亞與！考其數，則陽用三十，陰用十二，元會運世、歲月日辰之數極於六十四，而一元之運始於日月星辰甲子，皆造化自然之妙，而圖衍之派詳矣。不然，振古之豪傑程子屑許之哉！惜門戶不同，學偏術數，使天根月窟之襟、内聖外王之道，不獲與於斯文之正印耳。
範錫神禹而數弗傳，孰有補之如蔡九峯者？令觀《洪範皇極》之篇，以性命禮義爲宗，而體尚中正，教主民彝。
translation_en:
…five containing five makes the number fifty. Horizontally and diagonally, crookedly and straight, it works in every direction: is this not the essence of creation and transformation, the subtlety of Heaven’s workings? The various numbers follow different paths but reach the same destination; the Three Sages deliberate differently but arrive at one conclusion. They are alike in what is called plumbing the spiritual and understanding transformation. Is not Master Zhu’s account of their matching like the halves of a tally correct?
The Changes passed through four sages, and its images were already manifest; yet who has elaborated its numbers as Shao Kangjie did? Consider [?] his Book of the Supreme Principle for Ordering the World (Huangji jingshi). Through epochs, assemblies, cycles, and generations, it encompasses the beginnings and ends of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, and the successes and failures of governance and human affairs. Vast and boundless, it leaves nothing out. Although its applications differ and its wording verges on forced connections, through subtle insight and spiritual accord it carries forward Fuxi’s hexagram lines and grandly establishes a school of thought of its own. Surely he ranks just below the original creators! Examining his numbers, we find that yang employs thirty and yin twelve. The numbers of epochs, assemblies, cycles, and generations, and of years, months, days, and double-hours, culminate in sixty-four; the movement of a single epoch begins with the sun, moon, stars, and celestial stations at jiazi [?]. All express the spontaneous subtlety of creation and transformation, and the line of development from the River Chart and the Great Expansion is set out in detail. Otherwise, would Master Cheng, an outstanding man of all antiquity, have deigned to approve him? It is regrettable that, because his school differed and his learning inclined toward numerical arts, his breadth of mind embracing the root of Heaven and the cavern of the moon, and his Way of inward sagehood and outward kingship, were not admitted to the authoritative transmission of this cultural tradition.
The Great Plan was bestowed upon divine Yu, but its numbers were not transmitted. Who has supplied what was missing as Cai Jiufeng did? Consider [?] his work The Great Plan and the Supreme Principle (Hongfan huangji): it takes human nature, destiny, ritual propriety, and righteousness as its guiding principles; its substance esteems centrality and correctness, and its teaching centers on the constant moral norms of the people…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
祛迷障懲因事示戒雖學紹父師靡同易
象煞深造自得同歸易理直欲完補古文
之缺斯亦述者之雄傑與求其數則始於
一參於三究於九成於八十一備於六千
五百六十一散之無外卷之無內體諸造
化而不可遺而洛數之原昭矣不然與三
聖之易同功真氏其浪言哉惜享數弗遐
擇數未備使知來藏往之妙獨立物表之
見不能無俟於後之君子耳由是觀之因
===
道契數而因數闡道者羲禹孔子也聖之
神者也以靜觀數而緣數見道者邵子也
人之豪者也邵蔡之餘若洞極用書潛虛
用圖非無作也而牽合附會數滋晦矣京
房之易郭璞之技非無作也而非禮畔道
君子不由焉程子謂有之無所補無之靡
所闕非若斯人之所爲乎執事曰數即氣
也氣之流行即理也茲不亦達道之言而
深乎其數者哉愚請得究言之物必有則
punctuated:
祛迷障，懲因事示戒。雖學紹父師，靡同易象，煞深造自得，同歸易理，直欲完補古文之缺，斯亦述者之雄傑與！求其數，則始於一，參於三，究於九，成於八十一，備於六千五百六十一。散之無外，卷之無內，體諸造化而不可遺，而洛數之原昭矣。不然，與三聖之易同功，真氏其浪言哉？惜享數弗遐，擇數未備，使知來藏往之妙、獨立物表之見，不能無俟於後之君子耳。
由是觀之，因道契數而因數闡道者，羲、禹、孔子也，聖之神者也；以靜觀數而緣數見道者，邵子也，人之豪者也。邵、蔡之餘，若洞極用書，潛虛用圖，非無作也，而牽合附會，數滋晦矣。京房之易，郭璞之技，非無作也，而非禮畔道，君子不由焉。程子謂：「有之無所補，無之靡所闕。」非若斯人之所爲乎？執事曰：「數即氣也，氣之流行即理也。」茲不亦達道之言，而深乎其數者哉？愚請得究言之：物必有則
translation_en:
…dispelling delusion and obstruction, and drawing admonitions from events [?]. Although his learning continued that of his father and teacher, it did not follow the images of the Changes; through profound study and independent understanding [?], it nevertheless arrived at the same principles as the Changes. His intention was nothing less than to fill the gaps in the ancient text. Was he not an outstanding figure among transmitters of tradition? Examining his numbers, we find that they begin with one, proceed through three, reach nine, take form at eighty-one, and attain completeness at six thousand five hundred and sixty-one. Expanded, they leave nothing outside; drawn together, they leave nothing within. They embody the transformations of creation, leaving nothing out, and thus illuminate the source of the numbers of the Luo River Writing. Otherwise, would Master Zhen have spoken idly in saying that this work equaled the achievement of the Changes of the three sages? Regrettably, his allotted lifespan was not long, and his selection of numbers remained incomplete [?]. Thus the marvel of knowing what is to come and storing what has passed, and his insight standing beyond the realm of things, still had to await later gentlemen.
Viewed in this light, those who accorded with numbers through the Way and elucidated the Way through numbers were Fuxi, Yu, and Kongzi: sages of wondrous understanding. The one who contemplated numbers in stillness and perceived the Way through them was Master Shao: an outstanding man. Beyond Shao and Cai, works such as Penetrating the Ultimate (Dongji), employing writing, and Fathoming the Void (Qianxu), employing diagrams, were certainly undertakings of substance; yet their strained connections and forced correspondences only made numbers more obscure. Jing Fang’s interpretation of the Changes and Guo Pu’s techniques were likewise undertakings of substance; yet they contravened ritual propriety and departed from the Way, so gentlemen would not follow them. Master Cheng said, “Their presence adds nothing; their absence leaves nothing lacking.” Does this not describe what such men produced? You, sir, say: “Numbers are precisely qi; the circulation of qi is precisely principle.” Are these not the words of one who comprehends the Way and understands numbers profoundly? Permit me, in my ignorance, to explore this fully: things necessarily have their governing norms…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
數者盡天下之物則也事必有理數者盡
天下之事理也中人以上達乎數者也中
人以下囿於數者也聖人因數以明理所
以教天下後世也君子因數以明理所以
自淑其身也是故探天地運化之原參人
物古今之變窮義理之精微究興亡之徵
兆微顯闡幽彝倫攸叙秩然有天地萬物
各得其所之妙夫是謂以理觀數而非以
數觀數者與邵子曰天地之本其起於中
===
乎人居天地之中心居人之中君子能主
靜以觀中之體致一以窺數之原則未發
之中即天地之蘊既發之和即羣聖之道
斯可以得意而忘言窮理而樂天矣斯可
以達命而順義循理而致和矣尚有理與
數之殊哉是以君子貴中也謹對
第五問
殷士儋
同考試官教諭魏　批　時務一策難認識亦難
punctuated:
數者，盡天下之物則也。事必有理，數者，盡天下之事理也。中人以上，達乎數者也；中人以下，囿於數者也。聖人因數以明理，所以教天下後世也；君子因數以明理，所以自淑其身也。是故探天地運化之原，參人物古今之變，窮義理之精微，究興亡之徵兆，微顯闡幽，彝倫攸叙，秩然有天地萬物各得其所之妙。夫是謂以理觀數，而非以數觀數者與？邵子曰：「天地之本，其起於中乎？」人居天地之中，心居人之中。君子能主靜以觀中之體，致一以窺數之原，則未發之中即天地之蘊，既發之和即羣聖之道。斯可以得意而忘言，窮理而樂天矣；斯可以達命而順義，循理而致和矣。尚有理與數之殊哉？是以君子貴中也。謹對。

第五問
殷士儋
同考試官教諭魏批：時務一策，難認識，亦難
translation_en:
…Numerical patterns encompass the governing norms of all things under Heaven. Affairs necessarily have principles; numerical patterns encompass the principles of all affairs under Heaven. Those of above-average capacity comprehend numerical patterns; those of below-average capacity are confined by them. Sages use numerical patterns to illuminate principle, thereby teaching the world and later generations; gentlemen use numerical patterns to illuminate principle, thereby cultivating their own persons. Thus they investigate the source of Heaven and Earth’s workings and transformations, examine changes in people and things across past and present, fathom the subtleties of moral principle, and investigate the portents of rise and decline. They bring the subtle to light and elucidate the hidden [?], and the enduring human relationships are duly ordered. In this orderly arrangement lies the marvel of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things each attaining its proper place. Is this not what is meant by viewing numerical patterns through principle, rather than viewing numerical patterns through numerical patterns?

Master Shao said: “Does the foundation of Heaven and Earth not originate in the center?” Human beings occupy the center of Heaven and Earth, and the heart-mind occupies the center of the human being. If the gentleman can make stillness his guiding practice to contemplate the substance of equilibrium, and attain unity to discern the source of numerical patterns, then equilibrium before the feelings are aroused is the inner essence of Heaven and Earth, and harmony after they are aroused is the Way of all the sages. He can then grasp the meaning and forget the words, fathom principle and delight in Heaven. He can comprehend destiny and follow righteousness, accord with principle and bring about harmony. What distinction would then remain between principle and numerical patterns? This is why the gentleman prizes equilibrium. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question
Yin Shidan 殷士儋
Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: “In a policy essay on current affairs, understanding is difficult, and it is also difficult to…”

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
議處此作曲盡利弊而作用有條真可見之施
設況才思充周知天馬行空無所拘泥經濟之
〔才也錄之〕
考試官教諭文　批〔有學有才有用是之取〕
〔爾〕
考試官學正王　批〔識時務者在俊傑此子〕
〔以之〕
裕民厚俗之道何先亦曰知興替之端也
達利害之原也明得失之故也知通變之
===
術也知其端而後損益有方矣達其原而
後興革有機矣明其故而後斟酌有地矣
通其變而後法制可久矣盡是四者則上
順天時下盡地理中盡物情以之疏民困
而民困疏以之經國用而國用足以之厚
風俗而風俗美蓋不惟復豐阜之舊而熙
皞之休猶將致之舍是弗圖而欲苟且一
切以幾幸於目前吾恐植之者未幾而什
之者即繼一時之績効未收而歷年之積
punctuated:
議處。此作曲盡利弊，而作用有條，真可見之施設。況才思充周，知天馬行空，無所拘泥，經濟之〔才也，錄之。〕
考試官教諭文批〔有學，有才，有用，是之取〕〔爾。〕
考試官學正王批〔識時務者在俊傑，此子〕〔以之。〕
裕民厚俗之道何先？亦曰知興替之端也，達利害之原也，明得失之故也，知通變之術也。知其端而後損益有方矣，達其原而後興革有機矣，明其故而後斟酌有地矣，通其變而後法制可久矣。盡是四者，則上順天時，下盡地理，中盡物情。以之疏民困，而民困疏；以之經國用，而國用足；以之厚風俗，而風俗美。蓋不惟復豐阜之舊，而熙皞之休猶將致之。舍是弗圖，而欲苟且一切，以幾幸於目前，吾恐植之者未幾，而什之者即繼；一時之績効未收，而歷年之積
translation_en:
…to deliberate on their handling. This essay fully explores the benefits and drawbacks, and its proposals are orderly: they could truly be put into practice. Moreover, its talent and thought are ample and comprehensive, like a heavenly steed coursing through the sky [?], constrained by nothing—a talent for statecraft. Include it in the record.
Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “He has learning, talent, and practical usefulness. These are the reasons for selecting him.”
Examiner Wang, School Director, comments: “Those who understand the affairs of their time are outstanding men. This young man is one of them [?].”
What comes first in the way of enriching the people and improving their customs? It is understanding the beginnings of prosperity and decline, comprehending the sources of benefit and harm, discerning the causes of success and failure, and knowing the art of adapting to change. Only after understanding those beginnings can one reduce or augment things methodically. Only after comprehending those sources can one find the right opportunities to establish or abolish measures. Only after discerning those causes can one have a basis for weighing decisions. Only after mastering adaptation to change can laws and institutions endure. By fully accomplishing these four things, one accords above with Heaven’s seasons, makes full use below of the advantages of the land, and takes full account in between of the circumstances of things. Apply these principles to relieving the people’s distress, and their distress will be relieved; apply them to managing state expenditure, and the state’s resources will suffice; apply them to improving customs, and customs will become good. Indeed, one will not merely restore the abundance of former times, but also bring about the blessings of radiant harmony. If one sets these principles aside without considering them, wishing instead to improvise expedients in everything and gamble on immediate good fortune, I fear that scarcely will some have planted when others will follow to [undo their work?]. Before the achievements of the moment can be realized, the accumulated burdens of successive years…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
蠹滋甚矣此誠父母斯民者所宜深長思
也愚嘗讀周禮而知成周所以裕民之法
矣大司徒有土會之法以辨五地之物生
而時其賦令以土宜之法辨十有二壤之
物以教稼穡樹藝以土均之法辨五物九
等以制天下之地征而又有草人掌土化
之法以物地相宜而爲之種稻人掌稼下
之地以時其蓄洩畛種其所以教之力田
畢賦至纖悉也厥後太公明之以治齊因
其俗簡其禮通商工之業便魚鹽之利而
人民歸管仲假之以修政相地而衰征山
澤各致其時連五家之兵設魚鹽之利而
至於霸諸侯何其盛也是故全齊之盛轂
擊肩摩家殷人足其見於蘇秦之說者可
徵也東有瑯邪即墨之饒北有渤海之利
其見於田肯之說者可徵也膏壤千里洋
洋乎大國之風其見於太史公之說者可
徵也自井田廢而阡陌興貧富不均民務
punctuated: 蠹滋甚矣。此誠父母斯民者所宜深長思也。愚嘗讀《周禮》，而知成周所以裕民之法矣。大司徒有土會之法，以辨五地之物生，而時其賦令；以土宜之法，辨十有二壤之物，以教稼穡樹藝；以土均之法，辨五物九等，以制天下之地征。而又有草人掌土化之法，以物地相宜而爲之種；稻人掌稼下之地，以時其蓄洩畛種。其所以教之力田畢賦，至纖悉也。厥後太公明之以治齊，因其俗，簡其禮，通商工之業，便魚鹽之利，而人民歸。管仲假之以修政，相地而衰征，山澤各致其時，連五家之兵，設魚鹽之利，而至於霸諸侯。何其盛也！是故全齊之盛，轂擊肩摩，家殷人足，其見於蘇秦之說者可徵也。東有瑯邪、即墨之饒，北有渤海之利，其見於田肯之說者可徵也。膏壤千里，洋洋乎大國之風，其見於太史公之說者可徵也。自井田廢而阡陌興，貧富不均，民務
translation_en:
…the accumulated abuses grow still worse. This is indeed something that those who act as father and mother to these people ought to ponder deeply and at length. I have read the Rites of Zhou and thereby learned the methods by which the fully established Zhou dynasty enriched its people. The Minister of Education used the method of classifying land to distinguish the products of the five types of terrain and to time the orders for levies accordingly. Through the method of determining land suitability, he distinguished the products of the twelve kinds of soil, thereby teaching the cultivation of grain and the planting of trees and other crops. Through the method of equalizing land assessments, he distinguished five categories of products and nine grades of land, thereby establishing land taxes throughout the realm.
