There was also the Grass Officer, who administered methods of improving soil, matching crops to suitable land for planting; and the Rice Officer, who administered low-lying agricultural land, timing its retention and drainage of water, the laying out of field boundaries, and sowing. The means by which they taught the people to cultivate diligently and pay their levies in full extended to the smallest details.
Later, the Grand Duke elucidated these methods in governing Qi. He accommodated its customs, simplified its rites, facilitated commerce and craftsmanship, and made the profits from fish and salt readily available, so that people flocked to him. Guan Zhong borrowed these methods to reform government: he assessed the land and graduated its taxes, ensured that mountains and marshes yielded their resources at the proper seasons, linked every five households for military service, and established the profitable fish and salt enterprises. Thus he achieved hegemony over the feudal lords. How splendid this was!
Hence, at the height of the prosperity of the whole of Qi, carriage hubs struck one another and shoulders rubbed together; households were affluent and individuals had enough. The account of this in Su Qin’s speech provides evidence. To the east lay the abundant resources of Langye and Jimo, and to the north the benefits of Bohai: the account in Tian Ken’s speech provides evidence. Fertile soil stretched a thousand li, with the expansive bearing of a great state: the account of the Grand Historian provides evidence. Ever since the well-field system was abolished and fields divided by boundary paths arose, wealth and poverty have been unequal, and the people have devoted themselves to…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
逐末周官樹藝之教既罷不行而太公管
仲之政亦復斬焉歷代以來雖時有功令
之布而經界不正四民失業今日之齊非
復昔日之齊矣故在昔禹貢青州之田厥
等上下而今且以爲潟鹵之區何怪於嵩
萊之彌望而室廬之不保哉故曰知興替
之端而後損益有方者此也夫人情莫不
懷舊土而畏流離則其所以棄親戚墳墓
而逃亡者豈其得已哉夫不得已而爲之
===
其弊可知已蓋徭役之不均也賦歛之不
公也催科之太急也籍藪不實則戶口之
登耗非真勾稽不密則土田之飛詭無藝
富者巧於欺蒙而得免重大之賦貧者坐
以縮懦而代輸額外之征有司據簿以追
呼吏胥倚法而迫脅㣲瘝之民其不受斃
者鮮矣又況貪黷之吏非止此也藉征歛
之常而行其饕餮之欲甚者猰㺄其民而
用之柰之何民不失業也是故弱者挈老
punctuated:
逐末，周官樹藝之教既罷不行，而太公管仲之政亦復斬焉。歷代以來，雖時有功令之布，而經界不正，四民失業，今日之齊非復昔日之齊矣。故在昔《禹貢》，青州之田厥等上下，而今且以爲潟鹵之區，何怪於嵩萊之彌望而室廬之不保哉？故曰知興替之端而後損益有方者，此也。
夫人情莫不懷舊土而畏流離，則其所以棄親戚墳墓而逃亡者，豈其得已哉？夫不得已而爲之，其弊可知已。蓋徭役之不均也，賦歛之不公也，催科之太急也。籍藪不實，則戶口之登耗非真；勾稽不密，則土田之飛詭無藝。富者巧於欺蒙，而得免重大之賦；貧者坐以縮懦，而代輸額外之征。有司據簿以追呼，吏胥倚法而迫脅，㣲瘝之民，其不受斃者鮮矣！又況貪黷之吏非止此也，藉征歛之常而行其饕餮之欲，甚者猰㺄其民而用之，柰之何民不失業也？是故弱者挈老
translation_en:
…pursued secondary occupations. The instructions on planting and cultivation in the Offices of Zhou had ceased to be practiced, and the policies of Taigong and Guan Zhong likewise came to an end. Throughout successive dynasties, although official ordinances were issued from time to time, field boundaries remained improperly defined, and the four occupational groups lost their livelihoods. The Qi of today is no longer the Qi of former times. In the Tribute of Yu, the fields of Qingzhou were formerly ranked in the lower division of the upper grade; now the region is regarded as saline wasteland. Why, then, be surprised that weeds stretch as far as the eye can see [?] and that homes cannot be preserved? This is what is meant by saying that only after understanding the causes of flourishing and decline can one find proper ways to make changes.
It is human nature to cherish one’s native soil and fear displacement. Could those who abandon their relatives and ancestral graves and flee possibly be doing so willingly? Since they are compelled to do so, the abuses responsible are readily apparent: unequal labor service, unfair taxation, and excessively urgent demands for payment. When registers are inaccurate [?], recorded increases and decreases in households and population are untrue; when cross-checking is lax, fraudulent transfers and concealment of landholdings know no bounds. The rich skillfully deceive the authorities and escape heavy taxes, while the poor, through timidity and weakness, pay levies beyond their quotas in their stead. Officials pursue and summon them on the basis of the registers, while clerks invoke the law to intimidate and coerce them. Among the afflicted common people [?], few escape being driven to their deaths! Moreover, the conduct of corrupt officials goes beyond even this. They use routine tax collection to satisfy their ravenous desires; the worst devour their people like man-eating beasts and exploit them. How could the people fail to lose their livelihoods? Thus the weak take their elderly along…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
幼而移之四方其強者則暴悍抗令已耳
去生人之樂而即于囘其罪豈獨在下哉
故曰達利害之原而後興革有幾者此也
在昔滕君修井田之政四方歸之唐李絳
開營田之法即有明效今之土地即古之
土地也歸逋而興利宜無難者何乃招之
耕藝而民反避而去之若陷阱然者往歲
憲臣建議欲官給牛種矣官給農器矣三
年而後舉稅矣而迄至無成豈其終不可
===
爲乎亦曰主持之未定也奉行之未至也
倡率之無方也計口授業而或病於豪強
之兼幷給資散利而或歸於奸滑之侵漁
復之稅矣而其後又或責以歷歲之需是
以死易生也而民其爲之乎故曰知得失
之故而後斟酌有定者此也夫是議也苟
不欲行之則已如欲行之則復業之民姓
名可別籍也而力役不可槩征也輕稅可
稍出也而積逋不可幷責也勸課可行也
punctuated:
幼而移之四方，其強者則暴悍抗令已耳。去生人之樂而即于囘，其罪豈獨在下哉？故曰：「達利害之原而後興革有幾」者，此也。
在昔滕君修井田之政，四方歸之；唐李絳開營田之法，即有明效。今之土地即古之土地也，歸逋而興利宜無難者。何乃招之耕藝，而民反避而去之，若陷阱然者？往歲憲臣建議，欲官給牛種矣，官給農器矣，三年而後舉稅矣，而迄至無成，豈其終不可爲乎？亦曰主持之未定也，奉行之未至也，倡率之無方也。計口授業，而或病於豪強之兼幷；給資散利，而或歸於奸滑之侵漁；復之稅矣，而其後又或責以歷歲之需。是以死易生也，而民其爲之乎？故曰：「知得失之故而後斟酌有定」者，此也。
夫是議也，苟不欲行之則已，如欲行之，則復業之民，姓名可別籍也，而力役不可槩征也；輕稅可稍出也，而積逋不可幷責也；勸課可行也，
translation_en:
…and the young, and migrate in all directions; the stronger merely become violent and defy orders. They abandon the joys of human life and turn toward wrongdoing [?]. Can the blame lie solely with those below? This is what is meant by saying, “Only after understanding the sources of benefit and harm can one have a prospect of success in introducing reforms and abolishing abuses.”
In former times, the ruler of Teng restored the well-field system, and people from all directions flocked to him. When Li Jiang of the Tang instituted a system of agricultural colonies, it immediately produced clear results. The land of today is the same land as in antiquity: bringing back fugitives and developing its benefits ought not to be difficult. Why, then, when people are invited to cultivate it, do they instead avoid it and flee as though it were a pitfall? In past years, censorial officials proposed that the government supply oxen and seed, provide farming implements, and begin levying taxes only after three years. Yet nothing has been accomplished to this day. Can it really be impossible to carry out? It is simply that direction has been uncertain, implementation inadequate, and leadership ineffective. Land is allotted according to the number of mouths to feed, yet the powerful may encroach upon and engross it. Resources and benefits are distributed, yet they may fall prey to exploitation by unscrupulous men. People are exempted from taxes, yet afterward they may be required to meet demands accumulated over successive years. This substitutes death for life: would the people undertake it? This is what is meant by saying, “Only after understanding the causes of success and failure can one reach a settled judgment after due consideration.”
As for this proposal, if there is no desire to implement it, let it rest. But if it is to be implemented, the names of those returning to their livelihoods may be entered in a separate register, and labor services must not be imposed indiscriminately upon them. Modest taxes may gradually be collected, but accumulated arrears must not be demanded all at once. Measures to encourage and oversee cultivation may be put into effect…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
而刑督不可遽施也賑貸可先也而輸償
不可驟入也井田難復而稍爲限制可也
讀法未舉而稍爲聯屬可也鼓舞倡率宜
責之監司而不期以近效可也權宜施設
宜責之有司而不裁以禁忌可也故曰妙
通變之術而後法制可久者此也然其要
則惟在乎人焉耳矣孔子曰文武之政布
在方冊其人存則其政舉其人亡則其政
息是故趙充國之田金城曹孟德之田許
===
下郭子儀之田河中葛師德之田豐州爲
之兵戈倥偬之時而迄有成效得非數子
者以身任其責而不惑於異議耶爲今之
計莫若
朝廷之上申敕監司慎選守令專其責成緩
其遷代任其張弛明其功課表其循良黜
其貪刻績著則褒勞秩久則超遷六事不
舉則旌薦不及使爲守令者不得以苟且
目前之圖以應上之期會而僥倖於一旦
punctuated: 而刑督不可遽施也；賑貸可先也，而輸償不可驟入也。井田難復，而稍爲限制可也；讀法未舉，而稍爲聯屬可也。鼓舞倡率，宜責之監司，而不期以近效可也；權宜施設，宜責之有司，而不裁以禁忌可也。故曰妙通變之術而後法制可久者，此也。然其要則惟在乎人焉耳矣。孔子曰：「文武之政，布在方冊。其人存，則其政舉；其人亡，則其政息。」是故趙充國之田金城，曹孟德之田許下，郭子儀之田河中，葛師德之田豐州，爲之兵戈倥偬之時，而迄有成效，得非數子者以身任其責，而不惑於異議耶？爲今之計，莫若朝廷之上申敕監司，慎選守令，專其責成，緩其遷代，任其張弛，明其功課，表其循良，黜其貪刻。績著則褒勞，秩久則超遷，六事不舉則旌薦不及，使爲守令者不得以苟且目前之圖，以應上之期會，而僥倖於一旦
translation_en:
…but punitive enforcement must not be imposed hastily. Relief loans may be provided first, but repayment must not be exacted abruptly. Although the well-field system is difficult to restore, some limits may be imposed on landholding. Although the public reading of the laws has not been instituted, some organization of households into mutually linked groups is practicable. Encouragement and leadership should be made the responsibility of the regional supervising officials, without demanding immediate results. Measures adapted to circumstances should be entrusted to the responsible officials, without constraining them through prohibitions. This is what is meant by saying that only through mastery of adaptation to changing circumstances can laws and institutions endure.

Yet the essential point lies solely in the people entrusted with these tasks. Confucius said: “The government of Kings Wen and Wu is set out on tablets and documents. When the right men are present, their government is put into effect; when those men are gone, their government ceases.” Thus Zhao Chongguo established agricultural colonies at Jincheng, Cao Mengde at Xuxia, Guo Ziyi at Hezhong, and Ge Shide [?] at Fengzhou. They undertook these projects amid the turmoil of warfare, yet ultimately achieved results. Was this not because these men personally assumed responsibility and were not swayed by dissenting opinions?

For present purposes, nothing would be better than for the court to issue renewed injunctions to the regional supervising officials and carefully select prefects and magistrates; hold them individually responsible for results, defer their transfers and replacement, allow them discretion in tightening or relaxing measures, clearly assess their achievements, commend the conscientious and upright, and dismiss the greedy and harsh. Those whose achievements are conspicuous should receive praise and rewards; those who have served long in their posts should receive exceptional promotion. Those who fail to carry out the six duties should receive neither commendation nor recommendation. In this way, prefects and magistrates would be prevented from using expedient schemes for the immediate present merely to meet deadlines imposed by their superiors and hope for a momentary stroke of good fortune…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
其於民也省其刑罰薄其稅歛賑其凶饑
恤其禍災時其力役息其鬬爭聯其什伍
禦其攘掠使之相生相養相糾相受真若
赤子之依於慈母者而又先之以仁義孝
弟導之以睦婣任卹以作其良心而匡其
不逮由是而流離可歸由是而地利可興
由是而經賦可足由是而儲符可充由是
而禮義可作復豐阜之舊而成熈皡之休
蓋運之掌矣又何必屑屑於周官之經畫
===
與太公管仲之令而後為得哉愚青齊之
民也目擊時弊而欲以進聞久矣敢因明
問以對
punctuated:
其於民也，省其刑罰，薄其稅歛，賑其凶饑，恤其禍災，時其力役，息其鬬爭，聯其什伍，禦其攘掠，使之相生相養，相糾相受，真若赤子之依於慈母者。而又先之以仁義孝弟，導之以睦婣任卹，以作其良心而匡其不逮。由是而流離可歸，由是而地利可興，由是而經賦可足，由是而儲符可充，由是而禮義可作。復豐阜之舊而成熈皡之休，蓋運之掌矣，又何必屑屑於《周官》之經畫與太公、管仲之令，而後為得哉？
愚，青齊之民也，目擊時弊而欲以進聞久矣，敢因明問以對。
translation_en:
…In their treatment of the people, they should reduce punishments, lighten taxation, provide relief in famine, aid those suffering calamities, time labor services appropriately, quell disputes, organize households into groups of ten and five, and protect them against plunder. They should enable the people to sustain and support one another, correct one another, and take one another in, so that they truly resemble infants relying on a loving mother. Furthermore, they should lead them through benevolence, righteousness, filial devotion, and respect for elder brothers, and guide them toward harmony among kin, amity through marriage, mutual responsibility, and aid for the distressed, thereby awakening their innate moral sense and remedying their shortcomings. Thus the displaced could return, the productive potential of the land could be developed, regular tax revenues could become sufficient, reserves [?] could be replenished, and ritual propriety and righteousness could flourish. Restoring the former abundance and achieving the blessings of peace and harmony would then be as easy as turning something in one's palm. Why must one fuss over the arrangements in the Offices of Zhou and the ordinances of Taigong and Guan Zhong before deeming one's efforts successful?
I, an ignorant man, am a native of the Qing and Qi region. Having witnessed the abuses of our time, I have long wished to bring them to your attention. I venture to offer this reply in response to your discerning question.

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
洪濛既闢聖哲迭生天下古
今獨宗師孔子顏曾二子乃
親得其傳者然皆山東之產
焉或者泰山渤海巉巖浩瀚
秀靈鬱積鍾而爲人有此盛
耶抑天生聖哲氣數不偶又
===
弗在山川之秀靈而已也孔
子之後厥孫子思子出繹演
道原紹述先業再傳而得孟
子明仁義息邪説挺然以孔
子自任然亦不出鄒魯之墟
焉今讀其書真足以想見當
時之盛信乎一元之氣妙合
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

洪濛既闢，聖哲迭生，天下古今獨宗師孔子。顏、曾二子乃親得其傳者，然皆山東之產焉。或者泰山、渤海巉巖浩瀚，秀靈鬱積，鍾而爲人，有此盛耶？抑天生聖哲，氣數不偶，又弗在山川之秀靈而已也。孔子之後，厥孫子思子出，繹演道原，紹述先業，再傳而得孟子，明仁義，息邪説，挺然以孔子自任，然亦不出鄒魯之墟焉。今讀其書，真足以想見當時之盛。信乎，一元之氣妙合
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

After primordial chaos had opened, sages and wise men arose in succession; yet throughout the world, past and present, Confucius alone has been revered as the supreme teacher. Masters Yan and Zeng personally received his teaching, and all were natives of Shandong. Could it be that the craggy heights of Mount Tai and the vast expanses of the Bohai Sea accumulated such spiritual excellence, which concentrated in human beings and produced this flourishing? Or rather, Heaven’s production of sages and wise men involves no chance conjunction of vital energies and destiny, and cannot be attributed solely to the spiritual excellence of mountains and rivers.

After Confucius, his grandson, Master Zisi, emerged, elaborating the source of the Way and carrying forward his forebear’s work. Two transmissions later came Mencius, who clarified benevolence and righteousness, quelled heterodox doctrines, and resolutely took upon himself the mission of Confucius. Yet he too came from the lands of Zou and Lu. Reading their books today truly enables us to envision the flourishing of that age. Indeed, the vital energy of the primordial unity wondrously combined …

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
疑定發洩于是邦太史公謂
齊魯文學乃其天性良有見
也我
皇明尊崇孔孟之道以治天下建
學設科敷求俊彥山東取士
每三歲必七十五人重文邦
也然才藝彬彬蜚聲海內後
===
先相望代不鮮人而孔孟之
統吾今于爾多士屬望焉夫
文章道德本一也人自二之
耳孔子之教曰博文約禮多
識畜德何嘗不欲人學文哉
今縱觀爾多士通貫六經旁
搜子史厥文雄渾玄奧變化
punctuated: 疑定發洩于是邦。太史公謂齊魯文學乃其天性，良有見也。我皇明尊崇孔孟之道以治天下，建學設科，敷求俊彥。山東取士，每三歲必七十五人，重文邦也。然才藝彬彬，蜚聲海內，後先相望，代不鮮人。而孔孟之統，吾今于爾多士屬望焉。夫文章道德，本一也，人自二之耳。孔子之教曰：「博文約禮，多識畜德。」何嘗不欲人學文哉？今縱觀爾多士，通貫六經，旁搜子史，厥文雄渾玄奧，變化
translation_en:
…[the primal vital force] settles [?] and finds expression in this land. The Grand Astrologer’s statement that literary learning is innate to the people of Qi and Lu was indeed perceptive. Our august Ming dynasty reveres the Way of Confucius and Mencius in governing all under Heaven, establishing schools and examinations and seeking widely for outstanding talent. Shandong selects precisely seventy-five men every three years, honoring it as a land of literary culture. Men of refined talent and accomplishment, renowned throughout the realm, have followed one another in succession; no generation has lacked them. Yet it is to you, the assembled scholars, that I now look to carry on the tradition of Confucius and Mencius.

Literary accomplishment and moral virtue are fundamentally one; people themselves divide them into two. Confucius’s teaching says: “Broaden your learning through texts and restrain yourself through ritual; acquire wide knowledge and nurture virtue.” When did he ever not wish people to study texts? Now, surveying you assembled scholars, I see that you have mastered the Six Classics and ranged widely through the philosophers and histories. Your writing is powerful and full, profound and subtle, varying…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
抑揚而其氣亦浩然剛大塞
乎天地之間莫非一世之英
也而吾尤以孔孟之統惓惓
焉者豈好迂哉蓋攻于博文
而忽約禮銳于多識而不暇
畜德固學者之通患也夫以
包羅該括之才苦心極力終
===
身所得盡役役于詞鋒筆勢
之間以馳騁于一世厥藝誠
精專奇絕足以煒煌化理矣
復能反之此心而擬議于言
動發揮于事業進而獮
皇猷賛國是脩和庶政振舉紀綱
感通華夷昭格天地以成俊
punctuated: 抑揚，而其氣亦浩然剛大，塞乎天地之間，莫非一世之英也。而吾尤以孔孟之統惓惓焉者，豈好迂哉？蓋攻于博文而忽約禮，銳于多識而不暇畜德，固學者之通患也。夫以包羅該括之才，苦心極力，終身所得，盡役役于詞鋒筆勢之間，以馳騁于一世，厥藝誠精專奇絕，足以煒煌化理矣。復能反之此心，而擬議于言動，發揮于事業，進而獮皇猷，賛國是，脩和庶政，振舉紀綱，感通華夷，昭格天地，以成俊
translation_en: …with modulation and cadence, while your vital force, too, is vast, firm, and great, filling the space between Heaven and Earth. You are all outstanding men of your age. Yet why do I remain especially concerned with the tradition of Confucius and Mencius? Is it because I delight in impractical ideas? To strive for broad learning in letters while neglecting the restraints of ritual, and to pursue extensive knowledge eagerly while finding no time to nurture virtue—these are indeed common failings among scholars. With talents capable of encompassing and comprehending all things, you labor painstakingly and exert yourselves to the utmost; yet everything acquired over a lifetime is spent toiling amid sharp phrasing and forceful brushwork, seeking to distinguish yourselves in your age. Your literary art is indeed refined, accomplished, extraordinary, and unsurpassed, sufficient to lend splendor to moral transformation and good governance. If you can further turn this back upon your own heart, deliberate upon it in speech and action, and give it full expression in practical undertakings, advancing to further the imperial designs [?], support the guiding policies of the state, put the various affairs of government into harmonious order, uphold its governing principles and regulations, move and unite Chinese and non-Chinese peoples, and manifestly reach Heaven and Earth, thereby accomplishing outstanding…

title: 嘉靖十九年山東鄉試錄
text:
偉光明之烈則六經子史既
擬其華復覈其實表裏本末
渾融透徹而
國家元氣將有賴焉孰與文藝
獨成名者爲得耶斯道已在
我惟一轉移之耳爾多士其
猛省之哉陸贄司考校得韓
===
愈至今爲科目美談豈徒爲
文耶蓋愈丁道衰文弊之日
雄裁灼見識孟子于異端擾
攘之中慨然號于一世真吾
道之豪傑也而爾多士每每
淺之誠謂因文見道也若究
厥攸諳復徒文而已焉無乃
punctuated: 偉光明之烈，則六經子史既擬其華，復覈其實，表裏本末，渾融透徹，而國家元氣將有賴焉。孰與文藝獨成名者爲得耶？斯道已在我，惟一轉移之耳。爾多士其猛省之哉！陸贄司考校，得韓愈，至今爲科目美談，豈徒爲文耶？蓋愈丁道衰文弊之日，雄裁灼見，識孟子于異端擾攘之中，慨然號于一世，真吾道之豪傑也。而爾多士每每淺之，誠謂因文見道也，若究厥攸諳，復徒文而已焉，無乃
translation_en:
…great and illustrious achievements, then, having emulated the literary splendor of the Six Classics, the philosophical masters, and the histories, you will also have examined their substance. Outward expression and inner substance, root and branch, will be thoroughly integrated and understood, and the vital strength of the state will have something upon which to depend. Compared with winning fame solely through literary skill, which is the greater attainment? This Way already lies within us; all that is needed is a single change of direction. You scholars should awaken resolutely to this!

When Lu Zhi oversaw the examination, he selected Han Yu. To this day this remains a celebrated story in the annals of the examinations. Was it merely a matter of literary composition? Han Yu lived when the Way was declining and writing had become corrupt. With powerful judgment and penetrating insight, he recognized Mencius amid the turmoil of heterodox teachings and impassionedly raised his voice to his age. He was truly a heroic champion of our Way. Yet you scholars repeatedly take him lightly. You do indeed speak of perceiving the Way through writing; but if one examines what you actually understand, it is once again nothing more than writing. Might this not be…
